title: Returning item - no support from Linksys
text:
On paper the EA4500 seemed an ideal router for my new home network. I wanted to use it for wi-fi with my iPhone 4S and for an ethernet broadband connection to my Dish satellite TV. Wired connections to both my PC and the Dish receiver seemed to work fine. Wireless was sporadic at best. Worked fine in the same room with the router but often could not join the network from a room 25 feet away even though it recognized the network was there and the signal seemed good. I've used the iPhone on several public networks and one private one with excellent results so it's not a problem with the phone.

Called Linksys support 24 hours after installing the router. Hoped it was just a change in settings needed to make the wi-fi work properly. First CSR was friendly and after getting all the info said she would transfer me to engineering support, but the call was dropped in the transfer. Called again and at first the new CSR was helpful. Then he told me he would transfer me but I would be charged for the support service. I explained I had just purchased the router and it was less than 24 hours since install. Asked why I would be charged as a brand new customer who needed some help with installation. He became abrasive and insisted it was my phone's problem. I told him the phone has worked on several networks with no problems. In some cases for several days when I was coming and going and the phone always instantly reconnected to those networks. He still insisted I must pay for Linksys to help me. I again said that didn't seem right for a new customer and a new installation. Then he suddenly said have a nice day and hung up.

I called Amazon and asked what my options were. The very friendly CSR said I could return the router for a refund. She sent me the return authorization and label while be were talking. I'll ship it back on Monday. Can't say enough good things about the way Amazon is handling this. I can repack the router in the original box but,of course, can't replace the cellophane wrap. CSR said that is no problem.

I'm back to the drawing board in router selection but two things are certain. First, I'll never buy another Linksys product. Second, whatever router I select I will purchase from Amazon.

title: This is a WONDERFUL DVD player!
text:
It is NOT a ripoff! You just have to "hack" the player using the code I found on a forum:

Here are the directions:
1. No DVD in the tray, the tray is closed, and the player is on.
2. Press "Setup" on the remote.
3. Press the "down" arrow repeatedly until the top heading shows "Preferences".
4. Then press "OK" and Audio will be highlighted.
5. Press the "down" arrow and the next category "Subtitles" will be highlighted.
6. THEN enter this 6-digit code: 138931. Immediately the screen will show "Region Code 1".
7. Press the "up" arrow and "Code 1" becomes "Code 0" meaning All Regions or Region Free.
8. Press "Setup" to exit.
9. Turn off and then back on and it will play dvds from any region.

title: AWESOME product and convenience
text:
I've been in the market for a golf GPS or rangefinder and have been undecided for a long time. The laser rangefinders are definitely appealing, but the form factor and having to dig a large item out of your bag when you need to get the pin distance was a major drawback. I also looked at a bunch of the new GPS systems, but many of them almost had too many functions and features - enough that I knew I would be distracted during my golf round. Really, all I want is a good, reliable, accurate distance to the pin. This product is it.

I bought this a week ago on Amazon and have tested it at several golf courses -- a few I was unfamiliar with and my home course where I am already dialed into the distances from playing the course several hundred times. This item is very accurate. After I bought it, I was obsessively checking the distance and comparing it with markings on the course. It always matched the plaques or sprinkler head covers of all three courses I ran this on. On one round, I was with someone using a laser and on another round I was with someone using a SkyCaddie. This item matched both each time.

But the biggest plus to this product is the form factor. You can easily clip this onto the side of your hat or your belt and forget it is there. Need the distance to the pin - simple: press the button and it tells you. Need the distance to the front or back of the green - press the button again for three seconds and it tells you. It is very easy to hear, yet is quiet enough that it will not disturb your playing partners - in fact when the volume is turned down halfway, I doubt a playing partner five feet from you could hear it at all. If you don't want the voice, you can just peek down at your belt and see the distance in big numbers on the display, which update in real-time as you walk.

This item has two other features. One is where it will show you the actual shape of the green, and rotates that shape depending on your approach angle. I never really used this, because the graphical interface is simplistic, and I really only needed the distance to the pin. The second feature is very nice -- it will record the distance between any two points. So say you want to know how far you hit your six-iron. You press a small button on the side, then the main button. Then you hit the ball and walk to it. When you get there, you press the main button again and it will tell you how far you hit the ball. I suppose you could just as easily look down before and after you hit and then do a little math, but I still found this feature to be a big bonus. I am already pretty dialed into my club distances, but if you are not exactly sure how far you are hitting each club, this was a nice feature to have.

The first round I played with it was a five-hour round, and I obsessively hit the button as I played to test it out. I still had half the battery life left, so I believe this could easily last two full rounds, especially since under normal conditions I wouldn't be activating it every single time I saw a yardage marker for comparison.

This product is small, the clip is strong so you won't lose it, and it just plain works with an unobtrusive form factor that makes it a huge bonus. The voice is a computer-sounding female voice not unlike Siri on an iPhone.

I was not sure this would be the solution I was looking for -- but now I am certain that every GPS/rangefinder company will be copying this product in the next 6-9 months. It is really great. I love it.

PS - when you get it, it comes with a micro-USB cord. You should go to the GolfBuddy website and make sure you have downloaded the latest firmware version. Mine needed an update, but installing it took only a few minutes and clicks on my Mac.

UPDATE: NOVEMBER 2015 -- Well, I have played about 300 rounds with the Golf Buddy, and it finally died. But to update my old review, I can say that I played with this device all over the United States and the distances were always accurate. I will be replacing this with the new version, which shows front/back/center on the screen without having to cycle through -- a great improvement.

title: Excellent Customer Service
text:

The computer arrived in what seemed like perfect condition, and set up without any major difficulties once I realized that the gazillion included manuals/installation guides were for hardware and software already installed that I might want to reinstall later on. Fortunately, the people on their end were very patient and spent a sizable amount of time on the phone with me walking through the installation and putting up with my questions about which screw was which.

title: Don't buy for backing up your network.
text:
Hi all.

Here's my story and here's why you should not buy a Linkstation if you intend to use it to backup a network.

I use a Linkstation Pro to backup the pcs on our home network. A hard drive recently crashed on my PC. After installing a new hard drive, loading windows, etc., I went to restore my PC's data off of my linkstation. I could not get any of the data to "import" to Novastor, the backup software that Buffalo sells with the Linkstation. After hours of frustration, reading websites etc., I finally reached Novastor Tech support and learned....believe it or not... Novastor is capable of backing up to a NAS device but cannot restore from a NAS device when the data has to be "imported" (look up what Novastor means by this, but essentially importing is required if your PC's hard disk fails). Novastor's solution is for me to go down to best buy tonight, buy an external hard drive that connects to my PC via usb. Then, copy all the data from my Linkstation to the hard drive. Then I will be able to "import" the backup data and restore.

So, bottom line is if you have a linkstation, do not use Novastor for backup. If you ever do need to restore your data there will be a great deal of extra time and expense required. The "backup solution" Buffalo Technology is selling is horrible.

If you are shopping for a NAS for network backup, don't buy Buffalo Tech. Take advice from a very disappointed user.

And, BTW, I spoke to Buffalo Tech Support. All they could do was escalate the problem. They did explain that it really wasn't their issue because it was a software issue. They didn't seem to grasp that I purchased the software from BUffalo Tech, not Novastor. I tried to use the analogy that if my steering wheel fell off and I complained to Ford, Ford wouldn't claim that the problem was with the steering wheel company and that Ford just builds the car. They didn't seem to get it, though.

title: Works well, so far
text:
My rating is conditional in that I have not exercised all the features of this writer, or the NERO trial-package of CD/DVD burning software, but of those I have tested, it has worked very well.

IP Camera shipped my order immediately using standard delivery and I received the product within 3 working days (vice the estimated 1 - 2 week delivery period for standard shipping). Excellent service from IP Camera, with follow-up as to my satisfaction with their service.

I chose this product based on its feature-set, its compatibility with MS, MAC and Linux OSs, and on years of satisfactory experience with LITE-ON's OEM optical drive products - verses the rather sketchy reported performance of equal, or lower, priced similar models by competitors. It augments my laptop's built-in PCI-bus CD-writer and CD/DVD reader with a USB-2 DVD read/write capability.

To date, I've used it on a Toshiba Tecra A9 laptop with XP Pro using free CDBurnerXP, ImgBurn, InfraRecorder, and Windows Media Player, but not the included trial version of NERO.

It comes with no installation instructions, but, on plugging it in, XP Pro recognized it immediately and properly mapped it as CD-ROM 1 (CD-ROM 0 being the built-in CD/DVD already described), and it appeared as an option on all installed burning software. The immediate recognition and proper mapping were only obtained when it was plugged directly into a USB-2 socket on the laptop and did not occur when attempts were made to plug it into an externally powered USB-2 hub. The short (7 inch) Standard-USB-2 to Mini-USB-2 cable included limits the ability to position the drive for the user's convenience and easiest access, but fortunately, it works equally well with a 25 inch USB-2 jumper cable, as long as that cable is plugged into a USB-2 socket on the laptop. To this unit's credit, it burns disks well with the power and data supplied with only a single USB cable - not like many others that require a split/dual cable that takes up two USB sockets (with the laptop on external power - not battery power, assumed. This latter requirement is also true for burning CDs on the internal CD burner of this particular laptop).

I've burned music, video and data on -R CDs, -RW CDs, -R DVDs, and -RW DVDs with reliable speedy burns, but not yet tried the 7 other types, including dual-level DVDs. I expect equally good performance with them. To test a few Linux distros, I've burned an Ubuntu Live-DVD and openSUSE Install DVD images (latest versions) and, with appropriate changes in my BIOS, successfully re-booted my system from the live Ubuntu DVD in the LITE-ON drive. Of course, given the inherent bandwidth bottleneck of USB-2, one wouldn't want to operate Linux this way, but it did demonstrate the drive's ability to do as advertised on MS and Linux systems. I'm yet to burn any CD/DVDs from Linux but expect no problems there either.

Like all super-slim DVD drives, this one feels somewhat delicate and probably is not for the ham-handed or clumsy, but with reasonable care and use, should give good service over a wide range of uses.

title: It will not work out of the box due to poor construction
text:
I have purchased many Orion products in the past so I was quite surprised by the poor component fit of this device.
I feel compelled to warn purchasers about the issues I discovered.
The Canon T adapter tangs are much too thin to properly mount a Canon camera body. The camera flops around on the mount which is unusable. I compared this to tangs on my Orion T adapter (which works) and the good ones were twice the thickness. (So Orion cannot maintain common dimensions across their own product line.) I made spacer tabs from electrical tape which made the camera junction usable.
Then I discovered that the guide camera junction is also malformed and allows the guide camera to flop around as well. I placed a tape spacer on the periscope tube which was machined too small for its opening. The set screw only clamps the tube in one axis and frees to swivel the camera loosely in the other axis.
A third issue is that the supplied extension tube at 1" is much too long to match the Orion Starshoot with a Canon DLSR FL. I happened to have a 1/2" extension tube and ground it down to ~3/8" in order to get both cameras in focus. I would have expected to do this anyway but the Orion description implies that this unit will fit a Canon DLSR camera and Starshoot together when that is not the case at all.
It took 5 hours in the workshop to get this product to actually do what it was intended for. That is, hold a Canon DLSR and an Orion Starshoot together in good mechanical connection with a 2" nosepiece.
A purchaser without mechanical skills or time to correct this item will be seriously disappointed with its performance out of the box.

title: Question, Do YOU really need this Device?
text:
What a long strange trip this search has been!

Since upgading in the 90's to a car CD player, I missed having my Personal Cassette Tapes to use on the daily drive. Be it Jazz, Rock, Soul or Pop, I put alot of time into making them. They are the music I loved back then.... and Still Do! But alas they could only be listened to on my Home Stereo Cassette Player or old Walkman.

First I started looking at "New" in-dash Automobile Cassette Players, and let me tell you if you can find the space on your dashboard, there are only a few New Auto Cassette Players on the market. Then I thought... I already have a 3.5 jack on my Car Stereo for my MP3 player, so why not just plug-in my old Walkman into that. Hey, IT WORKED!!! Did you know you can still buy new Sony Walkman cassette players? But they have been discontinued and now comanding high prices.

Then I thought what could I get to "Digitize" my old cassette's to my laptop, and playback on my Portable MP3 player and thus ended up here. Amazon has the only reviews on these Cassette To MP3 Converters (thank's Amazon), and all are made by the same company with different names on them. I read all the reviews and decided it was a gamble for a sucessful tape transfer and sound quality. But without a Manufacturers warranty, my ultimate question was How Good was the Sound Quality and How Long would this device really last? Your best results will always come from the Best Playback Source. The old saying about recording is "Junk-In, Junk-Out"!

I already had Audacity on my Laptop and it's an Excellent Free Music Editor program. The Audacity program has a "Record" mode, and the site has instructions on how to hook up your devices at their web site. Then you can set the Record Volume, Edit the tracks and add Fades, Split the Tracks, EQ, and even Noise Reduce your music files to either Flac, Wav, or MP3. I also had a 3.5 Record Input jack on my laptop. So all I needed was a Stereo 3.5 Male to 3.5 Male cord plugged into the headphone jack on my Walkman, with the other end plugged into the Record Input jack on my laptop. You know what, IT WORKED! So you really don't need a cassette player with a USB Output.

So if I can use my Walkman Cassette player to transfer tapes to my laptop, why not my expensive Home Stereo Cassette Player? The Home Cassette Players have ALOT Better Spec's for Tape Transport and Audio Quality playback than these Walkman or Ion Cassette Players do. To make the Hook-up, all I needed was a Phono Plug (from Home Cassette Player) headphone jack to 3.5 Male Plug (to My Laptop). Then hit "Record" on Audacity and hit "Play" on the cassette deck. You can also make the Hook-up using a Double RCA Male from the Rear-Out RCA Jack (on back of cassette deck) to 3.5 male jack on your Laptop record input. This Setup worked "The Best" offering Superior Audio Playback, plus you have Dolby option. There are No Weak Tape Transport Speeds or "Tinny Sound" that you get from a Walkman or Ion cassette player.

So the question I ask you, if you have a Walkman or better yet Home Cassette Player do you really need this converter? If not, then this seems an alternative. But really what you are buying here is a low priced Walkman with a USB connection. Thats it, there's nothing Hi-Tek about this player. My advice is buy a "New" or "Used" Home Cassette Player if you really want "The Best" Sound Quality to work with!

I hope I have helped out with my quest to Keep Your Old Cassette Tapes Alive in your Daily Lives, I'm Happy to hear mine Once Again!

title: Not worth it
text:
Got this router based on Amazon reviews. I was pretty excited about the dual WAN capability as well as the gigabit ports (my existing wireless router is only fast ethernet capable and not gigabit). Once configured, I discovered that internet connections are dropped intermittently. Upon examining the logs, I found out that the router was refusing LAN->WAN connection, based on "Policy Violations", inspite of default policy settings that has no restrictions for LAN-> WAN traffic. A similar case has been logged by another Small Business User with Cisco and the SMB team has said that the issue "may be addressed as part of the next firmware release, and ETA is not known yet". Your support is a JOKE, Cisco - you put crap in the market for a premium price and don't even support it? My old router handled netflix streaming perfectly even when my blueray player was connected wirelessly. After buying this router, I connected the same blueray player via the ethernet port, and it is SLOWWWWWWW.......This is totally not acceptable - even the basic router function is not implemented properly and I attribute this to buggy firmware. Cisco had a lot of time to fine tune the RV0XX line, and this router just added gigabit capability (which is just updated hardware). Not sure what kind of nasty surprises await when I configure dual WANs.

01/30/2013 (Update) - I tried to flash the firmware again in the hopes that my problems would be resolved, but the router bricked. It is as good as a paperweight now. Stay away from this router like a plague. Cisco should be ashamed of themselves for putting such a substandard product in the market.I wish I could give zero stars......

02/01/2013 (Update) - Opened a ticket with Cisco. The support person tried to connect to the router and couldn't do so, so authorized a return. Once they get the unit in their return center, I heard that they will ship another unit to me and transfer the warranty to the new unit. However, I am liable for shipping the unit back and I will be getting a factory refurb. unit. Not too happy, but I am going with this option in lieu of this whole situation. Keeping my fingers crossed on the performance of the new unit. Will post an update.

02/11/2013 (Update) - Received the replacement unit and connected to my network with a lot of skepticism. However, the new unit does work satisfactorily. I have been throwing everything at it - no dropped connections, no refusals, streaming works perfectly (even with 2 movies streaming at the same time) and no hangups so far in the past 3 days. Changing my rating to 3 stars. Will post an update after more real world tests.

07/06/2013 (Update) - I am satisfied with this router thus far. No reboots over the past 5 months and my samsung Blu-ray player has no issues connecting to Netflix. Neutral rating still applies, as the product seems to be unpredictable. This will be my final update. Thanks to all for the encouragement.

title: 5 stars For My Viewing Area- Revised read full review.
text:
There are several reviews on Amazon with conflicting opinions. I believe that has more to do with each person's individual tastes/ set up. For me, this TV is absolutely perfect. The color reproduction is extremely accurate, the motion handling is nearly perfect and does not create and weird SOE (soap opera effect).

Fist off let me tell you about my set up. My tv room is extremely dark room, darker than a typical movie theater, so there is no ambient light which can cause glare. The TV is basically a giant black mirror when powered off, but when it is turned on, ANY and ALL reflections are eliminated. Now your room probably isn't as dark as mine, and if there are any bright lights your tv is going to show reflections. There is an anti-glare coating but it probably won't help you.

I personally do not care for the stand, but I do plan on wall mounting it anyway so it's not a deal breaker. I honestly don't see how it is a huge issue for people, get some black felt and cover it up or paint it black. Cheap and easy solution right there

Now let's get to the actual performance of the TV. Here are my settings, I use them for everything. Set it and forget it. These settings provide a natural skin and color tone. It may be too cool for you, and I do plan to update this review with some warm settings when I recalibrate it.

Scene Mode: General
Picture Mode: Standard
Back-light: 1( again its a super dark room, you might need to be higher)
Picture: Max (but reduce to 85 or even 60 for 3D content to help with crosstalk)
Brightness: 52
Color: 60
Hue: 0
Color Temperature: Neutral
Sharpness: 65
Noise Reduction: Off
MPEG Noise Reduction: Off
Dot Noise Reduction: Off
Reality Creation: Manual with Resolution 20 and Noise Filtering Min OR Off, based on preference.
Smooth Gradation: Medium
MotionFlow: Standard
CineMotion: Auto 1
Black Corrector: Off
Advanced Contrast Enhancer: OFF for 2D content. LOW for 3D content to help with 3D pop AND reduce crosstalk!
Gamma: 0
LED Dynamic Control: Standard
Auto Light Limiter: Off
Clear White: Off (or Low if you don't mind bluish whites in some cases)
Live Color: Off
White Balance: Defaults EXCEPT set G-Gain to -6 to reduce the overly greenish yellow skin tones on people on TV. Does not affect green intensity.
Detail Enhancer: Medium
Edge Enhancer: Off
Skin Naturalizer: Off
Display Area: FULL PIXEL change it to this as soon as you get your TV!
ALL ECO SETTINGS OFF
HDMI Dynamic Range: Auto
Color Matrix: Auto

I mostly watch blurays and play games on it. Both of which look amazing, now tv broadcasts can vary wildly. I find that certain channels/shows look better/worse than others. ESPN, Discovery/History channels look very good. Fox sports, honestly, kinda looks like crap. I suspect it is because of the high contrast and excellent picture that this set is capable of, the TV may bring out the natural flaws in the source. Garbage in, garbage out so they say. I'm not saying that you will be disappointed in your general TV viewing, but you wont be wowed by it.
For me, this isn't a huge issue. My general TV viewing is done in another room, not in my home theater. I really only bought this TV to watch blurays and play games on and if that is what you plan on doing, then this is the TV for you.

If you have any questions, feel free to ask them.
Thanks

UPDATE #1

After downloading a software update, I noticed that TV broadcasts have improved. Most channels now look good, though no where near as good as bluray. There is still some blurring but it is something I can live with.

I am still working on some settings for Warm viewing, I gave the Dark Knight a run through and I found that blooming can be a little bit of an issue with my above posted settings. After applying my Warm 2 settings, I found that blooming is almost eliminated. It's still there, but you really have to look for it.

My next update will be about 3d. I am still waiting on the glasses.

UPDATE #2
I received my 3d glasses, the PlayStation branded glasses, the other day so i decided to give Prometheus a watch. I saw Prometheus in IMAX and I originally thought that the 3d was very subtle and well done, on the XBR the 3d is much better and really "pops" at you. Now i all honestly, I do typically hate 3d, it usually gives me headaches it and makes movies unwatchable because of picture quality loss. I experienced none of this while watching Prometheus. The image does get a little darker because of the glasses, but I did not notice any loss of detail or dip in quality in the picture. Best off all, i could tilt my head, lie on my side and the picture never degraded. AWESOME! I am actually very impressed by this TV's 3d capabilities.

That being said, I did try and watch some non 3d content( Adventure Time) in Forced 3d mode. And I immediately noticed some crosstalk and had a headache within a few minutes. There are some options which may or may not help with the crosstalk, but I did not play around too much with that as my head was getting ready to explode.

Next update will be about the Warm settings I promised or gaming.

UPDATE #3
God Frakking Dangit! OK. SO after some serious game playing and movie watching sessions, I started to notice some DSE (dirty screen effect). For example, while playing Borderlands 2. When i slowly moved the analog stick, I would start to see blotches on the screen. Basically my awesome picture would deteriorate. Even in blurays, I started to see the same thing. TV sports,like hockey and football became unwatchable.
I'm not sure if my tv always had this and just didn't notice it, or if it started to wear out(the tv is less than a month old at this point). Either way it will be exchanged.

UPDATE #4
Good news, bad news.
Fist bad, I received my 3rd TV and it has a single dead pixel.
The Good news is that the blur surrounding everything is much better on this TV.

I have not decided what i will do with this set. I may keep it depending on how noticeable the dead pixel is or if i am done with the 950 all together.

For those keeping track, this will be my 3rd set.
1st set - 2 dead pixels
2nd set - motion blur and DSE
3rd Set- 1 dead pixel less blur and DSE

text:
I usually don't write reviews but after seeing all the less than favorable posts on this one i had to butt in. This is by far the most robust, no-frills, non-tinkered with router you can use out of the box. Pretty flawless so far. I have 3 Gigabit ports occupied along with 4 WLAN clients. Not to forget a 1 TB passport Hard-disk attached to the router that acts as a media server.
I have always been a fan of DD-WRT firmware. I used the legendary [[ASIN:B000BTL0OA Cisco-Linksys WRT54GL Wireless-G Broadband Router]] with DD-WRT firmware for over 3 years before I made the upgrade to E4200V2. After using this for about 10 days, I don't even think about not being able to load custom firmware on this one. We've had seamless streaming of High-Def Video, Local File Transfer, Printer sharing between our Windows 7 machines using the HomeGroup setup. I cannot stress this fact enough. Practically zero packet dropping.

Make sure to have separate SSID for the 5 GHZ and the 2.4 GHZ transmission. That way you can connect your high performance 5GHZ capable wireless clients to the correct SSID for maximum performance. You can use my setup as an example as depicted in the screenshot( [..] )

I'll probably give an update after 2 months of usage. Hoping it would be a non-event.

Update:

Sorry I promised a quicker update but here goes. the Router is still fantastic. Never had to RESET even once. The Device count gre to 15 at my place. The new firmware update gave us the ability to disable WPS.

title: Absolutely worth it for the price!
text:
This keyboard is very good for its price! It shipped all the way from Hong Kong, and it took about 10 days to get here.

Looking at this keyboard online, it seemed like a really cheap and flimsy thing with lights on it. I was reluctant to buy it, but I needed a budget keyboard until I can pick up a mechanical. So far, I really like this keyboard.

PROS
~~~~
+ Nice feel
+ Stunning LED backlight *
+ Windows Lock (Disables windows key while gaming so you can't accidentally press it)
+ Comes with a keycap puller and 8 clear keycaps for minor customization
+ Comes with 6 media keys: Mute, Vol. down, Vol. up, play/pause, back, and forward.

CONS
~~~~
- The enter key is not shaped like standard keyboards (It doesn't bother me because my old keyboard was like that)
- Instructions are in Chinese, and come with poor English translations (But you'll understand what everything means)

KEYBOARD FEEL
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The keys, compared to my last keyboard, feel a lot softer and quiet. They are soft and quiet, but they do not feel very squishy like a lot of rubber dome keyboards do. If you need a quiet keyboard for a quiet environment, this is a nice keyboard for you to try out.

*LED
~~~~
The LEDs in this keyboard are stunning. There are 4 modes of brightness for the lights: Off, low, bright, and breathing mode, which slowly turns the lights on and off, like a fade. It's actually really pretty

There are also three colors which can be changed by holding the FN key and pressing 5 on the numpad. There is blue, red, and a purplish-pink color. They all look really nice, especially at night.

FINAL THOUGHTS
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
This keyboard is absolutely stunning for it's price of only $25-30. A lot of people have had problems in the past with this keyboard with broken keys, LED problems, and connection problems, but you occasionally see problems and malfunctions on just about everything, right?

If you are looking for a good budget keyboard, I definitely recommend you pick this up.

(I will update my review if any problems occur in the future.)

title: Use the largest earpiece for great sound and heavy base - Tight Storage Case
text:
I was in the market for bluetooth earphones, and was looking for something with APT-X support - I liked the price on these but that these don't support APT-X codec was a bummer. I anyway went ahead and bought a pair as soon as the ones with the charging case were released. I am happy to tell you that these sound great!

At first I was a bit frustrated by the way these fit in my ears - I have medium to small ears - so naturally at first I tried them with the medium rubber pieces that they came with - they fit alright but would dislodge themselves while moving around, so I tried the smallest, they were worst than medium - finally I decided to try the largest, knowing that it was a futile exercise. However, after getting over my mental block, I realized that the largest ear rubber pieces fit the best and most snug - they are just a thin sheet of rubber so they expand and mould into the shape of your ear canal - if you haven't tried them - give it a shot and keep them on for atleast a few minutes - once you get over the mental block, they not only fit snug, but let you enjoy the best sound and good base (by blocking out outside sound due to a good fit) - give it a shot, whats there to lose?

Now I enjoy these earplugs a lot - the sound is great and very loud, but unlike others i find the base to be a bit on the heavy side (perhaps due to the snug fit of the largest ear buds?). On my 7th gen ipod nano I use to use the Bass Reducer equalizer preset. Thats how much bass I get!

On your android, if you can install an equalizer app, the sound goes from excellent to fantastic.

The case that came along is very useful to store and recharge the headphones, but as others have already mentioned, its a bit tight. I would be afraid to store these earphones without a case.

Pros:
Thin form factor and very light
Flat cable that does not tangle
Great sound with snug fit
Easy to recharge with charging case (I plug in the case charge cable into the headphones every time i put them back in the case, so I ve never had out of charge problem)
Easy to pair with the latest BT devices (with separate selectable phone/music profiles via BT device - I use it for music/movies only not for phone calls)
Common USB Micro charger, so can charge with your mobile charger as well (since that is the most common charger these days for most devices)

Cons:
Tight Case
No Apt-X support
Flat cable that sometimes gets caught in the collar behind the neck
Tight Case
Tight Case

Overall, these are excellent and I would recommend them to anyone looking for great sound and small form factor.

(I use these with Samsung Galaxy Note 2, Ipod Nano (7th Gen) Ipad 3)

title: For the sake of anyone looking for repair info. ...
text:
For the sake of anyone looking for repair info....
I had one stop working after 2 years. I tried swapping in all the included IR extenders to no avail.
The red LED would blink as though it was receiving from the remote, but it didn't appear to be generating an IR signal.
Finally ordered another remote/PowerBlaster bundle and confirmed it was the old PowerBlaster that was the issue.
Having the new one to use, I tore the old one apart and discovered that the built in IR LEDs were incredibly dim when viewed through a cell phone camera. They appeared to be daisy chained, so a problem with one would prevent them all from working.
No idea why they would be dim rather than just not working, but IR LEDs are cheap so I replaced them all (5mm 940nm) and lo and behold the old PowerBlaster works again.

title: Antec 302 is a Big Improvement over the original antec 300 Case
text:
Being a lover of the original antec 300 case (did 4 different builds in them) I had to give the antec 302 a try.

PROS:

**Mini ITX, Micro ATX, Standard ATX Compatible
**Easily removeable side panels and front bezel
**Mounts for 6 x 120MM fans (2 front, 1 side, 1 rear, 1 behind mobo trey) and Mount for 1 x 140MM (top)
**Fan speed switches on back of case for included rear 120MM fan and top 140MM fan
**Watercooling Ready Rubber Gromet holes on top of case
**USB 3.0/USB 2.0 Ports, Mic Port, Headphone Port, all on front of case.
**8 expansion slot bays (most midtowers only have 7)
**Power Supply Filter at Bottom
**The Front 2 x 120MM fans mounts have a filter
**BIG BIG improvement on cable management (most of the wires can now be tucked behind the mobo trey
**Sideways Hardrive Bays (to allow up to 12.5" video cards)
**the 3.5" hardrive bays will hold up to 6 hardives and also use quick removeable rails (no more screws needed)
**the 3 x 5.25" Optical Drive bays are also screwless, simply slide them in and they snap into place.

CONS:

**1 of the SSD mounts is on the mobo trey (Really antec? Seriously? you have to remove the motherboard to change the SSD?)
**No cable management place to route a 8 pin motherboard plug for the cpu, this was the only cable I had to keep in front.
**120MM fan mount behind motherboard trey requires a low profile fan, if the fan frame is too thick it could hit the motherboard.
**8 expansion slot bay mounts are now on the outside of the case and requires removing a seperate bracket that covers all 8 slots before installing your cards. I found this to be big hassle.
**Included 120MM and 140MM fans are garbage, too weak, and only 2 speed. The 140MM fan actually started rattling on me after just a week of used as well. So I ended up using my 120MM and 140MM fans from my old antec 300 case that were 3 speed, they work better, and have way better airflow.

CONCLUSION:

Overall this is a nice case for the most part and I love that antec kept the classic 300 look and just did a redesign of the case frame. Just wish they included a 3.5" to 2.5" adapter for the SSD's instead of having a mount at the bottom and behind the motherboard trey, and also wish they kept the explansion slot mounts inside the case like they did on the antec 300.

title: Is this the best we can do? Maybe so.
text:
This review is about a Toshiba DVR670KU DVD/VHS Recorder.

I recently bought a Magnavox MDR515H with a hard drive and sent it back it was such a frustrating POS. I then got this Toshiba DVR670KU DVD/VHS Recorder. Looks to be the same lousy firmware as the Magnavox by the menu screens and horrible channel selection method, etc. but I kept it anyway. (I can't keep wasting money on return S&H!) At least it only records a black silent screen on some of the channels as opposed to most of the channels like the Magnavox, and 5 to 10 seconds can add up when you have to wait that long between every channel change. It can literally take several minutes just to go from a channel at the low end of the tuner like 4-1 to one somewhere in the middle like 20-2. And yes, you have to wait for every single one in between. You can't see the channel you are programming as you set the timer so you don't know if there is actually a channel there and you can't label the channels so you better remember that 90-6 is actually channel 38. Also, you cannot remove subchannels from the channel list, so if you have one subchannel you want to keep like 120-11, but you don't want the other subchannels 120-1 thru 10 and 120-12 thru 22 say, which may not even have programming there, you're stuck with all or nothing. Now, some of the channels look fine when you tune to them, but when you set a timer recording you end up with 60 minutes (or whatever) of blackness with no sound. It records alright... there's just nothing there to see or hear, so you have to figure out which channels do that and hopefully find the same program on a different channel that will record actual video and audio. (I know, I know... whaddya want, everything?) Other than the aforementioned difficulties it has been pretty reliable timer-recording-wise.

The remote is aggravating. Maybe it's all me, but I can't help pressing the wrong buttons all the time when I want to pause, play, rew, ff, etc. When you pause you can't just hit the pause button again to resume you have to hit play. Simple, I know, but I just don't think the buttons are laid out very well. If you accidentally hit next program instead of fast forward you've got to go back and start at the beginning and ff till you get to where you f'ed up. The trouble with that is the fastest speed isn't all that fast and the incremental (up to 180 secs.) skip speed isn't either. Editing titles isn't a lot of fun. A lot like typing on a telephone. Maybe texters are better at it than me but I prefer a display that you can navigate. The remote is also very directional. If I don't have it aimed exactly at the sensor on the unit it doesn't respond. The remotes I'm used to were good anywhere in the vicinity, even bouncing the signal off the tv screen.

I've found that formatting discs in VR mode on the Toshiba eliminates the need for "finalizing" if I want to play a disc on my Panasonic. Also, the Toshiba will play the DVD-RAM discs I record on my Panasonic though it won't record to them and I lose the ability to play back at 1.3x speed. Another good thing is being able to record to VHS from a digital signal (unlike the Panasonic), especially since we have no analog channels provided on our cable system anymore. (Now, Comcast... THERE's a topic for disgruntlement! Some other time and place.)

I would recommend it, hesitantly though keeping in mind the problems mentioned earlier, because it has been pretty reliable once I caught on to it's wierd limitations recording certain channels. I would not recommend it for it's tuner capabilities. You're better off with a converter box if that's what you're looking to do.

title: ATI Drivers cause BSOD within 5 minutes of system boot.
text:

title: Works on Late 2012 27" iMac After Changing Slot Order
text:
I initially installed this memory in the already-open slots 1 and 3 (the factory RAM was in slots 2 and 4) and got 3 beeping sounds and no bootup. After following the advice of another reviewer here, I turned it back off, opened the memory compartment back up, and swapped the positions of the factory RAM and the Crucial RAM so it went like this:

Slot 1: 4GB Apple RAM (Top slot if iMac is upright)
Slot 2: 8GB Crucial RAM
Slot 3: 4GB Apple RAM
Slot 4: 8GB Crucial RAM (Bottom slot if iMac is upright)

That worked fine and I now have 24GB of RAM installed on the Late 2012 27" iMac.

Tip 1: the Crucial RAM is a tight fit in the memory slots. To get them back out to swap their positions, I first had to remove the Apple RAM so that I could get a better grip on the Crucial RAM.

Tip 2: I had difficulty getting the memory access panel off of the iMac because my finger wasn't going far enough in to depress the button all the way. I used a small key (a screwdriver would work too) to push the button in all the way to get the access panel to pop open.

title: Works as advertised, but with some important caveats for Mac OS X users: puts drives to sleep way too quickly!
text:
This unit is of average light-weight plastic build quality. I've had mine for about 6 months and have had no operational issues with it, i.e. it mounts & unmounts drives reliably, and transfers data reliably.

However, on my setup, which is a 2012 Mac Mini 6,2 (2.6Ghz core i7), under both OS X 10.8 and now OS X 10.9, ---> THE UNIT SPINS DOWN ATTACHED DRIVES AFTER ABOUT 10 SECONDS OF IDLE TIME. This is *extremely* annoying if you are trying to use the unit for anything other than large, continuous transfers. I.e. if you need to just browse through a folder of PDFs every now and then, or your database serves up image files from this drive, there is a very annoying delay every time the drive(s) have to spin back up from the excessively-short sleep interval.

I have found no way to disable the 10-second idle sleep interval. Unchecking "put drives to sleep" in Energy Saver pref pane doesn't affect it, nor do any Terminal.app-based command-line solutions. This issue is probably something related to a slight difference in the way USB3 is implemented in the dock & on the Mac Mini, and as such there is probably no way to resolve it.

So, in summary, I find the dock is only useful for mounting drives for period backup & restore purposes -- operations that keep the drive constantly busy, so it doesn't spin down & sleep. This limitation is rather hobbling as it removes about 50% of the usefulness of the device.

title: Not the best, but not the worst antenna on the market
text:
Receiving over the air television is a tricky thing, especially if you live in an area with many trees. You have to have the proper height and the proper angle to actually get in anything during the daytime, but at night you are looking at a different story. I won 2 of these in an online auction for less than you would pay for a set of Rabbit ears. Knowing that the price was so low, I knew I would have to look up many different ways to get these antennas to work. My solution placed them outside almost 40 feet in the air ( the entire cable length. ) I then used a combiner to place the signals together and was able to receive in the daylight hours 4 channels. However since I do not watch television until 6:00 pm, I noticed something remarkable about these little antennas. My reception improved and I was able to get 80 channels using 2 of these pointed in opposite directions. So they do work, if you know what you are doing.

Now the cons of this antenna. The rotor is a single button which does not allow you to choose which direction the antenna will turn in. Older rotors had actual directional points that helped you place the antenna in exactly the right direction everytime. Another problem is the rotors may or may not work for you. I have 1 antenna whose rotor still works; however, the other one lost its ability to rotate after 1 day. The coaxile wire is very thin so it might not last long.

However, when you consider the price of this antenna against the big ones, it does what it claims to do. The antenna itself is small and light weight. But is made as well as the larger ones ( so do not let that argument work against your decision ). The only gripe I have about mine are the rotors, but considering my closest digital station is over 60 miles away ( and it picks it up great ) this little antenna will do the job you want if your patience holds up to all the work you need to do to get in over the air TV.

title: Location, Location, Location
text:
Let me preface this review with a little geographical information. I live in a first floor apartment in a relatively flat part of central NJ and I am about 25 miles from the NY broadcast towers.

Like most people, I was tired of paying close to $200 per month for cable. After a lot of research on what signals I could potentially receive, I was finally able to convince my girlfriend that we could cut the cord and with an antenna to pull in at least the big 4 networks, and Netflix filling in the gaps, we would never miss it. I originally bought this antenna for nothing more than a proof of concept. I figured, if an $8 pair of old rabbit ears could pull in at least a couple, then I could justify spending at least $35 for the (almost) universally praised Mohu Leaf.

When the box arrived, I hooked it up, ran a scan, and pulled in 3 stations (well, only one was audio and video). That was good enough for me. Within a week or so, I put this antenna away and ordered the Leaf. While I won't go into my full experience, after playing around with positioning, I was able to pull in 24 channels.. While the design of the Leaf is more aesthetically pleasing than rabbit ears, I feel the drawback is that it can limit where you can place the antenna.

Things were going well, but my girlfriend missed watching Good Morning America while she got ready for work. I knew going in that the Leaf would not pull in VHF, which our ABC station is. In the interest of science, I decided to give the RCA antenna another shot. I bought a 25' cable and a coupler and decided to put the antenna in a kitchen window, facing NE towards the towers. I ran a scan and almost fell over when the antenna picked up 42 channels. Granted, most were in another language, but CBS, NBC, FOX, and ABC came in crystal clear and in full HD. To be fair, i tried placing the Leaf with the longer cable as well, but it just could not compare. I couldn't send the Leaf back fast enough. Now, I'll admit, running a wire from my living room to the kitchen to achieve this is not the prettiest solution, but we don't watch TV constantly, so it's not too big a deal to us.

My advice to anyone considering cutting cable would be to do your homework. If you're 35+ miles from a tower, you're just not going to get results with an indoor antenna. There are lots of websites that will help you find out what signals you can pull in (antennaweb.org comes to mind). Once you get your antenna, put it in different places through your house. A few feet can make a huge difference.

title: Great camera, great lens
text:
I have owned Sony digital cameras all the way back to the F717. I bought this to replace my A55 for recent a trip to Europe (Italy, Switzerland). All I can say is I am not only in love with this camera, I am in love with this 2.8 16-50 (24-75) lens.

The digital EVF works fine. In 2 weeks of shooting hundreds of pictures I never said, "I wish this was a real viewfinder" and actually the fact that when you change settings you see the result in the viewfinder BEFORE you take the picture is a big plus.

They cramed about as much resolution as you can in a 2/3rds sensor, and I kept waiting to see extra noise, but it just was not there. Now I did keep all my shooting at ISO 400 and under, but no issues if doing that. What I love about the resolution is I can take a picture and still have plenty of room to zoom in and still have enough resolution to print even up to a 16" wide print.

The layout, 2 dials (as opposed to 1 on the A55) and joysick make navigating around about as intutive and easy as any full featured DSLR can be with all the gazillion options. It is solidly built and weather sealed (and I did take it out in the rain with no issues).

Now the lens. I have had the Zeiss 3.5-4.5 16-80 (24-120) lens as my prime for years. Awesome lens, but I hate to say it, I like this new 2.8 16-50 (24-75) lens even better. (I think this is the first time a camera came with a default lens that was not junk!) Read the professional reviews. Yes it is a bit fat, but man, that constant 2.8 is awesome and allows you to take photos in much less light at higher speed (or lower ISO) then the Zeiss. Now you do loose a little in zoom, but again the resolution allows more cropping so essentially I have the same resolution with this camera at 50(75)mm as I do with the A55 and Zeiss at 80(120)mm.

Back at home I took a bunch of action photos of my Godson's soccer game with an inexpensive Tamron 70-300 (105-450) lens. Oddest thing, I was very dissapointed with the quality of this lens and the A55, figuring it was the lens and you just get what you pay for. But with the A77 the pictures looked great. Better then with the A55. I have no empirical data to back this up, but all I know is those pictures of my Godson playing soccer came out fantastic.

This package, even at full price is a deal (the camera by itself is $900, the lens $800, so you save $200 with the bundle). I would love to get the full frame A99, but after printing out a bunch of 16" wide prints on my Epson 4880 for display I can not imagine the quality being any better, certinally not enough to warrent spending 3x the money. I think this is the best quality and value package for a full prosumer 2/3rds DLSR out there.

title: Great mid level receiver with powerful sound and new features
text:
Denon has always made high quality audio products. Their receivers have consistently ranked among the top 5 in every review. Safe to say, that Denon is a much better brand in AV receivers compared to Sony, Panasonic or Pioneer. And yes brand name does matter not only in terms of sound quality but unit life and components quality.

This Denon E-300 sits right in the middle of the lineup. Surprisingly, this unit was half the weight of my Denon 2106 that it replaced. The size is also smaller. Fitting in in my TV cabinet was a breeze.

The wire connectors on the back are a no brainer. My prior AVRs had binding posts but this one has easy inputs. Just push the knob, insert the bare wire and let go. No more screwing in of the binding posts. My finger tips thank me.

One high speed HDMI cable connects this to my blu- ray player. The cable can be a cheap purchase but make sure it's high speed.

The remote is really light and much smaller than my older Denon remote. I keep it encased in plastic so as not to get any spillage from food and drinks since I watch movies while eating.

Set up was easy. The onscreen display walks you through it all. The provided mic was interesting. usually, it makes you sit at one position while it adjusts. Not this Denon. It asks for 6 different sitting positions.

Tip: The positions start with center back, left back, right back, center front, left front and right front. The six different sitting positions are provided so that if you have six people watching movies with you, each of them would get the enveloping surround sound effect perfectly. I think the idea is ingenious. I simply sat at these positions holding the mic on top of my head. I didn't worry about getting a tripod. This worked easier for me.

Once, I inserted a blu-ray disc, the system came to life. My cheap onkyo speakers never sounded better. The screen lights up with either DTS HD MA or DOBLY HD when playing movies. The sound quality is better than what I've ever heard. With my Denon 2106 I had the volume up 75% to get the sound but with this Denon 300, I have it only 30-40%.

The on-board apps for radio need internet connection. I connected it with an Ethernet cable to my modem. The internet radio choices are too many. I love it. The dance music radio station sounded awesome. The base was tight and in sync. The audyssey adjusts the sound and balances it when you play at low volumes so sound elements are not lost.

Overall, I love this unit. I paid $200+tax for it. Highly recommended!!

title: Device is OK, but tech support is worse than awful and Netgear won't stand behind its tech support.
text:
I've had one of these since 2012. The device is not the easiest to configure, but it does seem to work OK once you get it configured the way you want it. But this required using Netgear's technical support, which can be awful. The initial device I had was defective, but before he would give me an RMA the tech wanted me to test my hard drives. I asked how, and he told me to put it in a computer. I asked how again, and close to an hour later the guy confessed he'd never seen a iMac before and had no idea how to test a bare drive in my iMac. (Which requires special tools and disassembly of the screen to access drives, and substituting a drive would remove the OS so the system wouldn't work.)

The I had an issue using the ReadyNAS for Time Machine backup. The drive on my iMac crashed, was covered under Apple's warranty, and I wanted to restore my files. The techs at the authorized repair place couldn't do so. Partly because TM sparse bundle is not visible to the end user, even with admin privileges. But when I got the iMac home, I also couldn't restore from the ReadyNAS. So I called Netgear, and their techs accessed the ReadyNAS directly and did all kinds of things, but they never told me exactly what they were doing. Over a year later, with Netgear repeatedly closing the case even though things weren't resolved, I learned on a Western Digital NAS site to check that I was using the Time Machine password. On the ReadyNAS this is something you set when you set it up and never use again unless you need to restore from TM. Even though early on I told the Netgear tech people I was trying to restore using either my own password or the admin password, with no success, they never ever mentioned the TM password. Instead, they accessed the ReadyNAS, made a bunch of undocumented changes, and screwed around with the files, doing things like duplicating the sparse bundle. In the process, I wasted hundreds of hours following their instructions, doing things like copying the extra sparse bundle to a USB drive and then attaching it to my iMac and trying to restore my files that way. In the meantime, I needed to use my computer, so I set up another TM backup on a USB device. When I realized the problem was the TM password, I contacted Netgear and asked for help merging the two TM backups and putting the ReadyNAS back into the state it was before Netgear's techs screwed around with it. They refused, but offered to give me support for several hundreds of dollars. You've got to be kidding.

FWIW, even though Netgear advertises this device as supporting Time Machine, according to people at Apple that I spoke with, Apple does not support Time Machine on any NAS other than Apple's Time Capsules. While this might be expected, the Apple techs I spoke with said that in their experience Time Machine just doesn't work with third-party NAS drives. It may work for a while, but sooner or later it has serious problems.

I'll never buy another Netgear NAS. The product is OK, but tech support is as likely to waste your time as solve the problem. And Netgear won't stand behind its awful tech support.

title: Blocks Ambient Light Sensors 11-12-2014
text:
Update,12-19-2014: The new pictures of the color version of this case show cutouts that should fix this problem, but the black one does not yet. Check the picture before you order to make sure that the cutouts are there on the one you order. They have promised to send me a new case with this fix within five business days.
12-27-2014 Update: The replacement that they sent me from their Florida facility was the same design that covered the light sensors. Finally I contacted their home office in England and they sent me a new design case that is perfect. I have no idea what you would get if you ordered one from Amazon today. Reviews as late as 1-5-2015 show that they continue to ship the old design units without warning and only replace them when they get a complaint. Even more recently, they have changed their Amazon product pictures to show the old design, which indicates they have a lot of defective cases to unload.

This case covers up the ambient light sensors so that the automatic brightness adjustment does not work. This was not a problem with earlier iPads because they had a single sensor that shared an opening with the front facing camera. The Air 2, on the other hand, has two sensors that are near the top corners and need their own openings to function. You can see the exact locations of the sensors by shining a flashlight on the front corners of your iPad. Fortunately the sensors are redundant so that I was able to solve the problem by punching a hole over the one on the left. The one on the right is too close to the sleep wake magnet and I avoided it. My auto brightness function on my iPad Air 2 now works exactly as it would without the case and I am quite happy with the result. To avoid making a mess, you will need to use a 5/16 inch hollow leather punch and get your alignment just right. I do not believe that I should have had to do this and hope that Snugg will eventually fix this problem in their factory. I will rate this product five stars when they do as it is otherwise a great cover.

text: When I first set up this laptop it would drop the wireless connection every time I left it for an hour or so. I have two other computers and neither had a problem with the connection so it had to be this computer. I called Dell support, and after transferring me to three people who said they could not help I finally got connected to the right person. She updated all my drivers and the BIOS and the connection problem seems to be fixed, however my download speeds as measured by the xfinity speed test web site are very inconsistent. I have a Surface Pro Three in the same room and it consistently gets 26 - 29 mbps download speeds, this Dell laptop varies from 25 to 6. Hey, I am pretty impressed with this unit, it does everything my Lenovo Windows 8.1 laptop can do and is so useful to me I am surprised just how much I use it compared to previous Android tablets I have owned.
I have Office, Adobe Photoshop Elements 11, and Corel Video Studio X6, plus drivers for my Epson Workhorse Printer and a host of other software installed.(4 gig of ram is barely enough for video editing but it copes well without crashing)This thing can run anything a regular laptop can and does it well!
It is a pleasure to use, after it updated flawlessly to 8.1 I am even more pleased with it. The addition of the new (old) start button is welcome but because I never really missed the old one, it is not a major change for me.
The cameras work very well, Microsoft does not tell us how many megapixels they are but I would guess about 4 or 5 and the photos and video are adequate. Skype really excels on this and folks tell me the video quality they see on the other end is terrific!
The touch-pad is OK, I have tried out a friends keypad and I do prefer that and may spring for one soon, though I must stress the touch pad is quite usable, I love that you can fold it back out of the way and it becomes inactive.
The sound is perhaps not loud enough though very clear, however we are talking about a small tablet so it is quite expected. Bluetooth works very well and the HDMI output is also excellent. I doubt that the included HDMI adapter is OEM but it does work perfectly and I have used this a lot to watch certain programs and documentary's on TV, the images are great.
As everyone has stated in their reviews, battery life is a little on the short side, I get about 5 hours which is workable and I managed to easily watch two full length movies on a long distance back recently.
The screen is excellent, even you tube videos look good on it.
It is a little on the heavy side and gets warm to the touch. As with every tablet I have ever held, they do hurt your hands after a while.
All in all, a very nice tablet for work and leisure, it fits perfectly into my expectations and does everything I need. I deducted one star for the less than stellar battery life but I think Microsoft have made a really nice quality tablet.
I would imagine that the Pro 2 will be even better but I am really happy with this version....it is a real keeper!

So yeah, if 1) you want a pretty big TV on which to play games, 2) you're like me and see no need to double-dip by having both Smart TV and Xbox One apps that literally do the exact same thing, and 3) you're on a budget, then this TV is a GREAT choice.

title: Best Buy For The Money
text:
First let me say this is the first turntable I have owned since the "70's" when all music was recorded on LP or 45's. With the advent of 8 track, cassette tape, CD and digital downloads I was certain I had seen the last of vinyl. And then I listened to a vinyl recording of the Miles Davis classic Bitches Brew and found that I enjoyed the music "the way it was intended". No digital assistance or enhancement for the artist, just music.

I started to research turntables and the first thing I found was most low and mid priced receivers do not have phono jacks that allow a turntable without the additional purchase of phono preamp. Another thing was that the vast majority of the lower priced turntables on the market were designed to allow vinyl to be converted to digital downloads. Not having any lp's or a desire to convert to digital, these were not for me. And then I came across the AT LP60. I read technical descriptions and customer and professional reviews. This seemed too good to be true......a fully automatic, belt driven turntable in the $100 range that comes with a preamp s well as a cartridge and stylus. Okay but it's going to be cheaply made, ugly, and sound terrible right? I placed the order fully prepared for the worst.

After a very simple set up and connection, placing the switch in "Line" to allow connection to my receiver without phono jacks I placed a newly acquired lp on the turntable and hit the start button. I was blown away, the music was rich and true. The auto feature works flawlessly, the pause picks up the tone arm when the button is pushed and places right back in the same groove when pushed again. It sits atop my stereo cabinet and is a pleasure to look at. It appears to be very well constructed.

I'm sure there are turntables out there that are better, do as much or more, and allow better adjustments (balancing the tone arm, etc. ) but for my money this is everything I need to enjoy my re-found vinyl recordings. I'm a kid again and I'm happy.

title: Great case that can double as a purse

The camera did not come with a neck strap, doesn't have a grip, and is the most expensive camera I've ever owned, so I was a bit phobic about dropping it. I really liked the sense of security I got from having the camera anchored to the bag strap. Most of the time it works well to use the camera attached to the case strap. At the same time, I've found that it is easy to detatch the camera from the strap when I need to.

As it happened, my husband and I were going on a cruise soon after I bought the camera, and I would need to carry some sort of small handbag to dinner & elsewhere on ship. The central section of the Snapr 20 is a little bit long for my camera, but that meant that I could shove a fold up nylon shopping bag in behind the camera. I used the side pockets to hold my spare battery & SD card, as well as cabin key and any other necessities.

On an everyday basis, I carry my camera in a snug case in my handbag, but when we travel, I like to use a small backpack, and keep valuable items in some sort of small bag in front of me. On the cruise trip, when we went on shore trips, I put my passport, coin purse, and credit cards in a pocket of the camera bag. This meant that I had the important things right under my hands where I could protect them, with less important items (water bottle, umbrella, etc.) in my backpack. It worked wonderfully.

I also got the smaller size Snapr, thinking it would fit my camera better. My camera fits into the smaller case very snugly, and I have not found it as useful as the 20 snapr.

I learned about BlackRapid when I was reading reviews of the camera (which I bought from Amazon) because some people reviewing the camera recommended BlackRapid. I ordered my case from the BlackRapid site. (I think Amazon didn't carry the cases then.)They were very helpful about getting me the case in a rush, and were very responsive to my questions. All in all, I highly recommend the company and their products.

title: Lets put things into perspective
text:
This review is tailored towards those new to photography and enthusiasts who are budget conscious. The 5 star reviews only screams buy buy buy which I find to be misleading. Let me try to convince you otherwise.

Does it perform (compared to the A mount equivalent) like a 1k Zeiss glass should? Short answer is, very close. So if your looking for that Zeiss rendering at 35mm equivalent and have no regard for cost, this lens is your only choice without using adapters.

On the other hand, if your in the camp that is wondering just exactly how much difference in sharpness, color rendering, 3D pop (I call it more contrast), are these reviewers raving about. Well I got good news for you. It is not much. In terms of sharpness, very little compared to the 20mm Sigma ($100) at F4 and pretty much none compared to the 50mm ($300). The average enthusiast will be hard pressed to see the difference among these primes, even with their face stuck to the monitor. There is no night and day difference, especially if your not making huge prints.

Here is how I test my lenses. I take some similar shots and I ask some friends (some are into photography some not) to pick out the ones shot with the Zeiss. Result are, If you must have a 24mm prime lens I would suggest getting the sigma 20mm and 30mm (total of $200) to cover and get use to the 24mm distance first. Value wise, around $300 for a prime is the sweet spot. You get significant improvements from a kit zoom without breaking the bank.

Personally I was expecting a Zeiss 1.4 for that price but that is another story. Why is there so many 5 star Amazon reviews? Some are paid and some stand to benefit. Mostly, when someone pay 1k for any prime they really want to believe it is the best and blows all competition out of the water. And when they get you to believe the same thing, and lust over their lens, it is like added value to their purchase. Bottom line is if your just jumping into primes from the kit zoom, try the cheaper one's first.

title: Uncleanable Filter

I purchased this filter for my brand new Canon 70-200 L F4 IS lens due to the glowing reviews found here. Unfortunately, my experience with this UV Filter has been nothing short of abysmal. Before every shoot I thoroughly clean my lenses and filters and the first time I attempted to clean this filter I was appalled at the ghosting and smudging that was impossible to remove. Both methods of dry and wet cleaning were applied with microfiber cloths as well as lens pens and every effort made to restore clarity to this filter was for naught. Im unsure if this is normal build quality or not for Hoya since this is the first product from them I've purchased and it will likely remain a mystery since I will never buy from them again. It's a shame considering the good reputation this company seems to have in the filter industry. I'll stick with B&W and Marumi from now on.

TLDR; This filter is impossible to clean and ruined a good majority of my images for two back to back weddings I shot. STAY AWAY!

title: Perfect Travel Tripod!
text:
I was searching forever for the perfect travel tripod. My requirements were that A) it weighed less than 3lbs, B) folds down to less than 13in, C) has an interchangeable ball head, D) extends over 50" and E) costs less than $100 (don't want to spend more than that on an aluminum tripod). I was looking at the Benro Mefoto, the Sirui T005 and a Beike 555 (sold by CowboyStudio but mainly on eBay). I like the Benro and Sirui but they cost over $100 and only extends to 50". The Beike 555 was a good price but I was skeptical about the leg locks and overall quality. I was lucky enough to find this tripod on Costco.com (buy it there if you have membership cause it's only $70). Going to the Dolica website it has the tripod listed as a Costco exclusive. I've owned a Dolica tripod before and trust the brand as far as budget tripod goes. And with this tripod there was no compromise on any of my requirements and it's full blown with features.

The tripod feels very sturdy. Even the smallest extension section has good thickness. It doesn't feel like a cheap tripod and carries the Dolica Proline badge. I'm not sure how it will handle with a full size DSLR, but it handles my OMD with battery grip just fine. I also sometimes use it to hold a full size flash with umbrella. I have no problem with the twist locks and it doesn't slow down the set up much more than latches. I actually prefer them to having cheap plastic latches. If you don't overturn to unlock then locking is only a quarter-turn. It's easy to over turn since it doesn't really stop when unlocking. You just have to get used to it. The finish looks very nice and I love the silver accents. The ballhead has more features than the others that usually come on the travel tripods. There's a separate knob for panning with a degree marker as well as a bubble level. Although it gets covered once the plate is on. You can also swap it out if you prefer something else later. The quick release system holds strong without any play. My last cheapo travel tripod had a plastic latch which didn't hold on to the plate very well and eventually broke. This one even has a safety catch. There's also a spring loaded hook for adding weight for stability. Even the carrying bag is pretty solid quality. My only gripe right now is trying to find an additional quick release plate seems impossible. I've contacted Dolica and hopefully they'll respond.

If you're looking for a compact and light travel tripod that doesn't cut corners on quality (meanwhile not breaking the bank) look no farther.

title: Compared to nikkor 35G
text:
This lens is sharper and has that 3D look that the [[ASIN:B0037KM0X0 Nikon 24mm f/1.4G ED AF-S RF SWM Prime Wide-Angle Nikkor Lens for Nikon Digital SLR Cameras]] has.
This is my second copy of the Siggy. The first copy had significant focus issues, it was not amenable to AFFT on my D800.
This copy is tack sharp. I'm not going to test it on a focus chart because it seems perfect. 4 stars because my first copy was crap.

Okay, so compared the the nikon

Sigma better than [[ASIN:B0042X9LB0 Nikon 35mm f/1.4G AF-S FX SWM Nikkor Lens for Nikon Digital SLR Cameras]]
1. Sharpness
2. 3D effect, the subject seems to pop out from the background.
3. Price

Nikon better than sigma
1. Weather sealed.
2. focus seems smoother and more sure of itself
3. Bokeh is less jittery, especially with leaves and small flowers in the background.
4. colors seem better. The sigma to me seems too saturated, especially the reds. Also, the sigma vignettes more and underexposes, it needs +1/3 EV sometimes (no big deal, but if you are batch processing a bunch of photos that you shot with different lenses...)

Nikon and Sigma almost equal
1. They both have a quality feel to it. The nikon is a bit more bulbous and the sigma a bit more sleek. I know people complain about the polycarbon feel of Nikon, but seriously, which is more high tech, aerospace material or steel? Would you want a heavy steel bike or a light polycarbon bike? especially if function was equal? The more I think about it, it still feels like a Sigma..Those of you who have owned sigma lenses will probably know what I mean. The only think different about it is the finish. The finish is a rubberized material as opposed to that crinkly paint they used to have. It is heavy, but like I alluded to before "heavy/tank" does not mean high quality. Not that I would shake a lens...but I feel if i shook my sigma, I'd feel bits rattle around. If I shake the Nikon, it would feel solid and tight. Stupid and subjective, but it's my review. So Nikon has a slightly better build, but only time will tell how much better. Will the sigma die? A reputable store told me how they sold a bunch of siggy filthy fifties, only to have the customers complain months out that the focus motors died or misfocused.

Reason to keep nikon over sigma.
1. Future proof. I don't care if sigma has a USB that allows you to update your lens. I don't have to with my nikon. That USB should be free, if that was the case.
2. You know Nikon or canon will do something to their bodies to make it harder than just a firmware update to get your lens to be compatible with future bodies.
3. I don't care what people say, I think sigma still has QC issues. My first lens was way off. Also, it's not realistic for a company to "turn it around" without a huge capital infusion. Have not heard of sigma getting millions of dollars to invest in new manufacturing equipment or have not heard about any lean processes to make sigma waste less to spend more on quality.

If money is not a factor or having the best overall lens is your goal or looking long term value (with a mirrored camera), and quality, get the nikon.

If you want the sharpest lens or like the 3D look, and you are only thinking of your current setup, willing to play "Sigma Roulette" and you'll worry about the future compatibility later, get the sigma.

If you're on a tight budget, i'd shoot the [[ASIN:B001S2PPT0 Nikon 35mm f/1.8G AF-S DX Lens for Nikon Digital SLR Cameras]] in FX or 1.2 crop and post process.

If you want to try something different. Get the [[ASIN:B00ATM1MVA Fujifilm X100S 16 MP Digital Camera with 2.8-Inch LCD (Silver)]]. It's cheaper than the nikon and comes with an Xtrans sensor attached to the 35 f2.

Come on Nikon or Sigma, make a compact and cheaper 35 f2

UPDATE 5/20/13
THIS LENS IS FREAKING SHARP! But you knew that.
It's like the 24G, but 35. The rendering except the bokeh, is everything the Nikkor 35G should have been.

UPDATE 5/22/2013
So I've used this lens for a few days now. Again, sharp as hell. How sharp? okay so in my simple way of putting it...When you zoom in using the (+) button on your camera when you review an image, it's sharp down to the last tiny yellow square. The nikon would be about 1-2 frames behind that. I use the eyelash test, imagine sitting 3-4 feet across form someone and focusing on their eyelashes...

HOWEVER, A BIG NEGATIVE. Missed focus! I've had more than several shots misfocus. I absolutely am positive it is not from technique. These are relatively static subjects too. The first really obvious time was focusing on a distant object. The next several times were when using flash. Not sure why that is...I'm sure if more people complain about this on the net, Sigma will have a firmware update, but again...if sigma anticipated these issues, the USB docking station should have been included with the lens.

Update 1/27/2014
Selling this lens.
1. prefer 24 to 35. If i need 35, FOV, I just throw my Nikon Fx into Dx. 24g is lighter too.
2. 35 for me is a walkabout FL. I've been using my 35g Dx in Fx and fixing the corners in LR. Can't wait for the 35G fx.
3. Sharpness isn't everything.

title: A great alternative to the GoPro
text:
I've had this for several months now and put it through a LOT of heavy use. I have not written a review earlier because I wanted to give it time to settle in.

Two things stand out that make this a superior product:

1: Price! This has pretty much the same guts as the GoPro. It produces similar image quality. It's build quality is pretty good. It has a screen, it has its own lights and comes with a TON of accessories. You cannot beat this for the money. Period. For the money, the GoPro is overpriced.

2: Interchangeable lenses. That alone should be worth the price of admission. I regularly plop an infrared lens on this sucker with *NO MODIFICATIONS*. When I'm done, I drop a standard super wide angle on it. All of them work with the underwater case, so no surprises. I can easily go out and buy a handful of other lenses in a variety of angles...again, no modification. Period.

That should sell you.

Other facts.

Battery life: About 90 minutes. Buy a spare, they're cheap. It does run while charging, so I have a small battery pack I can use for longer runs.

Accessories: The plastic waterproof housing is awesome, no complaints! I use it all the time. The other accessories are good as well. This thing sits on a motorcycle some of the time and has had no issues.

Image quality: It's a small, small, small camera...it's good, but don't expect miracles. If I'm using it at night I have an IR spotlight and use the IR lens. Other factors will be effected by the quality of the lens you use.

Sound quality: ...well, that sucks. Again, it's a small, small camera. I didn't expect to use the microphone on this thing so no big loss (thus the 4 stars instead of 5, really).

Build: Metal body, with exception of the battery cover and the little rubber flap over the ports. The flap is a bit tight and gets in the way some times, but no big deal. The battery cover can be a pain at first (stiff), but that gets better and never seems to be "too loose".

View Screen: It's tiny and I wish you could leave it on longer. It's decent for the size, so again, I'm happy with it. You can buy alternatives to use through the mini-HDMI port if you want bigger, full-time viewing.

All-in-all, I highly recommend this camera!
