title: Seems good so far........*UPDATE*
text:
I just received the Case Crown keypad and I'm not sure that I can give it a complete and accurate review just yet. I believe I will need to update this review in a few weeks to see how I feel about it. Initiallly I can say that I like the silicone keypad more than I thought I would. I was afraid that I would not like typing on the keys, but it is suprisingly easy to type. I have noticed occasionally typing the same letter twice. I'm not sure yet if that is because of me or the keyboard but I will give it some time to get used to typing on it and then revisit that issue in my next review.
The Ipad 2 fits securely inside the case. I like the feel of the PU leather. I would have expected a little finer material for the price but I am not unhappy with the feel or the overalll look of the case.
I would like to mention one thing that the case description leaves out. The case sits inside of a frame which is velcroed to the outside keyboard folio. This inside frame can be removed via vellcro from the back and repositioned to portrait view. I actually prefer to type in landscape view; however I have read many reviews of people that appreciate when a case allows for this option, so I thought it woulld be worth mentioning. When I received the case it was not fullly charged but did have some charge on it. I plugged it in and it was fullly charged within a couple of hours. Siince I was not startiing from zero, I am not sure how long it would have taken if the battery had been draiined.
The one gripe I would have with this keyboard is that there is no shift key on the riight side. I have constantly been hitting the = key, meaning to hit the shift key. I Don't have allot of experience with these mini keyboards so I am not sure how much compromise is normal in fiittiing alll the keys into a smaller package such as for this case. The two keys that have given me grief is the missing shift key on the right side and the apostrope key that normaly sits on the right. It is still on the right but lower and I tend to hit the enter key. These are probablly just compromises that I need to get used to and am willing to get used to for the convenience of this case.
I am typing this review on the keypad and am continuing to have letters type out twice instead of once. Again, in all fairness too the case, I am not sure if this is due to operator error or if it is the fault of the keyboard. I will have to test it out a little longer too determine the cause and will probably have some friiends try it out and get their opinion on the repeat keys. I tried a llittle experiment, typing out the alphabet.........afcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz. I was a little more aware of my typing and not rusihng so much and didn't have one repeat, so it is possible that I need too slow down a bit and maybe these keys are just a llittle more sensitive and I need too adjust.

Again, I will update this review in a few weeks too follow up on the issues I mentioned. Oh, one more thing. The sleep/wake feature seems too work just fiine.. Another good thing about this case. If the price had been a llittle lower, I would highly recommend. It seems llike a lot to pay to have to make compromises, but, I'm going to see how things go for now.

UPDATE -- Well, I only lasted one more day with this keyboard. I just couldn't get over all the double typed letters and the missing shift key on the right side. I don't always want to use a keyboard like when watching movies or playing some games, but I thought havng the keyboard attached to the case would be convenient when trying to travel light. So, far, I have not found a keyboard I like better than my Amazon Basics Bluetooth keyboard. I pair it up with my IPad 2 which I currently have in a Case Crown Ridge Stand By Case, which I love. It is very sturdy and versitile. I guess I already had a good combination with what I had. I'm not willing to give up my right hand shift key and I don't like having to constantly back space to erase all the double letters. I decided to send the keypad folio back and for now, just stick with what I already have. I purchased my first CaseCrown Stand by Case through this same seller. Excellent customer service and no hassle returns. My only gripe was with the product but I would definately recommend doing business with this seller anytime.

title: Possibly Samsungs Finest High-end laptop.....
text:
I've just bought one of these machines, and although I haven't had the chance to fully test it (or run any games on it)...I just wanted to give you a first impressions of this incredible laptop..

First thing you'll notice when you fire up this laptop is the phenomenal screen, it really is quite remarkable, with a full HD 1920x1080 display, and with the brightness set almost blindingly bright (obviously this can be turned down), I have to say that the display, with the possible exception of the new `Retina-display' Mac laptops is the finest I've ever seen amongst P.C. laptops..and on a par with top-of-the range Mac laptops. In that even simple things like web-page text and images just jump out of the screen and are incredibly detailed and pin-sharp. The display is so bright and vibrant, that I normally like to have a break after 30-40mins of use...as my eyes tend to blur a little...

Something I want to briefly mention whilst talking about the display when surfing, is how quickly it loads internet pages, and videos....I'm still using the same 10meg virgin fibre optic line as on my old laptop, and pages and images just load so much quicker, that I had to do a speed check on my line to see if the line speed had been increased...

Another thing to note, is the speed of the laptops drives (2 x 750gig hard drives), with a 8gig SSD which seems to have windows pre-installed on it...which means windows 7 boots up in 22-24 seconds. So if you are regularly having to reboot the machine after having installed / Uninstalling programs (such as the quite frankly rubbish ` Norton's internet security' that comes pre-installed). It's not a chore restarting the machine, as it boots up so speedily...

To put the speed of the drives into real-world usage perspective...I had to re-import my 1.1 terabytes of music back into iTunes on my old Pentium4 3.2ghz laptop a good few months ago....and I had to leave it overnight and it took (very approximately) 8-9 hours to fully re-import the library.....well, the Samsung did it in about just under 2 ½ hours....and that was whilst I was downloading an album, watching HD movies on gametrailers.com and generally surfing the internet with absolutely no drop in performance, to say I was shocked is an understatement. (admittedly this was mainly because it was now using USB 3.0 instead of USB 2.0 but it gives you a very rough idea of the speed, and it's multitasking abilities)

It's also worth noting that the keyboard design is sublime....the keys have a real throw-back to the older style `Clicky' keyboards, where each of the keys feels weighted and clicks when you type, and you can really feel each press of the button, and the fact that the keyboard lights up (you can switch this off, or dim the brightness) you can work in the dark, or with minimal lighting (which I quite like to do). There has been some regular criticism of the track-pad on the keyboard...and I have to say that I can't stand track-pad's and I just plug a mouse into any laptop I use, so I can't comment on how good/bad it is

Sound is incredibly impressive for a laptop....most laptops sound leaves a lot to be desired, but this laptop has a excellent set of speakers (with a built in Sub-woofer) that produce surprisingly clear (and loud) sounds, straight-out-the-box. Don't get me wrong they're no substitute for a pair of really good laptop speakers, and I do intend to buy a pair...but the fact that I had keep turning the volume down as they were blaring out when I was watching videos...has made me think `Do I need a set of External speakers??'...

There is plenty of connectivity, with two USB 3.0 ports (which is what your likely to plug your external drives into) two USB 2.0 ports (for mice/speakers)...and the usual collection of HDMI, VGA out, etc....that you'd expect to have on laptop..

Did I really need a Laptop, with this much power in it?....not really....am I likely to be playing games regularly on it to make the most of the power?...very unlikely....and for what I use it for mainly (iTunes/organising my large amount of music/surfing the net/watching videos-trailer online) it's total overkill....but you know what...I absolutely love my laptop and I have absolutely no regrets buying it, and anything I throw at this laptop, it just laughs at me, as it just rips through any task thrown at it. And again I must re-iterate, that I haven't made use of the turbo-boosted `Gamer mode'...but everything I mentioned that I've done above, was done in the `Balanced' mode (`Normal' mode to me and you).

This isn't a laptop that is designed to be taken places (maybe if you have a car...) but it's really a desktop replacement...and in that regards it more than delivers (as I don't really have the space for a desktop)...so you should really always look at having this thing running from the Power AC/mains, as there is a performance/frame rate hit, when running games from the battery. So I'll end in saying that this is (up to now) probably Samsungs most powerful laptop. And it compares extremely favourably with high-end: Origin, Asus, Alienware laptop's (only the dual graphic card Alienware, can comfortably outperform it). But the screen on this thing, is just astonishing (probably nothing high-end Mac users haven't seen before), but for the rest of us....this is a gamer-ready high-end laptop, that runs rings around (*most of...*) similarly priced £1,000-£1,400 laptops.

P.s. Again, I have to mention, that I haven't had the chance to try any games on it yet..but the general consensus from the tons of reviews, I've read online about this laptop, is that it can play (pretty much) any current game with very high (to ultra, in some cases) resolution, with virtually all the effects turned on, with a still playable (30-60fps) depending on the game..

title: Pricey but well-made
text:
Had two great big cardboard boxes of vinyl in my storage room which were taking up WAY too much space. Plus, they were heavy--- youngsters today, with their fancy-pants lightweight CDs and high-falootin' e-lec-tronic MP3 files, are clueless (clueless I say!) <shakes cane for emphasis> as to how tough we grown-ups had it when WE were kids, blowing out our backs whenever we wanted to move our record collection across the room. So I recently decided there's no way I'm going to turn over my precious Herb Alpert collection to the Salvation Army just because the boxes were always getting in my way. No, I needed a storage solution. Enter the Crosely CR401-TA.

My first reaction---it only holds 30 records? Hell...that meant I had to buy four! The size seemed skimpy---until you remember the weight of stacked vinyl records. Actually 30 is reasonable. If you shoved 50 in there, you wouldn't enjoy lifting the thing. Remember, the case itself adds another 10 pounds. My second reaction---fiddy bucks? I've had root canals that cost less (they do them at the local veterinary dental school for free). But after I received my cases, I was duly impressed with the quality of the construction---heavy duty sides, with corner bumpers and a strongly-mounted carry-handle. And the attractive beige vinyl finish imparts the charm of Corinthian leather, without the haunting guilt of bovine slaughter. The cases look like they should last a lifetime. Still, I would say they are a tad overpriced for what you get. I price-shopped these aggressively on the interweb for a few months before buying, and came away empty handed. If you can find one for an even fifty, or a buck or two less, that's as good as it gets. Hoping the explanation is that they're made in America.

The odd "free hinge lid" design is an acquired taste---the lid completely detaches from the case when you flip it open. Perhaps removing the lid makes it easier to flip through the records without the weight of the open lid tipping the case over backwards? Still not sure I get it.

So, a nicely-made, good-looking, space-saving product which telegraphs "I'm a card-carrying hoarder who can afford the best." Minus one star for the weird lid thing, and the price.

title: I can now watch dvd's on-the-go on my android tablet!
text:
I bought this to watch dvd's on-the-go with my asus transformer infinity. It took a little bit of tinkering, to make it work. So, to save you valuable time, here's how to make it work on your android tablet.

(1) Install mxvideo player on your tablet.

(2) Plug your dvd writer SE-218 into your tablet via usb.

(3) Press the eject button to eject the tray.

(4) While the tray is open, press and hold the eject button until the green light on the tray stays lit. Then release. This brings your dvd drive into av mode.

(5) Close the tray.

(6) Now, eject and open the tray and put in a dvd.

(7) Your tablet will now recognize your dvd as a usb device. Your tablet will appear to be frozen for about 10 seconds. Don't panic! It's just reading the dvd disc. Just leave it alone until it's read it.

(8) Using a file manager, navigate into the usb device and find a vob file that is big, like a couple gigs or so. Play it with your mxplayer.

VOILA! You can now play dvd's on-the-go. Please spread the word. Amazon is only selling this puppy for 34 bucks. Well worth it!

Edited

I forgot to mention. Every time you plug in your drive to watch a dvd, you will have to eject the tray and press the button for 3 seconds.

title: Okay for what it is. It probably shouldn't be labeled "professional" in any capacity.
text:
I purchased this tripod to basically use as a throwaway for a recent trip as I knew I would not be able to return with it (the country I was flying out of has strict restrictions on certain items, tripods being among them). In that capacity it served me very well as it's an extremely tiny unit and the included bag made for very easy packing and storage. In the capacity of it being an effective tripod, I was a little let down but it served me well as long as I stayed within certain limitations. For the sake of reference, I use Gitzo tripods with Really Right Stuff heads for most of my photographic work and my normal travel tripod is a GT1542T with a BH-40 on top. If I compare this unit to my normal travel tripod then it's hard to view this as anything other than a sick joke, but such comparisons aren't really fair to anyone. Anyway, this unit was good in a lot of ways but it wasn't without issue.

The size is definitely the major selling point of this unit but it's obvious that stability has been compromised in several places in order to make it as small as possible. The 5 section legs are relatively flimsy and you'll do well to avoid extending the 2 section center column. I found that by keeping the smallest leg sections retracted and the center column all the way down I could get this unit to be somewhat objectively stable. This further improved by adding some weight to the hook. I then extended the smallest leg sections and adjusted the weight to find a decent compromise and it was reasonably stable as long as the wind didn't pick up too much. Every attempt I made at using the center column resulted in headache and me chastising myself for even trying. Seriously the center column on this unit is beyond terrible. I even couldn't get the center column all the way locked down without putting what seemed to be a rather extreme amount of pressure into tightening it.

The overall fit and finish was okay for what I paid for the unit, but wasn't objectively good. The first couple of times I set it up and collapsed it I ended up with grease stains on my hands. The leg locks felt like they required too much effort for such a small tripod, but this might be me being spoiled by the effortless locks on my other tripods. I found the metal leg sections themselves to be appropriate quality. The angle adjustments for the legs are of the push/pull type rather than being spring loaded which is struck me as unusual for a tripod of this caliber as just about every tripod with independently moving legs except for some ultra high end ones uses spring loaded angle adjustment. That said, the push/pull adjustments are an inconvenience with a tripod of this size. They're irritating enough on my big Gitzo, but on this unit they're a little ridiculous.

The head was the high point of the unit by a fair bit but it too was not without issue. As initially packaged the head was oily and required a thorough cleaning before I could use it. From there the detent pin in the clamp was both stubborn and got stuck inside the clamp easily. I ended up removing the pin altogether as it was monumentally frustrating. Outside of those two issues, I can't really fault the head at all. I used it with a full frame Nikon body and a 70-200mm and it held well with no issues. The clamp is standard Arca-Swiss style and worked fine with my RRS and Kirk plates. I didn't do anything with it that I thought might exceed it's limitations, but honestly the head did seem to be of a slightly higher caliber than the legs.

Overall I feel like this unit is just okay. It's certainly not great and it's certainly not terrible. I think the manufacturer labeling this as "professional" quality is extremely misleading as I would not trust this unit for any type of long term work or for anything rigorous at all. Given the price and the size, it's not bad.

title: Does what I need to do.
text:
I have bought another one of these because it works well for my purposes. But before you go with this product read below:

PROS:
1. QQDVR Camera server (HYQQDvr_EN7.1.6.3.exe on CD)(runs on PC that has cameras connected) has nice motion detection recording or full time recording settings and scheduling. Nice video file organization (very obvious when a video clip was recorded and by what camera). Couple that with a FTP server and you'll have nice instant access to recorded video clips externally over the internet.
2. Camera client (Client_Setup6.3.exe on CD)(runs on all other PCs and speaks to server to get real time camera picture) easy to use and setup. Allows you to see whats going on at home real time, when you are away. Just open up ports 9881 and 9880 on your home firewall and point the client to your home IP address.

CONS:
1. Product and software is made by some small chinese company ([...] and if you go to their website for software updates or additional info, good luck ... you are going to need it.
2. Server software user interface a little amaturish. Takes time to figure out how the window works.
3. Video clips are recorded in a proprietary codec (QDMF/QDM/QQDVR) that no one has heard of and will only play back on PC that has server (HYQQDvr_EN7.1.6.3.exe) installed. On other PCs, that have only client (Client_Setup6.3.exe) ... video clips will not play back ... Even if you install a really good codec pack or have VLC player. So here is what you do ... after you install the server software on the server PC, copy (C:\QQDVR\plugins) onto a flash drive and then take that flash drive and plug it into the other PC and run the "regqdm.bat" off the flash drive. That will install the codec you need. And then the clips will only play in Windows Media Player. This one took me days to figure out because there is no info in the internet about this codec at all.
4. I seriously doubt (but am not 100% sure), there exists a smartphone app to interface with the QQDVR server. So you may be limited to a PC when wanting to view the real time camera video.
5. Other better aftermarket camera software will not work with this hardware unit, since this unit is not considered a CCTV DVR video card. so if it matters to you and you want to use other CCTV software, you will want to buy a "cctv dvr pci card" ... google it. But for me, $40 for this unit ... I'm pretty happy with it.

title: Not Ready For Prime Time Player...But Getting There Rapidly! (UPDATE)
text:
This device fascinates and baffles me at the same time. It is basically a streaming device that combines the new Sony entertainment network with google TV and I have yet to figure either one out. It works with a couple of updates (automatic) right out of the box. It is small and sleek and well built. Seems sturdy and the remote is a small wonder. However it is advertised as being backlit and mine is not or at least I have not figured out how to trigger the 'lit' part yet! It includes a touchpad on one side with basic remote controls and a complete keyboard on the other side for browsing via the Google Chrome browser (default). As far as surfing the net from the TV that is something that I have never done before but this makes it very easy to do. If you text you'll appreciate the keyboard size and location of keys. I still won't be surfing much because I just don't do it. The real plus for me is that it streams my Netflix and Amazon Prime videos much better than my WD box or the Roku...The picture seems better and the sound certainly is(the Amazon takes some digging to find the right app which is already installed - to save you time it's under the Sony Entertainment Icon) To give some idea of Netflix dominance in the streaming marketplace it has it's own Icon under the Home screen. Navigation of all this takes some trial and error and is anything from cumbersome to very quick depending on what you're doing. The remote is light years ahead of other streaming devices but the streaming device itself is slowed down by the very fact of it's ability to do too many things. If you just want to stream movies stick with Roku. If you want additional access to surfing and entertainment options for the future then this is the baby for you.

It comes with three free movies from Sony Entertainment by the way which I didn't see mentioned in the literature (but it may be there) and you can redeem the included coupon until the end of July 15th 2014 (limited selection but good movies) and they get added to a youtube account you either already have or have to open. But they stream from youtube right to your tv with full surround sound and great picture. It can install and use tons of apps from The GoogleStore (both free and paid).

Someone more technilogically savvy than I would have a field day with this little toy I assure you. So it depends on what you want. If you want pure and uncomplicated with simple control then stick with Roku. If you want your horizons expanded by a wide margin and have other viewing choices by the ton then this is the way to go. For double the price you get more than double the content and a net surfer that puts the others to shame. Requires a net connection (wireless or wired - wired is always best) has HDMI in and out and Optical audio out along with RCA's. It has usb support (two slots) and will play content stored that way on external drives. It's pretty nifty for the new generation and can be as simple as you'd like for the geezers like me. I'm keeping it because the picture and sound seem better on Netflix and Amazon Prime Video and the streaming controls seem more responsive and intuitive. So if you can figure out what you need to know from this rambling review then I hope you'll get one for yourself and step up to the world of tomorrow.

Update 08-30-2012

The light on the remote is operated with the function key. You press function and then a key in the same color labeled light and behold! there is backlit! See...you just have to learn all the abilities of this remote. As usual the included paperwork is lacking and you have to go online to learn anything tho this I just happened to notice on my own...I may be slow but I'm sure. :-)

title: Great UPS
text:
I am a software entrepreneur and work out of my home. This is the UPS I use to protect my workstation. At any given time my workstation is running a minimum of four guest virtual machines, along with the host. All of my primary work is stored on these machines(of course it gets offloaded to the cloud and my NAS nightly) and it's really my lifeblood. In the rural area I'm located in, power outages are commonplace.

This UPS has seen it's share of fun over the last year and half. It has yet to do something wrong. Here's the kind of punishment it's had to endure:

1) At least 30 outages since I purchased in 2012.
2) In every outage it successfully switched to battery backup without hiccup.
3) I average about 1 hour of runtime on battery.
4) The governor was off on one of my Generators that powers part of the house when we loose power. The UPS accurately refused to switch to utility(generator) power, when the generator was producing power too far out of safe frequency(in North America should be 60Hz). Frequency problems can often times be worse for equipment then voltage issues.
5) Extended outages whilst I was away. The UPS correctly forced my machine to go to sleep before it ran out of battery power.
6) Always alerts me if I'm away and there is an outage using the built in SMTP client.

I've definitely gotten my use out of it. Prior to my entrepreneurial ventures I served in a Director level capacity for a number of technology companies. I was always accustomed to buying APC and was a bit apprehensive about buying CyberPower instead. However, I'm glad I did. The price point is better, and as far as my experience, they are just as reliable, if not more so.

The only glitch I ran into, is once after a power failure, the UPS reported a battery issue. After it charged for a few minutes, I reset the UPS and it went away.

I would definitely buy CyperPower products again.

title: Bought two 48", Samsung and Vizio.
text:
I bought at the same time the VIZIO E480i-B2 48-Inch 1080p Smart LED HDTV and the Samsung UN48H6350 48-Inch 1080p 120Hz Smart,

VIZIO was almost 200 bucks cheaper. The main use for this one is to connect to an Xbox, and have the kids see movies in Netflix. the Samsung, for my room, mainly to see series in Netflix and now, the world cup!

My Wife was complaining at the beginning on why spending more money for the same thing, but actually, She also is backing up me now on the fact that there are some differences worth the price but depends on your needs.

Both products work well, but there are some differences:

1) Picture Quality: slightly better in the Samsung. Cannot define exactly if it's the color, definition or contrast. not giant difference but you can note it having both, probably not if you have only one of these
2) Smart TV: Interface is simpler and easier in Vizio, but much more complete in Samsung. Vizio is lacking a internet browser, and the Samsung has one that even supports HTML5, so most of the web sites can be viewed correctly. I use it to access sites to see TV channels online from other countries, I cannot do it with VIZIO. Apps like Netflix and Amazon are way much better in the Samsung, and there are others like games. Vizio is just ok.
3) Overall Quality: all seems to be better in the Samsung. When I was assembling the base the Samsung felt solid but itself, and solid over the base when assembled. Vizio felt more fragile but of course if you are not moving or touching it there is not a big difference.
4) remote control is much better on the Samsung. VIZIO one is smaller and simpler. Samsung is bigger but it has the capability to support the set top box from your cable provider (in my case UVERSE) so with one control I can do everything from seeing cable to manage smart apps
5) screen mirroring: This feature from Samsung, not found in VIZIO, is for sharing your tablet/smartphone screen with the TV. You can see pictures and videos from the phone on the TV screen. I was able to see a soccer game in HD, being transmitted from the phone browser to the TV screen. I could not believe the quality of the transmission. I used a Samsung S 4, not sure if other phone brands have this capability

Summary, very happy with both purchases by their prices. but based on your needs, you may want to pay a few more bucks!

title: Helps Bring my 5 Year Old Desktop to Current Performance
text:
It works nicely and is a good replacement for a 5 year old desktop after a Windows 8.1 upgrade.

Truthfully, I didn't need to upgrade the old card (an ATI Radeon HD4800). Current drivers exist, but ATI no longer supplies a version of the Catalyst software that can be used with my Win 8.1 build. Since I'm planning on a new monitor for photographic editing, being able to make calibration adjustments with software designed for with my GPU made sense, and hence the upgrade.

Five years' technological advancement brought me a modest performance improvement, with less heat output (no fan required for this GPU - just the heatsink in the photo). I can't speak to absolute performance as I'm not a gamer, but if you are, you're likely looking elsewhere anyway.

Note that the depth of the heatsink could eat up an extra PCI slot, depending on how your board is laid out. The old ATI card was very "flat" in this regard - even with the fan assembly. In my HP Pavilion Elite (HP-180t), I had to sacrifice a TV tuner card to have an empty slot to accommodate the heat sink depth. I've never used that card so it was no loss. I can't speak to your motherboard's design in this regard. You might be able to swap "short" cards into this position - cards which don't extend as far as the heat sinks.

All in all, I brought this 5 year old core-i7 based desktop to current performance for the price of Win 8.1, this graphic card, and a USB 3.0 card.

title: It's a pole... no it's a mast.... no it's a SUPERMAST!!!
text:
I needed a standard TV antenna mast to pair with my Channel Master 2018 antenna. The word standard is important as many universal antenna mounts are not the standard diameter for TV antennas, which is 1.25". Antennas generally come with U-bolts/clamps which attach to masts up to 1.5". Many universal mounts are at 1.66" or wider and wouldn't fit those bolts.

While I only needed a standard mast, this mast has many additional features which I thought might be useful in the future. The mast is tapered on one end so that it will fit inside the end of another mast. The diameter of the mast is 1-1/4" and tapers to just under 1-1/8" for the last 4-1/2" of the mast's length. The untapered end has a crimp about 4" from the end and a 5/16" hole to accommodate a set screw . The tapered end has a 1/4" gap that allows the crimp of another mast slide inside the gap. This prevents the masts from twisting.

In lamens terms you buy two or more of these to make a 10' mast or taller. With the crimp and set screw you could be assured that you wouldn't have any problems with the masts slipping or twisting.

For reference: I used the GC 8799 clamp along with a Directv J-mount, this mast, and a Channel Master 2018 antenna. The setup was quick, easy, and is working wonderfully.

title: Still not as good as a Harmony One
text:
I received a Harmony Ultimate from Logitech because I own several Logitech Harmony One Advanced Universal Remote remotes and have recommended them highly. I was looking forward to the Harmony Ultimate, since I had given an unfavorable review to the Harmony Touch, and I was hoping that the Harmony Ultimate would correct the design deficiencies of the Harmony Touch. It does correct some problems, but it also introduces new ones. Here are some good things and bad things:

Good things:

1) The removal of the number buttons to make the Harmony Ultimate a more convenient size was a good move. The on-screen numbers are easy to find, when they are needed.

2) Overall, the size of the Harmony Ultimate is convenient and comfortable.

3) Most of my settings were successfully imported from one of my Harmony One settings, so that saved me some time during set-up.

4) Having a dedicated button for the DVR and for the four colored buttons is a great addition.

5) The remote comes with a "hub" and a pair of "IR blasters", which one could place in a cabinet to control concealed electronics. That's nice, I suppose.

Unfortunately, there are quite a few things that make the Harmony Ultimate a bad fit for my living room experience.

1) The location of the play-stop-forward-reverse buttons to above the screen makes using the Harmony Ultimate more awkward than using the Harmony One, even though the Harmony One is significantly larger. Using the play-stop-forward-reverse buttons on the Logitech Harmony One Advanced Universal Remote can be done one-handed. On the Harmony Ultimate it requires awkwardly shifting the position of the hand, or using two hands. This is a significant step backward in usability. However, what's worse is....

2) Putting the touch-sensitive screen between the play-stop-forward-reverse buttons and the up-down-left-right buttons is a terrible design. I was constantly hitting the screen when trying to use the play-stop-forward-reverse buttons, causing all sorts of mayhem. This rendered the remote useless.

3) The addition of "favorite channels" is a needless complication. Every DVR has favorite channel lists built in.

4) The Harmony Ultimate itself does not control a Roku box. The remote *only* sends commands to the Roku box through the "IR blaster" widgets. For me, this would require putting the Harmony Ultimate "hub" in my already crowded entertainment cabinet and re-arranging it so that the Roku box can face one of the "IR blasters". Why not just have the remote itself send the commands? That's what the Harmony One does,and it works perfectly. Even the Harmony Touch was able to get this right. This is a bad design.

5) The Harmony Ultimate does not have physical buttons for "skip forward" and "skip backward". To activate those frequently-used commands, you have to hold down the "fast forward" and "rewind" buttons. This is a bad design.

6) There is no obvious way to access the commands for Devices, in order to send a command directly to one of your components. On the Harmony One, the "Devices" button is always easily accessible at the bottom of the screen. On the Harmony Ultimate, the Devices button is hidden in an on-screen sub-menu.

7) After the activities are set up, they are listed on the screen, much like they are on the Harmony One (a great improvement over the Harmony Touch). However, the on-screen button for the bottom-most activity is located *behind* the on-screen "Menu" button for the remote itself (this menu is where the "Devices" menu is hidden). This makes accessing that fourth activity ... difficult.

Conclusion: in a world where the Logitech Harmony One Advanced Universal Remote had never been invented, the Harmony Ultimate would be a nice addition to any living room. However, the Harmony One does exist, and has existed for years. That being the case, there is really no excuse for the flaws in the design of the Harmony Ultimate.

Suggestions for the Harmony Two, or the Harmony Ultimate Plus, or whatever the next version will be called:

1) Put all of the physical buttons, including the play-stop-forward-reverse buttons, below the screen, where the user can reach them with one hand.

2) Have physical buttons for "skip forward" and "skip backward", located beneath the "fast forward" and "rewind" buttons, as the Harmony One currently does.

3) Do not put any physical buttons above the touch-sensitive screen.

4) Eliminate the "Favorites" screen and replace it with a list of the user's "Devices".

Update 2014-02-23: After another reviewer recommended the Logitech Smart Control, I bought one of those to replace a dying Harmony One, and I have been very happy with it.

title: Great Value & Great Picture. Beware For PC Use!
text:
**UPDATE** 03-20-15
The below observations are still true, however, if you intend to use this in conjunction with a PC - I suggest finding a different television. I have been able to get it to work in the past, but it is shoddy - and changes based on GPU driver versions. NVIDIA being the only GPU manufacturers with HDMI 2.0 support, there really is only that option - a GTX 970 or 980. The problem is that these cards are designed for top notch picture which means chroma 4:4:4 colors. The Vizio is 4:2:0 to reach its low price point. I think the colors are okay from a consumers perspective, but NVIDIA currently doesn't allow you to output customized signals through the HDMI 2.0 port - its trying to feed a 4:4:4 signal to a 4:2:0 port, and it does not work well. If you want to use a 4k TV with your PC, make sure it supports 4:4:4 colors. More information available here:

https://forums.geforce.com/default/topic/783120/geforce-900-series/vizio-p-series-60hz-2160p-4-2-0-chroma-/1/
______________________________________________________________________

When its running 4k, you can totally tell. Streaming Netflix is stunning. (On that note Netflix has added some of Sony's "Mastered in 4k" movies, not just Breaking Bad and House of Cards).

The bezel is tiny, and I love it. It has a good array of inputs and I had no issues setting its audio out jacks into my powered loud speakers as a pass through from my AMD TrueAudio signal coming over HDMI.

I just got it yesterday so no deep picture quality reviews.

I have one con though -- this is HDMI 2.0 - and 2.0 ONLY! What I mean by that is that while it passes A/V over HDMI 1.4, it does so only at 1080p -- no 4k (HDMI 1.4 is capable of 4k at 24-30 Hz). Rather than giving an option for lower refresh rate, it simply can't do 4k at all. It has one HDMI 2.0 port, and four HDMI 1.4 ports (these they label "4k at 30 hz") - Unless using an HDMI 2.0 source none of these give 4k video (at any Hz) -- why label ports 4k @ 30 hz if they are 1080p only, period?

This is a problem because HDMI 2.0 outputs are a rare thing these days... only the BRAND new GTX 900 series cards support it. My R9 295x2 GPU has no HDMI outputs -- just mini displayport (and of course no TV can have a displayport input). Those can be used with adapters to become HDMI outputs. Sadly, they don't convert mDP 1.2 signal to HDMI signal, the port detects that its connected to an HDMI input and actually sends an HDMI signal from the get go. It only supports HDMI 1.4a out (for now, praying for a firmware update). Because of this, I cannot use it as a PC display for gaming at 4k.

Streaming 4k is beautiful, up-scaling my 1080i Directv is decent. I haven't tried any Bluray movies yet.

For the record this has an ethernet jack and wifi - it has an AC wireless card for 5 ghz wifi.

In summary the picture quality is great, and 4k is great using its Smart TV features, but there is no 4k support for prior HDMI standards like other 4k displays. Your A/V source will need an HDMI 2.0 output for any 4k from that source.

**UPDATE** 9/30/14
I have had this television for ten days now. While the original negative portion of my review is unchanged, I am still enjoying the television for its independent functionality.

The first hours of upscaling my Directv looked a lot grainier than its looked since then -- maybe the channel I was watching had bad encoding or something, I don't know. Watching satellite shows from HBO, Comedy Central, and CBS HD upscale really well for the most part (source is 1080i). Watching shows and movies from the Netflix and Prime apps is seamless and easy, and the picture quality is quite good.

The Youtube app doesn't work the best - if the video isn't in the television's native resolution it will chop off the edges during scaling. There may be a way to manually set the resolution, but I only tried for a few minutes. Also using my smartphone or laptop to find videos and then watch those on the smart tv did not work well -- it was essentially streaming from those devices rather than providing the location of the video and then using the app itself to locate and play it -- meaning really grainy low-res playback.

The local dimming is nice, but you can see it sometimes - if you have a total black scene and then a title pops up at the start of a movie for example, you can see the area around the word that is controlled by the same backlight bulb go grey instead of black. Not sure how / if that could have been designed better though. Its only detectable on an all black screen with a small non-black area, and I generally don't notice it once things are really playing.

I love the keyboard on the back of the remote, and its easy to switch which inputs are being displayed on the television. Using my computer works well other than issues discussed above (please re-read all of that with the understanding that the term "output" means where the video is coming from, not the "input" on the television -- the 4k @ 30 hz ports can support 4k I am sure, just not if the SOURCE port is not 2.0). I have a pair of GTX 980's in the mail and I will update this next week once I get a true HDMI 2.0 output port and get a chance to game at 4k.

Quality of the product and packaging was really high, and I have zero complaints. I would purchase this product again in a heartbeat.

UPDATE 10/11/14

After using it with my new GTX 980, the 4k functionality works smoothly when using a true HDMI 2.0 output. Scaling issues make using a computer on this display quite hard, but when in a full-screen program things look pretty good. Not noticeably better than my 27" 1440p gaming monitor, but at 55" its not noticeably worse either, and thats a big deal.

I have experienced a few slight issues with it - once using the Netflix app there was random blanking out of the right half of the screen into pure static - almost like its running in an MST type configuration. It was only in Netflix, and only on that day. Perhaps it was a problem with the content. Also in Netflix, some programs will randomly stop as if the App crashed and the television is back on its default input. Slight problems that don't make much of a difference.

Watching the later seasons of Breaking Bad in 4k is really amazing, and things will only get better as time goes on. This is really an exceptional value, and if you're in the market for a good bang for your buck television I recommend this one.

title: Love it
text:
This a very well designed, incredibly light keyboard. The keys are a comfortable size for my hands (I'm 6'3"), and have a pleasant amount of vertical travel. I use it with my Nexus 7, and in my opinion, this is a MUCH better option than getting a keyboard case for it - the keyboard in the keyboard case is way too small, whereas this is almost a full-size keyboard that weighs about the same. It takes two AAA batteries, so even there weight has been reduced compared to the larger AA batteries. The batteries last a long time, if you remember to switch it off during extended periods of disuse.

Amazon sells two versions of this keyboard - one for iPad (this one), and another for Android. They have slightly different key layouts and have somewhat different dimensions. This one has function keys (F1-F12) which I need for work - the Android keyboard does not. It also has arrow keys, which are great for editing - as does the Android version. Both versions of the keyboard will work with either device, but the "special functions" (e.g., volume control) will not work if you are using it with the device it was not intended for.

Why only four stars? Two reasons. The main one is that it does not come with any kind of a case or bag - it ships in a clear plastic bag only. When I was pulling it out of my bag the other day, one of the keys must have snagged and broke off. Amazon being the incredible company it is, shipped a warranty replacement with one-day shipping (wow). But really, it should come with some sort of protection - even a simple nylon bag would have done the trick. This is the major "con" for me.

The other con is that, when you start typing after a hiatus, the first letter you type will usually repeat multiple times. This, I think, is not a problem with the keyboard, but rather with Android, as I have seen other reviewers complain about this issue with various other keyboards. It must have something to do with what Android does when the keyboard "wakes up" and reestablishes its connection. This is not a big deal - a few strokes of the backspace take care of it, but the added convenience of this keyboard over even the nicest on-screen keyboard (I use Swype) is unbelievable.

title: Incredible photos, but numerous quality issues too
text:
I have been using the Olympus OM-D E-M5 as my primary camera for about 7 months now, with the exception of the two months it was with Olympus for warranty service. I love the images that this camera produces, the size, the in body image stabilization (IBIS), and the excellent Olympus prime lenses. However, I have also experienced a number of serious quality issues in the short time that I have had this camera, and I am considering other options now.

Within two weeks of receiving the camera, the paint below the Olympus logo and around the lens mount on the front of the camera started to flake off. I had not dropped or dinged the camera, so I believe that this was just a bad paint job. The flakes that were coming off looked like tiny black pepper flakes, which is the last thing that I want to see around the lens mount of an interchangeable lens camera. I also noticed that the bottom of the frame that surrounds the rear screen had a hairline crack near the center screw. After a little research, I learned that this defect was common in a certain batch of OM-Ds and mine was one of them. Apparently the cause was an over-tightened screw.

I sent the camera to the Olympus America repair facility in Hauppage, NY as directed by the Olympus America website where I filed an online repair ticket. What I did not know is that Olympus was in the process of moving their repair facility to Texas. It took Olympus almost two full months to repair the camera and return it to me, and for the first month and a half I could not even confirm that they had received my camera despite numerous emails and calls to customer service. I finally learned that my camera had been forwarded to the Texas facility where it was assigned a new repair ticket number, and I was finally able to track the repair online. However, I signed up for email notifications and never received a single one.

Since receiving the camera back from the repair center, I have had no further issues with the paint flaking off. However, one of the plastic textured grips popped off the front of the camera, and I discovered that it was only held on with double sided tape. The person who installed the tape had put a large crease in it, which meant there was less surface area to hold the piece in place. The repair center also lost the accessory port cover that prevents water intrusion when the accessory port is not in use. Finally, less than a week after I got the camera back, the hairline crack was clearly visible again near the center screw on the bottom the rear screen frame. After learning that the crack does not affect the integrity of the weather sealing, I opted to not send the camera back again after my first negative repair experience.

Yesterday, I was shooting some photos before work and noticed that each time I engaged the IBIS, I would see either green or magenta horizontal lines within the EVF. I have the IBIS set to engage with a half press of the shutter button so that I can stabilize longer lenses in the EVF for more accurate framing. I was also disappointed to see that the same green and magenta lines appeared in several of the photos that I took, completely ruining the photos. At this point, it looks like I have no choice but to send the camera back in for another repair.

When this camera is working, it is one of the best cameras that I have ever used and the image quality is exceptional. I love the small size, light weight, and tilting screen too. However, I have completely lost confidence in this camera, and have returned to shooting with my DSLR for the time being.

I cannot recommend this camera based on my experience with it, and with the Olympus America repair center.

title: A fantastic do-it-all flash trigger and shutter remote!
text:
I purchased two of the Cactus V5 sets to use as a remote flash trigger and remote shutter trigger, and after eight months I can say the V5's are absolutely fantastic. I have triggered many thousands of photographs and strobe firings and the Cactus V5's have worked flawlessly each and every time.

One of the greatest features is each unit is both transmitter or a receiver, selected by the power slide switch on the side, slide it one way it transmits, slide it the other way it receives. If you only buy a pair you won't see this as an advantage; but for those of us that use more than two its a huge feature providing tremendous flexibility. For example, I have four V5's and have used them in the following configurations:

1 V5 set to transmit on camera hot shoe triggering between 1-3 V5 equipped strobes set to receive. I can set each flash to a different channel and by changing channel on the transmitter select any individual strobe OR by changing to a group channel I can fire them all.

Yesterday I was firing a complicated setup:
#1 V5 in my hand to transmit, #2 V5 set to receive and plugged in to the camera remote shutter port; #3 V5 on my camera hotshoe mount is set to transmit and has a bounce flash "daisy chained" on top and finally #4 V5 is set to receive at my umbrella reflector. When I press the button on #1 half way, #2 focuses the camera. When I push #1 button in all the way #2 trips the camera shutter, the camera hotshoe tells #3 to fire the bounce flash and the flash connected to #4.

I hope that made sense. With any other brand, to do what I did in my second scenario I would have needed to buy a second transmitter, but with my Cactus V5's I just flipped a switch.

I'm going to buy two more to increase the number of flash units I can fire wirelessly, and I'm considering buying more after that just to keep on hand as spares, I expect to be using my V5's for many, many years.

title: Excellent camera
text:
I had Canon S45 and SD1000 few years ago and its low light pictures were horrible (other than than, a good camera). After Canon I tried a newest Olympus, a cheap VG 110, and it was huge letdown. I also had Casio Exilim, Sony W55 for family members. But I was always wishing for more low light capability as these cameras' evening and indoor pictures in low light were not good as I wished.

So I studied Panasonic LX5, Canon S95 and S100 and after a lot of reading and comparing the cameras in store, I selected Nikon P310 because of its low-light settings - a combination of a 16.1-megapixel BSI CMOS sensor, wide ISO range up to 3200 (Hi1 6400 equivalent) and a fast, wide-angle maximum aperture f/1.8 lens plus an advanced optical VR image stabilization. It has several scene modes including Advanced Night Portrait mode, Night Landscape mode and Backlight/High Dynamic Range (HDR) mode. Mechanical precision advanced VR is very important for me because I shoot without tripod.

The camera has manual exposure control (P/S/A/M) same as my DSLR, Nikon D60, and a new Zoom Memory function that enables the selection of popular prime focal lengths during shooting. P310 also includes huge number of effects and filter effects that can be added to photos in-camera for a quick artistic touch. It also has unique, very bright 3-inch high resolution (921,000-dot) LCD screen.

As for video, there is the ability to capture Full HD (1080p) video at 30 frames-per-second (fps) with AF, stereo sound and the use of the optical zoom while recording and in-camera editing, but I don't intend to use it for video, maybe only occasional one.

When I bought p310, I first tried in almost absolutely dark room and picture was clearer than I could see myself! Thats when I thought I made a right choice. I am continuing to experiment with p310 and now I am going to use exclusively its user mode. Have no complaints about other modes as well, auto has been very good too.

While its sensor is smaller, it utilizes backlight and doesn't require as much light as conventional ones. DxOMark.com have published test results that 1/2.3" BSI-CMOS sensor such as in Nikon P310 beats the larger 10mp, 1/1.7" CCD sensors in Olympus ZX-1 and it matches the S95/G12 sensor. Whatever the story is, the combination of backlit CMOS and fast 1.8 lens seems to to produce excellent low light pictures to me. It is so good in low light that I never had to use flash indoors and in the evening: I just forgot that flash exists and pictures are excellent.

The camera has Fn button (as different from p300) and I customized it for Continuous shooting mode, but it can be assigned WB, ISO and functions too. In terms of cost, the camera is significantly cheaper than S95/100 or LX5.

It has 99 focus points, Contrast Detect (sensor), Multi-area, Center, Tracking, Face Detection (face priority) modes. It has also a better macro, can shoot as close as 2 cm or 0.7 inch. The camera has HDMI and USB ports and charges through USB cable. When I download pictures, I just leave the camera plugged in PC and it charges automatically, so its always on full battery.

The camera has very fast AF, excellent low light capacity, mechanical precision VR image stabilization, bright and fast f1.8 lens, custom designed Expeed C2 latest processor from Nikon and its image quality is great. its very small, truly pocketable and light. I couldn't be happier with the camera

title: Extremely Disappointing
text:
Just over a year ago I finally broke down and bought a Kindle Keyboard. I am a staunch book person, but also an avid traveler, and after many friends recommended a Kindle, I was convinced that it was a worthy product to in which to invest. I also purchased one of the Kindle-specific protective cases.

I only traveled once in the year that I purchased the Kindle, and never once dropped it or abused it in any way. The Kindle remained in my house, mostly untouched expect for a two month period when I was recovering from surgery and used it daily. Shortly after the warranty ran out, I went to go download a book onto the device only to discover that there were white striations across the top 50% of the screen (and some running down it vertically as well). These lines completely obscured my view of at least half of a Kindle page, rendering it impossible to read. I also found a forum post (http://www.amazon.com/forum/kindle?_encoding=UTF8&cdForum=Fx1D7SY3BVSESG&cdThread=Tx1KLL7BRK6MCSB by a customer with the same problem whose warranty had run out but had received a free Kindle replacement since it was clearly a product defect. I spoke to customer service, and although they handled my frustration well, they refused to send me a free replacement even after hearing about the forum post. They claimed that Kindles have lasted 5+ years, and so it couldn't possibly be a case of planned obsolescence. Sure, is that the case with a normal Kindle, or is that an outlier?

I am extremely disappointed in this product and the way Amazon handled the situation, since it clearly is a common issue with Kindles as demonstrated through their established trouble shooting and Kindle problem pages. I have been officially reconverted to books, and might even boycott purchasing any volumes from Amazon.com again (and believe me, this is where I used to get them all). If you are looking into buying a device that will last more than 14 months, I'd recommend going with a company who stands behind their products, and not just for 12 months.

title: If it ain't broke...
text:
Before I left the store with my newly purchased first generation iPad, I had a Zagg screen protector installed. About a week later, my OtterBox Defender case arrived from Amazon. My shiny new device was now protected from wear and tear, and I had something I could get a grip on. I felt safe handing my iPad to my friends or laying it on a messy coffee table.

When I recently upgraded to the 3rd generation iPad, I once again had a Zagg screen protector installed before I left the store. As soon as I found one available on Amazon, I ordered the OtterBox Defender case.

Sadness. OtterBox has made changes that I'm sure they thought were good, but have forced me to return mine:

- I don't remember having so much trouble figuring out how to install my first OtterBox. I had to search on YouTube for installation videos for this one. (The videos on the OtterBox website showed only the older cases, which install differently.)

- The rubber gasket seems to be much stiffer. I was genuinely concerned that I was going to tear it while taking it apart for installation. After installation, it took too much effort to push the home button - very stiff.

- The killer for me was the inclusion of a built-in screen protector. When you swipe the screen, this built-in protector would stick to the Zagg and cause foggy streaks. (The Zagg was plenty dry. It was installed over two weeks ago.)

- The corners of the OtterBox's cover are clunky. I see how they are supposed to be more protective than the design of the old model, but they are too obtrusive.

- Finally, the new model just doesn't have the "grip" that the older one had. It felt like it would slip from my hands, not much better than the naked metal of the iPad itself.

I'll be looking for a different case. I have to say that the combination of the Zagg and older model OtterBox Defender have left me with a virtually mint-condition first generation iPad. I'm sure this will be a big factor in what I get when I sell it. I intend to protect my new iPad in much the same way but sadly, it won't be with the new OtterBox Defender.

title: It worked for me, but needed a powered HDMI splitter
text:
I have used the [[ASIN:B0002EXJ8Y RF-Link AVS-5811 5.8GHz Audio and Video Transmission System with IR Repeater]]for almost 3 years, but wanted to add HD capabilities to a TV in our home gym. I read all of the reviews for the Actiontec product prior to purchasing and thought I would give it a shot. My setup is a Verizon FIOS QIP-7100P1 (software version 1.9) HD set top box, with the TV's about 20ft apart, going through 2 interior walls (sheet rock, wood studs). The initial setup was really simple and had everything up and running in 10 minutes. Everything worked great for about 10 minutes and both displays just went blank. While researching this product, I was aware of the issue that some set top boxes limit the HD output to only 1 connection. To get around this issue I read from another review that you can use [[ASIN:B0015YRMXI SANOXY HDMI Splitter Amplifier 1 In to 2 Out Dual Display]]to get around this issue. Using the powered HDMI splitter did the trick for me. I plugged the HDMI cable from the cable box into the splitter, one HDMI cable going to out to the TV, the other going out to the Actiontec transmitter. Everything is working flawlessly now.

Pros:
-Actiontec includes everything you need in the package (2 HDMI cables, transmitter, receiver, IR extenders with tape, remote with battery)
-The remote included allows you to use on screen tools to check signal strength (I am showing full strength at 20', through 2 interior walls)
-HD quality picture and sound

Cons:
-it took an extra $20 part and an additional HDMI cable to make my setup work
-Price, this will pay for itself in 18 months but this costs nearly double than the RF Link that does non HD

The bottom line is that this product works and will save you money over time. If you are using this with cable set top boxes, be prepared to purchase the powered splitter and take some time to position everything just right for optimal signal strength and to utilize the IR remote extender. I would give this product 5 stars if I didn't need the splitter.

title: Sony A3000 compared to Canon T3i, Nikon D3100, and Olympus E-PL1
text:
I have come to the conclusion that most of the reviewers of this camera do not own any other cameras with which to make a competent and accurate comparison! Unless you are looking at a review from a professional site that does nothing but camera reviews, most consumer reviews have to be taken with a grain of salt! You have to keep in mind that for a review to have meaning, you must know what camera(s) the consumer is comparing the A3000 to and if the photos are being taken under similar conditions. Comparing the A3000 to a 6MP Canon is useless and so is comparing photos that are shot under different lighting conditions or using different ISO settings or different lenses (zoom versus wide angle).

I am not going to go into all of the details as to which camera has what features since my primary concern is picture quality followed by video quality. Features are great but would rather have fewer features but better photos and videos!

I took all four cameras, put them on a tripod and shot photos using the standard 18-55mm kit lens that came bundled with the camera. I took photos of a house on the side of a hill that is located about 500 yards away and then enlarged the resulting JPEG files on my computer using a 23" HP LCD screen. I did not print them out but viewed them at 200-300% to check out every bit of detail. I used ISO speed from 100 to 3200 to get an idea of how well the noise reduction worked on each camera without sacrificing image quality,

RESULTS: The best camera from ISO 100 to 1600 - Sony A3000. The second best - Canon T3i ( not as good as the Sony from ISO 100-1600, but just a little better than the Sony at 3200), third place goes to to the Olympus E-PL1 which did very well when you consider that it has a 12mp sensor versus the others that range from 14.2MP to 20.1MP. In LAST place is the Nikon D3100.

The D3100 is better than my old Nikon D40x for sure but not as good as any of the other cameras I used in this comparison. You could say that it is not fair since the Nikon has 14.2MP and the others that rated better have 18-20MP. But then, the Olympus with 12.3MP also did better than the D3100!

In terms of Video quality, the Canon T3i and Sony A3000 are pretty close with the T3i being slightly better. The Olympus PL1 fell to last place because the output is in 720p when all the others are 1080p. Nikon D3100 took third place in video quality.

Hope that helps a little in clearing up some of the picture quality issues between at least this batch of cameras.

title: LCD inside a mirror - sounds great.......but
text:
This is a great idea with some poor execution. They have taken 2 working products, mashed them together, and made one very ineffective product.

The mirror is tinted glass with the screen behind it, so that you can see the screen when it is turned on. Anyone that has looked at a one way mirror like this knows it's not as good as a real mirror. However, the mirror isn't the worst part of this product.

The LCD screen is too weak to shine through the tint and still be effective (especially in daylight). The screen works great if you remove the glass, but with the glass front, you see the mirror image more than you see the screen. As much as I wanted this to work, it just falls short.

For $30, you do get a working LCD and the ACC wire attachment is great for having the screen power up when there is a signal to it (I used mine as a backup camera screen). I have since decided to remove the screen and just build a quick box for it to sit on top of the dash.

If I did have a complaint, it would be that they are almost too lightweight. EDIT:
I bought this mouse from another seller that clearly stated that they were selling the version with the BLUE LASER. Sure enough, the blue laser mouse arrived and WORKS FLAWLESSLY!

So, to make it clear

YES, THERE ARE TWO DIFFERENT VERSIONS OF THIS DEVICE. ONE WITH A RED LASER AND ONE WITH A BLUE LASER. BASED ON MY EXPERIENCE (and also based on reading other reviews here) THE RED LASER DEVICE IS PRONE TO SERIOUS DEFECTS, AND THE BLUE LASER DEVICE WORKS AS DESCRIBED. I SUGGEST THAT YOU NOT PURCHASE A MOUSE OF THIS TYPE UNLESS THE MERCHANT CLEARLY STATES THAT THEY ARE SELLING THE VERSION WITH THE BLUE LASER.

title: Works Perfectly.....after some head-scratching
text:
First off, this arrived from Amazon very quickly using Free Shipping.

My PC recognized this USB device immediately when I plugged it in. I did not connect the Centronics connector to my printer until I was satisfied the PC was happy with just the device. At no point have I had any problems directly related to this device, and once I got over one hump, my printer performs perfectly.

The only reason I gave this 4-stars rather than 5 is the absence of any guidance or literature-none! If it was truly just a plug and play operation there would be no problem, but there was a problem.

My computer (Win XP) has always printed to port LPT1 by default. When I switched to this cable LPT1 was no longer connected to anything yet my PC kept trying to print to it. It was not intuitive enough to know to print to a different port. It took me a good 30 minutes to an hour to learn how to redirect the printing to this device. I am only very modestly computer-skilled and needed to fumble around a bit before I learned what needed to be done and how to do it. Once I directed printing to this new port the problem was immediately solved. Just a little bit of printed guidance or a web reference would have been really helpful and appreciated. A couple small clues would have helped a lot. I believe anyone who simply uses a computer as a tool with no knowledge of it's operation would have to ask for help to use this device, but there is no telephone number or web reference for any kind of manufacturers or distributors contact or support.

I would recommend this to anyone but with the caution that they might have to seek some help getting past the initial print port issue. Also, this is only rated up to Win XP machines according to the card in the blister pack so whether it is further certified for Win 7 is questionable. Perhaps the card is outdated or perhaps it is truly not rated beyond Win XP??

title: Great Camera for the Money.
text:
I would consider myself a complete amateur photographer but with the desire to become better. In my college years I took a lot of pictures with a 35mm Canon and loved doing it so I am a bit biased in the brand. However I have used several Nikons and other brands as well so I have a bit of experience with the other brands.

What I like about this camera is that it is easy to use if you want it to be, and has quite a bit of adjustments if you want to try your hand at semi-professional photography. Of course it is not full-framed but I really can not tell that much of a difference.

You can set it to fully automatic and use it as a relatively easy point and shoot type or you can change the settings to suit your needs. I tend to play around with different settings and see what works the best. All my shots are in Raw mode so you do have some adjustments when you go to 'develop' the pictures. It gives you a bit of more flexibility.

Overall I like the shots that it takes. I have taken some great shots with this and the color detail and clarity have been exactly what I wanted in a mid-range DSLR. Usually I take outdoor shots so the lens is fine for what I am doing, but if you want to take more indoor and portrait shots then definitely invest in a 50mm f1.4 or better lens. Low light conditions with the kit lens will almost always require the flash and if you cant use flash will be a little dark.

The video mode is great too. So far I like the tracking feature of the autofocus and how quiet the lens is. I have been experimenting with some different situations and like the quality of the videos. Most of the video has been of recitals and indoor use, and they have been good quality. The mic works well although it might be better to have a separate mic for better quality.

I give the product four stars because it pretty much does everything that I wanted in a camera, however the kit lens is only so good. It is perfect for what I need right now, but as I get to be a better photography I am sure I will find its limitations. As far as the difference between the T4i and the T5i, I have heard there is not much other than the lens. If you are purchasing this for video use, I would recommend this over the T4i, other than that I believe they are very similar.

title: Returned due to Poor Quality.
text:
There were problems with my Saitek X52 Pro. I returned it after one month. Here is my most Spock like analysis:

Pros:
(1) Once configured, it worked relatively well with A-10C Warthog.
(2) Nice configuration editor.

Cons:
(1) This flight controller worked for a period of ~1 month, then the primary fire button (index finger trigger) failed. And that is testing it with Saitek's Control Panel.

(2) It would BSOD my Windwoes 7 system under these two conditions: (1) Not in a game, like just after booting. (2) Press the pinky button ... (~1 Second Delay) ... BSOD. Totally. Repeatable. (3 times, I wasn't trying it anymore!) This system never BSOD'd EVER before/since in the 90 days I've owned it. (BTW...Norton AV Is Installed) (BSOD said (a) Illegal Process Attach & (b) IRQ GTE)

(3) Sometimes it would drift in roll and pitch. Dropping out of the game and examining the Saitek Control Panel would show the center point of the joystick anomalously offset in the same direction. Offset would not go away until reboot. Simply removing USB and reinserting would not remove offset. (2 confirmed instances). I'll grant this might have a probability of having something to do with the game...

(4) The LEDs, while pretty & bright, were installed with excess glue trashing the otherwise very nice surrounding plastic. The construction quality was amateurish, like a badly constructed model car with too much glue.

Summary: I expected better quality and orders of magnitude better longevity for the price. Now do I go spend 3X?

title: Key piece of my system
text:

The next step was a pair of Klipsch VF-36 towers and again the things I was apparently missing in my music and HT was unbelievable. Yet even with how amazing the towers were, I felt like they weren't giving me what I deserved. The highs were rather bright, the mids were almost non-existant and the overall sound was less then expected.

Well that all changed with this AVR. I haven't even set up multi-EQ and every level of sound from my system has greatly improved, my highs are leveled out and clearer, the mids sound like the woofers are actually moving and the bass, which was the only good quality before, has improved even more. This is exactly what my system was missing.

I haven't had the chance to configure anything yet and it seams a little daunting right now but i'm certain i'll get it all figured out. I don't think the AVR came with good instructions but the full manual can be found on denon's website in pdf format so i'm not very worried about it.

For my price range and needs this AVR did exactly what I wanted. The only thing I could have improved without doubling my cost would be some networking ability which holds no interest to me.

This AVR has good power and Multi-EQ XT, for pure sound quality you can't beat the price anywhere else.

My friends have Denon and after purchasing one, I can't see why anyone would want something else.

title: Both laptops delivered were defective, and completely unusable
text:
I ordered this laptop because I previously have had good luck with Toshiba laptops (I've had one for 7 years that has survived every accident, drop, and bump and works just fine) , and thought I would upgrade my setup. The first laptop was delivered and I liked the speed and performance. I did however notice that the keyboard had an unusual feeling to it, and that was because the entire left side was disconnected and warped on delivery and bowing out. The entire keyboard was clearly never installed correctly. I didn't even realize that the laptop was supposed to have backlit keys until I was delivered a non-defective item. Also, when examining the laptop more closely the back panel was not installed correctly, and was jutting out of the laptop. When I shifted the laptop there was also a noticeable rattle inside, like an interior component had not been installed, or had broken off.

5 stars to amazon allowing me to return this laptop for a replacement, which I received 2 days later. I was a lot more critical this time around, taking pictures of the packaging, noting every detail, but the laptop seemed visually pristine. Until I booted it up...

When I started the second laptop on first boot, the windows 8 "we're setting up your laptop" screen came on, followed immediately by a BSOD stating that there was a memory fault and that the computer required a restart. This was the first of many spontaneous restarts that occurred. After several attempts I was able to start the computer completely, but installing/downloading/starting any program caused an issue and the computer would restart. I did a memory integrity scan on the hardware, and detected that there was an issue with the ram shipped. The forced restart frequency was about once every 5 minutes, and without opening up the laptop and swapping out the memory until i found the defective stick this laptop was unusable. (And why should I have to modify hardware on a brand new $1300 laptop.. ) 0 for 2 in working laptops.. 100% disappointment.

I called amazon again, and they said this time I would be getting a refund when the item was shipped back.

TLDR: If you get a good one that's not broken and was made correctly, this is a great laptop. Unfortunately I received 2 unusable, broken laptops.

title: From an amateur's perspective
text:
No, I'm not a professional photographer. No, I'm not a semi-pro photographer either. I'm just a guy who likes to shoot beautiful pics when I hang out with my friends and family. On the other side, I don't want to drag around 5 lbs of equipment when I travel/go out with my friend. This Nikon baby has everything I want/ever need. I use the 18-140 mm kit lens and I'd like to share some thoughts.
_ Picture quality is top notch (on par with my friend's D7100).
_ Low light performance is also top notch (on par with D7100). Even at ISO 6400, photos are still very clean. No noise at all. Maybe if you're a professional photographer, you'll see it. But for me, the pics are perfect.
_ Focus is extremely fast, even in low light.
_ Camera is light even with the 18-140 lens.
_ Battery life is very good. I usually get about 500-600 shots every charge (with about 30% with flash).
_ Never tested wifi before, so can't comment.
_ Handling is okay, not impressed. Due to the small body size, the grip is a bit small. Bigger cameras (like D7100) have better grip, but also weigh a lot more.
_ No touch screen. However, most of the times, I shoot in P mode, and I'm not a pro photographer, so I don't need to change settings a lot.
_ Videos quality is very good. However, it's not silent. The lens creates noise when focusing. If you want silent video focus, go for Canon (t4i, t5i, 70d). People complain about not being able to change aperture during video mode. Well, it's nice if you have that feature, but at least for me, at my level, I don't need that feature.
_ If you want a walk around lens, get the 18-140 mm. It's an excellent one. Sharp, quick focus, light weight, and reasonable price. If you buy it with the body, it's only $300. Since the camera performs very well at high ISO, you don't need really larger aperture (f2.8 or f.18). The lens also has VR - vibration reduction which is a very nice feature.
_ Build quality is good, not excellent. But hey, it's lighter and cheaper than the D7100.
Overall, this is an excellent camera for hobbyists. The camera performs very very well in most shooting situations (except action in low light). If you're reading this, chances are you are like me, a hobbyist, and this camera is all you need.

title: Make sure you are ok with this!
text:
I have had this keyboard and mouse set for about five years.
CONS:
1. The wireless dongle is not very solid, and I have been through two of them. They are somewhat expensive to replace
2. The left mouse click button stopped working somewhat fast, so I used the provided software to change it to the little left hand button, which was ok. A few months later the mouse stopped working at all.
3. At first the keyboard has a really nice feeling rubberized coating on it, but unfortunately it degrades and gets sticky, collects dust, and doesn't clean. I'm pretty careful with my things- this was just bad material planning.
3.5 I read that rubbing alcohol removes the rubbery stuff when it starts getting sticky, and it worked with some of my of my other electronics. When I tried it on a corner of this keyboard, it did not help at all. So it is pretty gross to use.
4. The buttons on the sides of the keyboard are very easy to accidentally hit, zoom, music, etc. I liked the music hotkeys on the right, but I always accidentally hit the zoom ones on the left, very annoying.
5. Mouse ran through batteries FAST
6. Dongle is annoying to have sticking out of a computer case, it's pretty big and would be easy to break if you had it somewhere conspicuous.

Pros:
- Good range on the wireless, no wires is nice
- Looks good.

Overall, I wish this set had been built to last longer than it did, especially at the price I bought it for- five years is less than the average time you even have a desktop computer. I still use the keyboard sometimes, but the stickiness is really gross. I give it three stars because it worked, for a while, and was one of the better options when I bought it years back.
Today, I would try to find something without that nasty coating on it.
