title: Better than average, but still not great
text:
Overall, the concept of an Android based TV is a great one. When I read the description and the other reviews, I imagined the G2 as an Android device with a built-in TV tuner and a huge display. So I assumed I'd have access to all the apps from the Google Play Store, have a full browser with flash support, etc. After buying one and playing with it for a few weeks, it's *almost* what I had imagined but not quite. It does have an OS that is based on Android but it's a different version and MOST apps from the google play store aren't compatible with the Google TV Android OS. As of Jan 2013, on average each category (games, entertainment, etc.) only has 10-20 apps that are listed as compatible, and even then if you install them some of them won't run (so popular games like Angry Birds, Cut the Rope, etc. all DO NOT WORK). So keeping that in mind, I'll go through the pro's and con's as I see them:

Pros:
- Nice display quality (I have the 55in)
- TV has swivel stand (maybe about 25 a degree turn each way, not much but it helps)
- 3D capability is nice, even though it's only at half of 1080 resolution (540 lines for each eye)
- 3D glasses are passive (no electronics embeded), and you can use the polarized glasses that they hand out at movie theaters
- More apps than you would find on other "smart tv" platforms
- In the future, more apps are sure to come as developers port their apps to the google tv version of android
- Remote control has full qwerty keyboard and "wii-mote" like capability for mouse control
- There are a few apps that give you free tv/movie/sports content (ad supported) - Crackle, TvPortal, Thuzz, YouTube
- Has a browser with flash support, so you can watch streaming video via flash players (although hulu doesn't work)
- Generates a guide of all shows playing on channels your TV receives, which is very nice
- The TV looks nice - it has a small silver bevel and is thin and sleek
- Has both wired ethernet port as well as wifi

Cons:
- TV's main user interface is poorly designed. You have to drill down into levels of the main menu to do simple things like turn captions on/off, switch inputs, change aspect ratio, last channel recall, see program info, etc.
- Even though the remote has 4 programmable buttons, most functions I would want to program aren't programmable (like turning captions on/off, changing tv input)
- Even though the TV turns on with very little delay, you can't bring up any of the main menu for about 30 seconds. So if you want turn on the tv to run an app, you have to watch live TV for 30 seconds or so before you can bring up the menu to kick off the app.
- Even though you can save favorite channels into a list, you can't seem to change the order in which they appear
- The vast majority (I'm guessing about 99.5%) of apps from the google play store aren't compatible as mentioned above.
- Web browser interface using the remote is klunky, is too inconvenient to use (it's better to just browse on your computer)
- Remote is too klunky for any app that requires precision or rapid movement (ok for word games, not good for action games)
- You can play content from a hard drive that is connected via USB, but you can't play content from a remote network drive (i.e., from my NAS that has directory shared via NFS or samba), although probably someone will create a media player app with that capability at some point
- Only has 1 component input, no S-video (so you're out of luck if you have lots of older devices that don't support HDMI)

In terms of price, compared to similar LG TV's w.o. the GoogleTV feature, you're basically paying a couple of hundred bucks for the addition of an Android OS, which is a bit pricey. Overall my feeling is that the G2 is better than the average smart tv, but still has lots of room for improvement. I would recommend it if you think you'll get a lot of mileage out of downloading and running apps on the TV to get free content or play games. If you mainly watch live tv shows or mainly use your dvr and you don't think you'll be making use of the available android apps, the extra money probably isn't worth it for you.

title: Pretty neat gizmo for the $
text: I have moved on to a NANO but the shuffle was my first apple product.  Loved it.  For the price it is quite a great device, especially for workouts.  My first one was run over by a car so I replaced it, even though it could still function with some effort on my part to regulate volume.  It has two weaknesses that led me to the NANO.  The first is capacity.  If you manage your I-tunes account in a way that limits what you store on the device, then capacity can be a non-issue.  But I like lots of different music and have many hundreds of songs and like to play what I want to hear when the mood strikes - not limited by what my device will hold.  So, for me capacity is an issue.  Second, the quality of sound, though good and plenty good for most people, but doesn't meet my very high standards for long term listening.  The NANO is better in that regard; the I-pod touch and I-phone yet another step better (really very very good).  I have the Iphone for work and have some songs on it.  Amazing quality especially if matched with Bose earbuds or a high quality car stereo system.  But I still have my two shuffles and would not hesitate to take one with me if space or risk of loss were a major concern.  In my workouts I need diversion from the physical strain and the shuffle, with my Bose earbuds, does the job just fine.

title: First Impressions - on the fence
text:
Even though I'm giving this 4-stars, I'm on the fence. I do like that it is smaller than any of the available Garmin choices because I have small wrists. As the other review has said it needs a yards option for swim laps since nearly all US pools are either 25 yards or 50 meters.

Battery life seems better than my Garmin bike computer and GPS connect seems to be just as fast.

Main Gripe:
The swim, bike, run display options are a little frustrating because their are three display field (top left, top right and main large display) So there are 5-7 display options for each event but only three spaces to display them.

Maybe I'm missing it but there doesn't seem to be a way to select what shows up on the main large display without playing around with the left and right display and hoping the main display defaults to what you want. This is frustrating since the top left and right are really too small to easily read when you are in motion.

If it just records my runs and bike rides accurately for a couple years I think it is worth the $, but it needs some tweaks.

Four month update: Like most gadgets it is great when it works, frustrating when it doesn't. It seems to be variable in finding satellites. I start in the same open field on most runs and sometime it take 30 seconds and sometimes 3 minutes. Once it is locked in it does quite well even when I run through some fairly narrow canyon trails.

title: Wow.  Nikon.
text:
I had a very positive reaction upon opening the box. It is really refreshing to open a product and see the things you'd expect, like a user's manual and a CD. And then to go to the manufacturer's website and see downloads, FAQs, and more manuals. Right from the start, I felt like I had really gotten a deal -- like this used to be a $300 camera, and they put the love and attention into it that you'd put into selling a $300 camera.

Now, some additional notes, as I got into the website and the camera.

The manual didn't tell me where to find my serial number, and neither did the product registration page. Neither the outside of the box nor the bottom of the camera indicated that the number shown there (which, inspection confirmed, was the same) was the "serial number" OR "S/N." Oddly, the Nikon product registration page indicated that no manuals or updates were available, when that was obviously not true.

I wish electronics manufacturers didn't find it necessary to use proprietary jacks and cables. That includes this Nikon. It would be a lot easier to pack for a trip, and there would be less risk of leaving an essential cable at home, if they would all just use the standard mini-USB cable. One cable would handle everything.

I installed the carrying strap, battery, and SDHC memory card. Mine came with a 4GB class 4 SDHC memory card, but I replaced that with an 8GB class 10. I had one lying around. Not sure if that helped. It didn't hurt.

The Nikon website is not well organized. For instance, I found myself at a page offering the answer to my question. But I had not asked any questions. The question being answered was, "Where can I download the latest Nikon software updates?" That was a good question. This page did not quite answer it. It showed 20 different updates, with no indication of which, if any, applied to my particular camera. Apparently I was supposed to load the included CD first, see what was on it, and infer that the only software applicable to me was whatever would be on the CD. But even then, no dates were supplied: I didn't see how I could tell whether the website's offerings were more recent than those on the CD.

Starting with the CD, I looked first at the proffered ViewNX2 software. I wasn't sure I needed it. I had prior experience with unnecessary camera software. I already had image editors I liked. I figured out that the included recharger was just a transformer, from 120V AC to the USB input needed by the camera, so I put that part back in the box and just ran the USB cable directly from the computer to the camera. As soon as I connected that, the camera turned on and let me set date and time. I also got a dialog on the computer, offering to let me browse or import pictures, etc. So I held off on installing ViewNX2 for now.

That meant I didn't download any other updates. There was one possible exception. Somehow I found a webpage indicating that there was a firmware update for my camera. But it wasn't applicable to Windows 7 nor to 64-bit operating systems. So it wasn't useful in my case.

Meanwhile, now that I had connected the cable, a light on the camera was flashing green. The manual said this meant it was charging, and it would require 2.5 hours to charge a fully exhausted battery, and then the light would turn off.

Other than that, I didn't go through the manual in detail at this point. There was too much to learn. Some of it was familiar from my previous camera; some was not. It seemed more efficient to check back as I came up against specific questions.

After charging the camera, I took some photos. Excellent quality. My previous camera was slow -- I would take a picture and then have to wait a couple of seconds before it was done saving it. That was not an issue here. (The SDHC card was the same one as in the previous camera.) It saved the photos within, I think, less than a second.

That was as far as I got at this point. So far, I really like this little camera.

Update, Dec. 1, 2013. This camera has been good for me for 11 months now. I wish it were easier to hold and use one-handed; sometimes I use it to take pictures of items indoors without a flash, and am holding a light in the other hand. Also, for some reason, it is not transferring via cable; I have to pop out the memory card and put it into the computer each time I want to transfer pictures. Not sure if that's a camera issue or a computer issue. There are also times when I think it could do a better job of identifying the object of attention, in medium to low-light conditions, so as to bump up its shutter speed and avoid blurring. Still glad I bought it.

title: Almost but..not quite
text:
Certainly an attractive offer, HOWEVER it ended up being a five hour trudge to get it to work. Firstly the offer is not accurate. You cannot take videos with the lens as shipped - it requires you to buy a micro SD card first. In the Mac version there are a number of peculiarities to contend with based on poorly developed documentation and obscure quirks. It doesn't call out the fact that in order to connect to the Wi-Fi network and enter the strange password the camera lens has to be turned on. Given that takes time to type in the password, the lens could easily, and did frequently timeout which if you didn't understand can keep you retyping the password and network settings indefinitely. (This is all related to an iPhone and may be different on android). Once you go out to take some pictures, and then switch to something else, you will have to go back to the internal Wi-Fi settings on your smart phone and reinitialize the pairing from your settings. This does not allow for quick opportunistic picture taking and becomes increasingly annoying.

The software App has a number of settings which determine the functioning of the lens. What each of the settings does is not explained and I found it impossible to discover this on Sony's support page which tends to be generalized across all of their camera products. I had to fight my way up to a senior rep who also didn't really know much about how the programming on the software (limited as it is) works. There is no access to your flash when this lens is attached so you will want to restrict its use to well lighted scenes. Sony technical help was only slightly informed about this lens, so both calls had to be bumped up to senior help which required additional waiting.

Other than that the lens is good and the added capability and easy attachment will give you superb pictures with its 10 X zoom. The size is right, and attaching it to your smart phone is easy and secure - once you purchase the necessary memory card and learn the peculiarities of having to continually reset (at least on my 4S) the Wi-Fi pairing. Overall, a great idea with lousy documentation and peculiarities.[[ASIN:B00EVIJWXS Sony DSC-QX10/B Smartphone Attachable 4.45-44.5mm Lens-Style Camera]]

title: Love These Headphones!
text:
Throwing caution to the wind, I purchased the Bose AE2w Bluetooth headphones, even after reading very conflicting reviews here. l guess there's no sitting on the fence when it comes to these headphones. I was shopping to replace my Bose in-ear headphones, and seeing a wireless Bose headphone made me interested enough to want to try them on for a test run. I've noticed many reviewers are expecting the AE2w headphones to perform like cabled headphones, I believe that may be expecting too much from Bluetooth linked device, at this time, hopefully we will see improvements to come. I got the impression from the Bose website that the AE2w's were primarily made for smartphones, iPhone, iTouch, iPads. Don't buy this expecting it to link up perfectly to your Bluetooth TV, PC, or Gaming Device. Bose stated on their FAQ's, "Most gaming consoles do not use the same Bluetooth protocols as AE2w headphones. A2DP is necessary for audio with the headphones, so they would only work for communications, not game audio. In general, the audio/video delay will be excessive and most noticeable in games where action and audio are supposed to be synchronized. Players of casual games with sound effects may not have an issue.".

I am very satisfied with the AE2w, they are extremely comfortable, and it doesn't make me feel like my head is being slowly crushed by a vise. I wore these headphone for 4 hours straight, and at no time did I feel any discomfort. I wish I could say the same for the other headphones I tried out. I advice anyone interested in getting new headphones over $100 to try them on first, for as long as you can without getting dirty looks from the employees. After a couple songs you should begin to notice if they would feel comfortable on your head for extended periods of time. Some reviewers have been disappointed with the volume, I'm not having this problem, and I have no static in the background. I change my EQ pretty often on my iPhone 5 to match my music and I have excellent sound washing over me as I walk around my home. These headphones are so liberating and have changed my opinion on wireless headphones. Now that I know what this kind of freedom feels like, there's no turning back! I will no longer feel comfortable being tethered by cabled headphones to my iPhone 5, or iTouch ever again!

As a result, I felt like I was just wasting money buying e-books from Nook so on cyber Monday, I bought the cheaper Kindle for $49. I'm assuming I'll make up for the price of the Kindle within 3 or 4 months a little at a time every time I purchase Kindle e-books.

A little bit of a learning curve was involved with this. The Nook was touch screen and this is touch screen. Little differences in functionality but easy enough to learn. I will only be using this Kindle to read books so didn't want or need any of the Kindles that have more bells & whistles. title: Total Rip Off
text: What a joke. Because you can't change the way this thing insists on turning EVERY device on and off every time you change "Activities" it is completely worthless for my pretty simple system. My receiver takes several seconds (about 10) to come on and won't accept commands from the remote before it is "booted up" (which Logitech should know). So when I use the canned activity "Watch TV" , the receiver ends up on the wrong input every time because the Harmony is trying to change it before the receiver is ready. No problem, I think, I can add a pause in between the the "power on" and change input commands, right? WRONG, when you go into the customize activity section, the built in functions are starred and it explicitly states that you cannot change the default actions, only add to them. Okay, maybe I can leave the receiver off of the "Watch TV" program... But then I can't control the volume... Okay, maybe there's a way to just tell it to use the receiver volume all the time.... Back over to the customize section.... Nope. Okay, maybe I'll create a totally custom, "Watch TV" but then the Favorites won't work, man that's like half the reason I bought this $250 remote... Oh and it still doesn't handle the power (the most basic function of any piece of equipment) correctly so that doesn't solve anything. Oh and by the way, the software to load the settings to the remote crashes about one in five time you you use it which bricks the remote and you have to a soft reboot (hold the off and menu keys down for 20 seconds). And so begins a cascading set of compromises that ultimately renders the Logitech Harmony One a very INCAPABLE universal remote. not even as good as one that can be ordered from this very site for about $20. I've played with this thing for a week and the only way I can make any use of it is to use the individual devices means of controlling things (like that good old $20 universal one). But becaeuse Logitech makes the cool features, like the "Favorites" dependent on their notion of "Activities" none of that works for me. Oh, and when you're looking at the touch screen for individual devices, The button descriptions take up the whole screen sooyou can only see 3 or 4 buttons at a time, making that pretty much worthless too. Well just the icons would do, maybe I can get rid of the descriptions... Back over to the customize section, you can change the label, but it can't be blank and you still only get one button per line..... You see where this is going. Do yourself a favor and stick to the $20 model.

title: BUY THESE...YOU WILL HEAR NOTES IN YOUR FAVORITE MUSIC THAT YOU NEVER SUSPECTED WERE THERE!!!
text:
I have $15K+ sound system that took me over 6 months to research, test various components, and end up with a two speaker system with one goal...to replicate a live performance as closely as possible. This system includes a $800 DAC that allowed me to hear notes that were not audible through the DAC in the DVD/CD player.

I am hearing high notes when using these earphones that I have never heard before on ANY system. My hardware is over 15 years old, but it still produces the best, most transparent sound that I have ever heard, even from systems costing 3 times what mine did. The key was matching the preamp to the amp. There were huge differences in preamps in terms of smoothness, richness, and transparency. These little earbuds are fantastic and provide clean, balanced, rich sound for peanuts. I am going to watch for the next $50 sale and buy a backup pair. They feel great in my ear and have made me aware that I have been lulled into listening to inferior sound from the cheaper Sony earbuds I have had for probably 6 years. Neil Young in his new book talks about how we have been technologyized (new word I just made up) into listening to inferior sound and don't realize it. I believe he is correct, sometimes digital sound grates on my nerves. Time to dig out the old turntable and compare the two. Neil's Puretone technology may be on the horizon for me and perhaps many others.

title: Works but don't expect miracles
text:
Tested on Sony A6000 w/ the following lenses:
Canon 50mm f/1.4 - Works okay. Focuses to infinity, autofocus is slow. It hunts AF slowly and then snaps into focus.
Canon 24-70mm f/2.8 L - Works marginally. Cannot focuses to infinity. It focuses to about 200M (~650ft), autofocus is slow. Hunts AF slowly and then snaps into focus.
Canon 70-200mm f/2.8 L - Works the worse of the lot. Cannot focuses to infinity. It focuses to about 100M (~320ft), autofocus is very very slow. Hunts AF slowly and most times stops out of focus.

The good:
The adapter is well made, makes good contacts (although a bit stiff) and mostly works as advertised. The camera can control the aperture therefore it is better than some of the manually controlled adapters that have a pseudo 'aperture' built-in and these apparently cause vignetting.

The bad:
Attaching and detaching the adapter is a pain. I am always afraid that I might sheer off my contacts because it is so tight. Autofocusing is not practical at all. Even for stationary subjects, I find it too slow and irritating. Thanks to Sony's focus peeking I can focus manually faster than the lens can. The reason autofocusing is slow is because of the way Sony and Canon autofocus using different mechanics.

Overall:
I bought this hoping that the autofocus function is not as bad as some have suggested but was disappointed. However, I am not returning it only because I can use manual focusing along with focus peeking and I can change the f-stop with my camera.

The grid came attached to the dish which I believe assisted in the damage of the grid and also caused some paint damage to the dish itself. Part of my grid was cracked along its lining and caused the comb's to stick into the dish and scratch it up. I had my boyfriend carefully realign the combs back along the rim, trying not to cause further damage or bend it. I also had some very visible dents at the center of the dish. I know I am going to use this a lot as I already see the benefit, and based on the price compared to buying the same dish from Paul C. Buff's site, it really is a great deal. title: Canon SX40 - Highly Recommended, Super Smart
text:
I just got my camera yesterday, having read all the stellar reviews, and I love it. I had to charge the battery (took an hour, but with the anticipation it felt longer) and took a whole bunch of shots, played with the video, tried to learn all of the buttons.
The only drawback is the size, which, while not even close to being a deal-breaker for me, is more than I'm used to. I don't really notice it when I'm shooting. Only when I go to pack it into my old camera case.
At the advice of others I got the class 10 memory card. It works great. I've already uploaded a ton of shots. It is feature-heavy, (fish eye, mini mode, color accents) but that is a selling point to me - I'd rather have the option and hardly use it than not have the option to use it at all.
The battery was flashing red after 24 hours,(but is still going) but considering that I was playing with it so heavily and using a lot of energy just shooting, testing, and erasing, coupled with the fact that I can RECHARGE and not replace (and I bought extra batteries to have on hand) that will also not even come close to being a deal breaker, either.
The macro works great, and the "play" features are awesome. HD Video is awesome. Haven't tried sports or night mode yet, but the AUTO mode really takes the guess work out of everything.It even switched to macro focus on its own with me having to toggle. Its a huge step up from the auto mode I'm used to on my old Canon SX100. ITS SO GOOD IN LOW LIGHT, I'VE HARDLY USED THE FLASH!

Over a year later... I still love my camera. My mom and my cousin have also purchased one and i get compliments on my pictures all the time. That battery still lasts through a day of heaving shooting and I really love using some of the fun settings like color swap and toy camera mode. My only caveat is this: If you are like me and you love to take interesting pictures but you are not at all a professional and yet you still find yourself on the fence between a point and shoot hybrid like this one, or an SLR, just spend the extra money and get the SLR. I love this camera, but have learned so much about it that I wish I had an SLR now. I will wait till this one meets its end (hopefully in several, several years :))

I also want to protect my phone while island camping out of a kayak, so I was thrilled to find this case. I just received and finished installing it(after doing the water test as instructed) when my wife called me. I asked her how I sounded without telling her that I had installed the case. She said that I sounded like I was talking from inside a bucket and was having a hard time understanding what I was saying. As it turns out, there was a drop of water in the slot for the microphone causing the muffled sound. I used a tissue to clean out the water and tested the call again, and my voice seems to come through just fine now. LifeProof should add this step to their instructions.

title: No Glaring Problems, Nor Shining Bonuses
text:
This case is ok. It is not bad, it is not great. At ~ $30, it is approaching too expensive for what it is/does, but not so much so that I feel cheated out of my money. Like most other people reviewing this case, I was looking for a magnet-free way to protect my new Samsung Galaxy Note 8 that wouldn't break the bank or add unwanted bulk to a lovely, slim tablet.

The cover material feels like that "vegan leather" that is being used on a lot of cases these days and it looks great when viewed from the front. The "leather" bends around the left side of the tablet as the case continues onto the back, and the bend/crease on the side is kind of bumpy (I don't know how else to describe it, except that real leather would fold smoothly and hug the contour of the tablet, whereas this material doesn't bend quite as well and results in some mild deformity right along the crease).

The plastic that holds the tablet seems well-formed and the tablet itself snaps securely into the case. Some people who have reviewed this case have mentioned that the elastic-and-plastic clasp that keeps the case closed doesn't work very well, but that has not been my experience at all. I use my tablet (in this case) to take notes during my class lectures, and I basically just toss it into my bookbag without any other protection around it. I have never had the clasp come undone while the tablet was bouncing around in my bag, as it snaps closed very firmly. Also, if one holds the tablet rather carefully while the case is open and the cover is folded back (for example, while reading on the tablet in portrait mode) one can hook the cover clasp to the case and it helps to keep the cover folded back and steady.

Overall, since it would seem that there are not many magnet-free cases for the Samsung Galaxy Note 8 to choose from, I would recommend this case to anyone looking for a reasonably affordable way to protect their tablet.

title: No Playlist Import Available!

After many hours of tampering with this device - updating the "songbird" software, double checking the firmware on the player, attempting multiple transfers to/from the computer, and finally - chatting live with a Philips Technician - I was informed (by a Philips technician) that these devices do NOT ACCEPT the creation and import of a personalized playlist.

WHAT?!?

The "songbird" software will allow you to build a playlist, but it WILL NOT TRANSFER to the device. What this means, in practical terms, is that unless you enjoy a totally eclectic and random playlist OR all your songs are in the same genre, you will not be happy with your playback options.

I purchased this as a gift for a family member, who wanted it for multiple purposes. (i.e. work out music, Sunday "soft" music, travelling in the car etc...)

Since playlist cannot be imported, she gets a giant mash-up of random songs.

Completely unacceptable.

Taking it back to the store. This is a ridiculous oversight from Philips, and would be so very easy to correct.

As for the sound quality - its good. 5 for sound quality - 0 for functionality...

title: Research pays - Know your device and OS
text:
First of all, my research for a new laptop which led me to the hybrids revealed that many online reviews are confusing the i3 (model 13-m010dx) and the NEW i5 (model 13-g110dx), across all website reviews. Second, I work in I.T. and understand not only hardware, but that some people have a difficult time with change and learning curves with operating systems. Users want stuff to work NOW and be easy, but often that means taking time to learn something new... like Windows 8. Finally, my research is never just online, it's only an initial review before going into the store to look, touch and play with new technology for myself. I'd never recommend making such an investment without a hands-on test as well. This review is from the perspective of a tech-savvy user, not a higher-level I.T. professional, because I think the former is who will make best use of the information. However, my recommendation would not change if my review had big geeky words and analyses in it.

I found that most of the low reviews had to do with 3 things:
1) Confusion over the different model numbers.
2) People don't know/understand Windows 8, and want to right out of the box. It's not going to happen. Even "experts" have to learn the new operating systems that come out. There are plenty of YouTube videos for all levels available. Watch them, be set free!
3) People got a lemon. It happens, and it really sucks. I'd be mad too, and for all the years I've purchased technology, it's happened to me too. If you order online from a seller who is also a local retailer, you can take advantage of their return policy and get the issues resolved quickly.

I'm an open source/freeware lover, so I've never owned an Apple product personally, I tend to lean toward the less "popular" stuff. My kids have iPods/iPads, because no one else had what they offered at the time... until Android tablets replaced their Apple devices. For my own purposes, I researched, purchased and fell in love with my ASUS Transformer Android tablet and keyboard. It was this functionality that I was looking for in a Windows laptop. The HP Split x2 i5 has everything I was looking for - as their slogan says, it's the ultrabook I need (as a writer/professor/IT professional) with the tablet I want. Yes, it's a little bit of a heavy beast, but who cares? So is my SUV. If you have more under the hood and on the pavement, you'll have some trade-off.

My observations:
- The battery life is amazing. I haven't gone past 60% drop in life whether using as a tablet or laptop, and use all day, every day so far. But I also put it on the charger every night, just like I do all my mobile devices.

- The keyboard is fabulous for a fast typist, laid out perfectly, best feel of all keyboards I tried in the store, and I typed on many.

- The screen viewing quality is great; but in all fairness, I'm not a huge gamer or movie watcher on computer/tablet, so folks with a higher standard may not agree with me. Because of the glass, there is some background glare (like from my Christmas tree lights behind me right now). I'd recommend an anti-glare screen protector if glare is a complaint for you.

- I have seen an issue that several online reviews mentioned - that the keyboard or mouse seem to freeze occasionally while in full laptop configuration. In contrast to statements that this required the tablet and keyboard to be disconnected/reattached, I find that just touching the screen so the connection was recognized again resolved the problem, well, with the tap of a finger. In my opinion, this is a Windows 8 hardware communications quirk that will work itself out in time. For the record, I tested for a few days on Win8, then updated to 8.1, and haven't encountered the problem since, so Microsoft and HP may have already tag-teamed and fixed this issue with a driver update or two.

- The processor/SSD/memory speed are really immeasurable at this point, because I haven't challenged this machine yet. I'm a multi-task/multi-window spreadsheet-crunching user. I do often close open apps in Windows 8 touch/tablet mode, just because I'm OCD about conserving resources, but I've seen no difference in performance when I have 20 apps or windows open.

- Haven't had the experience mentioned in some reviews of opening the device on my lap and getting "pinched" by the hinge. Easy solution - don't open the device on your lap if you're not wearing proper attire. Seriously?

As for the operating system environment, it's important to keep in mind that Windows 8 offers much the same that this hybrid laptop does - both a Windows desktop and touch-screen tablet experience. Once you take the time to learn the difference, you will appreciate it. Yes, I still occasionally balk at having to switch between the two, but I'll get used to it, just like I did every other change in OS interface back to DOS command line tweaks. Many of the "cons" that folks listed in online reviews about this machine had nothing to do with the hardware itself, but things about Win8 that they didn't understand or wanted to grumble about. Okay, make a sincere effort for 30 days to learn what's new in Windows 8, and I'll wager that you will not only quiet down, but will appreciate some of the new features. It's worth a shot. As for me, I love this device, and highly recommend it.

Now if the industry would just hurry up and make cool accessories for it, I'd be adding more stuff to my Amazon wish list!

title: Outstanding for entry-level photographers!
text:
I'm a beginner photographer and this is my first DSLR purchase. I had been playing around in full manual mode on a Canon G15 point and shoot before buying this so the transition was relatively easy. If you're having difficulty understanding what all of the numbers mean, the graphic display does a great job of graphically showing you what you're settings are. Another great feature for beginners is that if you don't know what a menu option does, you can hit a button and it will describe what the menu option does, differences between the settings, and which situations the settings would be optimal for.

You're probably reading this because you've looked at several entry-level DSLRs and are trying to figure out which you should purchase. I was deciding between this camera and the D3200. Why did I pick the D5200 over the D3200?

Firstly, the D3200 is not capable of doing autobracketed shots, however the D5200 is. You could manually bracket your shots, but it will take a lot longer and you run the risk of moving the camera or your tripod. With the D5200, I can take three autobracketed shots in less than one second. I do a lot of landscape photography so that is very handy!

Next, from other reviews I read and watched (feel free to correct me) it sounded like the D5200 had a little better low-light performance.

Lastly, I don't plan on purchasing another DSLR for at least a few years. The D5200 is basic enough that I can learn, but advanced enough so that I can grow. I wanted a camera that I'd be happy with for a while and this was a perfect buy. It has all the features I'll need for a while. I hope this helped.

title: Samsung seems to have done everything right.  Everything.
text:
I am really impressed with this speaker.

After topping off the battery, I paired it first using the Near Field Communications (NFC) feature with my Samsung smart phone (where NFC is called "tap+send"). I didn't have to power up the speaker. I activated NFC on the phone, tapped it to the side of the speaker, and accepted the pairing on the phone - voila! - the speaker turned itself on and I had instant Hi-Fidelity sound since I had already been playing music on my smart phone. After experimenting with it for awhile I was absolutely impressed.

I decided to try apt-X. My phone has NFC but not apt-X and one of my computers has apt-X but not NFC. This speaker is my first apt-X-capable receiver. I disconnected from the phone and manually paired and connected the computer - voila! - I had an apt-X connection. You'll like apt-X. After experimenting with it for awhile again I was even more impressed.

The sound is incredible whether on A2DP or A2DP with apt-X. It is perfect whether at low, medium, or high volumes. Speaking of high volume, I measured 90+ dB at 1 meter, with no distortion, on a pretty taxing track. I prefer the bass boost on but it is nice with the bass boost off, too.

I love the sound quality for music, videos, movies, radio, or television, whether from one of my smart phones or one of my computers. It is like having a small soundbar with big-soundbar sound.

"Rechargeable battery plays up to twelve hours"? I get over twice that. Recharge time is just a few hours. (I have gone through three or four recharge cycles.)

The controls are intuitive and work flawlessly.

Exterior design and construction are top-notch.

Samsung seems to have done everything right. Everything.

Jim

Update April 21, 2014

I wanted to get a better feel for rechargeable battery play time per charge and for recharge time. Quite frankly, it ran for so many hours over so many days that I kept losing track. I needed to log it.

I finished a battery test today and the speaker was going strong after 32.5 aggregate operating hours of intermittent operation on Bluetooth at intermediate (default start) power to full power. Probably 90%+ of the time at full power.

I plugged it in and it indicated fully recharged after another hour or two.

Wow!

Jim

Update May 11, 2014

I performed another battery check over a few more days. 30.0 hours. Again probably 90%+ of the time at full power.

Jim

title: Don't understand what the fuss is all about
text:
First off, I will say that I purchased this router with high hopes. After having done a fair amount of research and seeing the results at smallnetbuilder and everywhere else I was really expecting it to be better than my old D-link 655 and another Belkin (7302 ?) dual band router that I currently have access to. However it has turned out to not be the case. I messed around with this router over a month and I think now I am done with it. This is actually the second unit that I purchased. I returned the first unit thinking it was defective after messing with it for more than two weeks. However the second unit (the one in my possession currently) is behaving identically to the first so I have come to the conclusion that the first was simply behaving normally for my environment. I ran the first router with .108 firmware and I have the current unit operating with the .112 firmware. To its credit I will say that signal strength using this router was about 10- 20 dB higher than with my other routers (measured with inSSID on 2 laptops & wifi analyzer on 2 smart phones). However that is where the fun ends.
Here are some of the major issues I am having with it
1) Wireless connection rates ( As shown by the Windows 7 connection status ) on 5 GHz band are erratic , vary between 9 Mbps and 90 Mbps at a location where I am used to seeing a more consistent rate between 90 Mbps and 180 Mbps on the older cheapo Belkin router (7302?). This location is barely 30 feet away though the signal passes through two walls a level. I am unable to consistently stream compressed HD movies, (let alone uncompressed BD rips which was part of the reason to try another router ) .
2) Wireless N connection on 5 GHz band drops out every once in a while . May once a day or so.
3) If I am streaming on one laptop using the 5 GHz band and I turn on another laptop which only operates on the 2.4 GHz band I get an interruption in streaming on the first. I have not noticed this behavior with the other router(s).
4) I had to reboot the router twice last week because it dropped the internet connection over Wi-Fi
5) I am getting poor transfer rates using the USB interface. I only get about 3 MB/s read & 1 MB/s write speeds to a 3 TB Western digital external HD. I tried this even with a Gigabit Ethernet connection with the same results.

It could still be that I have another defective router, however the probabilities for that are fairly low. This router does have some good features and I was really hoping for it to work, however right now I am perplexed and don't see what the fuss is all about. If I am unable to get any improvement I will send this router back and try something else.

title: Solid, four-star tablet. Sleek, flexible, but imperfect.
text:
When I was doing all of my research on tablets, trying to understand what the options were and what made tablets slightly different from one another, it bugged me how no one would state the obvious in their reviews. So, I'm going to start with some really obvious features of this tablet, in order to help people who may be newer to the "tablet" world.

YES, you CAN stream Netflix from this tablet, so long as you first go to Netflix, on the normal Internet, and sign up for an account. Then, once you start up your tablet, you can go to the app store and download the Netflix app for FREE. The first time you access Netflix thru the tablet, you'll sign in using your regular Netflix account, and from that point forward, you'll use your Netflix account through the app. You'll have a Netflix "tile" on your tablet, and you'll just "tap" it, and your personal Netflix account will come up, including your queue, etc. You'll tap the tile for the movie you want to stream, and it'll fire right up and stream.

YES, you CAN read books through Kindle on this tablet. You don't need to buy any kind of separate Kindle functionality. Your tablet, in essence, becomes a Kindle. Through the Kindle app, you will be able to log onto your regular Amazon account and download/buy books offered in Kindle format. As with Netflix, you will have a Kindle tile that you can just tap. All of your Kindle library will appear. Just tap the book you want to read, and start reading. The great thing is that you turn the page simply by tapping the screen. You can navigate inside the book, etc. The Kindle function on this tablet it GREAT.

YES, there is an electronic keyboard on this tablet. You do NOT need to buy an external keyboard. In fact, the internal keyboard gives you a few different "configuration" options.

Now, to the general review, and first the good things: This tablet is lightweight and sleek. It has a good camera, and the graphic interface is fabulous. The colorful tiles are rich looking, and movies and old TV shows stream crystal clear. Because the tablet runs on straight Windows 8, a wide array of apps is available. Despite what you may read elsewhere, Windows 8 is embarrassingly EASY to use. I don't understand why people complain about it. You simply touch what you need, and it comes up. It's BETTER than earlier versions of Windows.

Back to the tablet, more generally, you can set up your system to have access to more than one e-mail account. I access both my Yahoo and my Gmail accounts. The battery lasts quite a long time. I'm able to charge the tablet at night and use it all day the next day (although it is asleep while I work). I regularly stream Netflix at lunch, and the battery holds out. Also, the "low battery" warning comes early. You have plenty of time to find your power supply and plug in the tablet. The news sources are great, and the entire "news" tile provides one-stop shopping. And, in general, you can drag the tiles into any configuration on the tablet. There is no "hard coded" tile layout that you're stuck with. The tiles are active, which means they "flip" or "roll over" as they display new information. The free twitter app includes a live tile that will update you with info from your twitter account.

The best thing is the fact that the Microsoft programs are on the tablet. I really need easy access to Word for what I do. It's fabulous to be able to switch from fun, games, movies, news, and all the other tiles with the swipe of a finger and pull up Word. The added bonus is that if you're stuck somewhere where there's no Wi-Fi (or you don't have the password to a Wi-Fi network), you can still use your tablet to get "Word" stuff done (or Excel, Publisher, etc.). Your tablet can still entertain you (or let you get work done). The Kindle works too without the Internet. You just can't use the dictionary function in the Kindle if the tablet is not connected to the 'Net. But you can read your books.

So, why not five stars? Well, a few reasons. (1) When you first unwrap the tablet and plug it in, because it is completely dead, it takes a LONG time to even turn on. You'll keep hitting the "on" button, to no avail. I literally thought mine was defective. After 10+ minutes of panic, it finally turned on and booted up. I thought it had maybe been a glitch until (2) I let the battery run down for the first time after owning it for a few days. When I plugged in the tablet on the day I let the battery drain all the way to empty, I had the same (scary) wait for it to actually turn on and boot up. Once it is charged a bit, you have to hold down the button for a specific amount of time to get the tablet to start, and, again, it will NOT turn on until it has been charging for several minutes. Since NO other device on the planet fails to function the SECOND it is plugged in, it is scary when you plug in the dead tablet and get no response for several minutes. Worse is the fact that nothing in the instructions or guide indicated that it would take the tablet several minutes to get charged enough to respond to being plugged in and to actually turn ON. Also, the power cord is SHORT. Buy an extension cord right away. The power cord provided by the manufacturer is a joke, length-wise. (3) Despite how great movies on Netflix look, ironically, the one app that will (too often) freeze your system and force a reboot is Netflix. I can't tell you how many times I hit the back button on Netflix to go back to my list of movies I want to stream, just to have the screen go chromy black. At that point, the entire tablet is frozen. I have to reboot (and with my fears about how long it may take for the button to respond to my reboot attempts), it's annoying that this app malfunctions in this way. Ninety-five percent of the time, Netflix runs fine. But...a five-percent freeze rate is lame. (4) As other reviews may have mentioned, for no reason at all, the tablet loses/drops its connection to the Internet/Wi-Fi. Even if it the connection is strong and it shows "connected," you still are not connected. So, you have to quickly disconnect and reconnect. It takes no more than 22 seconds, but it's a pain. It interferes with apps and videos you're running. (5) The speaker is pretty weak. It mostly doesn't matter, but if you're streaming something weak (like an old TV show or a YouTube video with weak sound), it's a tad annoying. MOSTLY, the speaker is fine, but it could be better.

In sum, this tablet is fast, sleek, light, entertaining, multifunctional, and way ahead of the iPad curve with the Microsoft programs. It's begging to be five-star. However, because it takes long to start if the battery has fully drained, freezes during Netflix, drops its Internet connection, has a very average/too-weak speaker, a short power cord, and a useless user's guide, it gets bumped down to four stars. In NO way is it three-star.

This is a solid four-star tablet that has been a great joy to own since I bought it, and for the price, you can't beat it. I would buy it again and definitely recommend it. The minor irritations are not that big a deal. Windows 8 is awesome, the tablet is light enough to carry everywhere, and the price is right.

11/30/13 Update: I still love this tablet. I'd even upgrade it to 4.5 stars. (1) I no longer leave it asleep at work and literally stream my favorite radio station all day AND watch Netflix at lunch, and the battery doesn't drain, so long as I leave for work with it fully charged. (2) Netflix or Microsoft must have heard a lot of feedback because, overall, Netflix performs a bit better now than it used to. (3) I use the SkyDrive to save things, and it works great. Videos too large for e-mailing can be sent to the SkyDrive and shared from there, including e-mailing them to a person. (4) I've used the camera and video camera bunches of times with great results. Still no five stars because of the continued drops in the Internet connection, etc. (see above). But...if I had to buy a tablet TODAY, I would go right back and buy this one. I'm getting tons of hours of use every, single day for such a reasonable price. I adore this tablet.

09/12/16 update: After three years of DAILY and SOLID use, I finally had to bump this tablet into "second" position behind a laptop I recently bought. The advent of Windows 10 made some of the functionality on this Windows 8 tablet ineffective as more and more "updates" were beamed to the system. Things loaded slower, apps began to fail. The Internet was rough going. And ASUS has a glitch you can google called "plugged in, not charging". Somewhere along the line, the battery began to be hit-or-miss, and I found, by trying to google the problem, that many people with an ASUS had this same problem. Mostly, it worked, but by the time I relegated this tablet to a word processor and not much else, often, I would use it plugged in, and it would still drain. Sometimes it would say, "plugged in, charging," but more often than not, it said, "plugged in, not charging," which is very frustrating. For the first three weeks I had my new laptop, I kept rushing to do things, expecting the battery to drain, so accustomed had I become to my ASUS's failing battery. The only time the battery charges without fail is when the tablet is 100% shut down. So, I can still charge it overnight and use it the next day.

STILL: I only finally changed to a laptop just over the three-year mark of owning this tablet. FOR THREE YEARS, not only was this tablet a walking desktop, but, under a pen name, I actually wrote and published (and designed) a 94,000-word novel on it. That required massive rewrites, use of all kinds of weird technology, and TONS of Internet research. I did it ALL on my tablet. I finally broke down and bought a Bluetooth mouse, but I wrote the whole book using the tap keyboard inside the tablet. When I finally switched to a laptop, I was almost sad for my tablet. It has had my back for three years and been my go-to device for EVERYTHING. Alas, the updates; Windows 10; and the battery ended the journey.

title: The HGST 1TB 7200 Hard Drive - Big, Fast, & Cloned!
text:
My Sony Viao Laptop was showing signs of Hard Drive Failure after 3 years. Bad Sectors and Very Slow Startups. About 14 days ago I started getting the S.M.A.R.T. Notice on startup that my hard drive failure was eminent. Yikes, I had never replaced a hard drive before! The following is the methods I chose to replace my hard drive.

Originally I set out to replace my OEM Samsung 320GB Hard Drive with a new 500GB drive, but with only 20 bucks difference I ordered this HGST Travelstar 2.5-Inch 1TB 7200RPM SATA 6GB/s 32MB Cache Internal Hard Drive.

VERY IMPORTANT: You need to Act Immediately to copy all the contents of your drive off the computer otherwise risk the strong chance to loose all of it's contents. You Also need to Order Your Replacement Drive Right Away!

Once ordered from Amazon and awaiting delivery, I needed to get the Windows 7 Operating System "Cloned" along with copying my personal files. These days you do not get a back-up operating system disc with a new computer which I think is terrible of the computer manufacturers. Should your computer have a major failure you are screwed! For those who don't know, New Drives do not come with the Operating System on them. Thus you need to "Clone" your Operating System or risk having to Replace the entire contents of your Hard Drive including re-buying Windows.

Firstly, I searched to find the Best & Easiest Method to "Clone" my old hard drive. There are many software programs available, and opinions differ. In the end I chose to use the "Seagate Disc Wizard" program which was originally created by Acronis, and is Free. However this program can only be used if your External Dive is a Seagate (Most Drive Manufacturers offer a Cloning programs). If you have a spare Seagate USB External Drive, Download this Free Program from Seagate and follow the instructions to create a "Bootable" Seagate Disc Wizard CD-R. This CD-R will be used to "Clone" an Exact Image of your old hard drive, and later to Clone that image to your new HGST 1TB Drive. If you don't trust your computer's abilities in it's present failure state, download and burn "Seagate Disc Wizard" on another computer.

Secondly, the Direction I chose to "Clone" my old drive was to use 2 USB External Hard Drives. To begin this process I "Moved" all non-essential files (Music, Pictures, Video, Documents) to a External Hard Dive (Drive-1) as soon as possible. I did this because removing the contents of a say 150 GB of files would just lengthen the Time in the whole entire Cloning process. You can Copy these type files to Any External Hard Drive, dosn't have to be a Seagate.

Thirdly, I "Cloned" the contents of the remaining Operating System Files (Windows 7, Programs, Browser) to an External "Seagate" Hard Drive (Drive-2) using the Seagate Disc Wizard. This process is easy. Insert the "Seagate Disc Wizard" CD-R into the media drive, Power On, and just follow the easy on-screen instructions to clone the entire operating system contents to the USB External Seagate Drive.

Once the Operating System was Cloned, and Music & Pictures were Copied to my external hard drives I knew my files were safe to reload to a new hard drive. Over the next week I received S.M.A.R.T. warnings at startup that the hard drive was failing and multiple "Nags" to back up the hard drive immediatley. But at 10 days into the failure the hard drive Activity Light was always on, and it was just impossible to do anything with the computer. No matter the program I disabled, it had no effect. In the Interim I did find that running the computer in "Safe Mode with Networking" made it functionable enough until I finally replaced the drive.

The Installation of the new HGST 1TB Drive was fairly easy. To do so you need only a small Phillips Screwdriver. First remove the laptop Battery and Power Cord. Flip the laptop over, remove the hard drive Access Panel screws, then remove the screws holding the hard drive in place. Once you have pulled the old drive out remove 4 screws of the 3 Sided Mounting Bracket Caridge from the old drive. Always touch something made of metal to remove any static charge you may have, then re-assemble the new drive in the reverse order.

Laptop Hard Drives are a "Standardized Form". New Hard Drives meet this standard form requirement. Some drives can be thinner than the original hard drive, and it's only advantage is to alow a little more airflow inside. If you still need assurance that a new drive will and fit into your laptop, look up the Original Hard Drive installed by your Laptop Model to find the the Exact Hard Drive Model Number & Manufacturer. Then do a search for a Exact Relacement of this drive to find it's dimensions.

Finally, to "Clone" your new HGST 1TB Hard Drive insert the "Seagate Disc Wizard" CD-R in the media drive, Power On, and follow the instructions to copy the contents of the operating system from External Seagate Hard Drive (Drive-2) to your new HGGT 1TB Drive. Once copied and completed, power the laptop off. Then re-start the computer and there is your complete operating system exactly as it was on the failing drive. Even the Favorites in the browser are in the exact order you left them. Next "Copy" the entire contents of External Hard Dive (Drive-1) to re-add your Music, Pictures, & Video. You Are Done!!!

The only unforseen issue I had with the whole process on the new drive was that my Intel i3 Processor used the Original Intel Rapid Storage Driver and was not able to run Windows Updates and other Windows Check functions. This is because this Original Intel Rapid Storage Driver on My Laptop was not made for use with A Larger Hard Drive such as the HGST 1TB. This issue May or May Not Occur upon New Drive Replacement depending upon Your Processor and Installed Processor Driver. Although my entire system was operational, this Windows Update Issue needed to be corrected. I searched around and found the Intel Rapid Storage Technology Driver that takes care of that issue at:
[...]

This HGST 1TB 7200rpm Hard Drive runs Great, Faster Startups, and Tons of Storage. It was the Best Priced for it's Size and Speed. I hope it will last a long while, and if It dosn't.... I will be sure to post it here. There are many methods to "Clone" your Hard Drive, I hope I have helped you with My Method in this Amazon Review!

title: Excellent Unit
text:
Installed in a 2011 F-250 4X4 crew cab.

I won't go into much detail because most of the reviews are spot on with regard to sound quality, navigation, etc and it won't add a lot of value repeating what is already well known. The one thing that I will say is that I am very satisified with this unit and would recommend it to anyone that wants a full featured unit that is very user friendly.

Parts
KW-NT810HDT
PAC RadioPro4 Steering wheel control interfact -RP4-FD11
Sirius/XM SXV100v1 module
Metra Installation kit 95-5812
TaoTronics CMOS back up camera TT-CC17 (Note 1)
Antenna adapter BAA20 21
Parking brake bypass
12V switch (see note 2)
12V diodes (see note 3)

I installed the unit myself in about 6 hours total over 3 evenings. I'll explain a few lessons learned on things not to do.

The first evening I opened up the dash to look at the space, existing wiring and where I wanted to place the modules, etc. It got late and I put everything back together. The next morning it was 30 degrees and I started the truck (4:30AM) to go to work. The lights on the tempature controls, fan and heater did not light up and would not work. So, I drove the 15 miles to work with the windshield fogging up and I was freezing. Come to find out I didn't fully re-seat the temperature control wiring harness.Lesson learned = Pay attention.

The second evening I actually installed the new unit, connected up the camera, Sirius/XM, etc. Again it was getting late and I was proud of myself that I actually had it working - except that I didn't get the steering wheel controls working correctly. So I started the truck to park it in it's normal position in the drive way and when I stepped on the brake the back up camera came on. I found that I connected the back up trigger wire to the brake light wire instead of the back up light wire. Cut the wire and parked the truck for the night. Lesson learned = Pay attention.

The next morning I decided to start the navigation for the trip to work so that I could see how well it worked. Well I hit the wrong button on the screen and set the destination to a street right outside of our neighborhood somehow. It was dark and I didn't know how to turn the navigation off so for the next 15 miles to work I kept hearing "turn right on 34th Street", "Turn right on 33rd Street", "in 2 tenths of a mile make a u-turn". Lesson learned = Read the manual.

Note 1 - The installation kit works well, but if the unit is not placed very carefully in to it, the tilt function does not work. When you tilt the screen up to insert a DVD (example) it will not close because the screen will get caught on the frame of the kit.

Note 2- Installed a micro switch in the glove box and wired the speed sensor so that I could find out what happens with the speed sensor connected and without. My concern was that even though I had the parking brake bypassed I though that the speed sensor would tell the unit that the truck was moving and limit the unit functionality. I found that the speed sensor does not restrict or limit any functionality even if you are driving at highway speeds.

Note 3 - I wired up the back up camera so that I can use a switch or put the truck in reverse and get the camera to come on. I pull a boat and need to be able to check and make sure the saftey chains are connected, etc. In order to make that work I had to install 2 diodes so that I wouldn't back feed 12V. I also did not want the back up lights to come on when I switched the camera on with the switch.

title: Jack of all trades, master of none.
text:
The 28-300 is a lens that's got a wide range of uses...and while pretty good (and certainly productive and reliable) at any of those uses (i.e. landscapes, portrait, zoom-action in daylight), it isn't in a class with The Trifecta (14-24, 70-200, 24-70). Of course, it's a good bit cheaper than they are...so in terms of bang for your buck, this lens is excellent because of its versatility (and you get VR with it, so tripod isn't necessary on casual longer focal length shots...a big plus for zooming in on your 7 year old all day). This lens is awesome for a family trip to an amusement park or going to your kid's athletic competition (as long as it's outside in decent light). If a hobbyist asked me what lens I'd buy, if I could only buy one...and money WAS an issue...this lens would be high on my list. It's lighter than its more gifted cousins, but is still rigidly constructed and feels sturdy. But, if someone is serious about working on a specific type of shot or genre, I'd opt for the more expensive, faster, sharper lenses that specialize in doing a few particular things remarkably well. In summary, it's not that this lens does anything at a sub-par level. It's just that it doesn't do anything exceptional.

On the wide end, there is significant vignetting at the faster apertures, especially with a filter attached. There's also some barrel distortion at the wide end. On the long end, the image has an unfortunate tendency to be a bit soft, from center to corner. That's why, on the wide end, you'd be better off with the 24-70mm zoom, if you do a lot of work just on the wide end. And, if you mainly work on the long end of this lens' range, you would get consistently sharper images going with either the 80-400 or either of the 70-200s with a teleconverter.

That said, in the middle range (around 50mm to 200mm) this lens does a very good job. Clear, crisp, and good saturation of color.

title: Two Major Headaches With My New Nano!
text:
After having my first iPod Nano for over 3 years I was excited when it was time for me to upgrade to a newer model.
Everything about my new Nano is as I expected except for two things that are really annoying.
I listen to podcasts about ninety-nine percent of the time and occasionally the CDs from my collection I have downloaded.
Also, I listen to it while I am driving around during the day and plug it into the cars' mp3 enabled stereo jack.

(1) When I turn the Nano on for the first time of the day it will shut itself off every 60 second for about the first 10 minutes.
It used to last for about 25 minutes (shutting off), but now it is down to about 10 minutes.
(2) The touch/tap sensitivity is too hard when selecting a track on the Menu. So much so that it causes the Menu to slide to the left
or right.
The most annoying thing is when I try to Pause the track or try to Restart it afterwards. The tap/touch function sensitivity is
way too high and I usually have to tap it 5-10 times to get it to pause or restart.
I tried varying the pressure of the taps, angle that my fingertip touches the icon, and even tried using my fingernail with no
success.
I still have to tap it at least 5 times to get it to react.
The worse time is when my cell phone is ringing and I am trying to Pause the Nano to answer the phone.
Not cool at all.

I like my Nano and will continue to use it during my work week.
However, I am very disappointed and annoyed with these 2 flaws.
I have a very favorable view of Apple and all of it's products, but they should have field tested this thing more thoroughly.

title: Easier to store and better friction than the beanbag, but too light
text:
The folding ball mount that makes this easy to store in most any glove box is fantastic, and probably makes the mount a worthwhile replacement for the beanbag all on its own. The sticky bottom also helps prevent it from sliding.

That said, I think Garmin friction mounts are still a work in progress. While this won't slide right off the dash under moderate to heavy throttle application like the beanbag friction mount would, it can actually tip end-over-end and fall off that way. This is especially noticeable driving uphill. The base is too light. Garmin cites this as an improvement, but I disagree. For the next revision, Garmin should fill it with lead or something. As it is, plan on practicing your hypermiling when this is in use; spirited driving in even a moderately powered car from 10 years ago (never mind the HP monsters of today) risks knocking the mount off your dash.

Furthermore, it rotates too easily from side to side. My aux cable is on the heavy side, and the weight actually tugs on the mount and moves the back end of it slightly toward the side the cable is plugged into. Not the end of the world, but a nuisance.

I continue to think these friction mounts are the best option because they are easily hidden and don't leave a mark on the windshield. That said, there is still room for improvement. I would like to see Garmin make this at least as heavy as the old beanbag mount while keeping the sticky bottom and folding arm.

title: Mixed feelings...........great sound but several flaws
text:
I purchased this sound-bar system in September of this year (2012) when I purchased my Sony Bravia 55HX750 TV. The JBL SB300 was an out-of-box model but not a scratch on it/did not look used so I only paid $285 for it instead of $499!!!! I almost hate complaining about this product because I got it for such a great price & I do love the sound. For those considering purchasing this system (especially @ $499), I felt I needed to post this review.

Pro's:
*The setup was incredibly easy. It took me about 10 minutes & I am far from a wizard when it comes to setting up TV, cable, audio or other devices.
*I thought my TV audio sounded just fine - until I turned on this sound bar!!!! There is instantly a noticeable difference in the sound quality when I turn on the JBL SB300. The sound quality is awesome!! Clear, crisp & bold audio no matter how low or high I set the volume. It definitely produces a more cinematic sound than the TV audio does.
*I read several reviews with complaints about the look of the subwoofer. I personally do not mind the look. Yes, it looks like something out of Star Wars but even though my house has Western décor it does not stick out in the least.

Con's:
*This is the issue that is driving me nuts! I've read several reviews w/ others who have had the same problem. My remote worked (sometimes) the first few days I had this system but hasn't worked since. I tried a new battery - still nothing. :O( I've spent a TON of time researching reviews for the JBL SB300 as well as reviews for universal remotes. All the while hoping to find something that confirms a specific universal remote that works with this sound-bar system, but no luck. If anyone knows of one, please comment on my post & let me know the specs.:O)
*Related to the above mentioned con......I now have to get up & go to the sound bar every time I need to raise or lower the volume. I know it's lazy but that's one of the reasons we love our remotes, right?!?! To make matters worse, the up/down buttons on the sound bar very often stick when I use them to adjust the sound - ugh! It happens so often that I have to keep a tiny screwdriver behind the sound-bar to pop the buttons out when they get stuck. Just makes me more irritated about the remote not working!!
*I rarely notice any 'surround sound' effect from the sound bar system so I am disappointed about that. From reading many reviews I understand to get great or true surround-sound it would take a different type of system/something with 5.1/7.1 options so I wasn't expecting that type of quality from this sound-bar. BUT.....since the manual claims that this system "will produce a complete surround-sound experience" I had hoped for some level of surround-sound effects.
*No HDMI inputs.

A few things to note:
1) If you are considering purchasing this system be sure to note length of the sound bar & measure the table/cabinet/wall where you will be using it. This sound bar is longer than most. 2) This system requires an optical digital cable. I am not sure if the system comes with this cable in the box or not. If you decide to purchase this system be sure to check on that/purchase the cable if it doesn't come w/ the system.

For easy setup & awesome sound quality (even though it lacks in the surround-sound category) I would definitely recommend this system - ONLY IF your remote that comes w/ your system works OR you could find a universal remote that works with it. Otherwise, I can't say that I would recommend this system because of the issues w/ the remote especially at the regular price.

title: Work much better than my stock tips
text:
I had some concerns going into getting these as I have the Bluebud X Bluetooth ear-buds and two comments seem to be prevalent: first is do they fit or not fit and second is they stay compressed. Since I was not 100% sure, I use my X's with the wire going over top of my ear for reference. I bought them to try them out and here are my findings.

Stock rubber tips. They work, but at the gym even if I am just starting out, they constantly move around. Some days seem to be better than others, but I had to find something else. The overall design of the headphones are good, but they need to stay in place. I do give the "bat wings" that fit into your ear a lot of credit--- my ears never get tired or sore which has always been a problem.

Fitment--- they do fit, and they are very tight to slide on. Is this a problem, no, but when I got done putting them on, it took a good bit of time for them to rebound to their natural shape. Once they rebounded, everything was fine. Again, a tight fit, but taking about 30-seconds each was all it took. Since they are universal of sorts, I would give fitment a 9 out of 10.

Compression/ rebound. I have found that they are on the firmer side and do work well if you do not compress them before putting them in. I have tried the large size first and will be stepping down to the medium to see how the feel changes. Now, if you squish them, they do take in my opinion too long to come back to size. I would like them to be like the earplugs I use when I have to go out in the warehouse at work--- squish them, put them in, wait 20-seconds to seal, good to go. These seem to squish and take minutes to return to size. If you just put the ear-buds in and not pre-squish the tips.... then they work well. Personally I would have liked to give them a little squish before putting them in my ears so they have a better chance of "grabbing on". So for this part, I give it a 6 out of 10.

Would I buy them again? That depends... I want to try their other styles. I use these for working out, so they have to stay in. So far they are much better than the original rubber tips, but there is room for improvement. Overall, much better than the originals and in that case, I would definitely recommend them. Compared to their other styles and other brands.... we'll see once I order them and get a chance to compare.

That leaves me with a final note for now. They work. Yes they take too long to rebound from a compressed state, but as long as you treat them with respect to that fact.... they work like a charm. For me I would also like to see them about an 1/8" longer.... I inherited my grandmothers ear canals that slope upwards slightly which makes fitment difficult for me. So when I find something that I like and works--- I know it is a good thing.

title: Takes a Beating!
text:
Man, this chick is sturdy! Seriously, she's well-built. I know this because I have, in a blinding fit of rage, thrown her into the floor of my passenger seat as hard as I possibly can at least 4-5 times. But no matter how much I curse at her and abuse her, she just gets back up and goes right back to work!

Don't get me wrong, there are times when Nuvi and I get along just fine. For example, when we're reaching the end of a journey and she gently guides me the last few miles from the freeway exit ramp to my final destination. Or when I'm out in the suburbs and can't be bothered to learn the roads because I harbor a deep-seated ambivalence towards suburbs which prevents me from committing a full effort to getting to know even the most attractive ones.

So why, you ask, do I abuse Nuvi so much? Am I a perfectionist who expects to have the complete package delivered to me on a $100 platter? Of course not, I tell myself. But the fact is that I live in Washington DC, and Nuvi is really just a country girl at heart. She can't keep up with the pace of life here. I've tried to explain the idea of traffic to her multiple times, and yet she continues to give me asinine recommendations, like driving down K street at 5pm. I mean, did she even go to school? She must have failed math, because her ETAs are always at least 25% off, and it frequently takes twice as long as she predicts to get anywhere. God forbid I try to explain the concept of the time-reversed Rock Creek and Potomac Parkway to her - I think her head would explode! But really, the routes she gives me are the absolute worst. No, really, I need you to understand that I'm being completely serious when I say this: the routes Nuvi gives me are literally the worst options available in 50% of cases, and the 2nd worst option in 30% of cases. DC is one of only a handful of major markets in the mid-atlantic, so why was there no effort put in to teaching her how to navigate the city? I am literally almost always better off pulling out a paper map and planning my own route than listening to Nuvi's maniacal suggestions. Which would be a completely moot point if Nuvi would just show me her maps. But noooo, she's a conservative type, and only lets me see little bits and pieces at any one time! What a tease! I know all the map goodies are there underneath that horrible unfriendly interface, but I just can't seem to access them all at once! It drives me nuts! I mean, sure, to be fair, she does technically let me access her maps, but she has all these difficult rules I have to follow when interacting with them. Really, it's easier to get elected to the House.

Here's a typical evening out with Nuvi:
First, I tell Nuvi where I'm going. This is difficult, because she frequently doesn't respond until the second time I tell her something. But after a solid 2 minutes or so, she gets it, and gives me a route. So then I have to turn to my side chick Googs and ask her what the big picture is. See, since Googs and I aren't married and I haven't bought her any expensive gifts lately, she's much more honest with me than Nuvi. Googs shows me the big picture and tells me I have a few different options, and I pick the one I like best. Then I follow Googs' directions all the way until the last mile, after which I let Nuvi guide me. This is not as easy as it sounds, since Nuvi is constantly trying to mislead me, and also because I have to continually sneak in conversations with Googs in order to understand my place in the world. I wish I could literally punch Nuvi in the face so hard that she grows up and learns how to navigate DC without making me want to literally punch her in the face, but unfortunately I've discovered that violence is not the answer.

God forbid I take 270 - it scares her to death! She spends the whole time telling me to get over to the local lanes, because "I drive too fast in those silly express lanes!"

Nuvi is a solid 4 out of 10, but easily bumps up to a 6 because she's such a cheap date and she likes to stay in shape. If I have no idea where I'm going and I don't mind being suuuuper late, then Nuvi is the perfect companion.

Did I mention that Nuvi has trouble reading house numbers? She says "here we are!" when we're still like 1000 feet away from the right house. Seriously, one of these days she's going to get me arrested for a B&E. On the plus side, she doesn't get confused by having to make decisions, unlike my side chick Googs who often gives me directions like "in 1000 feet" followed by silence.

I lie and say I'm in love with her. I can't find a better GPS.
