title: Wow
text:
Let's just say these speakers are worth every penny. I had looked and sampled several speaker setups from many different manufacturers over the last several years (Basically everything in my local store) so i decided to go online. Anyway, I connected everything up and they sounded AWESOME from the the start. Most setups I have had to tweak the EQ to get things to sound right but these were great without any modifications. In fact after I ran them through the break-in period they sound better and better every time I use them. Most speakers you can hear where the sound is coming from but these project the sound into the room surrounding you with music. Did I mention they were AWESOME! No need to turn on the simulated surround or any other sound fields for that mater.

Currently I'm using them as my mains but when I can save up some more cash I'll be swapping them to the rear speakers and get the NS-555's. If you simply need a set of bookshelf speakers for music these bad boys are all you will need. Some have reported the lack of bass but that isn't entirely true. Yes, these will not rattle your core (that's what a sub is for) but they do a very good job at reproducing the low end for music reproduction. In fact these speakers are very good at reproducing the entire frequency range. The reason I'm upgrading to the NS-555 for the main and setting these in the surround position is because the NS-555 are floor models and will look better with my setup but the NS-333 can handle it on their own.

I would consider myself an audiophile. I'm always looking for the best and I run professional audio equipment at my church for live concerts (indoor and outdoor performances). I hope my review helps you in your decision.

title: Light, affordable, accurate and reliable. Nike makes running fun.
text:
To keep it simple, I love this watch. The accuracy of the GPS is RARELY off by more than .05 miles which is no problem for me ( I check all of my runs with different running website tools to ensure accuracy. This watch is always within the margin of error for any GPS tracking device. When it is off, it has always been UNDER, so learning I actually ran a little bit further is icing on the cake).

I love the features that the Nike+ website offers and the motivational features it provides. This watch has become a staple with every run I take. It is simple, light, reliable and just right. I do still back up just about every run with my Runmeter app on my iPhone only because the Nike+ website erased a ton of my data. This was years ago before the watch while using the Nike running app. The Nike+ website has improved IMMENSELY and is a lot of fun but I am still a little paranoid and (and like additional backup) it doesn't have a feature to email your stats that I have found...something Runmeter is seamless with. People have complained about the time it takes for the GPS to sync. I travel a lot and have never waited more than 1 minute anywhere. Usually the wait time is less than 30 seconds. Part of this reason might be because I ALWAYS PLUG MY WATCH INTO MY COMP AND LET IT SYNC WITH SATELLITES. Nike makes clear that this should be done every time and it works flawlessly for me. Amazing what checking out the instructions will teach you...

Overall I LOVE my watch and after 3 months and over 275 miles, I would recommend this to anybody who wants affordable, reliable, accurate and motivating (via the Nike+ website features and data archiving process) running experiences.

title: Square Trade has your back. I am so happy that I bought my protection plan!! Exceptional Company!
text:
I am always reluctant to buy these extended warranties and have not had good experiences with them in the past, so I was not sure about buying the square trade protection plan for my 75" Samsung LED TV. My other TVs that I have owned for years never had any problems, and when my stereo broke that had a big-box retailer warranty they were absolutely no help at all..so I was having a hard time justifying adding on any extra money on a purchase that took months of saving up for because I thought in the unlikely event that something does go wrong, then the company would find a way to get out of helping me out anyway so it would just be pointless. After a lot of thinking, I decided to buy the warranty anyway to protect my investment and just hope for the best.

About a year and a half later my TV developed 3 separate white spots in the center area of the screen. The panel had a defect, which is one of the most expensive parts of a TV to repair. I called Square Trade with a lot of dread, scared that they were going to confirm my fears that I'm stuck with these ugly, distracting spots on my TV. I have worked customer service myself and I am always extremely polite and understanding with representatives on the phone...and I feel a lot of companies take advantage of this because I am not going to make a fuss about a problem, especially to a phone representative caught in the middle.

Square Trade was genuinely interested in helping me out with my broken TV. They always replied to my emails swiftly and even called me when I was a little slow in getting some photos to them of the broken TV. They went above and beyond my expectations and fixed the problem so quickly. Square Trade had my best interests in mind and was relentless in making sure they could come up with a solution that left me nothing but extremely satisfied. In my case, this was a reimbursement for the purchase price of the TV since the repairs would cost more than the TV itself. Square Trade had my back unlike any company I have ever come across and instead of sitting here sulking about my expensive lemon of a TV and kicking myself for passing up on the Square Trade warranty, I am happy and stress free. I would definitely recommend for anyone unsure about this product to just go for it, you will be thankful for the peace of mind even if you're lucky enough to never need the extra protection. I will never buy a warranty from any other company again, Square Trade has earned my business and trust and I am so glad a company like this exists.

title: Faster and Easier
text:
I really didn't pay much attention to lens caps until I jumped into DSLR video. I know many pro shooters are not fond of lens caps, preferring speed of run and shoot but still, I like to keep thousands of dollars of lens protected when not in use.

And its a good thing I did, because a few months ago after a long trip, late-night return, I grabbed my camera bag ([[ASIN:B003D5TVAO Tamrac 5788 Evolution 8 Photo/Laptop Sling Backpack Bag (Black)]]) and tossed it to my shoulder anxious to get in the door. For the first time in my life, one of my lens, my favorite (135mm) went crashing to the ground in the dark because a side pouch was not secured.

#%@#%(#*@#%! At first glance, all looked okay. Upon further review inside and in the morning, the lens cap took a direct hit and broke. Not a single mark on the lens - pure luck of the fall.

Which led me to this quick, center pinch replacement. Totally converted now and have replaced all my caps to center-pinch Canon caps.

For one, with the video, I shoot with a teleprompter glass/hood. Reaching into the hood to grab the old caps (sometimes it sits here for days, so I cap them) - a pain to find and release. Pinch-caps, no problem.

Also, shooting with lens hoods (stills/videos) and now a large matte box (videos) is it SO much easier to reach into the center and pinch/pull.

All other things being equal, I have to say - I think these center-pinch caps even look better, they look more rugged (although probably not) and they look more serious.

Whatever your reason or your need, you won't be disappointed in these genuine Canon caps.

title: 94dB sensitivity=amazing efficiency!
text:
I purchased the Infinity 1220se to efficiently use the 300W coming from my new Rockford Fosgate PBR300X1. I had been using an old 12" Sony Xplod I had purchased in the mid 2000's. The Infinity is rated at 94 dB of sensitivity compared to the Sony's 87 dB so I hoped I there would be an audible increase in sound output. Knowing that the dB scale is logarithmic every 3 dB increase in sensitivity is the same as doubling the power of the amplifier so going from 87dB to 94 dB should make my amp sound like a 1200W amplifier. I took this with a grain of salt knowing that manufacturers measure specifications a little differently and use tricks to "puff up" their numbers.

I received my Infinity 1220se and couldn't believe the size of the shipping box and immediately thought, "This is ridiculously huge and is going right back to Amazon!" I struggled to remove the 50# behemoth from its sturdy shipping box and quickly squeezed it in the modestly sized trunk of my 2014 Volvo S60 to hook it up. What I heard next was ASTOUNDING!! The Sony struggled to fill my car with bass while the Infinity easily filled my ENTIRE GARAGE with deep, rich, soul stirring bass. The garage door rattled and my dog ran for cover. My friends and I still can't believe that all this bass is created from only 300W. A friend hooked it up to his subwoofer amplifier with the same improvement in sound output and quality. To top it off, despite being ported, it still has tight, accurate bass. Needless to say I'm keeping my new subwoofer!

title: Good board, with a  bit of an issue (for me)
text:
First, the board looks fantastic! Even the (display) box it comes in is very nice. I had originally ordered a [[ASIN:B007G51UV0 ASUS P8Z77-V PRO]] but decided to return it for reasons related to overclocking. The additional features included in the DELUXE edition, despite the substantial increase in cost, are well worth it in my opinion!

For starters, you get Bluetooth connectivity via the WiFi Go! adapter. The cooling design of the board is also much more elaborate and successful at dissipating the heat produced from overclocked systems, as compared to the PRO vesrion. The power regulator on the DELUXE (vs the PRO, for example) is 16+4 vs 12+4, respectively. This helps to distribute and monitor power levels and create a more easily (and stable!) overclocked system.

I am running an Intel Core i5-2390T with a stock core clock of 2.3GHz - 2 cores/4threads - (2.7GHz w/ turbo boost). With the included AI Suite II, there is an automatic overclocking feature. You can select "Fast" or "Extreme", naturally I chose EXTREME.. the system reached a stable core clock of 4017MHz (4.017GHz) with the first run! You CAN go higher (let the auto-tuning attempt higher clock speeds) but I'm running with the stock CPU cooler heat sink so I didn't want to blue screen. For the RAM, I have 16GB of [[ASIN:B008MCZGEI Corsair Vengeance DDR3 Memory]] with a memory speed of 2133MHz in X.P.M. mode. I got the (2)x8GB set to have room for expansion, although I probably will never need more!

My boot device is a [[ASIN:B007R67FTY Kingston HyperX 3K 240 GB Solid State Drive]] setup with the 120GB model running on the ASUS SSD Cache. Boot times are ridiculous. 10 seconds WITHOUT the SSD caching. ASUS claims the boot time will be reduced to up to 40% with a 120GB SSD cache, which puts my boot times around 5-6 seconds!!!

I love this board! Very nice software pack included too. Driver and Utility installation went smoothly, although I did have to wind up re-installing Windows 7 Ultimate because this was a motherboard swap from an HP OEM board.

Hope this helps! Great board, HIGHLY recommend it for an enthusiast or gamer/do-it-yourselfer!

title: Apologies, my last update is mostly venting about costs, nothing bad about Amazon or the seller.
text:
One last update. Sigh... I knew this day would come. While this MSI was great, it's outlived its ability to play the more cinematic games that are available today. Also, it's not VR-capable and the nice folks at Microsoft (I keed, I keed...) are no longer going to support Windows 7. They're also going to charge full price for an update to Windows 10 Pro, and now I believe you must rent or lease or pay a premium fee for the full versions of Office, which is kinda ridiculous. I may keep the thing to harvest its organs, but gaming systems now cost twice the amount I paid for this one, as they've found ways to incorporate full desktop graphics cards into laptops, at the demise of all optical drives, adding extremely loud operating noise from the fans required to keep the system from self-destruction, and again, they've become completely unaffordable for the average user, unless you've won the lottery, or are a spoiled brat whose mother will just whip out the card for, probably spending the child support dad pays to stay out of jail because mom decided she wasn't in love or maybe she likes women now. Anyway, I can't afford $4000 for a 2019 MSI, so I'll have to wait until pricing comes back to Earth. Meanwhile, I'll take comfort in that the executives for Intel, Microsoft, NVIDIA, AMD, Google, MSI, Dell, HP, ASUS, and so many many more will be spending eternity in sulfur baths with saunas that cook their lungs with every breath, while I watch and giggle.
***Update III*** Ok, not to flog a dead horse, but I have now added a 500gb SSD to my system in the second hard drive bay, and now this computer absolutely screams. I now have a 120gb ssd as the primary drive and a 480 gb ssd in the secondary drive bay, for a total of 600gb of ssd goodness. I re-ran the Windows Experience Index and came up with 7.9s across the board so my score is 7.9 and the machine is an absolute monster. Have only played older games up til now (KOTOR, The Witcher I & II, and just began Lord of the Rings Online), and so far, the system is flawless. I am so glad I found a model with Windows 7 installed, everything is familiar to me and runs without a hitch. At this price point, there isn't a better gaming laptop available on the market, period. You simply cannot do better than this beast, no matter how hard you look, and trust me, I looked and looked for months before I committed to dropping $1500 plus on a computer. This thing will serve me well for years to come before technology outpaces me yet again and I need to upgrade yet again. Fortunately, today's newer machinesare much easier to add components to without the need to purchase complete new units. Bottom line: There is no better gaming laptop available at this price, and probably not even at slightly higher prices (at least not at $2000 or less). You should order one of these now if you can afford it and are looking for a blazing fast gamer unit. It just needs a couple of easy upgrades, and you will have a caged monster on your hands!!! Buy this model, from this manufacturer, now!!!

***Update*** This model apparently only has one hard drive bay, I'm not sure about PCIE slots, fingers crossed... I should have asked more questions before I bought it, but I read everything I could find on the internet, and didn't see anything, so I figured all the GT70s had multiple bays/slots. Know this before buying!!

First off, I purchased this amazing machine through a reseller rather than Amazon (they also sell their products on Amazon), because there was an extra incentive (instant rebate on any upgrades performed on the machine) and I wanted a few things that the base model did not offer. Also, buying from a reseller and adding upgrades guaranteed that my new computer would 1) work out of the box, as they had to test it before sending it to me, and 2) they would also make sure there were no blemishes on the casing/chassis or other glaring manufacturer's errors. I added a Blu-Ray RW-drive and an (smallish 120gb, because I was pushing the limits of my bank account as it was, and have USB 3.0 external HDDs lying around that I can use in the meantime) SSD for the OS, so I could get the maximum speed possible with my basic apps/programs. Also, after horror stories about Win8, especially non-touchscreens, I chose this model because it was the only one offering Win7 Home Premium. All I can say so far is WOW! I'm just starting to try out all the features, and I haven't even started gaming with it yet. The 17-inch screen is gorgeous, with the matte anti-glare screen looks great. There have been some complaints in reviews around the 'net about the Steelseries keyboard and the touchpad. I actually like the keyboard, it seems responsive and doesn't miss any strokes (except for those caused by my poor typing skills) and the multicolored programmable backlighting is pretty cool as well. Yes I can see some light bleed from under the front of the keys, but it does not interfere with my typing or view of the keyboard. I also found the touchpad quite responsive and user friendly enough right out of the box, haven't tried to mess with sensitivity yet because it works just fine. The touchpad texture is a bit rough (I'm already getting used to it after 24 hours, and I also love the fact that this MSI series has separate left and right click buttons, unlike most in this price range that I considered during months of agonizing research (it's hard for me to just drop $1500) that have the buttons included as a part of the pad itself). I am used to a more slick tactile feel from my previous laptop (also an MSI, but a low-end Core i-3 model) which I loved, it lasted me over 3 years without a problem, until I spilled a Gatorade into my laptop backpack one night (still cussing myself about that one...). It still worked, after drying completely and cleaning as best I could w/o opening the case, except the trackpad is now wonky and have to use an external Bluetooth mouse. Anyway, suffice it to say I love MSI's products and can't comment on customer service, because I haven't had any problems thus far. I like that they have a two year warranty as opposed to most companies' one year warranties. Anyway, that's all for now, I'll update about issues like heat while gaming as I get to them. Bottom line, most bang for the buck (I even tried Sager/Clevo build-your-owns, and almost went with a Fangbook, but once i added the OS, it was just too expensive, although I would have ended up with a better hard drive configuration) in a gaming laptop, I mean c'mon, it's got a Haswell Core i-7 4700M AND an NVidia GTX 770! Go! Buy this laptop now!

***UPDATE II***

Thanks to an answered question by Xotic PC, apparently there ARE multiple hard drive bays. All is right in the universe again.

title: Doesn't do the one thing it's supposed to do...
text:
I bought this at Best Buy but I want to warn buyers on Amazon.

I travel a lot for business, and I often rent cars and do hundreds of miles a week. I bought this unit and tested it close to home first to see how it performed. The first time out it told me there was construction on the freeway in front of me and advised me to exit to a side street. I was familiar with the freeway I was on and I knew if there was construction where Garmin said there was, then it would already have been stop and go traffic where I was, so I ignored its advice. As predicted, there was no construction and I saved myself a lot of time by ignoring the Garmin and staying on the freeway.

Far from home I plotted in a common restaurant for dinner, I believe it was T.G.I.Fridays. The location was about .25 (1/4) miles from my hotel. The Garmin had me turn out of the hotel onto a freeway going away from the restaurant for 2 miles. Get off the freeway. U-turn back onto the same freeway going the opposite direction for 2 miles, and get off the freeway on the very same street that I had got on the freeway, make a right, and there was the restaurant. In other words, I could have just went over the freeway from my hotel and been at the restaurant in seconds. In fact when I reached the exit ramp after this unnecessary tour, I simply looked over the bridge to the entrance ramp I was on 5 minutes before and not only was it clear and free of any problems, but cars where I had been five minutes ago were coming across the bridge and crossing in front of me. There was NO reason to have gone that route.

I adapted to my Garmin and simply got used to questioning where it was taking me. It got to the point where I would talk to the Garmin every morning to amuse myself, chiding it, "Cmooooon Garmin....how we gettin' there today? I know you got an EXTRA special route for me!" To avoid the Garmin's useless instructions I would touch the screen and zoom out so I could see most or all of the route it had plotted. I would note the directions I was going to avoid, which most of the time was an instruction to get off the freeway and take side streets parallel to the freeway for 5+ miles, then get back on the same freeway.

To that end, at least twice, the Garmin would tell me to exit, which I would do...and realize I was going parallel with the freeway I just exited, but at half the speed of course. Only to be told to get back on several miles, and several traffic lights, down the street. One time I decided to turn around, ignore Garmin, get back on where it told me to get off, and just go to see maybe there was some traffic or congestion or something...but both times...nothing. The freeway was wide open and there was no reason I should have gotten off the freeway.

OTHER ISSUES

When it detected that traffic had slowed, I would say it was accurate that traffic had slowed, however, I would say it was not accurate in detecting slow traffic. In other words, when it said there was, there was, but more often than it detected it, I would encounter slow traffic, and it didn't know about it. On two occasions the lane assist told me to exit to the left, but the exit was actually on the right. It seems to avoid U-turns...it would rather make you take a left, left, left or a right, right, right, even if the fastest correction is simply a u-turn. I know this because I would see what it was doing and just turn around and the "time to arrival" would suddenly drop when it recalculated. One direction was so bad that it showed me driving "off-road" because a newer cloverleaf ramp had been built it didn't know about and YES, before I left for my travels I installed the LATEST map updates - so Garmin loses this one too.

So as far as I'm concerned, this Garmin is garbage. If it can't plot a course without making me take side streets for no good reason, then what the hell good is it? I am going to try and return it and try a different brand. Bummer too, because I used to have a Garmin Nuvi 760 and aside from the garbage charger cable, it was accurate in plotting courses. Too bad. Now I'm motivated to try Tom Tom or whatever else there is out there.

title: Horrible weather radio
text:
I got this a few years ago. Mine is orange and I think was purchased at Target. As far as the quality of the weather radio, it is pretty decent. It feels sturdy and picks up weather bands clearly. The alarm also is loud and definitely will wake you up.

My only (but serious) complaint about this weather radio has to do with the alarm functionality. The alarm is very, very loud, like jump out of your bed anticipating an aerial bombing. You can turn this down after it has gone off but as soon as the alarm sounds again, it automatically boosts the volume to full. Also, if you are awake and are actively listening to the warning broadcast, about every couple minutes it will boost the volume to full as the alarm sounds on the radio so that the announcement is very loud. Of course you turn it down again but it boosts back up within a couple minutes.

How this plays out is that the alarm goes off warning me about a thunderstorm or flash flood warning in an ajacent county. I turn down the volume and turn it off again figuring it will warn me again if it escalates to something like a tornado warning. Several minutes later it has boosted the alarm all the way up and goes off again for the same exact warning in the same adjacent county. I decide to leave it on and just listen to hear if things change. As soon as the alarm goes off again, it boosts the audio and sounds the alarm loud again. It feels like I'm constantly holding it in my hand and constantly turning the volume down. Frustrated, I just turn it off completely and stay awake watching the news instead or go to sleep hoping conditions won't change.

This alarm is good for the initial warning IF you can remember to turn it on before you go to sleep. As you'll be turning it off everytime there is a warning, it's obvious that you will forget to turn it back on and so I consider this weather radio to be just about useless.

title: First USB WIFI dual band I got. Better than I thought.
text:
I usually get PCI/PCI-e wireless adapters, media bridges, or play around with DD-WRT. I also still use an old, but reliable PCI WMP300N (for 20 dollars plus free 3 antenna booster that I can stick on my wall above my desk, can't beat that, but this was 3 years ago).

Well, I needed a quick solution to get my cousin's computer on my wireless without having to worry about buying another router and load up DD-WRT. I did some comparing between USB vs PCI/PCI-e network cards and since USB 2.0 runs at 480Mbps, having a USB wifi adapter that runs at 300Mbps (8Mbit = 1MByte for those that don't know, so 480Mbps = 60MBps). Also being dual band, even more reason I wanted to get it.

My cousin's system and mine both run Windows 7 Pro 64-bit. Set up was easy. Plugged in the USB extension cable (which is only like 4-5inches long, but it was a flex cable so I could point the USB dongle upward, instead of having it just sit horizontal out of the back of the system. After that, plugged in the USB dongle, ran the set up disc, and was able to navigate easily through the utility. You can also use the Windows 7 default Wireless settings to use the adapter. Once you get on, go to the ASUS website and download the latest utility and drivers. The utility was easy, and I actually like it better.

Set up the computer for the 5GHz band and it was set, got full 300Mbps, sometimes drops down to 243Mbps minimal. Also that computer was the only one in the area that had the 5GHz set up, so no congestion.

This was an easy and quick set up, also being USB it's great for when family or friends visit and want to set them up with something quickly and easily. Also great as a spare in case your own wireless goes out in the computer.

I highly recommend this product.
- CCNA, Security +, and A + certified.

UPDATE 2/7/2012: Just ordered another one for my computer. Went from 130Mbps on the 2.4GHz band from my PCI wifi card to 240-300Mbps on the 5GHz band with just plugged the USB adapter into the back of my computer. Not even using the cable that came with it. Also picked up the N56 Diamond Router from ASUS, will update after setting it up. Changing out my e3000 for the N56.

UPDATE 8/12/2012: My Cisco e3000 finally starting getting buggy and the wireless was becoming more unstable. Switched it for the ASUS N56 Diamond Router and it works a LOT better. No drops in speed or connection. Had it set up and upgraded to the latest firmware. After about a month of fiddling and letting it run since the initial set up, it works a lot better than the e3000. ASUS finally has a firmware that works with no issues. It pairs nicely with the USB-N53 wireless adapter.

title: No bubbles BUT lost sensitivity
text:
I purchased this protector due to the overwhelming positive reports from other verified buyers. I do not like my cell phone's screen being unprotected and now with my first Kindle I feel the same way. The HDX screen is gorgeous and I want a way to keep it as such. This screen protector seemed the answer to my predicament.

This protector is, indeed, extremely simple to 'install'. It takes more time to remove it from its packaging and throw the trash away afterwards than it does to apply the protector itself. Simply line up the cutouts on the protector film with the camera and flash at the top and center of your Kindle and you are done. I found it helpful to guide the film into place by kind of rolling the sides down, guiding them to ensure proper placement. Then just apply a little pressure (basically, run your hand around the edges) to activate the adhesive.

Only the outer black margin of the protector has adhesive to stick it to the border and outer edges of your Kindle, thus leaving the clear center which covers your Kindle's screen loose, or non-sticky. This manufacturing and design approach has both pros and one con I have noticed so far.

Pros:

It allows for lightning fast and super easy installation.

Because of the solid black border, you can accidentally touch the sticky side while installing and lining it up without any fingerprints showing through as with a normal screen protector. This was a bonus to me as these things are always so difficult to install without this happening.

The clear center portion that covers the screen is completely 100% bubble free.

Due to some micro hairs/fibers being on the screen despite having wiped it down prior to installing the protector, I learned that I could remove the protector (lifted up one corner and peeled it halfway back to do a quick swipe with the MF cloth again) and it would re-adhere to the Kindle's surface just as well as it did the first time.

The company claims that, if it should lose its stickiness, the protector can be rinsed/washed and used again. I have yet to need to go this far so I cannot comment on the credit-worthiness of this claim, however from my experiences so far, I can see the possibility of this claim holding up.

I have not noticed any blurring or the rainbow affect the company mentions on its packaging. The screen is crystal clear and appears to not even have a screen protector on it.

Con:

Since the clear center portion does not adhere to the screen, it is allowed to float just above the screen thus reducing the screen sensitivity and requiring more force from either your fingertip or your stylus.

After using my Kindle for a few hours after installation of this screen protector, I have come to the above conclusions. As bad as the con is for me and my preferences, I will leave it on for a few days to give myself a little more time and to see if anything changes. This screen protector ranks very high on my list of desirable protectors (I even searched to see if they make a version for my Droid cell phone) so I am really hoping that the sensitivity issue works itself out soon.

I've been really pleased with this insert. It fits perfectly in a 12.2" x 11.4" x 4.3" messenger bag, transforming the bag into a fully functioning camera bag, as advertised.

I was pleased by how modular it is. The dividers are movable and attach via velcro anywhere on the bag's interior. The drawstrings allow you to cinch the insert closed in a nicely compact package.

Although the insert is very modestly sized, I can fit my DSLR (T3i) with battery grip, two M42 primes and assorted accessories (ND filter, lens adapter, quick-release plate, SD cards, etc.) with room to spare for another lens. Highly recommend.

title: Boom... There goes the dynamite
text:
Okay let me start off saying that like most I was sitting on the fence between 4 differant projectors for the last month. I thought and pondered and then thought some more, I frequented Projector central and amazon obsessively during this time.

I have a light controled environment from my previous projector so Based on the info about the epson 3010 and reviews saying it is just too bright in a cave and others costing more then double these two models prices I wound Up taking a gamble and decided I will try my first DLP unit. I ordered two pairs of the OPTOMA RF GLASSES and set this bad boy up.

Upon getting everything setup and without having fine tuned anything I turned it on and immediately began testing the unit with various 2d and 3d material via blu ray disc...I must say I cannot believe what I have witnessed and at this price point.. I was skeptical.. Not anymore...

I started off with despicable me 3d...Umm amazing...Then tron 3d.. Some scenes will possess you when the 3d is in full effect..Which is funny because I was hardly impressed with tron on my plasma...Then open season, and once again I am impressed..I cannot wait until my free copy of AVATAR gets here......

Now I Grab some good old anime..Yeah dont judge...I am an anime Nerd... Akira and neon genesis blurays totally got me back in the anime watching mode and looked fabulous..

Then I decided to make sure my WIFI was connected from the basement and tested out netflix.. The HD content usually looks close to a bluray or HDTV broadcast on my 50" plasma and although it was still pretty good it was more along the lines of 720p or 1080i at best. There just wasnt as much pop..but then again I just got done testing out some high end material previously so I was probably a bit spoiled at this point..

thank god my universal mount is an extended one and has 4 points of articulation because this would have been impossible for me to setup otherwise as it has a odd throw angle. to have a nice 120" screen size you need about 14' distance from the screen. the projector lense needs to be about 8-10 inches higher then the top edge of the screen as well as being level with no upward or downward tilt to avoid having to use keystone.I managed to get this done far easier then what I had worried about for over a month of trying to decide.. I have a weird ceiling and my cold air return for the central air happens to be lower then the celing and is between where the projector and screen are. I simply had to lower my screen some more and articulate the mount a certain way and Bingo I found the sweet spot..

Long story short, I am now in ecstacy and I think im currently having what one could only describe as a Nerd-Gasm... my brain is about to burst with excitement...Do yourself a favor and get off the fence, get this thing if your going to have some light control such as blackout curtains etc. Or if ambient light is an issue regardless then look at the epson 3010. I can vouch for the HD33 and this thing is fantastic...

In the last few days I have watched many more 3d movies, I also hooked my 360 up..

I just watched transformers dark of the moon 3d and I thought it was much better at home then in the theatre, at the movies I only noticed a few scenes with any good 3d depth, on bluray however it was pretty insane sometimes and the 3d depth was consistant from beginning to end.

Today I watched a very Harold and Kumar christmas, and This movie is now the new movie I base all my future opinions of 3d bluray on. The effects were insane, The movie benefits greatly from the 3d and it really just makes ya laugh..keep the kids far away from this one though.. Still waiting for avatar to arrive, mailed out for it about 3 weeks ago..

Then I hooked up my xbox 360 and played a multitude of my vertical scrolling arcade shooters, then castle crashers and then Halo Reach, This is a new 360 and I never played Halo reach.. I had boycotted microsoft 360 the last few years cause I had way too many units die on me.. I am glad to be back and very glad to report having no issues with Lag.

title: GPX CC312B Clock Radio with CD Review
text: Looks good. Fewer buttons than most. But there is always a catch.  Ah, if it only worked as described.  The instructions (obviously translated from Chinese to English) are missing steps and therefore you cannot complete some functions.  You go as far as you can with the instructions then you're on your own.  Try this, try that, find what combinations work and then hope you remember the sequence that worked.  It's maddening. When you're lucky enough to set the alarm to the radio, you cannot set the volume so when the alarm time is reached, the radio or CD or buzzer turns on and quickly and automatically increases the volume to wall shattering levels.  Speaker quality is not good.  And, oh yes, this bit of info:  There are two models of this, both showing the same model number, however, one model has an output plug-in, radio tuning wheel and AM/FM switch on the left (it's left).  The other has the output plug-in and USB port on its left side.  No tuner or selection switch.  Other buttons perform those tasks. To learn about the warranty you must go to a website provided in the Owners Guide.  If it had a correct guide for setup and better speaker sound this would be okay for the price. If you can figure out the setups it's worth keeping.  The jury is still out on how long it will last.  I have had mine for just ten days.  If you have my model (USB port on lefthand side) do this in setting the alarm: Follow steps 1 through 7 under "setting alarm", after choosing your choice of wakeup PRESS THE AL1 BUTTON.  In step seven is states to "use the VOL +/- to adjust alarm (NO, this won't work and screws up the original setup).  The fact that the wakeup volumn automatically increases to an awful level and therefore makes waking up unpleasant, this unit is being returned.  Shame because that one auto volumn feature makes makes the alarm way too stressfull.

title: Raystorm 750 AX240 is versitile
text:
Being a hobbyist system builder, I build several systems for my gaming family every so often (~5 years). This past year I built systems with closed-loop cooling solutions and decided I'd branch out and try something new and potentially stronger for my FX 9350 processor. I swapped this in for the Corsair H100 that I was using and noticed ~4-6 degrees difference idle and a whopping 12-16 degrees difference under load. As the 9350 is a HOT processor, to begin with, this was huge in my book and alleviated a lot of concern I had for the peripheral heat-related damage to VCore-1 (I plan on adding this to the cooling loop(s), in the future).

This thing was easy to install and convert for AM3+, using the provided pieces. I have a cramped tower with two video cards (using Crossfire). So, having the ability to mount the radiator/fans outside of the case was a welcomed change, as with the closed-loop solutions you cannot accomplish this without welding/cutting the case.

The CPU block they provided is a stellar block and I did a lot of research before purchasing this kit. Most reviews for this CPU block were very good.

The only reason I didn't put this at 5 stars, is that the pump may not be strong enough to support inclusion of an additional radiator and putting blocks on the video cards and motherboard components. It is a kit, after all.

Over all, I'd say this kit was priced much lower than its value. It was a great deal and provided a good start/introduction to a water cooling novice. I'm hooked, now!

title: Excellent Sound and Comfort without Comparison
text:
Thank you to KimBongUn420 for his outstanding review of the H6. My experience is fully aligned with his review.

Everyone should decide what is most important to them in selecting an expensive headphone like the H6. We all have different tastes, and I would strongly recommend that any potential buyer listen to any headphone they expect to purchase.

I listened to at least 20 headphones using my Sony Xperia as a source, and I was surprised by the results. Headphones that had received great reviews disappointed me, and I realized that two things were important to me: Comfort of an over-the-ear headphone and balanced sound quality with depth. I wanted an alternative to my amazing Ultimate Ear earbud phones to an over-the-ear headphone that would be easier on my ears and project a more deep and balanced sound stage.

The B&O H6 beat every other major, well-reviewed headphone that I tried. And I was lucky, because for my taste, they were the most comfortable over-the-ear headphones I tried, and they had the most balanced sound, with a strong but delicate and nuanced, soundstage. I've listened to them for hours now, and my initial assessment has been completely confirmed. I can hear new entrancing details that I never heard in my Ultimate Ear phones. There is depth and subtlety that I missed before.

Like many others, I am rebelling against the McDonald's sound quality that comes with normal iTunes, good smartphones and mid-level earphones. This is what I have learned.

There are four important factors in good sound, listed in my priority: 1) High quality headphones or earbuds; 2) Superior music file format; 3) A quality DAC (Digital to Analog Converter); and; 4) Amplifier capacity to drive headphones with purity and minimal distortion.

There are many new high-resolution sound files, and I'm no expert on the pros and cons of each. However, I am convinced that there is much better sound quality on a CD than on an MP3 file, which is what most of us listen to if we use iTunes or other digital file transfer systems. So, I think the second most important factor in high-quality mobile sound is the source, which should not be a standard MP3 file. The most common alternative file is flac, which you can read about here: http://bn2.pictureview.com/2014-11-21/1459/3608298/Spunkd%203%20-%20Clip14.avi

Here's a good article on where to find high quality music downloads: http://www.forbes.com/sites/ianmorris/2014/10/28/tidal-lossless-music-streaming-review-forget-spotify-get-cd-quality-music/

I am leaving my MP3 library and moving to a flac and alac library, but this will take time. Even with these advanced file formats, we will still have less detailed analog quality than we had with our old 33 lps--but that's another topic.

Every smartphone has a DAC built into it so that we can connect any headphone and hear an analog version of the digital music stored on the phone (or computer). However, the quality of smartphone DACs is low, so they usually produce muddy, un-nuanced, and sometimes compressed sound. A good headphone will make the best of a smartphone's analog signal, but it cannot change the source.

To address both the third and forth factors mentioned above, I purchased a Fiio E17 DAC and headphone amplifier, which cost about $140. This has been one of the best purchases I have made to enhance my mobile sound experience. When configured properly, this high-quality DAC will replace the McDonald's DAC in most smartphones and deliver superior analog sound to your headphones. I'm still learning how to best obtain a clean digital input from my Sony Xperia to best utilize Fiio's DAC, but I think this has great potential. As an amplifier, the E17 is fantastic. It allows you to listen to music at a higher sound level without straining the basic amplifier in smartphones. This leads to clearer and richer sound regardless of the better DAC advantage.

To conclude, if you want superior mobile sound, spend your money on great headphones or earbuds. If you want a more natural, speaker like sound, go with a headphone. If you have really high standards, get rid of your MP3 files, and consider buying an external amplifier and DAC such as the Fiio E17.

Thanks to so many reviewers who helped me understand the basics summarized above.

Great music to all!

title: A brilliant lens, though not always the best choice
text:
This is the best telephoto zoom in this class by any manufacturer for any mount. I'm going to focus on why that is and why you might opt for something else.

NUMBERS:

Canon 70-200/2.8L IS II ($2150)
* 3.5" x 7.8" (hood adds 3.5" in length)
* 52.4 oz (3.25 lbs)
* 77mm filters
* 4' closest focus
* 4-stop IS
* Weather-sealed w/ front filter
* 1-year warranty to anyone with the purchase receipt

Canon 70-200/2.8L IS I ($1300 used)
* 3.4" x 7.8" (hood adds 3.5" in length)
* 51.9 oz (3.2 lbs)
* 77mm filters
* 4.6' closest focus
* 3-stop IS
* Weather-sealed w/ front filter
* No warranty, but parts available

Sigma 70-200/2.8 OS ($1250)
* 3.4" x 7.8" (hood adds 4" in length)
* 50.4 oz (3.15 lbs)
* 77mm filters
* 4.6' closest focus
* 4-stop IS
* No weather sealing
* 4-year warranty to anyone with the purchase receipt

Tamron 70-200/2.8 VC ($1500)
* 3.5" x 7.8" (hood adds 3.5" in length)
* 51.7 oz (3.2 lbs)
* 77mm filters
* 4.3' closest focus
* 4-stop IS
* "Moisture Resistant" construction
* 6-year warranty for original purchaser only

They're all about the same size and weight. The two Canons are white, the others black. The Canon II and the Tamron are sharper than the other two. All four are usable at f/2.8. All four have maximum magnification at infinity and lose some range, significantly, with closer objects. The effective maximum focal drops as low as 135mm. The Tamron is actually 70-185mm even at infinity.

Autofocus is superior on the Canon II, excellent on the Canon I, and somewhat slower with the other two. The difference will be most apparent tracking fast objects and in low light. The Canon I and Sigma are mostly parfocal (maintains focus with zooming). The other two aren't. This is mostly of consequence for shooting movies.

While the Tamron has a panning mode for VC, it's automatic. The other three lenses have a manual switch detent for panning. On a tripod, you'll want a strong ball or gimbal head and a lens collar. All four lenses include a collar new, though used copies of the Canon I may not have it. The stabilization systems in all but the Canon I can detect tripods (in theory). Exposures longer than 1/4 of a second on a sturdy tripod will be sharper with that feature disabled no matter the lens.

For a comparison in bulk, almost all of the f/4 and f/4-f/5.6 lenses (e.g., Canon 70-200/4L IS, Tamron 70-300/4-5.6 VC, Canon 70-300/4-5.6 IS) are half the weight and an inch or two shorter.

OPTICS:

Almost unimpeachable. Sharpness is high across the frame for the entire range from f/2.8 to f/16. Distortion is minimal. Chromatic aberration is minimal. Bokeh is circular and smooth.

Sharpness hold up well with a 1.4X teleconverter, better than the other three lenses. It's also uniquely suited to a 2.0X, though Canon's 100-400/4.5-5.6L is faster to focus and slightly sharper.

The only significant weakness: flare. Despite modern lens coatings, you can still provoke loss of contrast and ghosting with the sun in the frame. All four zooms suffer from this, as do Canon's 135/2 and 200/2.8.

WHY BUY IT:

* You like this range and you need f/2.8 over f/4 for subject isolation or low light.
* You intend to use the lens with teleconverters often.
* You intend to use the lens in the rain.
* You need the fastest focusing performance available for sports or otherwise.
* You print very large or crop significantly such as to require maximum pixel-level sharpness.
* You may resell the lens in the future and want to recoup the largest percentage of your investment.

WHY BUY A DIFFERENT 70-200/2.8:

* You're willing to sacrifice the last 15% of performance in focusing speed, sharpness, and general ability to save 40% or more at the register, of which you'll recoup somewhat less at resale.
* You don't like white lenses.
* You're shooting in high-shutter scenarios (e.g., sports) that don't merit stabilization and the associated cost. The original 70-200/2.8L non-IS delivers similar results for half the price.
* You value the longer warranties of Sigma and Tamron lenses.

WHY BUY THE 70-200/4L IS:

* You want the same optical virtues in a smaller, lighter package at less than half the price.
* You don't care as much about subject isolation or you have other lenses to achieve this purpose.
* You're willing to use ISO 3200 or higher in low-light or high-shutter scenes.

WHY BUY PRIMES:

Because all of the 70-200/2.8 lenses are large, heavy, and obvious. Some uses profit from alternatives:

* Traveling. It's over three pounds, a burden for hiking and a theft target.
* Shy subjects. If your plan is to party with friends and take a few pictures, this lens is liable to intimidate a few of them.
* Venues with high security. It's fun to take pictures from the stands at sporting events, but security is often told to exclude any kit with a white body.
* Situations that require maximum subject isolation or high shutter speeds in low light.

Canon's primes in this range are all optical peers with this 70-200. If you're shooting with a recent full-frame body, the noise performance is adequate to forgo IS even with lenses like the 200/2.8L. It may be, particularly indoors, that an unobtrusive 85/1.8 generates better shots.

WHERE TO BUY:

If new, here. Amazon has the best price, no tax in most states, and a liberal exchange policy that covers shipping both ways. It's possible to receive an underperforming copy of any lens at any price, perhaps just because the box was abused in transit. The major NY stores like BH Photo and Adorama will make you eat the cost of return shipping, which is nontrivial for a lens of this weight and cost. There's no risk of that with Amazon.

If you're price-sensitive and willing to wait, buy direct from Canon's refurbished store. Refurbished lenses are indistinguishable from new and come with all accessories, though only a 90-day warranty instead of a full year. Canon periodically offers 20% off sales that bring the price to around $1700. You can set a Deal Alert on Slickdeals to email you when one occurs.

IN SUM:

The 70-200/2.8L II is a superb and tremendously versatile lens. You pay for that brilliance in cost, size, and weight. Consider whether you're actually willing to pull the thing out on a whim. Professional shooters won't blink twice, but speaking as a largely recreational photographer, I often choose less onerous alternatives.

title: A lot in a very small package
text:
I didn't know what to expect when I ordered this projector, I guess somewhere in my mind I thought about big, heavy, office style huge DLP machines with lots of cables.
I was therefore taken aback when the outer package containing everything arrived measuring just over 4" x 7"
Inside, a small white box about the size of two cigarette packets side by side, and a ROKU USB stick, that looked almost as big as the unit.

Setup = simple
Plug in the ROKU stick
Turn it on
Point it at a blank light colored wall
Tweak the focus wheel
Turn up the volume [I'll come back to that]

After it's warmed up, it looks for your wireless network, asks for passwords and so on to connect to the internet, and then you must activate it from your PC.
If you have a ROKU account fine, if not it's a simple online registration (you will need a credit card on file although no purchases are necessary)
Punch in the code from the screen (your wall) into your PC and you're done.
Straight off it asks you if you want all the free stuff activated, I said yes, Netflix, Amazon Prime, Hulu, Pandora, Facebook, Disney etc. etc.
Later you can link your Netflix and Amazon accounts if you have them with passwords and so on for instant access.

Remember I said I would come back to sound? Well it has an integral speaker, it's OK but small, and you won't hear much, headphones or external speakers via a standard 3.5mm jack work fine.
Picture is great, and depends on what you are watching of course for quality and resolution.
It's worth mentioning at this point that you can forget VUDU - you need a higher level ROKU box with HDX compatibility, it didn't even show up on my list, even after I checked it on the free page.

PROS
Completely portable, and only confined by the range of the wireless network it's using, it's also rechargeable if you have no outlet - the battery will run for about two hours, good for most movies
There's a ton of free TV and movies, or use your existing accounts, simple
Did I say it was small already?
Will show up to 120" wide with clarity
So far Iron Man 2, Rango, and TV show Flashpoint look great on a standard wall.

CONS
Remote feels small and fiddly
Focus wheel is tiny, and needs adjustment between different things, for example when I went from Netflix to Amazon, I had to adjust, even though the projector hadn't moved.
It's very small, and although that's also a plus, you will need to prop it on a box for required viewing height, not a big negative, just a fact. It does however have a standard screw hole underneath that will attache to most tripods.
A little pricey

Now you don't have to take a movie to your friends, take the whole package! Pick a big flat light colored surface and fire it up! - Jeez, if it's warm, sit outside and watch it on the side of the house or the garage door if you want!
It seems technology is getting smaller everywhere, will products like this put an end to giant flat screen TV's? I doubt it just yet, but this is so nice to take to any room in your house with a blank wall and watch your favorite shows and movies - it has to be 5 stars

title: Full of bugs, does not function properly at all
text:
If you are considering buying this product I strongly suggest you either reconsider or at least wait until the unacceptable amount of bugs and lacking features are fixed. From just using this product a couple of days it is already clear to me that it was not adequately tested before release. Here are the specific problems:

*This device doesn't work at all as an MP3 player as it is advertised to do. Adding music directly through USB and copying to the SD card does not work, even though the manual says this is possible. I tried adding albums to it using Sony's (almost useless) Media Go program and it shows all the songs and albums as being on the SD card (filling up about half of a 16GB SD card) but it takes a VERY LONG TIME to load into the music select menu.

*Once the device does finally get to the music select screen, you can only play the first song of any artist or album and then it stops dead. The skip next button just pauses that one song when you try pressing it. The only way to see the other songs is to scroll through the entire list of unsorted songs, which is of course a ridiculous way to play or categorise music, and then once it reaches the first song listed and you try to scroll backwards, the device resets itself!

*You are unable to create any playlists for the device, so it's a bit pointless even listing it in the menu.

*In addition, the Android Bluetooth (BT) call features hardly ever work. Even if it's paired with my Samsung Galaxy Note phone through BT and a call comes in, I can hear the call ringing and despite pressing the black button as the instructions say, nothing happens at all and I need to take the call on the phone instead. Using it with Viber to try to call, it cuts in and out in the middle of the call, switching between the phone's speaker and no sound at all. I had the MW600 before this product and at least that was able to do basic music playback with correct artist/song information (which this device does not do at all) and the bluetooth functions of the MW600 worked (which they don't on this piece of junk).

*If that wasn't enough, the text to speech function is sporadic in its operation at best, mostly non-functioning the majority of the time, for both gmail and text messages, even after installing the required apps from the Play market.

*The FM radio function is really a joke. You can't store any preset stations and then each time you start it up it always begins from 00.0mhz every time, not even remembering which frequency you used last time.

*How can this be called a "premium" device when it doesn't even support basic .mp3 playback, let alone common lossless filetypes like .flac?

*When I first turned the product on and paired it with my phone it said it was updating. Then when I looked up the Sony support website it shows a .bin update file with instructions to update. Is this the same update? I tried installing it exactly as the instructions said and there was absolutely no response from the device as to whether it updated or not. It is ridiculous to assume that posting an update file without a date or version number on a website will be of any use to users because how can we possibly determine which file is required? Regardless, no updates or firmware revisions have fixed any of the issues I have mentioned so far in this review.

I paid a lot of money for this device (especially compared to cheaper but similar products from other brands) because of the advertised premium features it should have come with and because I thought Sony was a reputable brand and I expect it at least to do the basic functions that it is claimed to. I assumed that perhaps it was just me that had a faulty device but after reading reviews on other sites as well as this I have found that it is the device itself which is seriously flawed.

For a brand that supposedly prides itself on high quality products, this is totally unacceptable from Sony.

title: Awesome bargain phone; or simply use as a music player/wifi web-surfer/GPS.  For the price, can't go wrong!
text:
For $30, what a great bargain! I have to caveat, however, that I'm only using this as a portable wifi device/MP3 player, not as an actual phone. Thus, my review only covers the functionality of the device except for the phone function, and of course, is my subjective, non-expert opinion.

Cosmetically, it is a simple yet elegant design. The back cover (black) has a matte finish that has a nice texture and keeps the device from slipping out of your hands. The smooth back cover is only interrupted by the camera lens, and engraved Nokia logo, speaker hole, and subtle ATT logo. The front is also simple, with only the earpiece speaker and Nokia logo at top (flanked by some sensors, which you cannot really see) and the capacitive touch buttons on the bottom bezel. The glass is smooth, but as one reviewer noted, the surface of the screen has a sort of "stickiness" to it. Hard to describe, but it almost feels like extremely fine sandpaper (like 5000 grit or higher). Nothing that's uncomfortable or detracts from the functionality of the screen, and as I've been using it more and more, that "stickiness" seems to be gone. One other thing with the screen, where the glass ends to meet the plastic framing of the phone, it is elevated ever so slightly from the glass surface, interrupting what would otherwise be a completely smooth/flush face of the phone. Again, nothing big or uncomfortable, but a completely flush front face would add more class. Overall, this phone has a simple elegance to it that makes it look/feel like a much more expensive phone, and is very comfortable to hold.

Physical functionality, this phone works as well as many higher end phones. The screen is vibrant and very responsive to touches/swipes, and despite the sub-HD resolution, everything looks pleasant. For me, texts are easy to read, and images look sharp. I'm sure the smaller size of the screen (4" diagonal) helps in this regard. The "soft buttons" work well and are simple and intuitive. All the physical buttons are on the right side of the phone (if looking at the face of the phone); of note, the volume rocker is at the top, the power button below that, and the camera button (very handy!) is below that. I note this because in my experience, the power button is usually the top most button, with the volume rocker below that. Also, having a physical camera button is something not found on many smartphones, but I find is very handy to have and makes snapping pictures easier. Also, pressing the camera button from the home screen automatically opens the camera, so you don't have to look/find your camera app to activate the camera. The speaker is reasonably loud, and sounds typical of "any given smartphone." The camera shoots decent shots on par with many smartphones, but like most smartphone cameras, works best in well lit situations with a stationary subject. Low light shots are only OK to bad at best, and expect moving subjects to be blurry when the picture is taken. Also, there is no flash or front facing camera, so no selfies or video chats like Skype (though oddly, you can download a flashlight app and Skype is pre-loaded). 4 out of 5 for this category, with the main detractors being lack of front camera and flash for rear camera, but for the price ($30) this is an outstanding piece of kit.

In terms of performance, I am highly impressed particularly because of this price point. Despite only having 512MB RAM (I prefer a minimum of 1GB) and "only" a dual core processor, it is extremely fluid in operation. Comparatively speaking, I'd put it slightly above my old Galaxy S2, which was a flagship phone back in it's day. Compared to other equivalent Android phones (like an LG Lucid VS840, which has similar specs) I'd give this phone the win (at least for operation). Out of the box, this came with Windows 8, which I promptly updated via Over the Air update to Windows 8.1. I primarily use Android OS, followed by iOS, and comparatively speaking, my opinion is that Win 8.1 is every bit as good as either OS. The interface is intuitive, and I like the tile setup on the home page. I particularly like how the "live tiles" provide updates and realtime information, like widgets do in Android OS. Swipes and transitions are very smooth, better than many Android phones, particularly those that have carrier or manufacturer skins overlaid, like Samsung and transition smoothness is near if not on par with iOS -- actually, the smoothness reminds me much of iOS. Animations occur without lag or stutter. Wifi works great; connected without a problem and have surfed the web and downloaded a few apps already. Speaking of apps, the Microsoft store is still barren compared to iTunes App Store or Google Play. However, the really popular apps all seem to be available. Overall, this phone impresses (at least me) with how smoothly everything runs, particularly because of it's "lower end" hardware specs. Honestly, I'd say the user interface experience is as fluid as the most high powered Android phones, and on par with the industry "standard", iOS, and as intuitive as either.

Overall, this device, for the price, is easily on par with other phones costing much, much more. For those looking for an inexpensive device that works well, is intuitive to use, and meets what most might consider basic functionality, this is a deal that must seriously be considered. Only power hogs, gamers, fanboys, and the selfie addicted would turn their nose to this device. Regular people, however, would find this to be a great device at a bargain.

UPDATE: 10 days later...
I continue to be amazed with this little device. I'm still only using it as a portable wifi device, but have had an opportunity to use it extensively as a GPS unit as well using the HERE DRIVE+ app that comes loaded on the system. I have to say....it works great, particularly because you can use it offline (i.e. without a wifi or mobile data connection). You have to take some time to download maps up front, and one big gripe is that the maps are stored on the phone's internal memory--at least I haven't been able to move it to the SD card. Thus, you can't download all the maps for all 50 states in the US as it exceeds the total remaining phone storage left. You have to be selective in what maps you download, but that's fine as most won't be travelling through every state all the time. And, as a GPS, this thing works like a charm! Directions have been spot on and timely (no "Turn Now" as you're passing the turn), however, if using offline, you can't get real-time traffic updates. But otherwise, this works as well as my dedicated Garmin GPS unit.

Also, I have to comment on the versatility of this device as an MP3 player/walkman. First, the MUSIC MIX app that came loaded on the phone. It's a free music streaming app let's you stream via wifi or data, but the real win is that you can also download playlists to listen to offline! It's awesome; certainly a good alternative to streaming music if there's no available wifi and/or if you don't want to burn up your data plan if you've activated the phone. Also, this device has a built in FM radio (needs headphones though, to use as the antenna) which is nice and works great...not even my Nexus 6 has a built in FM tuner. The radio is another way to get music or your favorite station without wifi or burning up your data plan. And because of it's small size, this device is easy to bring along while working out or running.

I've also downloaded some games as well. Unfortunately, diversity of games in the Microsoft store is much less than iTunes or Google Play, and even then, some games won't play (or load) because the phone doesn't have enough RAM, storage space, or both, to play. That said, games like Angry Birds Star Wars and Hill Climber play just as well as they do on other devices. I did notice that when playing Angry Birds, the back of the phone got pretty warm. However, all of my Android phones get warm if not hot playing Angry Birds as well. Bottomline is that while this device can play games, don't expect too much out of it.

The additional time with this phone has made me like it even more. Seriously, I can't believe this only cost $30!!

UPDATE 1 YEAR LATER: Wow, 1 year later and I'm still impressed by this little device. Still only using it as my MP3/wifi device, but I've also used it as a GPS unit as well; the HERE app is so good, I use it now on my Android devices for off-line GPS capability! I've also been using it paired to a set of bluetooth headphones and it's a great combo for working out. Still can't believe I got this for $30 when it does just as well as an iPod Touch costing hundreds more!

*EDIT February 4th 2013*

I had a request to add some pictures today, so after I added them I figured I would go ahead and post an update since I have had this almost a year. I am still very satisfied with this CB. I have had no issues with it at all, and still pick up people loud and clear. I will say that if someone is serious about using it all the time I would invest in a better MIC though, this one is a bit lacking, and it feels "chincy", but for me it works well enough. I bought this mostly for when I travel 8 hours to visit my parents. Listening to truckers yammer on the highway is more entertaining at times than any radio station.

There is no static from the knobs while turning between stations, nor any "pops", it is very quiet. It picks up quick enough to where you can "roll through" the channels and it will still send out the audio when someone is on the channel.

All in all, if I could do it over I would still pick this unit, I like the size, the lack of chrome, and the simplicity.

title: Fabulous and awesome...
text:
I have had many sets of headphones over the years. Recently I have had Bose noise canceling, Bowers and Wilkins in the ear and also the B&W P7 Headphones. I have a set of Sennheiser wireless HD170 which sound good but I wanted more out of headphones, something that would come close to sounding like my Home Theater System when I don't want to wake up the entire neighborhood. I am a very critical listener and to give you some idea of what I mean, in my car I recently purchased it had a Beats 10 speaker system which sounded OK but was anemic in the subwoofer area. So I put in a pair of J&L subwoofers powered by their 1000 Watt subwoofer only amp. The Beats were great on mid and bass and the J&L gave it what it needed, in fact too much that I am only using the amp at 1/4 of its setting. So I decided to once more buy a set of Headphones which at the time were a set of surround sound TurtleBeach 350's. They sounded so bad and even with their software which had equalizer settings, filters etc, the sound just could not be improved. So that brings me finally to the Vmoda M100's.

I read the reviews and was looking at a set of Sennheiser Headphones that were recommended but cost $1,400, which is a lot of wood for a headphone. Then I read about the Ultrasone 750 and 900s, but in reading the reviews I was turned off by the negative things being said about them. I like good low but not boomy bass. I love cymbals and tympani that is high and has a metallic sound rather than sounding like the hiss of a snake. So having stumbled upon the V-moda I went to their site and did some investigation. I liked the fact that they had two separate drivers to keep the bass from infecting the mids and highs. Nothing is worse than having distortion which I hate come into play when there is a lot of musical action going on. Listen to the Soundtrack of Tron by Defpunk as a good test, or the song Primodona or any Movie Score music by Erich Kunzel and if your system can not handle it I guarantee that you will be underwhelmed with the sound you hear. I read positive and negative reviews on Amazon about the Vmoda varying from the ear pads being uncomfortable, the head band being to tight or the sound being lousy, but I thought the positive reviews outweighed the negative. So I placed my order and received my headphones the next day. I purchased a headphone 1/8" plug headphone extension cord as where I would sit is on the other side of the room from my amp. So with great anticipation I plugged the headphones in.... and WOW.. did they sound bad... I could not believe it. I put on movies and music and they were the pits.. something was way off. I was playing with the DSP settings which only made things worse. Then I hit the test switch which cycles a signal from the left to the center to the right... and the signal was in one spot and never changed. I said, what the heck. So I got up and plugged the Vmoda's into the amp direct and hit the test signal and all was working correct. I then inspected the plug and noticed that the Vmoda's plug had many more rings on it to be used in an Ipod or Iphone. So I went to Radio Shack and got a 1/4inch plug extension cord and plugged the 1/4" adapter that came with the Vmodas into it.. and everything was working great. The sound I heard was really good and so I began to burn them in by listening to The Lone Ranger, The Man Of Steel, Oblivion and the soundtrack from Tron. The longer they played the better they sounded. I was really impressed.

So now I said, I know I have had a lot of trouble with my Ipod not having the power to drive headphones or expensive ear buds the way I like to hear music. I even have an equalizer app installed that can control the Ipod's amp to keep it from clipping, but anything with a lot bass was distorted, and highs were very thin and violins sounded terrible. So no expecting much I plugged the Vmoda into the Ipod and WOW WOW WOW... the sound was terrific. Bass was so punchy that on the Eagles Album Out Of Eden I can honestly say I never have heard a bass drum with such punch and power. The attack was amazing just like a real drum, my son in law is a drummer. The cymbals were clean and clear. On Bruce Springsteen's Live In Dublin, which will show off all sorts of things due to the band he has from sax, to trombone, to tuba, to guitars to accordion to piano.. The trumpet on this Album just sang out with such clarity and power.

OK.. enough of my blathering here. As you can tell I love these headphones and I am so impressed with how they have finally made my Ipod a viable source of music for me. By the way, I always prefer to download the Lossless formats like FLAC or ALAC or WAV, I do not care how much space the song or album will take up as the sound is what matters to me. I am the same way with my Dodge Charger Hemi using 93 Octane rather than 87 and driving in sport mode as it is the performance and experience that matters most to me.

I would recommend these without conviction, in fact I can not wait to let my brother hear how this headphones sounds. If you do not have an Alien oversized head, or a Hot Air Heater for your ears you will most certainly love these headphones. They sound great on all types of music from Rap to Classical to Rock... just make sure if you buy an extension cord that you buy the right one or you will have the same problem I initially had, shorting out things is never good. And I am speaking as a former Director Of Engineering...

Update one day later... After having some additional time to listen to the Vmoda Headphones my praise for them is even higher. I had a chance to listen to some pieces of music on my Ipod that I enjoyed the music but the quality was found lacking due to distortion and having to keep the volume low to keep the headphones from bottoming out on areas of the song with heavy bass. With the Vmoda M100's I am discovering so much more in my music that I never knew existed. The distortion and problems with the headphones not being able to handle the low low bass is non existent. The headphones easily deal with trumpets, guitars, drums, kettle drums, the snarly sound of a trombone, the very metallic and distinct crash and sound of cymbals and tympani, and I could go on and on. I was listening to an album by Erich Kunzel that involves the theme music from movies like Mission Impossible, Braveheart, Twister, etc... One thing that got my instant attention was that I was hearing some sounds like the tinkle of a triangle etc that apparently had been lost in the distortion that the other brand headphones were creating tryimng to deal with the very very complex music. I had the same experience with the Bruce Springsteen Live In Dublin album. Instruments came alive and to be honest, the sound almost sounded like 3D with the audience clapping and cheering behind me and the instruments blending from the middle to in front of me... It must be due to the design Vmoda has for their drivers or the crossfade design. The sound stage is very wide, and I am now trying to get my high end to begin to sound more like my headphones than visa versa... I do not find the headphones uncomfortable or hot on my ears or any of the other negatives I had read about. But things like this are very personal as is the sound. As I said initially, I am a very critical listener and look for all the nuances in the sound of a band or orchestra. I am looking forward to listening to my full collection of music on my Ipod, along with my CD's and movies. It is like I am starting all over again for the first time. The great thing about Amazon, and I can not praise their customer service high enough, giving them, based on my experience on a scale of 1 being the worst to a ten as the best, a solid 12. If you order these headphones, make sure you have a good source and if using a cable don't make the mistake I made above, and play them loud and let them burn in, playing by themselves if you go off somewhere else. Oh, and I am amazed at how loud these headphones will effortlessly play with the miniscule amplifier in an Ipod... it totally blows me away.. as I have the volume up only at about 3/4 and they are loud.. really loud... and no distortion, only sweet wonderful sound. When music lacks distortion, playing it louder does not hurt your ears.. it is the distortion that will make you reach for the volume control to turn them down. You will not experience that with these headphones. Hope I was as honest and open as I could be and was as much help to someone as the previous reviewers were to me. I am so glad the positive ones turned me on to these marvelous headphones... and I thank those reviewers from the bottom of my heart for being clear and descriptive with their experience. I am now off to listen to more music... have a great day.

title: Absolutely Perfect!
text:
This worked great on my Nikon AF-S DX 55-200mm f/4-5.6G ED. Cheap fix for a lens that would be too expensive to send to the repair shop IMO. If it ever breaks again, I am just a few dollars away from a fix.

The repair itself was easy but you do need to be careful. Check youtube for how-to videos. Be careful though since this piece will fit in multiple lenses but the repair may be slightly different depending on if they are repairing the same lense or not. This took about 10 minutes and I was going slow. I used a small philips screwdriver (you will need a very small screwdriver) and a pair of needlenose pliers. Tweezers would have worked as well.

1)Remove the five screws around the bayonet. (Screws going towards the rear lens element) Pay attention to where they were, I had two different kinds.
2)Remove the ring that is around the rear lens element. (Not the bayonet piece itself but between that and the center lens)
3)Remove the three large screws parallel with the barrel of the lens.
4)Push the piece containing the metal contacts back and work the old bayonet off carefully. It will not come all the way off. You will need to remove one screw on the bottom side which is holding a small wire and contact assembly in place. This will also release a small spring and metal piston. (When replacing, the larger end of the piston goes in to the new bayonet)
5)Remove the larger (aperture) spring from the old bayonet.
6)Reverse these steps with the new bayonet piece.

Basically, if you pay attention to how you take it apart, you just put it back together the same way.

title: Does not work with my Apple Macbook Pro
text:
I looked at various HDMI switches before picking the IOGear GHDSW3 switch. To be honest I picked it because I know the brand name IOGear better than the many others I saw and figured that IOGear would support their product. I am disappointed to report that they don't.

I have two computers I want to share the same monitor. One is my Windows 7 desktop and the other my 2012 Apple Macbook Pro. The Windows side works perfectly well through the switch; however, the Macbook has all sorts of noise (white specs flashing all over the screen) which can go from annoying to preventing me from using the Macbook with the monitor. The Macbook works perfectly well when directly hooked up to the monitor using the same cable as I use with the switch. Furthermore, I have another 5-port Sabrent HDMI switch which works with the Apple. (I intend to use the 5-port on my home entertainment system) The Sabrent system has a power supply.

I contacted IOGear's support through their web-chat and after explaining the problem the rep said it was either defective or required a power supply. The rep then declared the unit defective, in my opinion hastily, when he learned I had bought it through Amazon within the last 30 days. However, I suspect the problem is that the Apple side does not supply enough power through its HDMI connection. A power supply would solve that issue; however, the unit was sold without a supply.

Since I really don't believe the unit is defective I am reluctant (honesty is a curse) to return it to Amazon vendor. So I am left with a quasi functional switch for which the only recourse is for me to buy a power supply or eat the purchase.
