title: SIMPLY BEAUTIFUL!!!!
text:
I have to confess to having a bit of a `thing' about shower/bathroom radios - I love to lie for ages in the bath (can't understand these people who get in and out in a flash - and I don't like showers) and cannot bear silence, and so always need a nice radio on hand that I can take through with me to listen to my favourite station Classic FM while I'm in there. I do have quite a few it must be said, but every now and then I will be surprised with a really nice one. This one is absolutely GORGEOUS! Having had quite a bit of experience as to the quality and life-span of some shower radios, this looks very well built and designed indeed, and I should imagine that with loving care this will last probably a lifetime! The buttons are the `press' type and are all `flush' with the unit, and so can hardly get damaged or dirty with normal use. The plastic body is BEAUTIFULLY finished in hi-gloss! GORGEOUS aqua blue colour and it sits perfectly on a corner of the bath. It looks just like an over-sized tube of shower gel! A very large clear and easy to read screen for tuning and also contains a clock! Sound quality is SUPERB! (please remember though that you get a `transistor' radio type sound - not stereo hi-fi - but still one of the best sounding ones I've bought for some time!) I do have a more expensive rechargeable radio for the bathroom - but the recharging facility is a nuisance and unreliable, and so I highly recommend one of these. I purchased this from Amazon USA - they do ship to the United Kingdom, (I love Amazon1) and it was dirt cheap - even including the shipping!

A real MUST for anyone who loves listening to music in the bathroom!

FLAWLESS!

NOTE: Clock also has a blue light that lights up the whole display!

title: New favorite day-to-day headphones
text:
I've been searching for a pair of good headphones for a long time through Amazon and I can tell you that I was VERY unsure of which headphones to get. I've never found headphones that I can really wear for prolonged periods of time without hurting my ears- this is a problem since I listen to A LOT of music (nearly always have music on). I ended up with the JVC HAS400B and like every other review, I have to agree that it's REALLY good. I'm not going to use the "for its price" argument since I didn't find enough reviews that reviewed it as it is.
First of all, the bass and vocals are really good. It makes very good distinctions in most of the songs I listen to (and I listen to a variety of music like pop, dubstep and classic- but mostly deep house.) It sounds pretty good for classical/instrumental music too but can get a bit muddled for some deep house songs that have too much going on. I can imagine that it might sound a bit hazy for heavier dubstep as well. It's crazy how well it sounds for some pop songs though. It doesn't overpower or compress sounds like some of the headphones I've owned *cough*skullcandy*cough*
Second of all, it's relatively comfortable to wear. I've worn it the whole day -breaks in between- and have little problems. I need adjustments here and there but overall it doesn't press down on my ears too much.
The cord is also sturdy and a good length-not so long it gets in the way and not too short I cant move around with my phone. Not entirely sure what the carbon thing about these cables do but it works well.

What I dislike most about these is how bad they are at isolating sounds. Playing my music on medium volume leaks quite a bit of sound. I noticed that I need to put music at a higher volume than usual to get the same effect too. I would love it if it could be more sound-isolating but that isn't that big of a problem for now; I don't mind sharing my music with strangers.
It also sucks to have long hair because it gets stuck at the hinges. This is only occasional for me but might be a problem if you have crazy thick hair.
As for the style, I got the black and have to say that it's very sleek and cool looking. The chrome finish at the rim of the headphones are not really my taste but overall it looks pretty expensive.
I've accidentally crushed the headphones in my backpack and had it fall down a couple of times but it's withstood all of that force and is still looking and working like new. Not the mention the portability.

Overall, I would recommend getting these. Other headphones I've gotten at this price range have been pretty s****y but these are worth more than the 30 bucks. I hope this review was somewhat helpful.

title: Think Elmo at an affordable price point
text:
For presentations, I periodically need to have a document camera. I was even planning on concocting a stand to hold a MicroSoft WebCam until I came across this beauty. It has very high resolution (see the 3 pictures I posted on Amazon's page to get a better idea), focus to within 2" of target, a serviceable software interface, is easily portable, and has a very favorable price point, especially when compared to other document cameras (and I speak from experience, having used very pricey Elmos on occasion). The only criticism I have is that it does not have built in lighting, a bit surprising since many WebCams now have dimmable LED lighting integrated in. The software provides more control options than most, with my favorite feature being set once focus (there is also a button on the camera to trigger this), which eliminates the problem of focus resetting at slightest provocation.

My OS is Windows 7 and installation was trivial. Software is supplied on CD, or if like me you don't have an optical drive, it can be downloaded from the P2V website. One more thing that might be of interest, I often need to project the image of a device with a color touch screen, something cameras often have trouble with. This one has ample settings for making that work, especially when you place it in close (think iPhone). For my travel I ponied up for the manufacturer's travel case (about $20), well worth the added cost. It takes good stills, but if you want movies you will need third party software, something I prefer since I have an arsenal of cameras for various purposes.

They know full well that over 60% of the people that are due rebates don't bother with them. That's like stealing with your permission. I am not real organized when it comes to those things and about a third of the ones I send out never come back. I had that problem with Tiger Direct back in 1995 and I have purchased anything from them since then. The same goes for HP and for Dell and for Staples and for Sprint. Smith and Wesson took over four years to send me a rebate check. I called and called and emailed to no avail. I finally gave up, but apparently they have an amazing person working there who noticed that I never got a rebate check and I finally got it last September. My purchase was in April of 2008. I say all this, because I am going to add Asus to my "bad" list. No more Asus for me. I hope it was worth the ten dollars to lose me as a customer for life. title: Coral Peach: Because, Damn it!
text:
Well yes! I made fun of the new HP Chromebook 14 (in Coral Peach, Turquoise and Snow White) when I first saw it. The new HP Chromebook line comes in pastel colors that they seemed perfect for a child’s bedroom. However when you take this beast for a spin, you may become inclined to paint the walls to match.

This isn’t my first Chromebook. I own a slate grey Acer C710 with a 11 inch screen. It was hard on these old eyes of mine and I kept pumping-up the screen size to adjust. This Chromebook’s 14 inch display is just right. HP is known for it’s build quality and the HP Chromebook 14 doesn’t disappoint: excellent quality keyboard, speakers and an array of side port options such as two USB 3.0 and one USB 2.0 an HDMI port and an SD card slot for additional memory - Google take note! I love the Chrome environment. It does more than I ever use. At work I use Windoze computers and all day long I trouble-shoot Internet connection problems, password issues and viruses. Always Windoze, always windoze machines. Chrome is a pleasure to have because there are none of the burden of the Microsoft OS to worry about.

There is no Ethernet option so it’s Wifi only, and the display pales compared to others I have seen. There are some trade-offs to a lower price, but I dropped one Star because of this.

Yes, I bought the coral peach. Because I’m secure in my masculinity. Wanna make something out of it??!

title: Compact Yet Practical
text:
I have a variety of sizes of laptops from the larger Thinkpad to the smaller HP Elitebook. This backpack fits both of these beautifully- together or separately. I can also put my Kindle in its case in another pocket, my cell phone, glasses case, and a few books too.

There are places for pencils and even bottled water - a smaller bottle. I love the front pocket which makes it easy to access things I need to access quickly on days when I can not carry them in my pockets or coats. The straps are comfortable and don't hurt my shoulders like some of them do.

If you are carrying a huge load of books and supplies to class or other places, this might not be a bag for you. It is primarily for a smaller loads of books and supplies as well as the laptop, ipad or other tablets. This is not for the long day of carrying all of your books with you everywhere, like I have done in the past.

I have brought this with me on quite a few trips and found it really handy, but I only had a few books with me. I have also used it for other things like shopping trips at fiber festivals, and craft fairs too. It was helpful as I needed to have my laptop for later in the day so I could carry it with me, protected and separated from my other stuff.

This is not waterproof, but resistant, so if you have to walk a long way, you might want to put your electronic components and books in plastic bags inside the backpack, just to be extra careful.

All in all, I love this backpack because it is not over-sized and is perfect for those times when I want to carry my laptop and smaller other things, and don't need a large backpack for larger loads. It is handy and well divided for convenience. For larger all day loads- I suggest a larger backpack.

text:
Sturdy, durable, does what it claims to do. For the most part I'm very happy with this product. There are a few minor things I would change, but for the price, I can't really complain at all.

-If your laptop is any bigger than 15", this may not work well for you. I know there are other reviewers claiming that it works fine with 17" computers, and in a pinch I'm sure it does. However, if you are bothered by your computer hanging over the edge of the table or want enough space for both the computer and a mouse, 15" is the max.

-It would be nice if the built-in USB hub could be powered by an external adaptor. Seeing as the computer's USB port is running the fan in addition to the hub, the power levels sometimes dip too low for some devices to behave reliably.

-The insides of the two compartments are not nearly as spacious as you would think. Don't count on being able to store anything more than a few USB cables or AA batteries.

title: It's a great enclosure, much better than the 'slide the drive in from the end' type.
text: This enclosure has a clamshell type design, which means it is made in two equal halves which allow you to securely fasten the two halves of the enclosure together with four screws. A lot of the slightly cheaper 2.5 inch drive enclosures have a small end cap that you screw to the end of the enclosure with two tiny screws, which is much less secure and reliable in my experience. This enclosure is made of metal (not sure if it's steel or something else) and coated in rubber which makes it seem like a high quality piece. It fits together very well, and it seems very strong. It's USB 3.0 for great speed, and backwards compatible with older USB standards. It has a DC barrell jack for external power supply, but it works without that because of the USB cable with two USB plugs on one end. There is a physical power switch, and a nice blue LED light on the end to show power and data transfer status. The screw holes are hidden by two silver plastic stickers which probably won't stand up to being removed and replaced more than once or twice, if you're very careful. once you put the drive into the enclosure, you should leave it in there unless you want to be able to see the screws, which would really take away from the nice look that the enclosure has when its properly assembled. It comes with the screws obviously, as well as a screw driver, and an imitation leather case, which is good for keeping mild dust invasion at bay, but won't offer any other protection. If you plan on dropping your drive on the floor or hiking in the rain with it, you should not rely on the enclosure or its case but, instead, plan on not dropping your drive or going hiking in the rain with it, or get a different enclosure or a Pelican case to keep it in. If you just want a case to keep a notebook drive safe from direct contact and dust and you don't want to spend 60 dollars pick this enclosure over any of the others on amazon in the sub 60 dollar price range.

title: Great screen protector, recommended
text:
This is a great skin for the TF700T. It is relatively thin so the tablet still fit in the dock. It protects and adds grip to the back side. Now the tablet is much easier to handle, while maintaining the nice metal finish and look. It cleans easy, and any nick and scratch to the protector surface seems to magically disappear in a day or so.

Installation is a bit intimidating at first, but it was actually quite easy. One trick is to not hesitate to put enough liquid on the protector. Enough for the skin to be able to slide around a bit but not too much (as the liquid could get into openings and gaps on the device). I made a mistake of not putting enough liquid on the plastic antenna part and a bubble could not escape (the bubble had somewhat disappeared but you can see something is there/not perfect). I was a bit scared to expose my tablet to liquid, but it was OK. Enough liquid allows the skin to be adjusted easily. The corners were a little tricky, they seem to refuse to stick at first, but once dry they held on just fine.

Note I only use the body skin to protect the body (back and sides of the tablet), so I can't comment on the screen protector part.

I highly recommend this kit.

title: Solid drive, good options, OK software, NOT NAS
text:
This very large 2-drive USB 3.0 RAID comes in a small, smart-looking, relatively quiet package. It is not a network drive like the [[ASIN:B00AGI7I2O WD My Book Live Duo 8TB Personal Cloud Storage NAS]], which is just as well because you would lose any speed boost you gain from drive striping (RAID 0). The Duo comes formatted as a single NTFS partition prepared for RAID 0, which prioritizes speed. The speed is nice, but if you lose one drive, you lose all of your data. You can reformat the drive with mirroring (RAID 1), if you like; this creates two identical copies of your data, but cuts the total storage in half. Alternatively, you can reformat for JBOD ("just a bunch of disks") and treat the two 4TB disks as separate entities.

The WD maintenance and diagnostic software work fine. The backup software shipped with the drive is confusing and appears to be tailored to those who want continuous backup of files from their working hard drives. WD offers a download of Acronis backup software (which I have not yet tried) as an alternative. It also offers dropbox integration; this is only likely to be useful to people who already have dropbox accounts and aready use the online storage facility extensively. Only 2GB of free storage are offered, so this is more a bit of cross-promotion than a practical feature.

The Duo seems reasonably fast when configured in RAID 0 mode, but I have not benchmarked it, and I do not have any USB 3.0 external drives to compare it to. I have not tried it in any other modes. When I first received the drive, I was awed by the 8TB of storage. This awe quickly dissipated when I began copying older backups from other drives onto this one (as a step in getting them organized and pruned down) -- backups take up a lot of space!

Buying advice: You are likely to realize some speed benefits from the Duo if you have a USB 3.0-capable computer (most computers older than 2 or so years have only USB 2.0 -- you should check) and use this in RAID 0 mode. It is not likely to be faster than a new internal hard disk, however, if that is an option for you. You can gain some data security by using the Duo instead in RAID 1 mode. This is not a "cloud" solution, so look elsewhere if you want network-attached storage. It does support Macs, however. If you need 8TB of storage, the real question here is whether two 4TB drives would fill your needs, or if your needs require you to pay the premium for a single package that potentially delivers better performance or data security. Speed isn't always important in a backup drive, and redundancy isn't necessarily more important than space for multiple separate backups. I can't say what's best for you, but if money is tight you should ponder carefully.

title: Can't go back to regular tablet resolution
text:
I did my research and waited a long time for this tablet. Overall I consider it the best tablet on the market. High screen resolution paired with top of the line graphics and processing capability and the best tablet OS family around make this the tablet to beat. If you're looking for a high end tablet capable of the best games, fast internet cruising, and problem free use then look no further than the Asus TF700.

Hardware
The build quality is really great, nice metal exterior, scratch resistant glass, buttons have a nice feel. The tablet feels solidly built, but is surprisingly lightweight and very thin. The screen resolution is amazing, once you use a tablet with this resolution for a few days going back to the lower resolution of other tablets is hard. Also the screen is very bright, and very responsive to touch input.

Software
Ice Cream Sandwich is a great OS. Android has consistently improved their OS and this tablet is in line to get upgraded to Jelly Bean sometime soon. The appearance of the OS is nice and crisp, and with the high resolution screen it really pops. One issue though regarding software. Because this is one of only 2 or 3 Android tablets with this high resolution some apps don't take advantage of it. For example a magazine e-reader I downloaded had a tile only occupying the middle portion of the screen because it was clearly written for the smaller resolution and did not resize on this tablets high resolution. That being said, most apps and games not only use the entire screen, they also utilize the high pixel count. You can tell some games are transitioning from low res to high res images in their games (Plants vs Zombies). Also included on this tablet is a nVidia app called Tegra Zone which acts as a portal to new and upcoming content that utilizes the Tegra 3 chip. This is a great source for high end games, both FPS and addicting arcade games alike.

Keyboard Dock
The optional keyboard available for this tablet is a great accessory. When on business trips this tablet with attached keyboard replaces my laptop 90% of the time and would replace the other 10% were it not for CAD related work that I sometimes need to do. It would not replace my laptop though for functions such as email if it did not have the physical keyboard. Although a little on the small size it clearly mates to the tablet well and has dedicated tablet function keys such as a home key and a back key. Also unlike generic bluetooth keyboards this keyboard when plugged into the tablet adds ~50% more battery over the tablet alone. It also adds a full size USB port. When the keyboard is attached to the tablet the keyboard battery is the main power source, draining it first. Also if left closed for some time the table will charge from the keyboard.

Covers
Related to the tablet is a tablet cover. I have tried several and the one I like the most for the tablet alone is the "MoKo(TM) Slim-Fit Folio Cover Case for Asus Eee Transformer Pad Infinity TF700" which is slim but protects the tablet effectively. Unfortunately there seems to be only one form factor available for the tablet with the keyboard attached. I purchased the "Poetic ASUS Transformer Pad Infinity Case TF700" and have been fairly disappointed with it. The cover is thick when used (more than doubling the thickness of the tablet/keyboard) and it can pull the tablet from the keyboard just enough so that it doesn't work. If you don't mind the extra bulk of this cover then it might be an alright case for you.

Electrical
One note is that unlike many other tablets this tablet does not charge with a standard USB cable. Instead it uses a charging cable with a proprietary plug on one end and a USB 3.0 on the other end. It will charge with the USB end is plugged into USB 2.0, but it does so slowly and the tablet never acknowledges it's plugged in. However using a USB 3.0 source works fine. The tablet and keyboard charge very fast when attached to a USB 3.0 source. Also you can charge both just by plugging into the keyboard when they are attached.

Packaging
The packaging for the tablet was poorly designed. The first tablet I received had a small dent on the box which I assumed would not impact the tablet. However upon opening the box I realized this seemingly small dent had damaged the tablet because it has no padding other than the thin cardboard box between the tablet and the outside of the box. Also the screen is placed very close to the top of the box only protected by a thin layer of foam. This is only an issue if you receive a damaged one, at which point Amazon will replace it but it can be frustrating when you were eagerly waiting for the tablet to show up. This seems to be the only major thing I had a problem with that Asus controlled.

title: A high quality and inexpensive HDMI cable, with durable plugs, a well-built line, and built-in interference protector
text:
I've got several devices that use an HDMI cable, and have used several different brands of cable over the years.

When it's a short line, it doesn't seem to matter much which brand you use. For longer cables, especially cables that need to travel through the wall or that are in the proximity of other electronic devices and cables, it does matter quite a bit. I've seen some awful interference patterns in the video feed from televisions and projectors that weren't properly cabled.

The 9to5Cables are very well-built. Apart from the gold plating on the plugs, what impressed me at first were the very solid connectors that surround the plugs and connect them to the cables. I've had cables that eventually pulled loose, or where the plug had some play in it to wiggle around. If you plug things in once and never reconnect that's not usually a problem, but where plugs get a lot of use it can be.

I've got two of these, one that's 15 feet and one that's 25 feet, and both transmit signal that's as clear as if they were only a meter. I use the 15 foot one in my office, in order to connect with an external monitor that I use to mirror my laptop when I'm giving demonstrations, or when I need to preview something on a larger screen than the one on my laptop. I use the longer one to connect my laptop to the television in our house, so that everyone can watch what I'm watching on Netflix. It works great for both purposes.

I don't have a 3D television, but these are rated for full quality 3D and HD video. There is built-in interference protection both on the connectors and within the cable. I've used these with a few different setups and been very happy with them.

(Note: I was provided with a sample for the purpose of testing and review.)

title: Huge value for the price!
text:
These cheap little extension tubes are great with m43 and manual focus (MF) legacy lenses. I do not do much close up or macro photography -- certainly not enough to justify buying a lens for that purpose. Still, on a rare occasion, I want to get close up for a photo. So I mount my MF lens on a m43 adapter, mount the adapter to the extension tube, mount the camera on a tripod, focus and shoot. The caveat is, focusing is extremely difficult -- even with the lens stopped down, depth of field is only a few millimeters. If you're photographing extremely close up, you need to have a ton of patience to get the focus down -- practice helps.

I like the three screwable levels of this extension tube (caution: do NOT screw them together too tightly). They give you three different distances you could shoot from. For me, I only used the furthest setup -- that was already very close up for me, and I only use occasionally.

If you want to experiment and give close up a try, or if, like me, you normally photograph other stuff but want a tool for that occasional extreme close-up, without putting up a lot of cash -- this is the way to go. Get your feet wet, as it were.

Finally, I would re-emphasize, I have ONLY used this product with legacy manual focus glass on micro 4/3. I've got a Konica Hexanon 50mm f1.4, and a Kiron 28mm f2.0 (Nikon F mount). I don't know how the extension tube would work with digital lenses -- such a setup doesn't make sense to me.

and it's all true what you've heard-- right out of the box, w/in five minutes i am online and working on something i was working on last night (because it was in the cloud)...

and if you're worried about having to be online all the time for it to work, i ask you this-- when are you ever w/out access to the internet? i mean seriously come on.. if anyone is that worried about this machine not having 3g or 4g then they need to get w/their carrier and add tethering to their phones because i have the tethering option and have only used it once... and printing is a breeze; i mean, how many printers out there are already internet or google print ready? i saw a printer just the other day for less than $60...

so much more than a simple netbook, and because it's google, everything works across all of my platforms-- my nexus 7 as well as my nexus 5...

great value, great looking machine, great working machine... get one of these things, you won't be disappointed.

title: Great Headphones, Great Price
text:
Ask any audiophile and they'll gladly tell you the problem with most mid-range headphones right now: way too much bass. I don't know if headphone companies just assume that people have stopped listening to everything except dubstep, but it's really hard to find a decent pair of headphones (without spending $400+) that don't focus their drivers exclusively on bass in exchange for a muddy-sounding everything else.

1. Sound

These headphones are an exception. They're not 100% neutral as other users have said and will lean *slightly* toward the bass-end of the spectrum, but overall the Sol Republic Master Tracks XC are very clean-sounding headphones that will accommodate a wider variety of musical tastes than almost anything I've seen out there for this price. This is especially true if the source of your music comes equipped with an equalizer (all smart phones/tablets, most PC sound cards), in which case you can get these sounding *exactly* how you want with a few very minor tweaks. That said, these are almost perfect right out of the box, and that's coming from someone who is REALLY picky about his headphones. Less particular listeners will probably enjoy them even more.

2. Design

If you can't tell just from the pictures, these really do look great. You should never buy headphones for their branding or appearance (lookin' at you, Beats), but if you want a pair of headphones that both sound good and look awesome, these are a great pick. They are marketed as headphones for people who make music (hence the Calvin Harris collaboration), and the burgundy/maroon dual-tone matte finish, plush cushions, and subtle detailing give them a high-end, quasi-professional look.

3. Comfort and Wearability

The faux-leather ear cushions are supple and comfortable, but don't completely surround the ear 100% and might place undue pressure on earrings/studs during long listening periods. Otherwise, they are very comfortable - I've worn them with glasses for hours.

4. Accessories

The zippered carrying bag that comes with the headphones is about as useless as you might expect, but not enough to take away a star. Especially considering that it's balanced out by the inclusion of a an extra-long "studio-style" cable with two jack adapters, which is a really nice touch. As with all Sol Republic headphones, the cups can be removed and the headband swapped out if you want to mix things up.

***

All in all, a great buy. I listen to everything from Deadmau5 and Massive Attack to neo-folk and Indie pop and it all sounds equally good. If you're looking for a semi-neutral set of headphones to accommodate a diverse musical palette, the Master Tracks XCs are the ones you want.

title: Excellent Quality; Also Features Compared with Nakamichi
text: Material quality, contactor, backshell, fit, finish, wire securing screw, and threads are excellent.  Backshell is two piece steel, knurled segment for ease of tightening.  Compared with two types of Nakamichi banana plugs there are some considerations.  Sewell backshell is longer, thus if using heavy gage wire, it will load the receiver sockets more and may require cable support.  Also, Sewell plugs have only one screw for securing the wiring versus two screws on the Nakamichi.  Nakamichi plugs contacts are longer than the Sewell.  Nakamichi plugs backshells are plastic with metal threads insert versus  all metal backshell on the Sewell.  In addition, the Sewell connectors will accomodate heavier gage wire than the Nakamichi plugs.  I am using Velocity 12 gage wire and it fits easily in the Sewell.  If I was to upgrade the Sewell design, I would make the backshell shorter, the contact pin longer, and include two screws to tighten the wire instead of one.  However, in the past two years I bought Nakmichi plugs, Monster, and others but found these Sewell Pro Maestros to be the best quality and value too.

title: Kindle Fire Rocks
text: I've been using computers since they came out in the 1980's and have built my own systems, doing my own programming on many. As the industry has evolved I've gone to laptops (have really enjoyed them) and eventually looked around at the tablets. I had purchased my wife a Xoom (which is awesome) and she will not let it go. I was waiting for something a little smaller and naturally wanted power in my tablet (eat your heart out Tim Taylor!). I was looking at the new Xoom tablet but wasn't happy about the price ... was interested in the Kindle Fire because of the price but concerned about the power. I waited for a little while and finally the money part in me won out and I purchased a Kindle Fire. Understand I like power and like it now. Every system I've ever gotten had to be close to the best, but after years of spending thousands on computers only to upgrade in two years for half the price, I finally realized I needed to be more reasonable. To my utter surprise, and I do mean that, I found the Kindle Fire is everything I need in a tablet. I use it to read books, play angry birds (so who doesn't) and my grandson even plays angry chickens (next it will be angry worms ... lol). I've used it to watch trailers of movies that I might like (I'm a superhero junkie so yes I've watched the Avengers trailers) ... watched an old movie on utube that is hard to find and expensive to buy ... I've pick up some kindle books from authors I enjoy and find reading the kindle to be easier than reading a book (not sure why though) ... my grandson has played many games on the Kindle and loves moving from game to game every 10 minutes ... one of my daughters has been reading a book and likes using the Kindle ... I've done some quick research on the internet and found the browser to be responsive and easy to use. (Any serious research I do is done on my desktop). The screen is sharp and easy to change to adjust to my eyesight. I was concerned about the audio. Audio speakers are ok but you really don't want to use them. I picked up some good earplugs to listen to the Kindle and wow ... awesome sound. I've downloaded music to my Kindle and have listen to it like an ipod. The battery life is fine although if your grandson is playing games it will drain it sooner, but it lasts for hours. Overall I have to say the Kindle Fire has earned 5 stars from me ... the cost can't be beat and the power is very good, actually better than expected for the price.

title: Perfect for logging power events
text:
This plugs into the Cyberpower PR1500LCD and other Cyberpower UPS models (check for specific compatibility) and it is great. I needed to deploy a UPS at an unmanaged site and had to track commercial power problems. This card can be configured to log between 1 day (short interval - log per minute) or over 255 days (long interval - once an hour) so you can see low and high values for load, input voltage, input frequency and output voltage per interval. It exports to CSV to make it easy to chart and track in Excel.

The web interface is the best way to access the data and configure the card. There are several options for sending the data (SMS, email etc) but I'm only using the card for onboard logging since there is a need for security.

This is the only card I found with onboard logging that could provide me with details of power conditions over 6 months.

title: Finally got it to work.
text:
We got this for our camper and it is supposed to work with 2 tvs if you have 2 boxes. well we had a devil of a time setting it up at the site and contacted dish and winegard several times.
Finally I had to pay a local satellite guy $100 to come in and set it up.
Turns out everyone at Dish and WIneguard was telling me to set it up on Western Satellites 110 119 etc.
I should have been setting it up on Eastern sats. in North Carolina.finding the 3 satellites using Lower numbered azimuths.
The guy had it working in about 15 minutes, but he still had to check the switches and search 3 times.
We left the camper and came back 6 weeks later and it did not work even though we had not moved the dish.
We were finally able to find all the satellites and lock them in but when we turned the tv off it lost them . this happened several times and we finally locked on and it worked for the next month. except sometimes weather related. We never got the second TV to work with this dish.
Also, if you have the Dish service at your home and want to transferr it to your RV you must call them when you get where you are going, and tell them where you are, and to give you the local channels for that area. Otherwise you would not get many channels. Then as you travel around you will have to keep doing this, and when you get back home you will have to call again and have your locals restored. We had decided to keep the Rv stationalry in one park from now on so decided on this unit because their cable only has 4 channels.
I am not sure if it is hardware or if our line of site is compromised and we don't have the best pathway to the satellites but it won't get any better as all those trees are just going to grow taller next year.

title: Dyaudio-The Absolute Finest
text:
Dear Audio Car Enthusiasts:

Years ago I installed a custom designed Dyaudio car sound system using their dome tweeters in the dash facing up, mid domes in the doors, 8" woofers in the rear deck, and 12" Dyaudio woofer behind the rear seat of an Oldsmobile Cutlass...a 1982. I used two Sony Amps and ran the woofers full range as they seemed to integrate better that way. The rear seat served as an "acoustic crossover" absorbing the mids and highs. The 12" woofers were acoustically isolated from the truck and also braced to a MDF board that was bolted to the car. I designed the crossovers using specs provided by Dyaudio using the finest capacitors, resisters, and air-core for midrange and tweeter and iron-core units for the 8" woofer passively. The sound was simply a new standard in audio reproduction. The car was literally a concert hall or disco on wheels. Bass was deep but not boomy and the system could handle peaks of power with ease. Dynaudio simply makes the finest drivers and auto sound systems currently available at any price. If you love high end car audio, you will be ecstatic about the sound of their drivers. The key is having a good enough ear to tune the system to your car. Their pre-wired kits are excellent in this regard and also their new drivers are designed to withstand the extremes of temps in the car audio environment. My Best, James.

title: Long range Bluetooth Rx/Tx with digital input/output, optical & coaxial.
text: The range is better than expected, farther than any other Bluetooth Rx or Tx I have, so it's really limited by my other equipment.  I bought this specifically to get S/PDIF digital optical input and output, and that works fine with my audio receiver.  I have it connected to the optical digital line out and aux in, so any source playing through the receiver can also be transmitted on Bluetooth.  There is a pronounced delay, which is a function of the Bluetooth protocol.  This Nolan TRX unit does NOT support the latest aptX Bluetooth protocol, which I don't have any experience with but may improve delay and sound quality.  The sound quality of this unit sounds great to me.  I've tried playing maximum bit rate mp3 songs, television, etc. and all sound as good as a straight connection to me, although I can't say I've tried really critical side by side comparisons. Besides the aux/coaxial/optical switch, there's only one button to control the unit.  Reading the instructions was mandatory.  Momentarily pressing or holding the button cycles through the Tx/Rx modes and Bluetooth pairing.  Once paired with your audio source and/or speaker/receiver, turning the unit on brings up the last mode and tries to pair with last device.  There's no way to enter a PIN.  So far, I've been able to pair it with every Bluetooth device I tried.  Overall, this is a great device and good purchase.  One improvement for future would be support for aptX protocol.  I've seen digital Bluetooth receivers with aptX, but no Rx/Tx in same unit, at least for home use at reasonable price.  NFC support for use with the newer cell phones would be a nice improvement also.

After the bluescreen, when the computer reboots the computer will be unable to boot since the drive has dropped from the system and is still dropped. This is further proof the drive is at fault. It requires completely turning your computer off from power then back on again to fix. This drive being the sole cause of bluescreens in my computer is unacceptable. AVOID!

title: High hopes dashed

I had high hopes for this device! It's attractive and should have offered the capacity to detect and report motion, temperature, humidity and light levels. The most important function to me was motion detection. This is the one function that does not work properly.

It does detect legitimate motion, but even at the lowest levels of sensitivity, it detects motion of apparently invisible objects. This defeats the purpose of a Zwave system that texts me each time my home is invaded. Just to verify it wasn't detection motion outside of my windows, I put it in a drawer in my unoccupied home. It continued to detect false motion at least every few hours. I had to turn off the motion detection capacity. The good news is that one CAN change settings for motion, temperature, humidity and light separately. You can also disarm each sensor capacity separately.

I contacted technical support for Aeon. They reported that this is a known issue. At first they reported that they hope to have a firmware update soon. They later recommended I return the device for a refund.

I've kept the device because I still appreciate the other three functions. Perhaps a new generation will be developed, or a firmware update offered. If so, I'll buy or install them!

title: Works Good on Kindle Fire HD
text:
UPDATED ON 02/04/2013

It took me no time at all to connect the controller to my Kindle Fire HD. The controller comes without a charge so I had to charge it but you can use it while it's being charged. It took me about 3 hours to fully charge the controller and the instructions say that a full charge will last for 30 hours of gameplay. So far it is living up to that length of battery life as I haven't charged it again since the initial charge.

Nyko is working on an app called Playground which I assume will be available on Amazon when it's complete. As I understand it the app is currently in beta testing. Regardless if you set the controller to HID mode (by setting the switch on the back of the controller to the position of the controller icon) you can use this on your Kindle Fire HD. On the main screen you can use the left and right directional buttons or the left joystick to flip through the screens and you can start whatever app is highlighted but that's about all you can do from the main screen.

The main reason I purchased this (and I'm sure most of you will as well) is to play games. I tried it with every game I had on my Kindle some of them work, some of them don't, and some of them kinda do. I'll go through a review of each game I have and how well the controller worked or didn't work. I'll update this as time goes on. Feel free to ask questions cause I always answer them when I get the e-mail that someone has commented on my reviews!

Alphedia: I really expected this game to work since the other Kemco RPG games did. This game doesn't work with the controller AT ALL.

Eve of the Genesis: I can confirm that this game works PERFECTLY. You can navigate every menu and access every feature straight from the controller. Using the playpad on this game is a prime example of why I bought this controller.

Final Fantasy 3: This is the game that I was super excited to use the controller with. I'm very sad to report that it does not work. You can push a button that will bring up a small menu that says "Close App?" and you can choose yes or no but that's all. I very much hope that SquareEnix updates the app to support HID. If you change the controller to "mouse mode" (by moving the switch on the back to the icon of a mouse) you can play the game but it's difficult to manage.

N.O.V.A 3: Very sad to report that this game doesn't work at all either. Very sad because it would be super cool to play an FPS with a controller.

Order & Chaos Online: It would be pretty awesome if I was able to use the controller to play this game. Similar to how you would use a controller to play Final Fantasy 11. I'm sad to report that the controller doesn't work.

Plants vs Zombies: I didn't expect this game to work, and it doesn't.

Quell Reflect: I really didn't expect this game to work with the controller but it did perfectly. Navigating the menu's is a little difficult but once you get used to it it's easy to do. Playing the game is as simple as using the joystick or D-pad to send the water drop in the direction you want it to go. When you get to levels that have multiple water drops you can easily switch between which drop your moving with the X button (where the square button would be on a Playstation controller). Because this game works so well I would assume that the original Quell would also work. Once I complete this game I'll most likely purchase the original Quell and give it a shot as well.

Sonic CD: Unlike Sonic 4 EP 1 this game works perfectly with the controller. You can navigate all the menus and play the game perfectly.

Sonic the Hedgehog 4 Episode 1: This was another game that I was really excited to use the controller with. I really enjoy 2D platform games and although the touch screen controls work pretty well they just don't beat using a controller. This game kinda/sorta works. When your playing a level you can use the D-pad or the left joystick to move Sonic and you have to push in on the right joystick to make him jump or spin or attack or whatever. It does work but it feels stiff and a little unresponsive. Not my ideal way to play the game but it's something. You can't use the controller to navigate any of the menu's, only play in a level.

Sonic the Hedgehog 4 Episode 2: Unlike episode 1 this game works perfectly with the controller. You can navigate all the menus and play the game perfectly.

Symphony of Eternity: Another game that works perfectly with this controller. Every menu/every feature of the game is accessible using the playpad pro.

Tetris: This is the version from EA. Controller works perfectly for navigating the menu's and playing the actual game. You can flip the blocks and use either the joystick or D-pad to move the blocks into place.

The Bard's Tale: This is another game that I was really hoping to use the controller on. Sad to say it doesn't work at all.

Twilight War: This game kind of works. You can move the main character in every direction, attack and scroll through dialogue. You can't save, open any menu's or use any special abilities.

title: Ridiculously complex (for audiobooks)

I have had my Kindle Fire for over a week and have yet to successfully download an audiobook from the library. After navigating an endless round-robin series of websites to download an unending collection of xfer software, I still cannot reliably listen to an audiobook. My only success so far is to download all the chapters of a book as individual mp3 files to the music section of the device. I can play them, but I have to choose the order and it does not remember where I was in the chapter.

I have used the amazon website to download audiobooks as well. It announces that it's transferring the audio files to the Kindle, but I cannot locate them once the transfer is complete. There appears to be no reliable way to listen to books with the device.

Downloading ebooks works well, though. They are easy to find as they appear in the carousel after the xfer.

I've tried using it as an ersatz web-browser, but find the interface to be too sporadic. Sometimes it recognizes a touch input, and sometimes it does not. It's simply too frustrating to use the device itself to browse for books. I end up going to my desktop PC to actually find titles.

The Kindle is essentially useless for my purposes. I will try to return it to the store where I bought it. The employees assured me it would work for audiobooks, but I find it well-nigh impossible to use.

This is a frustrating device and I wish I hadn't bought it.

title: Not the quality I was expecting... at all.
text:
I use flash drives often - often enough that I decided I would treat myself to a "higher end" drive. So I chose Leef because I liked what they had to say on their website, and because some of their other products had good reviews. When I bought this specific model, there were no reviews because it was so new, but it perfectly matched my desired specs: 32gb, USB 3.0, and a quality housing.

I'm giving the drive two stars because it does seem to be put together well. But that's where the joy ends. Here's what I found:

1. I had to return the first one I received because it would not fit into my USB ports. Wouldn't fit the ports on my desktop or my laptop. My wife's laptop is a piece of junk, so I was willing to use a bit more force. It went in after quite a struggle. Not cool. So I sent it back to Amazon and bought another (they wouldn't do an exchange from some bizarre reason).

2. The second drive was almost exactly the same, but required a bit less force. Just a bit. I'm still not happy about the amount of force I have to use to get this thing into my brand-spanking new desktop. But I wanted to love this thing, so I stuck with it for a while.

3. It's totally glitchy. I've never had problems like this with a drive. It "freezes up" while transferring files onto the drive, and off of the drive, and while viewing files on the drive... Seriously, Leef? I bought an 8gb Centon for $9 - NINE DOLLARS - and it's never had a single issue like this.

4. And the transfer speeds... 14mbs on average. Meanwhile, that 8gb Centon that I mentioned, which is USB 2.0, gets transfer speeds of about 25mbs. Is it my USB port configuration? Probably not, since I was getting 125mbs with my USB 3.0 Western Digital Passport. And I'm talking about transferring back and forth with an internal Samsung SSD. Something's wrong here, Leef.

5. (The final straw) So I sent them a note via their website. I thought, "Let me give these guys a chance before I rush a judgement." But you know what? I haven't heard back from them. They have time for a ROCK CLIMBING WALL in their office (which they display prominently on their website... which is totally corny), but they don't have time to get back to me.

Guess what, Leef. We're through. I thought you were cool. Thought you were sexy. Thought we'd be a great fit. But you turned out to be way lame. I deserve better.

title: Good Quality and Easy to Set Up
text:
I just bought a Home Theater in a Box with 7.1 surround sound. With nothing behind the couch but open space, there was really no where to place my rear surrounds on stands so I needed to wall mount them. After reading up a bit on the various mounts, I chose these because a) they got good reviews and b) they were rated for 20lbs, which gives me more leeway on what kind of speakers I can use them with. I'm not like alot of reviewers on here, in that I would rather use mounts that are rated for at least 1.5 to 2 times the weight of my speakers.

Normally, I'm not a fan of plastic/composite material for home theater accessories. However, these mounts look clean and sturdy, and they feel very solid. The composite material definintely seems to be high grade. Setup was a breeze. My surrounds came with a keyhole bracket on the back so I just removed it and screwed these into the speaker cabinet.

For mounting about 8 ft high I used the dry-wall anchors and 1 1/2" wood screws that came in the package. I don't know why a lot of reviewers warned against the supplied anchors, if you are careful and know a little bit about dry wall anchors and how finicky they can be you will be able to mount these just fine without worrying about finding a stud (provided, of course, your satellites are not too heavy).

The mounts look good, the setup looks clean, I am definitely satisfied with my purchase.

UPDATE 9-17-2012: I have the much larger BIC Venturi DV52si speakers mounted now with these brackets and they handle the extra size and weight just fine. Using drywall anchors on one side and stud-mounted on the other and I have no issues. These mounts work very well.

Cons:

title: LG 60PM6700 Not Bad So Far - See update 6/10/2012
text:
I ordered the LG 60PM6700 on Friday March 11th, with Free Supersaver Shipping, and it was already delivered this evening Wednesday March 16. That was fast! Two guys brought it in, set it up, and made sure everything was as it should be before I signed for it. I've only had it for about 6 hours, so I'll give my initial impression, then update it in a few days after having more experience with the set.

I had previously purchased a Panasonic TC-P60S30 from WalMart for a really good price, but in the end, I was not happy with its extremely dark picture and overall substandard picture quality, so I returned it.

Right off the bat this LG blows away the picture quality of the Panasonic model I had returned. Granted, this one cost me about $300 more, but I can tell you it's already worth it. So far I've tweaked the settings to where I like the color, brightness, contrast, and black levels. I used the Picture Wizard II, but then did a few more minor tweaks to suit my taste, which tends to lean towards a brighter picture. I did have an inexpensive Element Electronics 42" LCD sitting here while I was shopping for a replacement. I can say, the LG doesn't have quite the bright picture and vivid colors the smaller LCD has, but it does completely blow away the 60" Panasonic plasma I had returned. From what I've experienced, heard, and read, Plasma's just don't quite have the bright brilliant pop that LCD TV's do, but this LG looks pretty darn awesome. My tastes run towards a brighter picture, so I'm pretty picky when it comes to getting the settings I want from a TV. So far, I find this LG very pleasing. As far as the bright vivid picture I'm looking for, this set gets me where I want to be.

So far, I've viewed some HD Dish Network content (Restaurant Impossible on the Food Network), and it looked great. I then put on Rango through Netflix over the built in WIFI. The jury is still out on that since I'm not sure if my WIFI isn't the best, or the TV's WIFI isn't the greatest, but WIFI over my Panasonic BluRay player seems to look fine. I then connected a LAN cable to the TV and went back to viewing Rango through Netflix, and it looks great; almost DVD quality. I'll report back about the WIFI once I figure out if it's my WIFI network or if the TV's WIFI connection isn't the greatest.

Next I watched part of a DVD I burned to back up one of my movies (a DVD copy of a DVD movie) through my Panasonic DMP BDT210 BluRay player. The picture was crisp and clear, but I noticed a lot of motion judder. Even messing with the de-judder setting didn't help. It may just be my copy of the movie, but a couple of times I had previously watched it on the LCD I had and didn't notice the judder at all, so I'll have to watch a few more of my copied movies and report back.

I now have a store bought DVD of Alice in Wonderland playing, and it looks absolutely amazing, and with no motion judder at all. I still have to dig out a few of my BluRay disks to check that out, but I can't imagine even a Blue Ray looking much better than the standard DVD already looks. My family room is huge, so I'm sitting about 15 feet away from the TV, and I can count the individual hairs on Johnny Depp's Mad Hatter wig.

I took advantage of the free two pair of 3D glasses being offered through Amazon when purchasing the LG set, but they have not arrived yet. I should have them in a day or two, so I'll have to wait to report about the 3D experience.

I have noticed one design flaw in the TV stand. Due to the glossy black half inch beveled angle of the front of the stand, it tends to reflect brighter scenes, which is a bit distracting. It's a minor flaw, but if I decide to keep this set, I'll likely paint that thin strip of the stand with some flat black spray paint or use some flat black tape to cover it and eliminate the reflection. Of course if you mount this set on the wall, then this won't be an issue at all. (Update 6/10/2012 - As it turns out, this reflection from the stand is really not an issue. I rarely even notice it at all.)

So far I'm very pleased with the set. As I said, I'll report back in a few days.

5/20/2012 Update
It's now been 4 full days of owning the LG 60PM6700 and thus far it has surpassed my expectations. The picture quality, color, brightness, and black levels, etc... ALL AMAZING! I've been through three other large screen TV's. Let's just say I'm pretty picky when it comes to being satisfied with a television. My first was a 50" Samsung I had for exactly 4 years, and it died. I purchased a LG 55LW6500 LED 3D TV, which I sent back due to horribly intolerable motion blur and judder. I then purchased a 60" Panasonic TC-P60S30, which had an incredibly dark picture and overall substandard picture quality. That one went back after trying to live with it for nearly 3 months. I also own two 40" LCD TV's which are in our bedrooms. Both of the LCDs have great picture quality. Until now, the best of all of them was definitely the Samsung plasma I had, but this new LG blows them all away.

The picture detail of the LG 60PM6700 is crystal clear. The colors are awesome, the brightness is great, and the black levels are very good. I have some coppied DVDs that I burned to back up some of my favorite movies. Often the picture quality from the copied DVDs is far less than that of the originals. This TV converts the signal to a higher definition and makes even my worst copies of DVDs look pretty amazing; much better than on any TV I've ever viewed them. The 3D is pretty cool, especially the 2D to 3D conversion. It's pretty cool watching sports (I really only religiously follow drag racing) and flipping through family photos converted to 3D. This TV has so many bells and whistles. I love the apps. The web browser is a bit cumbersome, but with some practice I can see it getting easier. The smart phone app pretty much replaces the Magic Remote, so no real need to purchase that if you have an iPhone or Android.

I have yet to see a perfect television. In my opinion, as of yet, they just don't exist. It seems every set has its flaws. What one excels at in one area, has its shortcomings in other areas. I don't believe in rating a TV 5 stars if it has flaws, no matter how pleased I am. It doesn't leave anywhere to go with the rating when you do find that "perfect TV," so it just dilutes the whole rating system. This is why I give this TV 4 stars and not 5.

So here are the flaws:
*There is some noticeable ghosting on moving objects; some content worse than others.
*I've noticed some slight motion judder on occasions, and some motion blur; again only on occasions.
*That super thin frame doesn't remain as thin when watching the TV. LG has added an additional black boarder around the actual picture, when then increases the total frame width to about an inch when the TV is turned on. I wish they had not done that because one of the beautiful features about the TV's design is that very thin half inch frame, but even with the addition of about another half in when the set is on, it's still a very thin frame, and very attractive design. Odd that they did that though because it's misleading to claim a super thin frame, if it's only super thin when the set is turned off.
*The Active 3D isn't the greatest to watch is even a moderately lit room like mine. In the light of the room your peripheral vision will pick up the flickering of the glasses, when can be a bit distracting, or for some, even annoying. (In a dim setting, you can't see it, so it's not an issue at all, and the 3D looks great. The 3D has some nice adjustment features which does allow the viewer to tweak the 3D effect to their comfort level, and the glasses are very lightweight.)

So, as of day 4, I'm amazed at the picture quality, and all this set has to offer. If my opinion changes, I'll surely update my review.

Update 6/10/2012
I've now owned this television for exactly a month, and I have to say, this is the best television I've ever owned. In my opinion, those rating this TV 2 stars have not compared it in their home to other 60" televisions; but I have. I also believe they aren't realizing that all TVs have their flaws in some area or another. I've compared a lot of sets and I can say with confidence, there simply is no perfect television on the market, and the larger TV, the more magnified the flaws. I have compared the LG 60PM6700 to other 60" televisions I've owned, and to other's I have not owned, and can safely say this TV blows the others away; especially for the money. I originally purchased the television for $1,499 and since then Amazon has lowered the price to $1,299 I called customer service and they promptly refunded me the difference. Trust me when I say, for the money, even at $1,499 you can't go wrong with this television. The picture quality, along with all its bells and whistles, blows away much more expensive TVs that make all sorts of grand claims.

Also the fan is bigger and MUCH louder than my old card and of a cheaper build. Heck, I broke it on the first day but managed to superglue it back together. I'm actually tempted to put an aftermarket cooler on it but this negates the 3 year warranty. Even the power plugs are wobbly. I guess I can't really complain for the price?

title: Great Box but not perfect
text:
The Roku arrived promptly and in good condition and setup was as easy as pie. While the registration is easy and straight-forward enough, it is first of all a bit tedious to go through, and not sure if they really do need that much personal information? I provided accurate info, but I am not sure why they'd want all your address and phone information too?

While I am more than happy with it, I decided to retract one star for the following:
- Settings look to default to 720p screen format and lower bandwidths.
Not sure if the setup does some autodetect, but if it did, it failed. If not, users need to be aware that they may not be looking at the best possible picture quality, make sure to go through your settings and adjust if you do have 1080p and the bandwidth to go with it.
- Personal media and DLNA.
Roku still does not support DLNA or other common (local) media servers.
If you have a stash of media files on your computer, you need to run plex or similar server to watch it on the Roku. Not a deal breaker, but it does add setup, registration and some skills to get it all working.
Perhaps Roku thinks DLNA support is not an issue because more and more TVs have DLNA and network support built-in? They are discounting perhaps that a lot of people purchasing a roku may do this also for adding streaming to TVs that are not yet internet enabled? (Like my 6 year old Sony Bravia that is still working perfectly fine (HD 1080p), but lacks media / internet / streaming features.
- Youtube
Seriously? I know there is legal issues involved here too, but seriously? I know people where this would be the only argument they need to get apple TV or similar.

title: Comments on 20x80 models vs 25-125 zoom
text:
Tried both Celestron 20x80 and then their 25-125x80 looking for more power, mainly for daytime viewing. Also looked at some other brands, their websites for tech data, and some videos on YouTube.

My amateur observations, hope they are helpful:

OVERALL:
* Field of view (FOV) was more of a factor than I thought. Besides a wider, non-telescope view it helps with spotting far off objects, stars, and moving boats & planes. See specifics below.
* Some high end binocs for $2,000 only go to 25x-40x so extra power can be wasted on quality/FOV
* Built-in tripod adapters work very well--a tripod is essential
* Decent tripod for a DLSR is fine, don't need a huge expensive one for these ~5 lb items. Try to get one with a nice swiveling head & crank to easily raise/lower binocs for different height people.

SPECIFC MODELS:
*20x80... good power and best FOV. Celestron has 195' at 1,000 yds, Orion has 168', Baraska has 189'
* Celestron 25x70... FOV less at ~142' and Brightness factor only 7.8 vs 16 in their 20x80 model above. Weight is less at 52 oz vs 75-80oz in all 20x80 models above.
* Celestron 25-125x80... FOV only ~65' so looked like a telescope view. Zoom lever easy to use but could not get my collimation adjustment to cure the double image when zooming. Weight 76 oz and Brightness of 10.2.
* Baraska 30x80... FOV of 111' and weight of 69 oz. No other specs.
* Celestron 25x100... FOV of ~158', Brightness of 16 but weight of 140 oz!

SUMMARY:
* Happy with my 20x80, all 3 brands above are decent. Personally like the Celestron 195' FOV.
* Returning the 25-125 model and don't recommend it for its small FOV, wasted power, and zoom calibration issues.
* For slightly more power, the 25x70 or 30x80 might work but have not tried them
* The 25x100 costs 3x and weighs 2x so personally don't want it. But, should be better for night viewing.
* Do recommend a fixed vs zoom binoc at these aperture sizes.
* If power is critical, could also get smaller (40-60 aperture) binocs that zoom to 30x-40x for those special occasions. Maybe even a spotting scope.

Anyhow, enjoy whatever you select and good luck!

title: Great 7" tablet, except for the Wifi
text:
I was looking forward to getting this tablet. I couldn't wait. I tried every tablet that I could find at the local Best Buy, and this is the only Android tablet that I was interested in. I finally got it yesterday. Almost everything about it is great. The screen is amazing. It's bright and crisp. I've seen complaints about honeycomb, but I had no problems with it at all. My only other Android device is an Evo, so it took a bit of getting used to the differences. But I was fully up and running with a complete understanding of the tablet in less than an hour. The only problem I had with it is the Wifi. I don't know if it is is a problem with just the one that I have, or if it is a problem in general. If I am standing in front of the router with the tab aimed at the router, I get full bars. If I turn my back on the router, it drops one bar. If I walk twenty or so feet away, it loses another bar. I also have an iPad2 and an iPod. I tested it against the wireless capabilities on the iPad, iPod, and my Evo, and none of those suffer from the Wifi attenuation like my tab. In areas where the Galaxy Tab could not connect, my other wireless devices showed full signal, and were able to connnect and browse at full speed. I noticed that if I moved my hands a bit around it, I got a better signal. But the signal was the absolute worst when I had both hands holding it at the bottom. That is naturally where I hold a device of this size. I also tried all of this on two different wireless networks. Same exact results.
I am very sad. I was really looking forward to this purchase. But I have no real use for a tablet with flaky Wifi. I wonder if this is an issue with the positioning of the Wifi antenna, or if it is just a weak antenna. I wonder if it is a problem with all Galaxy Tab 7.0 units, or just the one that I had.

** EDIT, 10/19/14: I'm sorry to report that I have to drop my rating for the EZ-Swap4 down to one star. To be certain that the stalling wasn't a problem with the drive itself, I moved it to an external e-sata dock. The drive was still fairly hot, but it worked perfectly, so the drive is clearly in good shape (it's also a lot cooler, due to a proper functioning of the self-cooled external dock).

I'm not sure it's worth spending the money to send another unit back to the manufacturer, but at any rate, I cannot recommend the EZ-Swap4. **
__________________________

(previous review follows)

I bought this bay a few months ago, and so far its performance has been excellent, keeping a 7200 RPM, 3tb hard drive at or below 95 degrees Fahrenheit. This is far better than the last dock I bought which had no fan and let the hard drive really cook. I also appreciate the full size of the dock, as opposed to a smaller unit with brackets to meet the side walls of the tower's drive bay. I was a little annoyed at the Molex power connector on a dock built for SATA drives, but an inexpensive adapter took care of that.

One interesting bit of business is that in Windows 7 (64-bit Pro, if that matters), inserting a drive in this dock kicks up the systray icon for removing/ejecting a USB drive. I didn't expect this, but it's hardly a problem.

Also, it should be noted that while the stats here at Amazon and on the box say it only supports SATA I/II, Vantec's website specifies support for SATA III, as well (same model name and number). It appears that the stats here were written before SATA became available or common.

My only concern with this dock, and my reason for leaving off one star, is that within the past couple of weeks the fan has been very noisy at startup. This occurs whether the drive is in the dock when the computer is turned on or inserted in the dock after the computer is running. The fan quiets down to a very soft hum after about 20-30 minutes and runs regardless (the temperature would go way up without it) but the fact that this noise is recent is troubling. I'm past the return period for Amazon, so I'm contacting the company to ask about it.

EDIT: I'm a little late getting back to this, but I sent the unit back for a replacement and they sent it out promptly. The new unit was virtually silent at first, but I'm noticing some fan noise again. This will require continual monitoring, and I'll post back with any updates.

title: After a few months...
text:
Not sure if I would go as far as and recommend this cam after using it for a few months.

First off, there is ZERO support for this device from the manufacturer, Lukas. If you have any questions or issues you have to go back to the person or distributor where you bought it from. They more than likely will reject you.

Issues and concerns so far:

A. Poor GPS sensitivity despite unobstructed clear view of the sky. GPS typically doesn't work.

1. No support from anyone on this cam....it's like buying from ebay.
2. Lukas website is very poorly designed. You can download the firmware which changes monthly but it may not be easily found.
3. To update your firmware, you require the Lukas Viewer which allows you the ability to indepth change your settings and format your device's memory card
4. Lukas removed the Lukas Viewer manual from their website. The manual describes and instructs you on what settings to use for your camera
5. MicroSD ejection mechanism is overly aggressive. I lost the MicroSD in the car's vents because it was so powerful, it propelled it more than 1.5 meters into the vent, never to be found again
6. Life expectancy of OEM memory cards is no more than 6 months.
7. CPL filter is essentially useless. There is no instructions on how to install and more importantly, Lukas says it's not to recommended to be used in nightime which renders it useless.

Overall, if you need a front and rear cam, maybe, and I mean maybe consider this cam. Otherwise, consider a dash cam from the other major players like Garmin.

title: A good device, but has flaws that need to be considered before purchasing
text:
I have been using a GPSmap 62s for a couple of years now as my companion for off-road adventures (wheeling, hiking, kayaking, snowshoeing, backcountry snowboarding, and geocaching, mostly). It's a good device, but I have not been completely pleased with the quality or reliability. It's a good buy, but be prepared to deal with some of it's quirks and some minor annoyances.

First, the good:
- It's easy to hold in all weather, even with gloves on, thanks to it's shape and rubberized grip.
- It has physical buttons, not a touch screen, so that if you hands are wet/damp or you have gloves on you can still operate the buttons (unlike those touch screen units that become a little frustrating when water or gloves enter the picture). Love that about it.
- It gets great battery life. I use rechargeable batteries in it and this thing is a power mizer compared to what I expected. Very pleased with that.
- You can attach the device to a computer as a mass storage device and load/remove GPX files or view geocache logs, you don't need to use a cache manager, and this means that Linux users can use this for geocaching with little fuss.
- It gets a lock quickly and seems to hold tight. Dense canopies don't seem to bother it, and it does very well in the city too where some other units bounce too much. I've seen it have minor difficulty at high altitude, where it will have some trouble and bounce around more than you'd expect it to on wide open mountain summits, but reading changelogs on firmware updates makes it seem like that was a bug that may have been addressed.

But, the bad:
- The menuing system is a bit kludgy. Garmin would benefit from doing some UX work so that menus flow more logically and that it does not take so many clicks to perform actions or activities. In this day where user testing is common practice for software development it appears as if Garmin is shortcutting that step here and it shows. When you're trying to keep it clean and dry, or worrying about hands getting cold, that time clicking and navigating matters!
- It's not the most reliable device I've ever had. Occasionally with no real rhyme or reason the device seems to have a display freezing issue where even though you move your person, and the unit displays changes in distance to destination on the screen, the directional indicator stays stationary. Only pulling the batteries solves this. When it happens in the middle of a trip out into the woods it's very annoying.
- The buttons appear to be painted, as evident by mine losing their markings, which is a disappointment given that I try to treat it with care and this type unit should be able to stand up to regular usage without having buttons that lose their markings. If those are an issue I wonder what other build quality issues might be arising in the next year or two.
- Firmware updates have been regular but with inconsistent quality. I am currently running 4.60, and it seems to be smooth sailing, but the previous firmwares were all disappointments, some even causing random screen blankings or device restarts. With this device you definitely need to give it a couple of test runs after a firmware update to make sure that it's going to serve you well when it counts. You can work around it, but firmware updates should improve things, not be a crap-shoot. When you're out alone your device needs to be bullet proof, and sometimes I worry that mine is not.

And annoying:
- Firmware and map updates require you to add a browser plug in or download Garmin WebUpdater. Great it you like to use Windows and Internet Explorer, bad if you like browser choice or use Linux. I know it's nit-picky, but when I purchase a device I expect to be able to manage it 100% without need for software, plug-ins, all of those things. That means I want to download firmware updates and apply them by grabbing a file from an FTP site or other repository. I do not expect to have to install anything or be told I can only use a certain browser or operating system. If you're of a similar mindset prepare for frustration upon purchasing this device.

Despite the GPSmap 62s having issues, it is still a good device. It's middle of the road - 3 stars. I would buy one again. Solving the firmware inconsistencies, build quality issues, and a better designed user interface would go a long way to move this into the "great" device category and earn it 4 stars. Resolving those issues and simplifying the update process would make it perfect and earn it 5 stars.

title: Save Your Money!
text:
This antenna will pick up 150 miles away, except it won't pick up any Knoxville stations less than half that distance from me. This antenna will pick up 150 miles away, except it picks up ZERO VHF stations in Chattanooga, which is less than a third that distance from me. This means I paid 130 bucks plus $12.49 shipping for what turned out to be a UHF ONLY antenna with barely a better UHF range than the 90 dollar antenna I already had and most likely the UHF only antennas that you can buy here and everywhere for even less than 90. Let me state precisely. I got ZEROS on every VHF channel meter in both Knoxville and Chattanooga and ZEROS on all Chattanooga VHF stations, not low quality reception. NO RECEPTION AT ALL!

People that give these types of long range antennas glowing reviews are people that live 10 miles out of some metropolitan area and don't know a regular antenna will do the same job for less money. They THINK they're getting a better picture because they buy lies like this thing has a 40 gain amplifier and that's why the 150 mile distance is achievable despite all other indoor/outdoor antennas only claiming half that range. Putting it outside isn't going to make up enough reception to overcome the ZEROS inside either since it's been in every spot in my garage apartment and moved inch by inch since I got it with still ZERO reception. The antenna I already had included a VHF/UHF splitter so that 90 dollar antenna that shipped FOR FREE is getting the VHF and this antenna that cost 54 dollars more with shipping is getting the UHF with only slightly better reception.

Because Amazon requires you insure the antenna for the return trip it would be pointless for me to return it and buy either another VHF/UHF antenna or just a UHF antenna with the minimal difference in money I would make up and on top of the trouble of packing it and carrying it to the Post Office since I don't own a car. And that's how companies like the one selling this antenna make their money. Lie about what it does and rely on the fact that most people are just going to eat the cost entirely or use it for what it does pick up instead of returning it for a refund.

I'm a pessimistic optimist. That means I rarely expect things to work out but still try anyway. I knew there was a greater than 90% chance an antenna claiming to pick up twice the distance of all other indoor/outdoor antennas wasn't going to work. That went up to 99% when I went to the manufacturer's site and saw a one, single, solitary and very short about us paragraph. Not a page. A PARAGRAPH. I bought it anyway since I haven't had cable since February of 2012. Don't make the same mistake. Buying both a UHF and VHF antenna separately may seem like more money, $80 + $90 = $170, and this antenna is ONLY $130 but add it up again. 90 for the antenna I already had plus 130 and shipping for this UHF antenna is $232 compared to the $170. Save your money by just passing this thing on by.

Now, Amazon can delete this review and keep posting the glowing ones since that's in their best interest but not ours.
