title: Non-Intrusive Camp/Backpacking Light, Doubles as a Book Light
text: I'm a long-time camper with a basic belief that no single light or lantern can serve all possible purposes, but I sense that some reviewers expect more of these little guys than they can possibly deliver. I now have three of these little gems. The light is very pleasant and uniform with its diamond-cut diffuser. The older models have a pair of blue LEDs, but the newer ones have warmer white LEDs. They come with a set of 3 carbon-zinc batteries (batteries ARE included!) that will run the lantern for quite a while, then switch to alkalines for long-term use. They weigh practically nothing, can be placed anywhere, include a hanger and a hideaway reflector. That reflector, I've discovered, comes in handy when reading flat on your back in your bunk or bag. Close the reflector and rest the lantern on its side on your chest. The lantern illuminates the book but doesn't get in your eyes, plus you don't have to carry a special book light, and it doesn't annoy your trying-to-sleep tentmate. I always have one of these handy by my head to reach for in the pitch dark of the camp. It's true that they don't illuminate very far, but how far is far enough? The newer [[ASIN:B00168VA9A Coleman 3AA MicroPacker LED Lantern]] clearly sheds way more light, but reviewers there complain about it being TOO bright (!) and casting a strange pattern from its reflectors. We used to have big gasoline lanterns for car camping, but they blotted out the stars and can sometimes be annoying to neighboring campers. We quit carrying them and began relying more on candle lanterns and headlamps. Candle lanterns are nice, but hot and potentially dangerous. A pair of these tiny Colemans more than suffice for a card game on the picnic table, weigh no more than candle lanterns but can be safely used inside the tent. I like them so much I will probably buy a couple more, but generally all I find we need is two or three of these Colemans, a flashlight and a headlamp each. Everyone is different (!) but we need no more light than that, PLUS they are priceless as emergency power-outage lights. Pretty good deal for the price!

title: Paintball Player Action Helmet Camera Must
text:
I have played Paintball for two decades, and always enjoyed videography of the sport. The Contour ROAM 2 takes that videography to a new level. The camera's compact design and slim profile make it ideal for my sport over the GoPro in that A) it can be mounted via gun rail mounts, and B) the goggle mounting is much easier and less bulky. The camera shoots fantastic video with a wide angle lens and 60fps at 720P or 30fps at 1080 more than enough for the recreational paintball player who wants some awesome video of their gameplay. The microphone could pick up conversations through paintball masks from other players, which I have yet to see in a camera of this type. Additionally - although Contour recommends the waterproof casing for paintball action videos, I didn't use it, nor did I see any other contour cameras on the field I played at with the case - this particular game I saw a great deal of helmet cameras many of which were contour HDs or ROAMs. I believe that the camera could take a hit from a paintball and still function properly, but that's my opinion... After each mission I just sprayed the camera off with a squirt bottle of water and bam - was off and running again.

You can see a sample video of the contour ROAM2 in action here on my youtube channel wtuller

The only negative thing I would say is that if you make the camera beeps silent - it will not beep at you if it's having an error. I lost a great deal of footage because I had the beep alerts off, and with a better design they could have made alarm noises always on no matter what your preference.

The problem I had was an operator error - but just to save everyone time and the same frustration I went through - if you're using a large memory card - it takes a long time to format... The 32GB card I was using takes about 30 seconds to format and in their instruction manual, it indicates to hold the button down for ten seconds... I did a 10 count and was off and running without a formatted memory card and lost what I believe would have been great footage.

Anyway - all in all - an awesome product.

title: CAN'T in good conscience recommend anymore :(
text:
>> UPDATE << 10 years later.
If you look below at my original review, I LOVED my Adapt-Its and gave it a 5 star 10 years ago! But a few days ago when I attached my new R6 to my Blackrapid strap, I had a Come-To-Jesus moment! My camera crashed onto the hard wood floor! The front of my lens hit first and thank Gawd I happen to have my hood on the lens which broke. I am counting my lucky stars that nothing was damaged except my hood. Upon examination, the Adapt-It broke! (see my photo). Bear in mind, I have been using this for the last 10 years without problems and the only explanation I have is some kind of MATERIAL FATIGUE?!? The "rest" of the Adapt-It is still firm and tough, but for some reason at that point in the loop, it failed and split after 10 years?!? Whatever the reason, I can't in good conscience recommend (or use) these any longer. I have switched to a metal adapter for my strap (see photo). It's not as attractive, but it'll have to do. Be safe!

========== Original review 10 years ago ==============
As others have mentioned, you actually get 4 of these little things in a package. Can't beat the price for 4 of them! There are many uses for these cool little things. I use them with my BlackRapid Rstrap. The strap has a hook which hooks to these adapt-its on the left my Canon 7D. This method leaves the smallest "footprint" of a strap I know short of not having a strap at all.

Now, here is a big tip when installing these Adapt-Its. This is only my personal experience with my Canon XSi and 7D bodies. On one side, it will be easy to push this adapt-it through the hole. You may have to flex it and bend it a little but you should be able to get it thru that side with relative ease. Now the other side where the "eyelet" for lack of a better term is recessed in a "groove", I had a tough time getting it thru that hole. Finally I just tore a small piece of paper (or anything thin and small), placed it under the adapt-it and shoved as much of it into the hole as possible. With a small edge of the paper sticking thru, I grabbed it and pull on the paper while pushing on the adapt-it. That piece of paper basically helped give me some leverage and to guide it thru the hole/eyelet. I hope that made sense. I also read that you can throw it in some hot boiling water for a few seconds to "soften" them. Then quickly push them through your camera body's strap holes. I didn't do it this way, but it makes sense and should work.

Some free advice from personal experience... if you happen to own the OPTech Utility Strap Swivel Hook, don't use that strap with these adapt-its! In my opinion that strap's "hooks" have a flawed design which enables the strap's hook to easily detach from an adapt-it or anything it's hooked to. This has nothing to do with the awesomeness of the Adapt-Its, but just thought I'd mention it :)

A note about the strength of these little things. I have them on my Canon 7D with battery grip and a 70-200 f/2.8IS attached and the Utility Strap Swivel Hook By Op/Tech USA and I have no fears about my camera falling or breaking off my neck. I've also read others mention how they've tested these by hanging heavy things on these adapt-its overnight without problems. I tend to agree... so far I have no fear about these things breaking. They are tough little things. Try em. They're cheap.

title: Auto Mode Does Not Work Well
text: This amp has two features that make it not work very well when the auto power mode is selected.  First, it makes a single thump sound when it powers up from it's standby mode.  Second, it appears to go to standby too readily when connected to a receiver with a subwoofer output.  So what happens due to these two issue issues is that you get a frequent thump when listening to music that only occasionally has some low frequency (bass) content.  You can avoid this by leaving the power switch in the "on" position instead of "auto".  There will be a bit more power drain, but if nothing is playing, the amplifier uses only about 22 watts (the standy mode appears to consume about 11 watts).

title: Great TV Lousy kids Toy Remote
text: I have owned this great 65inch 3D HDTV for 3 months. I love the picture quality and the 3D is fantastic. I bought this 65inch set based on how happy I was with my 42inch LG set (now my bedroom set). Now for the bad news. THE REMOTE CONTROL is supposed to be simple by having a minimum number of buttons. It is supposed to simplify operating the TV. After 2 days of using this remote I was ready to throw it at the screen. Instead of pushing a button for a function you must now point at the screen to move a pointer on the screen, and then go through menu after menu to get what you want! If you have a shaky hand you will miss icons on the screen and have to start all over. My nephew has MS and can't hit an icon on this TV to save his life, yet he can text messages on a smart phone like a pro. There are no number buttons so now you must scroll with a thumb wheel or wave the remote to get an icon of a keypad then try to hit the channel number you want. LG should give you a regular remote option or include both with this TV. I will never again buy a HDTV with a made for kids toy REMOTE CONTROL. title: Evolutionary, not revolutionary
text:
There's a lot to like about the Amazon Fire TV. It's zippy, unobtrusive, and the remote feels luxe. There's also much to dislike: the perplexing lack of HBOGo, the Netflix app looks several-generations dated, and the strange choice to implement the marquee feature (voice search) solely with Amazon's content.

My biggest issue is as an Amazon Prime member. I expected a much easier way to find & discover Prime video content. This isn't the case, since the Fire has no visible notation of what is Prime content during search, until you drill down into a show.

As the UI on the Fire TV stands now, you are forced to select a show from Amazon's library, and then maneuver to that specific episode's page, and then select the option to watch for free below the purchase buttons. Prime video content, It may be included, but it's impossible to tell at a glance what is/isn't free without some effort. I understand that Amazon is trying to sell content, but offering Prime video as a selling feature, and then making it incredibly challenging to find isn't the way to build user loyalty.

Update: after reading this review, Amazon attempted to call me, and then sent a follow up email. The email is pasted below:

Hello,

Tried giving you a ring but wasnt able to get a hold of you, after reading your review figured I would give you a heads that what your looking for will be coming sorry for the wait though.

With a free software update being delivered to you this Spring, you will be able to browse several categories of Prime content, including, but not limited to: Top Prime TV, Top Prime Movies, Prime TV for Kids, Prime Movies for Kids, Prime TV by Genre, and Prime Movies by Genre.

HBO GO will become available on Amazon Fire TV later this year. HBO GO is HBO's authenticated streaming service offering subscribers instant access to over 1,700 titles online including every episode of new and classic HBO series, as well as HBO original films, miniseries, sports, documentaries, specials and a wide selection of blockbuster movies.

In addition, classic HBO programming will also soon be available on Amazon Prime Instant Video.

Thanks for using Amazon Fire TV.

Best regards,
Brandon H

title: Pass on this if you have large laptop or hips!
text:
I was dissappointed when I received this laptop stand for several reasons...

1) The other reviews are absolutely true that the attached light is totally weak and useless, the plastic this stand is made of is cheap and flimsy, and with the legs fully extended, this stand will topple over at the slightest bump because the ends are rounded and barely touching the surface.

2) If you are pear-shaped and full-figured like myself (size 22)or even if you are just very muscular with thick thighs, this laptop will not fit you with the legs extended to the "first" position. The hard, rough-edged bottom of the stand winds up digging into your legs, scratching you up and sitting crooked on your lap. In order for you to use it, you have to fully extend the legs out to its last position. This makes the laptop stand too high up to type comfortably unless you lift the split top up to tilt the laptop towards you. Which leads me to the next issue...

3) The split top is held up by a single plastic piece (on one side only) that you slide into plastic slots to raise it to different angles (functioning silimilarly like a car hood). Problem is, this plastic piece is flimsy and your laptop wobbles with every keystroke that you type. Also, the split top is barely wide enough to fit a 15-inch laptop. If you have a 17-inch laptop...forget about it! Your laptop won't even stay on the stand in "split top mode".

Overall, I gave this 2 stars only because for the right sized person, with the right sized laptop or netbook, this stand could be worth it for the price. Otherwise, I wouldn't bother paying for this. You would come out just as good buying a $10 breakfast tray.

And you can get a bunch of on-line services, movies and shows, which you can't with the standard bottom feeder digital cable box that you're paying $10 - $14 a month for.

The FCC has required the cable companies to mail you a CableCARD if you call and ask for one, so you can avoid waiting at home for the cable guy. Follow the onscreen step-by-step --it's easier than the printed "Quick Start" sheet. While cable industry support of retail CableCARD products used to be horrendous and still sometimes is, the requirement that they use CableCARDs in their own boxes, and that they must support mailed CableCARDs, has required systems to automate their support -- though you still have to make a phone call to read them the numbers on the screen after the CableCARD is in. Was real easy for me. Then it takes about an hour to download all the channel info online. (The free Guide is better than the guide in low-end boxes, at least in my system.)

I represent consumer electronics manufacturers who've been frustrated in trying to get support for competitive products like this. TiVo has made it work, now Samsung. (And it's about 1/4 the size of the cranky rented box it replaced.)

title: Big Impressive and Great Quality
text:
I acquired my Canon EF 400mm f4 DO IS USM lens (hereafter known as the lens) just recently and am very happy with it. I can say this with certainty "don't expect those fantastic shots to pop out of the camera the first time you use it". There is a learning curve to it. I've had other super telephotos (above 400mm) in the past from Sigma and even from Canon itself and generally was only OK with the results. The past lenses were either too slow or somewhat soft. I do have a Canon 300mm f4 L that has been fantastic so when I purchased this I had great expectations.

While this does not have an L lens monogram or red stripe it is absolutely a PRO lens. It is impressive to look at and stands out with its white finish. So if your trying to blend in with the crowd this is NOT the lens for you. The build quality is nothing short of superb. It is short and light for a 400mm lens. Shorter and lighter even than their 300mm f2.8 L. This was the reason I chose this lens.

I mated it up with both a 7d and a 50d so both were crop camera formats. I did my first day shooting (nothing more than testing it out) and was somewhat disappointed. I thought it was my technique. I had some fantastic hits but they were few. So I got out a yardstick and set it up at about 30' at a diagonal to the camera (on a tripod with stabilizer off) and focused at the middle of the yardstick. The lens consistently focused at the 26-28" mark while I was focusing at 18". So it was back focusing by 10" at 30'. No wonder it had such a poor hit rate. So using the cameras' micro-adjust I tuned the lens in for each camera. NOW, the hit rate was much more in line with what I expected.
The next day my friend and I went to a close by bird sanctuary. Generally the conditions were only poor with light being a problem (clouds) all day yet the lens did fairly well with a high ISO to keep speeds up. My hand held shots were better at first than with the mono-pod that I brought along. Even though I was using mode 2 for the mono-pod (this is supposed to be OK with a mono-pod) the lens made the pics blurry due to lack of movement to compensate. I guess I must be a rock when using the mono-pod. When I turned it off it did fine. I was able to hand hold with Stabilization to about 1/250 sec easily with a high hit rate. Pictures at 1/125 are possible with IS but I wouldn't recommend it. Birds in flight were able to be captured as the auto focus is almost instant and these were done hand held. I tried the 1.4X converter and it was still very sharp. In fact you really can't tell the difference. This isn't true with the 2.0X but still very good. There were NO discernible chromatic aberrations in the pictures even where you would almost always get them (dark lines on light backgrounds).

Was I elated with the performance. Not quite. In fact I would have only given the lens 4.5 stars if I could. The reason was the bokeh. Not always bad. Some results were spectacular and buttery smooth but when there were specular highlights the background looked weird with some "busy" patterns to the bokeh ( a result of the diffractive optics). Another reason is that it can be short on contrast in some situations. Both problems are easily taken care of in Photo Shop so it isn't a deal breaker.

So in conculusion
Pros- Light weight (for a super telephoto), probably the only 400mm that is truly hand holdable, sharp, excellent build quality, VERY fast
Cons- Expensive, can have busy bokeh, contrast low in some situations.

Is it worth it? If your like me and want to carry it on trails and hand hold when I need to there isn't anything else... So Yea!

UPDATE: As I have gained experience with this lens I have found that if you are using ANY support (tripod, monopod etc.) turn off the stabilizer. It will blur the pics (makes a funny clicking noise too). If I hand hold I can get great shots down to 1/250 sec with IS as stated in review. The instructions seem to indicate that in mode 2 you can use a monopod but I have found that not to be the case. If I turn the IS off and use 1/500th or faster with support I get tack sharp results. But I can do the same with equal results hand held and IS on.

From my own experience, as far as Netflix videos go, the app takes a little while to load... longer than you usually want to wait. Playing the videos is fine. However, it seems to re-buffer at random intervals during playback. This only seems to happen when your download speed is lower than around 12 Mb/s (megaBITS NOT megaBYTES). This also means that if your downlink is around 15 Mb/s and another device on your network is using half the bandwidth, this re-buffering may happen to you as well.

Other than that, a fair player.

title: Great alternative to Beats solo hd
text:
Sennheiser is a reputable company who specialize in sound. As far as quality goes, these headphones are comfortable and can be worn for hours without any noticeable discomfort. Style wise, I would say these are the best looking of Sennheiser's sub $100 price range models. The ear cups fit over the ear to help block outside noise and the foam is covered in a soft fabric vs synthetic leather. I find this material reduces sweat, especially if wearing for longer listening sessions. An added bonus is the set comes with two different length cables (1.4m & 3m) and a 6mm plug adapter (gold plated).

When compared to the beats solo hd headphones, both sets have a similar frequency range. The big difference is the Sennheiser's carry a relative flat curve across much of low and mid-range frequencies where the solo's tend to be all over the place. What does this mean? Basically the flatter the EQ, the more likely you will hear the sound the way the recording was intended to be heard. The Sennheiser's do a much better job delivering the sound the way it was intended vs the solo hd beats.

With that being said, I think the beats are stylish and they have the plus of an inline mic/volume controls. In my opinion, those two pluses do not justify having to spend twice as much money for lower quality sound. You'll be hard pressed to find this nice of a headphone for the price ($65-$70 on Amazon). I've been using mine since December and have been extremely pleased with the HD 439s.

title: My take but you might want to know
text:
**My review from the Microsoft Store**

UPDATE 12/24: Ok, so I had enough of the touchpad and bought a mouse. As far as the keyboard goes - I have some good days and some annoying days with it. I did see that Acer promotes that the screen is fingerprint proof but I would have to disagree.

UPDATE 12/3:
Me and this keyboard are still not getting along; it has gotten a little better but I am still experiencing mistakes that I usually just dont make. On top of that now the touch pad and I are also having our learning curve. There just seems to be some responsive issues with both. It is not a deal breaker with me because it has gotten better but I feel people will notice within the first day of use.

The battery life for me is pretty good; medium usage of browsing, office use, videos and varying brightness last me about 4-6hrs. Safe to say independent usage may vary and how it impacts battery life but on days where I have minimal use and low screen brightness I can squeeze 8hrs out.

I did have a nuisance with the auto brightness feature as it adjust to the surrounding lighting environment. I ultimately turned this feature off as it was so frequent throughout the day.

The hinge for the screen is still as good as day one; very solid feel and I am often changing the viewing angle as needed.

1 - WEIGHT: In comparison to a Dell Vostro 13 which is a fairly light laptop and thin; the R13 is thinner and lighter. 2 - SCREEN: The viewing angle, brightness and clarity are really nice. No complaints at the moment. The different movement positions of the screen is a key feature of why I purchased this laptop. I had always looked at the XPS 12 from Dell but the 13.3 in screen is my mark for laptops. It moves with an assured feeling in the hinge design. 3 - KEYBOARD: This is a grey area at the moment; Its not the same keyboard layout like the Vostro 13 which is fine but I feel as if I am making more typing mistakes. This might need more time but the best way I can describe it is that I get a lot of double letters in words which never happened to me before. I do enjoy the back-lighting. Just in writing this short review I have had to correct many spelling mistakes.

Overall I am excited about this laptop - this type of design as first seen from the Dell XPS 12 has always been on my radar and in my opinion is what a laptop design should be. This should be the standard - it provides the common use of a standard laptop but with the added benefit of taking laptop design to other configurations.

Battery life has been on the good side but currently with low to medium usage. Could this cheaper in cost; sure, but at this price still a good value so that if it does go on sale it will be an even better purchase.

title: Good for running in-wall
text:
This is a good cable for running in an enclosed wall.

Why use CL-Rated cable?
The main reason I'd recommend spending a little more to get the CL rated cable is not because it's going to give you a better signal, but because it means the manufacturer has tested the cable to meet the standards necessary to run in wall. HDMI signals aren't high power so it's highly unlikely they would cause a fire, but if you ever did have a fire you don't want to deal with an insurance company saying they won't compensate for damages because they found the wrong cabling in the wall. To me, that's the value equation you have to apply when considering running cable in an enclosed wall.

Why use this particular cable?
The cable itself is pliable and i didn't have any problems with kinking. I don't know the exact dimension of the plugs, but I used a 5/8 spade bit to drill my holes and I was able to pass the connector through. It's a snug fit through there, so if you're planning to run other cable in the same holes, I'd suggest running this HDMI cable first, then any other cabling. The plugs come with plastic guards on the end which helps keep drywall mud out of the connector - something to consider depending on your application.

title: These are awesome little radios; best price is at Amazon
text:
I can't add much to what people have already said about this great little radio. It's fun, it works well, it looks good and it uses no batteries. It is LOUD. It sounds just like the transistor radios from the seventies, but doesn't require the expensive 9v battery. Speaker is a little tinny, but what do expect from such a small unit? Tuning is very sensitive and forgiving, but it can be prone to change once you walk away from it, but that's all radios except really high end ones.

One important improvement over the old transistor radios is the shape. This radio is more cube shaped. The old transistor radios were tall and skinny and were easily knocked over, even from their own vibrations. This little unit is solid and stays put.

The other thing is that I shop around for the best prices and here at Amazon, this radio costs less than half here than what some other sites are selling it for ($40). Buy two and get free shipping. Keep one for home and leave the other in the car or the office in case of emergency.

Side note: I bought three green ones and a black one. The black one did not work very well. The wind crank was much easier to turn and operated more smoothly, which was nice, but it received no AM at all and both the tuning dial and the volume control on the BLACK one were sloppy compared to the green one. This was very disappointing. I don't mind that much. I'll get another green one to replace it. Now that I've seen both in person, the green ones, I think, actually look better.

title: This lens is a keeper
text:
This is the primary lens on my Nikon D5200. At 7.8x zoom, it covers almost all my focal length needs, with surprisingly few optical compromises. Build quality is solid with near premium materials. It's reasonably sharp at all focal length. Focusing performance is superb: lightning fast, and always on target. There is essentially no focus hunting, even in low light. At longer focal lengths, you get a nice background blur. The zoom gears are a little on the stiff side, but as a result there is absolutely no zoom creep. At 55 mm focal length, the aperture opens to f4.8, which is one-half stop brighter than the f5.6 value of Nikon's 18-55 basic kit zoom at the same focal length.

What are the downsides?
In the first place, a well built long zoom like this is going to be big and heavy. There is no way around it. It took me a couple of weeks to get used to its size.
When zoomed out, the top edge of the lens does cast a small shadow when the built in flash is used. It's only noticeable in certain situation.
There is minor barrel distortion at the wide end, but it can be easily corrected manually in-camera if it bothers you. Nikon has not issued a firmware update for automatic distortion correction yet.
The image colors taken by this lens are not as vibrant as what you get with a prime, but certainly no worse than the standard 18-55 mm VR kit.

Regarding the price. This lens is listed at $600, but the price drops down to $350 when purchased as a kit along with Nikon D5300 or D7100.

Verdict: A perfect all around lens for your Nikon DSLR if you don't mind the bulk

title: 70" --- Excellent
text:
I've had my Sony KDL 70R550a for about three weeks.

I don't know if the screen is different in the smaller sizes of this Sony HDTV, but I must say that my experience has been excellent. Right out of the box, enjoyed it. Did some calibrating using the Disney WOW disc and basically needed to tone down the overall brightness and not much more. With most items "OFF", the TV is great for sports...caught the final two games of the hockey championships, and enjoyed some golf and tennis, too. Used the Simulated 3D with these shows and the presentation was fantastic. I'm amazed what can be done by the set "on the fly."

Watching Titanic 3D made my wife a believer. Her initial hesitance has been brushed aside. And did I mention the tennis (she is an avid fan and this made her day.)

The screen is somewhat more reflective than my Sony XBR 52" Bravia, but not to the
point that it is a problem.
I do see a bit of drop off as I move about eight feet from center when twelve feet from the screen but I've got a Onkyo/Polk sound set-up and I'm not going to watch from a severe angle anyway. And, when in the kitchen (45* or more off center) it still looks good.

No light bleed or "pizza slices" of white, no dots, dead pixels, or other problems that seem to float around the HDTV reviews. Terrific TV experience and I lucked out on the purchase which included a Sony 3D BD player and year of Netflix and Hulu.

title: Awesome laptop for the price, if you take care of it...
text:
I dont know what all the negative reviews are about, but I paid less than $700 for this laptop on black friday nearly 4 YEARS AGO and I am currently writing this review on that same laptop. This is the first laptop I've ever bought or owned and I am so happy I got it. At first I used for standard uses like school and internet and storing my music collection and later I started using it with FL Studio for music production. I am amazed how well this laptop handles while running FL Studio, of course after making all the neccesary adjustments to give CPU priority to FL Studio. But, my more recent projects are more elaborate and require more RAM and a better processor, which is why Im finally starting to consider getting another laptop. In 4 years of use, the only things I've had to replace are the keyboard (a cheap, easy DIY fix) and the laptop battery which is to be expected. I will admit that some of the horror stories about the inspiron 1525 are true, for example,
1. The screen with no hooks is annoying and dangerous. Whenever I travel with this laptop, I have to surround it with towels/shirts to make sure it is safe and does not open.
2. The stupid "sunken left mouse button" issue. Ive heard this happens to literally every dell inspiron 1525, as it did to mine. Like others have said, it still functions fine, but no click. The button has sunk into the laptop a bit.
3. The trackpad issues. About 2 years ago, I did have to take this back to bestbuy because the trackpad stopped working. 6 weeks later, got it back with no problems. Heard this is a common issue.

Those are basically the only issues I encountered in the 4 years Ive owned this laptop and its still running strong. The HDMI output, 3GB RAM, low price, and Duo-Core processor are what attracted to me this laptop back in 2008 and I've been using this thing religiously since. My only complaints besides the 3 common issues above are the placement of the headphone jacks (why would you put them in the front of the laptop and not the side), and also the small 160GB harddrive. However, a 2TB external drive I just got made that issue irrelevant. My favorite thing about this laptop to this day is still the HDMI output. So awesome!

title: Great build quality, glitchy slow system
text:
When I first unwrapped the Thinkpad Tablet 2 I was in awe. Being primarily an apple user over the last few years I was seriously impressed by the build quality and construction of this device. I love the soft touch finish that makes it very easy to grip it is a simple and elegant device, and oh so very slim. The Thinkpad tablet 2 is so slim and light I thought whoa this is my dream note-taking device before I had even turned it on....

Then I turned it on....

Within ten minutes I was ready to sell it on ebay heres why -

The Thinkpad tablet is seriously slow with its Atom processor. I think full windows 8 on a tablet this underpowered and slow was an impossible dream. The pen could keep up with my writing and showed little lag but when trying to lasso text it was like using an archaic machine. When I began loading windows office on the device I was seriously shocked how long downloads took, and forget using the device while something is downloading in the background.

After less than ten minutes the tablet would not go back to the windows screen from tile mode when I pressed the home button. I decided maybe it was a glitch so I reset factory settings (which worked! But you should seriously not have to spent an hr every ten minutes resetting item to factory settings so that tablet becomes functional again)

I think it does a good job for note-taking and the pen was fluid and could keep up well. It would be an excellent device for highlighting pdf's, they just might take a while to load.

I think if you prioritize LONG battery life, Good looks, Slim and light profile, above all else and are willing to sacrifice performance and wait around for long load times you might just love this tablet.

Its not for me. I am too impatient :)

text: I bought this so that my wife could have a new laptop she could also use when doing educational software with the grandkids.  A key feature for that latter purpose was being able to use a relative large touchscreen rather than a mouse, and the size of the touchscreen has worked out well.  The FLIP part is not terribly easy to execute, but being able to position the screen in that fashion is also nice for grandkid touchscreen use (or video viewing, I suppose) once you get it flipped.  In many respects it is a fine machine (the numeric keypad is a nice feature), but the main problem is that it is very SLOW.  When a two-year old touches a virtual button on the screen, s/he does not want to wait five or ten seconds for something to happen.  I realize that using that AMD processor is part of making it an inexpensive unit (which is also a plus in this case), but Lenovo gave up too much in the way of speed with this model.  My other complaint has to do with the battery charging system.  If you leave it plugged in you get a message that battery is overcharging, and then when you leave it unplugged you have to deal with low battery issues before long.  They need a better battery management system so everything works if you just leave it plugged in all the time as we routinely have done with laptops when we are at home.  With a bit more speed and a better battery system, it would easily move to four stars and maybe to five.

title: Warranty Period May Not Be the Advertised 2 Years
text:
This drive failed without any warning on March 26, 2014--the dreaded clicks. Amazon showed I bought the product on September 3, 2012 and the product page stipulates a limited 2-year warranty, so I decided to get a warranty replacement. However, Seagate's warranty check stated that my warranty ran out on September 29, 2013. Upon calling Seagate's customer service, I was informed that this product only has a 1-year warranty. I am currently contesting this based on the clearly visible information on Seagate's product page that this product has a 2-year warranty. I trust Seagate will take appropriate action to remedy this inconsistency in their warranty validation database, but if not, I wish to warn Amazon users here that the warranty period listed for this product (and perhaps others) is incorrect.

Update 1: After sending documentation about the stated warranty period, Seagate agreed to update their warranty database for my particular case. (Although, scanning through more recent reviews, at least two other users already had this problem, so I don't know why the remedy wasn't global for this product line--one wonders if Seagate hopes most customers won't bother with contesting the warranty period). The response to the documentation was quick, which I appreciated. However, although they said the fix will propagate in 4hrs such that the RMA can be generated, it's been 9hrs and the validation tool still says my HDD is out of warranty. I'll leave another update once this makes progress.

Update 2: Twitter customer support is the way to go. I contacted @AskSeagate overnight, and once they woke up they sorted out my problem in relatively short order with appropriate ETAs for fix. Still think this HDD is not what it's made out to be (and the warranty info isn't fixed as far as I can tell) but added one more star for efficient customer service once you reach the right channels.

Update 3: Unfortunately, the HDD did not get shipped out within the period advertised (chose advance replacement). Downgraded to 1 star.

Update 4: The replacement HDD was dead on arrival (clicking already). Would downgrade to 0 stars if I could.

title: DROBO Poor Software Engineering
text:
I purchased a first generation DROBO zillions of years ago when it was brand new. It has been connected to my computer via USB since that time. It had its start-up problems, as all new-tech devices do; but, DROBO tech support was johnny on the spot back then. That ancient DROBO has been on-line for years. I use it and rely on it to this day.

Based on many years worth of good experiences with my earlier DROBO product, I purchased a DROBO-S. I was enthralled by the potentials of the proclaimed very high-speed eSATA-II performance. Sad, I was immediately confronted with the realities of DROBO's firmware that was designed by very inexperienced and amateurish software engineers. It crashes and locks-up frequently during use. Crashing of a data archive is totally unacceptable behavior. Sometimes the crashes were so severe that the lock-ups required power cycling to correct the crash. Power-cycling a data archive is a very severe, unacceptable, and very dangerous procedure. My DROBO-S amateur-quality firmware was not designed to support the high transfer rates capable of eSATA-II (and by extension probably to USB-3), so I cannot enjoy eSATA-II performance with no crash worries. I could enjoy only DROBO-S eSATA-II along with data archive hard crashes, lock-ups, and potential data loss.

Sad, the DROBO-S has the potential to be a fantastic four or five star product. The amateurish design techniques utilized by DROBO's inexperienced software engineering staff makes that potential difficult or impossible to achieve at this point in time. I want my DROBO-S to work great! I do not want it to frequently hard crash and possibly lose data as it does now when I use it. I am not holding my breath for its working acceptably in the near future as I gather there is very large communications gap between the DROBO customer service department and the DROBO engineering department.

With any disk data archive, failure to orderly power-down the archive and unmount the disk drives can cause severe disk data corruption and data loss. Such devices include integrated computer hard disks (archives) as well as stand alone archives such as the DROBO. You never use the power switch to power down a stand-alone computer or a DROBO without risking data-corruption problems unless the drives are unmounted first. The spontaneous DROBO-S crashes could have the same detrimental effect to the data stored on the hard drives as turning off the power without first properly unmounting the disks before power down. This concept was strongly emphasized to me by DROBO customer service itself with my first generation unit. Curious, it has never been brought up in relation to my DROBO-S that crashes and burns spontaneously. I have since read comments on Amazon where DROBO customer support now blames the customer for problems directly caused by their DROBO crashes. It is totally impossible to apply a safe power down and unmount when the DROBO messes itself up when it crashes and burns. And, it is not the customers' fault when the DROBO crashes.

I am a communications engineer. I tested the DROBO-S using standard techniques that I have used for years to test communication products. DROBO-S failed miserably. Instantly. Yes, I crashed it. And, yes, I have provided a continual flow of problem analysis reports to DROBO customer service. Do the DROBO engineering folks in Asia ever read them? I doubt it. I want the product to perform to expectations!

DROBO first level tech support was totally brain-dead and worthless. Second level tech support was very helpful; however, the tech support department obviously cannot influence the design engineering department, whose poorly-designed firmware is causing the performance problems and who must ultimately fix the designed-in design problems. Both departments seem to march to the beat of different drummers, and they do not seem to communicate well with each other. I believe they are physically located in different countries. On different continents?

If the eSATA-II firmware problems that cause the totally unacceptable hard lock-up crashes were corrected, I would edit this review and give it four stars. Fix all the bugs and then I would elevate it to five stars. Right now, it is worth one star at most as the USB interface only works stably when used in conjunction with a super slow USB-2 computer port that does not utilize the high-performance capabilities of the high-speed eSATA-II or USB-3 serial interfaces.

Update 0917

Just downloaded the latest DROBO Dashboard. No firmware updates in months for the DROBO-S. DROBO-S firmware still locks up (crashes) requiring a power cycling to force it to exit the lock state and resume normal operation when using eSATA-II. It contains very immaturely designed firmware. I get the feeling that the DROBO folks are no longer interested in supporting the DROBO-S any longer. They are not interested in correcting serious firmware bugs in the DROBO-S. DROBO seems to be concentrating on very high-end systems that generate lots of cash revenues to keep daily operations going. Based on previous experiences working for high-tech companies as they closed their doors and belly-upped, I do not think DROBO will ever fix the DROBO-S so that it works satisfactorily at high-speed. I think DROBO will go out of business first.

title: Nifty gadget
text:
I got a new wireless laptop for Christmas (yay!) with Windows 7. I have an old (okay, ancient) Xerox LaserJet with only a parallel port connection, no USB capability. I got this very nifty gadget to connect it to my wireless router and make the printer wireless too. My router only has ports for Ethernet wires, not for USB. (Ethernet wires, also known as RJ45 wires, are the ones that look like a telephone wire but have larger ends.) This print server is for Ethernet connections; if your router has USB connections there's a similar device for that. BTW, this device doesn't come with an Ethernet cable.
So here's stuff I think you should know before buying this print server, and stuff about setting it up if you do. I knew almost none of these things before, so I share this for other technologically challenged people like me. First, make sure your router is wireless and check the back of it to see if the ports are for Ethernet or USB.

Then, if you've updated your Operating System, say from WinXP to Win7, you'll need an updated printer driver for your printer. To get this you need to go to the Support section of the printer manufacturer's website. (If your old parallel port printer is connected to your computer with the new OS, then you can let the computer find the driver by using Add a Printer under Control Panel/Devices and Printers. However, if you have a new computer without a parallel port and you're getting this print server to connect it to your router instead - so the printer isn't physically connected to your computer - then you can't use this method. In other words, you can only use this method if your printer is connected in some way to your computer. Otherwise your computer can't search for new printer drivers.) NOTE: if you can't get an updated printer driver for your new OS, like the manufacturer hasn't upgraded for it, then this print server will NOT work. Sadly, this is what happened to me.

If all goes well with the above and you get this print server, here's stuff to know: It comes with an installation CD with 4 categories: Administrator Install; Client Install, Quick Install and User Manual. The User Manual is 146 pages - yikes! So if you run into problems with the setup, I recommend you call StarTech's Technical Support rather than read the manual. It'll save you lots of time, they're easy to reach and very very good. Also, their installation software doesn't include Win7 so you either have to get it from their website or let Tech Support email it to you for downloading when you contact them.

If you're brave and are planning on installing this print server yourself, it comes with a 4 page printed manual that may work for you. The CD's Quick Install section is more comprehensive though so you may want to try that. What neither tells you, nor does that huge user manual (and why I only gave it 4 stars), is this:
1. If you have only 1 computer using this print server and your router, then you must use the Admin install, not the client install. At least one computer needs this install; additional computers use the Client Install.
2. About IP addresses. Any device that connects to the Internet has one. You have to know what yours are to install this print server. To get them: on your computer hit Start and on Win7 it comes up with a blank search box. (With WinXP you have to hit Run to get this box.) In that box enter "cmd" without the quotes and this brings up a black command prompt window. Where the cursor is flashing next to your name enter "ipconfig" without the quotes. This brings up a long list of addresses. Near the top of that list, under Windows LAN, is an address labeled IPv4, that's your computer's IP address. A few lines below that is an address labeled Default Gateway, that's your router's address. Write these down.
3. Remember that Win7 users have to get an update for that OS for this print server (either through Star Tech's website or by letting their Tech Support e-mail it to you).

For this device to be set up you need to give it an IP address. It must be similar, but not the same, as your router's IP. So, for example, if your router's IP is 192.168.1.200 , then give the print server an address, for example, of 192.168.1.150 so it's similar but the last few digits vary. Again, it can't be the same as any of your other IP addresses. You can find all of them by entering your router's IP in a browser tab (just the number, nothing else) and that will bring up your network configurations. You can view the details, which will include all the assigned IP's.
I really do recommend that you let Tech Support (800-265-1844) help you with the setup. First, though, have the printer driver for your present OS and your IP addresses.

title: Great Product - Horrendous Quality Control
text:
***Quality Control Problem***

I have now been through 4 Kindle Paperwhites. One is excellent. The other three have had dark spots at the bottom of the screen. The one that is good was ordered from Amazon, and I paid the $20.00 premium to get it "Without Special Offers." The others have been a succession of defective ones that I keep returning to Amazon under warranty because I purchased the first defective one from Staples and let the return period expire before I realized that I had a lemon.

The problem is four dark spots at the bottom of the screen. They are very noticeable, and detract from the reading experience. Additionally, if you intend to resell the Paperwhite on eBay at some point when you upgrade to the next best thing, you will have to disclose the dark spots as defects.

If you go to the Kindle Paperwhite sales page, you will notice that none of the Amazon photos show Paperwhites with dark spots. Likewise the Amazon video of happy Paperwhite owners shows spotless Paperwhites.If you call Amazon, they will tell you that the dark spots are normal, but the ones they show in the advertising, and the one I got from them "Without Special Offers" do not have the dark spots. Each of the four that have come through my hands has had a different degree of the dark spots. They range from nearly perfect to annoying to completely unacceptable.

***Excellent Product if you get a good one***

For reading, the Paperwhite (without the dark spots) is the best experience I have had with an eReader. I have an iPad and had an iPad mini. I love those for web surfing and the many different apps. But, for reading, the Paperwhite is the best. It is light enough to hold comfortably in one hand, and you can turn the lighting down to where it is not offensive to someone trying to sleep beside you.

title: Excellent for organizing your adapter and cable but be sure to get the original version
text:
I’ve purchased a PowerCurl for every Mac laptop I’ve had over the past few years. I’ve always hated trying to coil up the adapter and power cord neatly since they stay the way I want for about .68 seconds before uncoiling into their natural state of complete disarray. While the PowerCurl isn’t the most svelte accessory, it keeps my power cord and adapter organized and I can put it exactly where I want without it uncoiling and ruining my attempts at keeping some semblance of order within my bag. If you’re looking for something to magically make your power adapter and cord take up less room, this is not it. The PowerCurl’s purpose is to keep it all organized and let you set the adapter upright to improve air flow around it to keep it cooler.

Note that Quirky has “updated” the PowerCurl to a new design. I use quotation marks because I really don’t think it’s an update since the new design doesn’t seem to be any improvement over the original. The new design packs the adapter portion into a circular holder and you wrap the cord around that but from what I’ve seen and read online, it’s incredibly difficult to wrap the cord tightly enough so it stays put in the new version. I intentionally looked for the original version here on Amazon since I knew that it would work well for me given my previous experiences. I didn’t get the color I wanted (gray) and had to settle for blue instead, but I’m happy I could still get the original version at such a great price.

The PowerCurl comes in multiple sizes to fit the different power adapter sizes that come with the different Apple laptop models. If you don’t know what adapter you have, just read the text printed on the adapter itself – you will see right there with your very own eyes which one you have so you can order the correct PowerCurl. There’s really no need to ask complete strangers on the internet which PowerCurl you need as long as you can pick up your own power adapter and read what it says.

title: To Use as a Computer Monitor
text:
How to Setup to Use as a Computer Monitor

Yes, these instructions can be extracted from the user manual, but I hope this posting makes things a little easier. If Samsung had spent a few extra pennies and used more paper for the User Manual, they wouldn't have had to cram everything in using such teeny, tiny text fonts.

1) - Connect your Samsung to your computer's video card. The Samsung has a HDMI connection. Your computer's video card will have a HDMI or a DVI connection. So, you will be using either a HDMI to HDMI cable or a HDMI to DVI cable. You will connect your cable to the HDMI IN1 (DVI) jack.

2) - After you turn on your computer and go through all the basic setup, your Samsung TV/Monitor, things will look pretty good -- until you try to read text. Text will look lousy. To use the Samsung as a computer monitor, you need to change the 'Input Source".

3) - Press the "Source" button on your remote. Use the up/down buttons. Choose HDMI1/DVI. Press the 'Enter' button which is in the middle of the four direction arrow button.

4) - IMPORTANT: You *must* "Edit Name" to properly configure the Samsung to use the computer input source. *This doesn't just give you a different name, it also changes the setup and setup options!*
- "To access 'Edit Name', press the TOOLS button when the Source List is displayed."

- IF you connected your computer to the Samsung with a HDMI to HDMI cable to the HDMI IN 1 (DVI) port, assign the name 'PC' to HDMI 1 in Edit Name.
- IF you connected your computer to the Samsung with a HDMI to DVI cable to the HDMI IN 1 (DVI) port, assign the name 'DVI PC' to HDMI 1 in Edit Name.

[As one poster on a Mac forum said: "For the HDMI - DVI port to work properly you have to RENAME the port from HDMI 1 ... Rename? Who thinks that by 'renaming' some port it will actually change its properties? Is this on purpose to annoy the user?"]

5) - Now you can press the MENU button - and then press right arrow when you are at the Video Screen icon to get to the video preferences - and fine tune. (As a check, if you set up everything correctly in step 4, your choice for video mode will be 'Standard' or 'Entertain' - NOT 'Standard' or 'Dynamic'.)

Now choose your preferences - and then set them by pressing the 'Enter' button.
You can see the effects while you are doing the adjusting. (I suggest having a colorful picture and also some text on a white page up on the screen on the far right so you can judge what you prefer.)

For whatever it is worth, my setting are as follows:
Mode: Entertain
Backlight: 20
Contrast: 100
Brightness: 45
Sharpness: 50 ('Sharpness" will have a very visible effect on how you see text!)
Picture Options: I use the default values: 'Color Tone' = Standard, 'Size' = 16:9, 'HDMI Black Level' = Low

Cheers,

-Skip

title: WARNING if Mackbook Pro Secondary/Optical Bay Drive
text:
I bought this as a secondary drive to be placed in the optical drive bay, but have come across much difficulty.

If you're buying this as a *replacement* for your drive in the primary bay, then I've read very good things -- but I'm not using it as a boot drive.

If you're buying this as a *secondary drive* in the optical bay, BEWARE! The 2011 MBPs 15" & 17" don't support a 6Gb/s drive (even though it is supposed to) and will only negotiate down to 3Gb/s. However, for some reason this drive will not complete that negotiation- it is recognized but throws I/O errors when you try to write files -- rendering it effectively useless. Oddly, the 13" MBPs work just fine.

The issue is well documented at these two links:
[...]
[...]

I've had to drop this in my primary bay and move my SSD to the Optical bay, substantially increasing my boot and access times. But I'll cope so that I may have the additional storage...

So if you have a 13" 2011 MBP, all is well. If you have a 15" or 17" 2011 MBP and want to use this as a secondary drive, I highly recommend buying the smaller XT 500 that's 3Gb/s.

title: Outstanding TV! LG does it again!  Firmware update today (7/20/12)
text:
For the first time, I will be writing and updating as the weeks go by for this item. The TV that this replaces was a 42" Sharp Aquos LCD. The reason why I'm replacing it is because:

1: The PCB (the printed circuit board) is malfunctioning to the point where any day the TV will die; it gets worse as the weeks go by. Sometimes, 1 "dead" pixel, a few weeks later it's 2 etc. Then everything seems fine.
2. The warranty just expired
3. My infant has become very mobile and was grabbing the old TV a lot; so if I'm mounting a TV, it will be a new one!

** You can skip this part if you don't want to know my research**
I went to several brick and mortar stores; namely PCR&Son, Abes of Maine, Sears, and BB. 6th Avenue Electronics was forced into closure. Amazon had the lowest price and I was skeptical ordering online as I heard horror stories about deliveries, yet thinking about it, how is it any different than ordering it and having it delivered from a brick and mortar store? I was all set to order from PCR&S as I showed him some quotes and papers I printed out. They quoted as low as $1986 and that was the lowest. I was really thinking that this salesman was saying take it or leave it. He wouldn't negotiate and he wouldn't go as low as $1900; yeah, I was even making myself pay more because I wanted to see if he'd go down. Nope! I even went to BB and they wouldn't even go lower than PCR or even match them. Well, I basically said screw it; I took a chance and the funniest thing was that the TV was $1749 on Amazon and when I accidentally left it in my shopping cart, a message was waiting for me," The price has gone down, the new price will reflect your purchase. It went down to $1699 and wow, it went back up to $2300 just today. I ordered the TV on Friday June 8, (before midnight), I was able to pick June 13 for delivery which was delivered by CEVA. I even called their office which is based in Seattle, WA and asked if they can deliver it close to 6pm since the window was between 3pm-6pm. I wanted to make sure I was home. My wife was home but I'm the anal one!! Their main branch gave me the local number (which was at JFK Airport) and told me to call. The JFK office didn't seem as nice but oh well, didn't let that spoil my excitement of getting this TV. Don't let a brick and mortar store fool you; the 6 pairs of 3d glasses is thrown in by LG not by the store. PCRicard salesman freaken lied to me, "the TV us so good that we are throwing in 3 extra pairs." Yeah, LIAR! Thank goodness I didn't listen to them. I will go there someday and throw it in their face that I bought the TV, just not from them!
******************

6-13-12

TV arrived. The delivery guy was very nice and said that he would unpack the TV and I can inspect it. He was very helpful, was not in a rush (or rushing me) and we put the TV together. I hooked it up to my Verizon FIOS STB. Word of caution, do not put the HDMI plug into the TV when it's off. It wouldn't recognize the HDMI source. When I left the TV on and unplugged the HDMI plug; I reinserted it and bingo; the TV recognized the new input and there was the Verizon logo on the screen.

At the ripe age of 36, I've grown anal. I turned on all the lights in the room and even brought a flashlight to inspect the whole TV for cracks and defects. Gladly; NONE were found!

The remote control manual is just a long piece of paper and it explains the basics. Not bad. You might get confused as to the paper that came with it that's in several languages. Ignore that. At first I thought that was the manual which was why I thought it was garbage! I was wrong! Only minor issue was how to put the batteries in the magic remote. It took the 2 of us to figure out how to get the batteries in. FYI, on the bottom of the remote, push were it says push. The bottom opens up. The TV manual, I mistook for being worthless as well. Nope, it was decent enough to understand.

When the remote and the TV first met, it was love at first site! The on screen instructions show you how to calibrate it and its features. I happen to like the remote, it's small and with few buttons. I love how it's a wireless mouse! The QMenu/Apps gets you to all the apps and if you want to change the inputs. Easy enough! I prefer a remote control with few buttons so this is right down my alley. The precision and use of the magic remote was easy and there were no issues. It's very responsive and all you need to do is pick up the remote and the pointer shows up on the screen. Leaving it alone for a while and the pointer goes away.

When I first turned on the TV, I saw some bleeding which got me nervous. When the TV went onto the standard channel; Channel 2 (Local news was on); no bleeding, no clouds, no nothing except a picture quality that was gorgeous! When there was a tremendous amount of "black" on the screen; still no bleeding. I was so happy! I love this TV. I went to a movie channel and turned on the Met game. Baseball never looked so awesome (sorry for the word awesome!). I changed from 2D to 3D and the baseball game looked Grrrrrrrrreat! Wow, I was amazed. I'm also amazed that the estimated power usage is $14 a year which is less than half what my LCD was rated at. I think my Sharp LCD was in the high $20s or low $30s.

I watched Meatballs (1979) and the picture on standard and HD was perfect. The picture quality was so clear and so gorgeous, I was mesmerized by it!

8:10pm 6/15...I'm watching Titanic. The colors and picture is amazing!

All and all, the picture quality is spectacular. It's like the actors and actresses are right there in your living room. I can't comment that it's better than plasma as I've never owned one. Believe me when i say this, when you turn the TV on; you will be amazed at the picture quality for standard definition, HD, and 2D->3D conversion. 2D-3D conversion is so crisp and lifelike, I was watching women's volleyball and I was AMAZED to the point of getting hit on the back of my head by my wife :)

**It would be wise to put the TV away from any window. The screen is very glossy. The manual also recommends you not keep it near a window that can become very bright. My laptop light when it's on (having the laptop open) does reflect on the TV so a word of caution; you might get the," turn it off or move away look."

I took some pictures of some of the channels I was on. Amazon seems to not want to upload them so they will be there soon.
=======================
to be continued in a week or 2.

*Update* 7/20/12

For those watching my review, sorry it took so long. I'm out of breath chasing my toddler around! :) Last thing that I wanted to do was go on my laptop! So having this TV for more than a month I have to say that I'm still loving it. I'm amazed at how thin it is and how close to the edge the picture is. I have my TV set to Vivid and Tru Motion turned up to max values. Vivid makes everything on the TV bright and lifelike. title: Item Does Not Match Specifications Listed
text:
I would have rated this laptop a 5, except for 1 huge problem.

I purchased this laptop for work because it had a full keyboard with a number pad and was advertised as having user upgradable RAM. As an engineer, I tend to keep multiple MS office apps and specific files open concurrently, along with MS OUTLOOK and a web browser, so I need to have the higher RAM capacity.

The labels on the sealed factory cartons in which my computer was delivered clearly identify it as an UX51VZ-XB71 (MSRP $2,699.00), and the serial numbers on the labels match the serial number on the computer itself. The AMAZON product description clearly states the UX51VZ-XB71 has "8 GB (four slots, two slots filled with a 4 GB stick, two slots open)".

ASUS technical support initially stated that based on my Serial Number my computer should have 4 GB of onboard memory, 1 - 4 GB DIMM in a user accessible slot that would accept up to an 8 GB DDR3 1600 DIMM, that would mean my -XB71 is really an -XH71, except there is no user accessible RAM bay.

If that is the case, then the computer I received is some sort of crossbred system with components of 2 different models, and it was mislabeled with an incorrect model number, an error that could have only occurred at the factory. There is no excuse for my receiving a bastardized system with components of 2 different models while being labeled as the high end model with its highest MSRP.

Update: I called ASUS Tech Support and talked to a different tech rep. They only show 1 model of UX51VZ. It has 8 GB of RAM as 4 GB onboard memory and 1 - 4 GB DIMM. They do not show any variations designated as -XB71, -XH71 or -DH71 which further confuses the entire issue.

title: Looks fine, but not very well constructed
text:
The case itself is nice. The materials on the outside and inside are soft, and the cover itself is hard enough to prevent light impact damage. This is really important, considering my last kindle broke inside of it's case from a modest amount of external pressure. The material does give off a bit of smell, but it's not overpowering or overly bad, but it is noticeable out of the box.

After a few days of use, I noticed the inner part of the case, where the elastic keeps the kindle in, was starting to warp away from the outer faux-leather. Where the elastic is sandwiched in between the materials, it had started to pull away from the backing, which was noticeable and resulted in the overall shape looking a little lumpy, for lack of a better word.

Even worse, the strap that keeps the front cover of the case closed has already started fraying at the base. By now, almost 1/4 of the strap has ripped and I've stopped using it for fear that it will snap completely. I have no idea why this would happen, as I have not excessively pulled on the strap at all.

Overall, the case looks pretty good, holds the kindle firmly, and offers at least a minimum amount of protection. The hand strap on the inside is a decent addition in theory, but it is awkward to use.

I've got to take 3 stars off for the poor construction and mediocre materials used, as well as the weird smell that still hasn't gone away after almost 2 weeks of use. I wish I had spent a little more and gotten a higher quality case.

And for the laptop docks for Lenovo or Dell which usually cost $250+ for the thinkpad or latitude business lineups, I just don't understand why anyone complains.

title: Carefully consider your physical situation and convenience factors (and annoyance) before buying
text:
I’ve owned this product for three years and thought it time to review.

It looked a bit odd going in. Fifty bucks for an amp & speakers? The reviews about the sound were solid. I had a very specific application: My Vizio TV in the bedroom has a volume setting that goes from zero to TOO LOUD in a single click. I needed something to fit the white-noise space that helps me sleep with the TV on. So that’s why I bought the unit.

Did it fit the bill? Amazingly, yes, it did. Within my very specific need, I’m able to use this little amp without too much trouble. But there are many quirks that I’d like to address.

This thing is WEIRD. Like all-caps weird. It’s bizarre. But first, the positive:

It sounds great. Like so many other reviews, I give it top rating for sound, for the price. The main unit is the subwoofer and it’s effective. Yes, I use it for very quiet time but I’ve used it to play audio and I really can’t complain. Look to other reviews about sound quality for more detail.

The weird:

Power: The only option is a switch at the bottom of the back of the unit. This box resides on my dresser so it’s convenient, but it’s only convenient to ME. Bless you if this goes anywhere but shoulder-level and easy to get to. The “convenient” remote has no Power button. So, your choices are easy access to the bottom backside of the box or a power strip. Good luck.

Powering on: It defaults to factory setting every time you turn it on. This means if you have a source feeding it, it will be quite loud when you flip that switch. I’ve learned to turn the unit on first, push the volume-down button for several seconds, then turn on the cable box (audio source). Handy to know if you’ve slumbering cats or spouses in the room. I’ve never seen an audio product that didn’t default to the last setting used, until this one.

Again, there is no power button on the remote, nor on the front of the unit. It’s a manual switch at the bottom of the back of the unit. An engineer dances on the edge of purgatory for this, but he/she probably doesn’t care.

The face: A large, ugly, useless blue LED that tries to be an EQ graph. With helpful Volume, Treble, Bass insignias you can’t see unless you’re within inches. A ½” circular blue something that blinks when muted. A compass-styled selection of buttons that replicate the bizarre remote functions. There is nothing about the face of this unit that is appealing or functional, it’s just annoying.

The remote: Oh, boy.

Yes, you can turn the volume up and down. You can mute the unit.

Is the equalization for some reason bothering you? There’s a RESET button for that. Along with treble and bass up / down buttons. Bear in mind that each time you turn the unit on (manually) you have to adjust these settings if you don’t like the default. The remote has you covered, giving you a choice of using the buttons on the unit or backing up a bit and using the remote.

That’s it. Volume, mute, Reset and treble/bass.

It’s not a case of “I have multiple inputs and use treble / bass to fine tune.” Unless there’s a discernable difference in:

Inputs: Two choices. “CD” is a euphemism for a standard 3.5mm jack. Fair enough. The other is “AUX”, a set of RCA jacks. But, there is no way to switch between the two. They are both live. If you have two sources, they both play.

Outputs: RCA jacks to the provided speakers. Which is fine until one goes out or you want to use different speakers. I haven’t seen speaker wires fitted with RCA jacks since the 1970’s.

To summarize:
It sounds good. My use has been limited and again please refer to other reviews for sound quality details.
Power on/off is a PITA, no remote control.
Doesn’t hold the last volume or EQ if you power it off, resets to default.
Looks bad. The LED will bother you or not, I find it annoying and it doesn’t provide any meaningful information.
No protection for the speakers. Cats & kids need not apply.
The remote has no power button. WTF. Volume control and mute are good things.
Two inputs, RCA jacks and a 3.5mm jack. Both are live and there’s no switching between the two.
RCA jack speaker outputs. What the hell people.

Oh, one more thing: My Charter remote for the TV box affects the volume on this unit, in that every button I push bumps the unit’s volume up a notch. I have to remember to turn the volume all the way down before using the cable box. Gets pretty loud pretty quick. Sheesh.

To be fair, I bought this unit three years ago, December of 2010. I haven’t read any of the recent reviews, so if changes have been made that contradict my experience, please leave a comment and I will make an update.

I’m not posting this to discourage your purchase, but if you’re considering it you need to carefully look at your particular application and see the limitations of this system. Like I said, it works for me for my very specific situation. I laughed my *** off when I unpacked it, even more when I set it up, wondered at my good fortune, pondered the engineering failures, and have been a happy user since. Like they say, your mileage may vary.

I've been using handheld Magellan GPS units for as long as they have been available. We used them for hiking, motorcycling, and off-roading. Our older models are a little too tedious to use for geocaching so we purchased the eXplorist GC to use specifically for geocaching. My wife and I love to walk and bike and the eXplorist gives us a purpose and destination for putting some miles on our soles or bike tires.

The eXplorist GC is simple to use but it does require a little familiarity. I always purposely try something first without reading the instructions completely just to see how intuitive the device is to use. We found our first cache doing so but it did get frustrating navigating through the unit's features as the day wore on. I now had a basic familiarity with the unit though so I read the instructions and found it extremely easy to use from then on. The center togle takes a bit of a learning curve to move without pressing "select," but it works as designed. Plus, to truly enjoy the features of the unit you do need a $30 online subscription.

If you only want a unit for geocaching, especially around town near roads, bike trails, and in parks, the eXplorist GC is simple to use and fills the need. If you want a hand-held unit for geocaching plus hiking, off-roading, etc, the eXplorist 110 or 310 is a better choice.

title: Very good keyboard and worth the price (which seems to vary?)
text:
Purchased this keyboard as a cheap upgrade to a dell latitude I received for college that needed a few things to bring it up to speed (also adding 4GB of memory and possibly a solid state drive). For starters I was a bit confused with the buying options for this keyboard, there were two different options for the same item from the same seller (Gadget Mart I think it was). One was $15 including shipping and the other came out to nearly twice that amount. I went with the cheaper one because what the hell right?

Item shipped immediately the next day, and I received it two days later, which was ahead of schedule, shipping from California to PA! It arrived two days ahead of the amazon portion of my order - the laptop memory - which shipped from the midwest.

Installing the keyboard was fairly straightforward thanks to a youtube video I found. Simply remove two screws and pull the old keyboard out, slide the new one in and screw it in. One thing I'd mention is these keyboards are very easy to bend so be careful, and take care to get all of the little side tabs that lock it in place down into the latches (I needed a flathead screwdriver to force them in on mine).

Keyboard is the same as the standard dell keyboard, except the right arrow key gains a small symbol for keyboard backlight when you hold down the function key, which is handy. It seems to have three modes: off, on, and auto on. Though I'm still not sure which is auto on and which is just on...they seem to function the same. The keys are well lit with a nice white light, not too bright but enough to make it easier to see in the dark and adds a classy touch to the laptop :)

Keys type softer than the standard dell keyboard, which I like, and it feels softer which I guess is nice but it seems just a little mushier than the other keyboard. Also, they keys, maybe because they are brand new, are a bit slippery to the touch when typing, but that's very minor and might change over time once I've used it more.

All in all a good purchase at a great price, from a great seller!

title: It cools great adds usb ports.  However there are quality issues we have discovered now.
text:
It is great. cools great adds usb ports. variable speed. multi tilt levels are handy. Rubberized surface keeps laptop from moving.

Update on this unit quality:

I would have to advise against buying this unit now. We are on our second unit. The first unit broke when the two power ports to power the unit up failed. I thought that it was a one time issue. We bought the second one because the first on did such a good job of cooling. However 4 months into owning the second unit it too has had both ports for powering up the unit fail. On both units the Micro USB port's literally broke out of the unit. I opened both units up after they broke and found that the micro USB port is only held in by the tiny contacts on the circuit board. This Micro USB port has no chance of surviving long. Simply plugging and unplugging the cable will cause this port to literally break out. The other port used for powering the unit becomes - expanded - after simple daily use and loses contact. I was able to get this port to work again by opening up the case and using needle nose pliers to squeeze the port a little to tighten it up again. This only helped a short time and it is loose and sloppy again. I may try soldering the cable into this port and try to create a more permanent connection. It is too bad these power ports are so cheaply built. The rest of the unit is a good unit but if you can't get power to it what good is it. I can bear witness that in the course of daily use of gaming with the unit on a persons lap you will probably only get 6 months use from this unit before both the Power ports fail

title: Great Set for Great Price
text:
Bundlemonster's 12 piece set is a great purchase if you're looking for iPad accessories but don't want to pay Apple prices. It includes a retractable and a standard AUX cable, a stylus, a speaker and earphone splitter, earphones, a car charger, a home charger, a standard USB cord as well as a retractable USB cord, a long USB cord, extension cable and a micro fiber pouch to keep them in.
The different USB cables are great and are definitely my favorite thing in this set, especially the long cord. It's nice to have the option of a longer length. I use the retractable USB cord to plug in my iPod and don't have to worry about knocking over stuff with a bunch of cords hanging off the side.
The earphones don't have the best sound quality, but they work fine, and that's all I can ask for. I go through them so quickly, I'd go broke if I paid for good ones. The car charger is great because it has two USB slots, so I can use one for the iPod, and the other is free for another gadget.
While I don't really use a stylus that much, the one included in this set is a good size and was easy to use. Some of them are too slippery or thin for me, but this one felt great in my hand. I haven't had a chance to use the splitter yet, but I'm sure it's fine as well.
All in all, this is a great buy. The accessories don't feel cheap, and all work well. Like I said earlier, it's definitely a good option if you don't want to pay hefty Apple prices. Thumbs up!

title: Excellent heat sink + fan
text:
OEM heatsink, for my AM2 CPU, failed after 3 1/2 years of 24/7 use. I first replaced the fan with another CPU fan, with pwm control. That was an adventure in itself. The replacement fan was far noisier than the OEM fan. I looked for a replacement heatsink+fan assembly, since they start at prices lower than I had to pay for the fan by itself. Eventually I discovered that Amazon sells AMD OEM assemblies, and I selected the nicest one that I could find. It cost on $6 more than the replacement fan.

Removing the old heatsink was a problem. It was so tightly attached to the CPU that I worried that I might break things.

The new heatsink's footprint is a tiny bit smaller than the original's foot print. It weighs 390 grams. The heatsink comes with pre-applied thermal paste. After cleaning the CPU, I had to wriggle the new heatsink and remove it about ten times to get complete coverage on both CPU and heatsink.

Installation was not particularly easy, in part because I did not remove the motherboard from the case. It seemed that that one heatpipe on each side might be just barely touching the mounting bracket on the motherboard. Eventually, using special curved jaw pliers, I was able to get the clip connected. After that, everything went smoothly.

Upon booting the computer, I worried that the fan might not be spinning at all, because I could not hear it. The hard drive is louder. I visually checked the fan to insure that it is moving. This is now running quieter than my laptop computer. The CPU runs about 16 degrees C cooler than it did with the stock cooler. (CPU only maxes out at 45 W, and this cooler apparently can handle 125 W CPUs, so this isn't a surprise.

The description contains one error. It says that the heatsink has two heat pipes. The heatsink I received has four heat pipes.

text:
