title: Not a Logitech K400 and the longer I use it the more I hate it
text:
The keyboard is fine but like others have said the software and touch pad ruin it. I have a Logitech K400 but because of a move I now have both my desktops setup as HTPCs. I read some of the reviews on this and recently had a good experience with a mouse made by MS so I figured I would give it a try. The Windows 8 gestures only work half of the time. It has gotten to the point I turned most of them off in the software settings. Not sure if the include paperwork had instructions for getting the software but I just searched on Bing and downloaded from online.Once I stripped it down to being just a plain keyboard and touch pad it worked fine.

Honestly I have read others saying this feels like a better build quality than the K400 but I don't see that, it may be a tad more stiff but it is still a plastic keyboard that flexes just about as much as the k400. The K400 I give 5 stars to, I got it just as W8 was coming out and was using it on a Windows 7 computer. It has been through heavy use, with the family using it to play games like Monopoly on our big screen. It has been tossed around and treated rough, yet hasn't skipped a beat. Looks like new except for part of the "S" has worn off. Still functions like new. If this keyboard stripped down of features last as long as the K400 I'll be happy with it. Honestly though if I knew what I know now I would have gotten another K400 just don't feel like returning this one. Amazon is great but I already threw away the box and it isn't worth the headache.

November 18, 2014
My most recent complaint is I have realized with the one piece button for both right and left click unless you click at the very right or left edge it is kind of like flipping a coin for which side registers. The whole single one piece design with the bottom having click function instead of independent buttons is just bad. It is way too buggy and I am so tired of left clicks registering as right clicks. I will be throwing this keyboard away after the holidays when I can afford to buy a Logitech to replace it.

November 26, 2014
I ordered this on September 15, 2014 and today I finally gave up on it. I really wanted to like this keyboard. I installed the Microsoft software trying to fix my complaints. In the end the touch pad sucks. The one piece button just makes it annoying to click anything. The closer of the deal is the battery life is awful.

The Logitech K400 batteries have lasted anywhere from two years to eight months. I've owned it for about 4 years. It was on my main HTPC up until I bought this and is now on the PC hooked to my TV in my bedroom. In the almost 4 years I have owned it, it is now on its fourth set of batteries. I can live with that. In the little over 2 months I have owned this, it is on the fifth set of batteries. The fact that it is not illuminated or anything special to justify it going through batteries so quickly. The fact that I turn it off every time I finish using it. Has made me decide it will be getting replaced.

The batteries I have used have all been brand alkaline batteries. It came with a set of Duracells, I used two sets of batteries from Harbor Freight and two brand new set of Energizer batteries. For now I am typing on my full-sized Logitech K320 keyboard as my living room HTPC is setup on a desk with a monitor and hooked to two TVs in different parts of the room, one for game play the other for watching movies. I have always had the two keyboard setup with the media keyboard at couch and full-sized at the desk.

I will be replacing this keyboard after the holidays with a new Logitech, either the K830 or the TK820. Microsoft has once again lost my keyboard business.

title: Very Good...but not quite Great!
text:
Overall, the camera performed well. The camera was used on dives over the course of a week in the Florida Keys, at depths ranging from 0 - 60 feet.

The good stuff - Easy to operate; Remote control so you don't have to fumble with the camera; No leaks,even at 60'; No fogging; Better video quality than I expected for the price. The ability to attach the camera to the scuba gear for hands free operation was also a plus. I bought an additional 8M memory card, but found that the camera held more images and video than I would have expected.

What keeps it from being a 5 Star - The remote control for the camera was great for shallower dives, but we found that at greater depths (30-60') the remote became almost useless due to the ambient water pressure. The ability to change from video to still photography while submerged is awkward. Since you have to rely on ambient light, photography at greater depths is limited. Since the video is in Quicktime,if you want to do any editing you must have a Mac, or buy a Quicktime Editor for Windows.

Overall - a very good camera for the price, especially for beginers. Very good, but not quite great. Add a compact light to this and it becomes a strong 5 star. Even without a light, I recommend without hesitation as it will be tough to find a better dive camera for the money.

title: Warning!!! Bootleg Product!
text:
Please do not waste your money OR your time buying this! This is NOT a genuine Samsung product, despite the claims in the product page saying it is. (Please note that Samsung did NOT sell this, and neither did Amazon, this is from a third party seller.) I actually have a genuine adapter, and this was bought as an additional item for my husband to have his own. I will compare the differences.

For starters, the box is came in is very horribly printed. The biggest telltale sign of it being a fake is that it is missing the genuine Samsung accessory hologram image that is on every genuine Samsung product. The box itself has badly printed stickers placed on it.

I decided to give it a chance anyhow based on the low price. When I opened it, I noticed immediately that the product was very light in weight. I took out my genuine product and compared them side by side. While almost identical in appearance, the Samsung adapter was clearly much heavier.

When tested with both my son's Samsung Galaxy S3, and my Samsung Galaxy S4 (which it states it will also work with - the genuine one DOES work with both), it does not function AT ALL. (Just to be sure it was not my phones or TV, I proceeded to test it with my genuine adapter, and it worked perfectly.)

Please note, I called Amazon and filed a formal complaint against the seller. They are having me send the item directly to them instead of the seller and are investigating this with Samsung's assistance to verify it is a fake. In the meantime, do NOT purchase this item. If I could give it no stars, I would have.

title: Excellent DVR, just like Phillips DVD-R3575H
text:
I have owned the Phillips DVDR3575H for about 5 years, and it's been completely reliable. Have only had to reboot it a couple times due to lockups, always records what it's supposed to. I was pleasantly surprised to find that the Magnavox is basically the same unit, same menus, features, and presumably the same reliability. One thing I noticed is that this unit has an excellent OTA digital tuner. I temporarily had a twist-tie stuck in the coax in, and it can pick up all local stations without dropouts!

This unit can do what no other DVR can do- it can reliably record to hard drive and burn DVDs if you want to save shows. Editing is very easy, you can remove commercials from a 2 hour movie in 10 minutes, as long as you don't get distracted and watch the movie as you're editing it like I sometimes do! I always record in SLP (lowest-quality mode) and the picture quality on my SD TV is very good, especially when recorded from OTA DTV.

One of my favorite features is the variable skip/replay. You can set it from 10sec to 2 minutes, I think, and skip through commercials in no time. That with being able to watch the show after it's started recording, you can start watching an 8:00 show at 8:25 and by 9:00, you're caught up to live TV.

It is intuitive, reliable, menus and channels have a fairly fast response time, and I'm very surprised these are very difficult to find these days. Break free of the renting the cable company's DVR, and be able to permanently save shows on DVD to be watched on any DVD player.

I highly recommend either the Magnavox or Phillips units. The only sad thing is that if your cable company encrypts the digital TV, you will not be able to tune it and will have to use the line in from your cable box. But that's one reason we dropped cable.

I will be ordering a 3rd one for another room in the house.

The bag itself weighs next to nothing, and the very first day I wore it, I noticed the difference in my posture and how my back felt at the end of the day. I like the special laptop pocket with padding, and between that and the foldover top, I feel my laptop is very secure in here. The straps are comfortable enough that I don't even notice them, without being bulky. The canvas seems rain-resistant but I wouldn't carry it in a serious downpour or wear it biking in the rain. The hook closures seem more secure than magnetic snaps, and the one outside pocket is roomy enough for everything I need.

title: Very great Amplifier! But see EDIT...
text:
Purchased this along with a JL 12" Subwoofer as a birthday gift for myself and installed it the following month myself. Following the review notes from Mr. West (Thank you Mr. West for the heads up) I checked the 'Minor Flaw' of the incorrect wiring that the other people may or may not find with this amplifier; luckily I wasn't one of them. But anyway, the amplifier works great! Installed it with high-quality cables, terminals and above recommended speced cables and everything sounds great. I've hooked up 4 Infinity speakers with 4 tweeters and the sub. System sounds absolutely wonderful, even with the original stock speakers on my little EM2 Honda Civic. One huge concern I had was that I found many reports of Boss Amps overheating. But happily this amp has none of those issues as it does not even run hot from running it. Very very happy with this amp and glad I took the risk of purchasing this instead of saving up for JL Amps and not having to buy a separate 4-channel just for my speakers. Only thing I would've liked to see was a bit of a bigger terminal insert so I could've actually put a 4Gauge terminal to get the best results instead of having to jam it in as much as possible under that tiny square washer.

EDIT (01/30/13):
Upgraded my Front Components to Polk Audio DXi6500s w/ Tweeters and tuned with clear vocals in mind. Using a higher watt speakers for better and louder vocals with my 12" JL W3-v4s we found that any higher than 1/3rd of the gain setting for the speakers results in static; any higher than 2/3rd of the gain results in clipping no matter what kind (and higher watt) speaker we installed. Tested at a professional car audio shop test if it was the amp, we used a higher quality Kicker and also JL amps and found no more static/clipping upon using the other amplifiers. Keep in mind that all wiring used were top quality Speaker cables, Terminals, Capacitor, and RCAs (all of the Monster Brand); as well as using Filters on the Constant and Ignition Wires as well as Ground Loop Filters on the RCAs and Noise Filters on ALL ends (to and from) of the Positive speaker wires.

Bought this unit May of 2012. It doesn't get a lot of use. I average maybe two movies a week on it. I put a movie in yesterday and it started acting like the video and audio was in slow motion except it was choppy. Tried a couple more DVDs, same thing. Checked for firmware update and it was up to date. I did an online return and sent it out today. I had to send it from Seattle to Texas which cost me $30.00.

I have always been a Sony fan except laptops. This unit is matched up to a Sony big screen that was bought at the same time.

The unit did work very good prior to this issue and was good for what it is.

I will update this as I go through the warranty process.

Got an email from Sony saying they received the unit about five days after sending it. Five days after that 11/15/12 I got an email from tech group saying that nothing is wrong with it. I sent the following response (the first part being what I put on the Sony website for return);

"I was watching a DVD (non Blue Ray) and after a few minutes the video and audio became very choppy and like slow motion. I put in a different DVD to make sure it wasn't the DVD. It did the same thing with the second DVD. I then put in a Blue Ray DVD to see if it would do it with it and it did. I checked to see if there was firmware update for it via wifi and there was none. Trust me, I would not pay $30.00 for shipping and go with out my home theater for weeks."

On 11/20/12, I got an email that my unit was being shipped to me. I received the unit about a week later. It was not the one I sent. I checked the serial number. The unit sent to me looked like it had been used for a wheel chock. It had deep scratches in it and was covered in "cheese". I guess some people don't wash their hands.

One thing I forgot to tell Sony when I sent it in was that I use the optical audio to connect to my cable box. The audio would drop out occasionally and slowly work it's way back to normal levels. The unit Sony sent me back does not do that. I guess this is a positive.

One last word on the website repair page. Your status is never updated. When you go to check the status, it has the same comment each time.

I would bump this up to a three star rating. I would give it more but now I am a little gun shy, waiting for ir to go bad again. Obviously someone else had sent this unit it.

title: An astonishingly good camera for the price.
text: But the power source needs a little work. This camera has an 8mm lens that gives a 44 degree Field Of View (FOV). With 8mm you can actually see something. The camera comes with a 12V 1A adapter. Even after 30 seconds the onboard voltage regulator (7805 SMT) gets too hot. Its trying to dissipate 5 watts of heat off it's tiny surface! I used a lab power supply and found that the camera draws a steady 100ma at 6.8V and above. (Below 6.2V the regulator drops out.) At 6.8V the onboard regulator was barely warm. The transformer and electronics board are both regulated. Just use a 56 ohm 1W dropping resistor to get rid of the extra volts. Four 220 ohm 1/4 watt resistors in parallel would accomplish the same thing for you.

title: The Sound Pulls You In!
text:
I would give 5 stars for sound quality and 4 stars for comfort. I immediately tried these cans on after receiving them from the mail lady. These hurt when I first put them on. They squeezed my jaw bone just below the ear. Very disappointed but decided to try them anyway figuring that the tension might give over time. This was a totally new and amazing experience watching a movie on my IPad2. I found myself completely immersed in the movie like nothing I have ever experienced before. Made some adjustments to the cans on my head and was able to take some of the pressure off of my jaw bone. By the way, I have a very normal size head in my opinion.

I'm happy to say that after using these for about two days the pressure on my upper jaw bone is about a 3 on a scale of 10 compared to a 8 out of 10 when I first tried them on. I realized that part of the initial tightness of the cans was due to the cold weather when they arrived.

The Cord:

Pros: Quality is the first thing that comes to mind. Long enough to plug into my home theater receiver and sit on the couch to enjoy a movie without disturbing anyone else in the house. An adapter was included that allowed me to plug into the receiver.

Negatives: Very heavy. Can be bulky at times. Not good for moving around because there is simply too much cord to tuck away. If you plan on being very mobile with these it could be annoying.

These do an amazingly good job of sound isolation at max or close to max volume on my IPad. Listening to these at max volume on the IPad is a pleasure and not over-the-top. At mid volume I would say the sound isolation is ok.
The sound I am referencing is coming from a household with 1 and 4 year old boys. Which I'm pretty sure they are kicking off some pretty high decibels.

Overall I would say that these are more than worth the money. The experience you receive in watching movies is something else! Like I said, the sound pulls you in to the movie.

title: It's a good camera but some issues with Raw conversion.
text:
This camera seems to do everything you ask of it. However, it's very complicated with it's never ending menus and electronically minded operation.

Now for the nasty bits. The shutter vibration limited my hand holding operation on this camera down to only 1/50th of a second. On my DSLRs, I can handhold at least one stop slower on the shutter speed and two shutter speeds slower on my Leicas. So a big no no from me on this point.

Here is my biggest complaint. Sony's .ARW raw format is proprietary to sony, so if you want the most detail out of your camera, you have to use the slow as molasses silkypix from sony to extract the most detail, sharpness and color out of your files. I'm not sure why Sony is so stubborn about not releasing their algorithms with Adobe Lightroom and Photoshop. As far as the .JPGs go.... well they're okay, definitely not fuji quality and definitely alot more information to be derived from the sensor in .raw format.

There are good bits to the camera too. It's image quality has promise of greatness, and it can take any lens on the market with the proper adapter. The EVF is nice bright and clear and makes manual focusing a joy.

In time I'm sure pressure from users will force sony to give up their .ARW secrets, but for now, I'm gonna hang out on the sidelines and wait until that moment happens. I'm sure in their next revision, they'll simplify the menus, improve the shutter action and share their raw algorithms with Adobe.

title: In-depth bullet points.
text:
I have been shooting with this camera for some time now, and I feel as though I have developed a good relationship with it. I am a wedding photographer, and while looking for a full frame camera I stumbled across the 1Ds MkII. For the sake of brevity, I have kept my review mainly to bullet points, as I find them easier to process!

PROS
- Incredible build quality, weather-proofed, solid
- Ergonomic and comfortable design, even for long hours shooting
- Fantastic image quality, just outstanding all around
- Full frame sensor (is there any other choice?)
- 17MP resolution is more than you will ever need (most likely)
- Autofocus is incredibly fast and accurate
- Deals with Dynamic Range better than most other digital camera
- Built-in grip makes portraiture more than easy
- Very good battery life (14+hrs non-stop wedding)
- Non-electronic shutter sound (I hate the rebel's sound)
- Comes with DC Coupler for studio work
- Digital noise is decent up to 800ISO

NEUTRAL
- 4fps for 11 RAW images
- Quite heavy, especially with L glass. Could be pro or con depending on how you shoot.

CONS
- Small LCD (by today's standards at least)

You need to know that the megapixel war going on between camera manufacturers is absolute marketing hype. It's true. Packing more pixels into the same size sensor DOES NOT GREATLY IMPROVE IMAGE QUALITY, in fact several of the latest professional DLSRs are being criticized for high digital noise, a byproduct of cramming megapixels in. 16MP is more than enough to print out large, movie poster sized images. I have printed LARGE canvas wraps for wedding clients and they look absolutely beautiful. This camera is not lacking in high-tech features, and even now in 2012 I find it more than enough.

Overall if you have the cash to spare and you're not interested in video capabilities, skip the 5D Mkii and go with this camera. The autofocus is fantastic, the image quality beautiful, and all in all it is a joy to shoot with. This wedding photographer won't be using anything else until the newer 1D series drop in price!

title: Small but Rugged
text:
Purchased to bring on my kayak when paddling. We had a particularly bad time this year on the river and many of us capsized. My Eton Rugged was strapped to the deck of my boat, which was turned under water. The boat ended up wedged, upside down, under a tree in the river. Rushing water forcing itself into everything I owned, including my Eton Rugged. I know it's water resistant, not waterproof. After struggling to free the boat, the Rugged was gone! We searched and searched and found the little guy 50 ft away in deeper water after it got washed away. So, 15 minutes of rushing water followed by a dunk for at least 10-15 minutes, no way was this thing ever going to work.
Back at camp the next morning, I took out the Eton Rugged and placed it in the sun all day to dry out, the red LED indicated the solar charge was working, no other buttons worked though. Poor guy was making death sounds as it dried out, I knew it was a lost cause. I kept trying all day and night to get it to come back on, but no luck.
Fast forward one week, I come back from another trip to find my little Rugged sitting on my counter. On a whim, I pressed the power button and voila! it powered on and stayed on! I got a little excited and fired up the music app on my phone, glorious bluetooth streaming music was being pumped out of my Rugged! It may look a little beat-up, but this guy still cranks!

TL;DR
It works after being drowned in a river. Your mileage may vary.

Unfortunately J&R ran out of stock so I can not replace them with the same pair. I have owned several pair of relatively high-end cans... my current favorites are my Bowers & Wilkins P5's, which blow the CitiScapes away (in all categories) the way a Porche would a Miata, in fact it's not even that close. I also own a pair of Grado SR-80's which rival and actually sound a bit nicer than my P5's. I did not except CitiScapes to rival either of those but I thought it would come much closer. I did take the time to break in the CitiScapes by playing a variety of music continuously non-stop for the better part of 3 straight days! After which I still wanted to trash them. I purchased these as a gift for my little brother who's been wanting a pair of the over-priced Beats. Now I'm embarrassed to give them to him and don't have any options to return these for anything better at the sale price I paid. Maybe I got a bad pair, in fact that's the only explanation that would make sense, however I haven't been able to get my hands on another pair to test that hypothesis. I do know the pair I have sound terrible and I can't imagine why other people here would give this product any more than 1 star. title: Highly protective, but bulky
text: The Otterbox Defender for iPad Mini Retina is a highly protective,  solid case.  I do not doubt that it will be protected during a drop or a fall.  Without the front lid (that doubles as a tilt stand), the mini feels nice in the hand.  The lid is great for protecting your mini in a purse or luggage.  Though highly protective,  the case is not without its flaws.  Firstly, it is bulky and heavy.  It adds a considerable amount of weight to what was once a feather light device.  Secondly,  there are Newton Rings (oil slick effect/rainbow rings) on the screen.  This is due to the static electricity between the built-in screen protector and the mini's screen.  The "oil slicks" are very noticeable when the screen is off, and somewhat noticeable when the screen is on.  Thirdly, the case is difficult to pry remove and pry open.  When installing, be sure to get every last speck of dust or lint out before you make that final closing snap together of the pieces.  Because one annoying speck of dust that you miss the first time around may require you to reopen and re-wipe and re-install.  Prying the pieces off can be a bear.  I feared harming my screen every time I had to remove fhe cover.  Overall, the case is built to protect and will protect, however not without the cons of added bulk, added weight, "oil slicks" and difficult removal.

title: I Gave Up On The K760
text:
I used this keyboard for a few months and it was very irritating in my setup.

In an environment with Bluetooth (Bt) speakers & trackpad, as well as a wireless DAC that uses the same spectrum, the K760 often lost connectivity with the desktop while typing. It was very bothersome. I have used 4 other Bt keyboards in this setup and have not had any issues with dropped connectivity. The concensus is another Bt radio in the environment is causing interference; however, the connection is reliable with my iPhone and iPad in the same environment. So, why does the K760 keyboard drop off and not the other keyboards? Also, why does this problem only happens with the desktop and not the iOS devices?

Since my original review, I have isolated the device interfering with the keyboard (the ADC) but it does not fix the issue: do I move a $600 piece of equipment to use the keyboard? No, instead I moved to keyboard out of my setup and replaced it with a Matias Slim One.

I wanted to like the K760 but, unfortunately, it is not compatable with my setup. I improved my rating from 2 to 3 stars since, for most people, I think this may be a good solution but I recommend buying it from somewhere you can easily conduct a return in case you experience the same issue as me.

title: Good value
text:
I ordered one of these for a friend who found herself needing to mount a small set-top box near a TV that is on a swinging wall mount in her kitchen. Her cable TV provider (Charter Communications) is phasing out direct COAX-to-TV connections.

This mount is the perfect size for the STB and it has a pleasant design. The glass is attached to the metal bracket with double-sided tape, allowing you to either mount the glass flush with the wall, or allow a small gap to pass cables between the wall and back edge of the glass.

There are only two drawbacks:

1. The mounting hardware isn't ideal for drywall installations. The included anchors are suitable for mounting into studs, but don't do a good job with drywall and hollow spaces. I replaced the anchors with toggle bolts.

2. The weight of the STB makes the shelf droop because the bracket isn't gusseted. The small Charter Communications STB is relatively light, lighter than a DVR or DVD/Blu-Ray player would be, and the front of the shelf sits about one inch lower than the back when the STB is on it. I worked out in my case because I happened to leave enough space to have enough clearance between the bottom of the shelf and the TV below it, but cosmetically it doesn't look great and if you don't anticipate the droop, you may wind up with extra holes in the wall that you will need to fill in.

title: The camera froze two weeks after I got it...this review is for both the camera and customer service experience.
text:
This review is being written for both the camera and subsequent customer service experience when the camera froze. Unfortunately, the abysmal customer service experience is driving the rating for this review.

The good: The camera takes great still photos and video. It looks amazing on a hi-definition television. The camera is easy to use and setup. Changing settings in the Go Pro app is a very nice touch as well.

The bad: I received the camera on December 31 2013. The camera was purchased to take on a snorkeling trip the second week in January. After a few uses, the camera froze on January 18. I contacted Go Pro customer service the day that the camera failed and spoke with Thomas who ran through the standard troubleshooting steps on the phone. After a few minutes, Thomas informed me that I would need to make a warranty claim. He set it up and told me to call back after the camera had shipped to expedite Go Pro getting a replacement in the mail to me. I shipped the camera on the 18th but because it was a Saturday, the camera did not actually go out until Monday morning.

I called and emailed Monday January 20th to let them know that the camera had shipped. I received an email from Sterling with the following “Thank you for reaching out to us today, I'm glad to hear the package has been shipped! I've created the order for your replacement camera to be shipped out and we will be dropping this in the mail shorty.”

I had not received the camera so I called back the following Monday (January 27th). I can’t remember the name of the person that I spoke with but he informed me that the cameras were back ordered the week before and my replacement had not been shipped yet but the replacement would go out that day. He told me that if I did not see my replacement by the end of the week to call back.

Friday January 31st comes and goes and I still have not received my replacement. I called Go Pro and spoke with Austin this time. At this point, I am getting pretty frustrated with all of the lip service! Austin informs me that the camera had not shipped yet but would that afternoon. I expressed my frustration with the process and informed him what was told to me in previous conversations. His response was “well, sir, that was not what you were told”. As a matter of fact, it certainly was! I am again told to call back if I don’t see my replacement by the end of the following week.

Friday February 7th comes and no camera. At this point, I call Go Pro AGAIN and speak with Nicole. Nicole informs me that she is not showing tracking information, nor is she showing that the camera has shipped. I am pretty irate at this point. Nicole tells me that she needs to go hunt this down and asks if she can call me back. Based on the poor customer service experience so far, I ask her is she is taking hours or a few days before she would have an answer and call me back. Nicole states that she will call me back within the hour. This was at 2:50 PM.
At 5 PM, I had not yet heard back from Nicole. I called Go Pro back AGAIN. This time I spoke with Ryan. Ryan puts me on hold for a few minutes to research the issue. When he gets back on the line, he proceeds to tell me that the camera STILL has not shipped because Go Pro did not fill out the shipping information correctly…specifically, they had entered a billing address but no shipping address! Are you kidding me? Why was no one else able to fix the issue, or at a minimum, figure out that the camera was never shipped. Ryan was helpful and very apologetic. He shipped the camera and I should have it tomorrow. Nicole never called back either to make sure that everything was squared away.

I guess when you are pretty much the only game in town you can treat customers any way that you want. While I have no issues with the fact that the camera froze (seems a bit odd, but sometimes things happen), I am appalled at the manner with which the “customer service” people treated the entire issue. If I owned Go Pro, I would be extremely embarrassed at the manner in which my employees treated a user of my product.

title: All Around Review
text:
I was torn between giving this 4 or 5 stars, and finally settled on 5 after checking out the competition at this price range. I'll sort my review starting with what's the most important to me to the least. Let me say I'm very very picky when it comes to headphones, and I really feel like I got a winner with these.

First, I want to go into comfort. While you buy headphones for sound, I believe that unless they are comfortable sound is irrelevant. Please note, these are ON EAR headphones. That means the cushions are supposed to sit directly on the cartridge of your ears. The cushion is very soft and very comfortable for short uses and decent for extended wear. In the end comfort will be based on your ears and how these sit on them more than anything else. I recommend you to go to your nearest electronics store (I found the Sol Republic Tracks HD at Best Buy) and put them on your head for a little. If you don't like the way they feel, don't get them. On ear is not for everyone, especially those with sensitive ears/cartilage piercings/glasses. I have worn these for up to 2 hours straight with no complaints, though.

I saw a lot of comments from people who claim their large heads make this headphone uncomfortable for them. Well, I have a XXL motorcycle helmet size and these are perfectly fine for me. There is enough tension in the headband to keep the sound engines (the speakers basically) firmly on my ears without feeling like someone's trying to squash my head. The headband does have a small pad of cushion at the top, which I found to be a plus.

Next, let's talk about sound. Before I go into this topic though, please note which "Tracks" you are buying! This is important as it will change the listening dynamic. These are "Tracks HD" have a V10 sound engine which is the mid-range between the Tracks and the Tracks Ultra. The headphones are bass-heavy, but unlike Beats, it does not muddle up the mids and the highs. I compared this to my brother's Beats Solo HD, and wow does this blow that out of the water! It's much much clearer in the mids and highs which makes the bass is MUCH more pronounced. Both of us also noticed that there was far less "static" or "white noise" coming from the head phones. The sad part is my brother paid over $200 (after taxes) for his Beats Solo HD, while I paid $96 (after taxes) for these Tracks HD. I have yet to hear headphones in the $100-$150 price range that produce as an enjoyable sound as these do.

As a side note on sound, I do like noise isolation which is why I almost gave this a 4 star rating. The on ear design and fit of these headphones is great, but since it is not over ear design, there will be limited sound isolation. It'll keep out softer sounds (like a keyboard typing) but anything louder than that comes through pretty easy. I decided not to knock down a star for this since it is on-ear and not over-ear, and it doesn't purport itself as noise isolating. One plus is it also knocks down what I consider to be it's top rival at the price range (the Beats Solo HD) in isolation. I wore the two of them and noticed a definite difference Although if you compare the two side by side, the SOL Republic Tracks do have larger speaker bodies, so this is what probably helps.

Next, is aesthetics. You can see it for yourself in pictures, but they don't do it much justice. The sound engine's rims are a dark purple with a slightly textured metal finish, and a "matte" silver finish on the face plate. Both elements have a sheen to them rather than a shine. The frame is a transparent plastic with the inside being of a black color. I must admit it looks really nice when all pieced together. I use it at work and while at the gym and I have gotten quite a few comments and compliments especially since it doesn't look like the carbon copy Beats every else owns.

Finally, I want to talk about the build. I like that cord that comes with the Tracks has a three button in-line remote & mic which is Apple friendly. While the center button works on every device I own that supports in-line remotes, the volume buttons don't work on most other devices. For those who own non-Apple devices, the stock cable will not support the microphone (that means no calls) that comes standard with the Tracks. You will need to go get yourself a set of ClearTalk Cables with Single Button Remote and Microphone (also made by SOL Republic) to get microphone support. Also, as others have noticed, the part of the cable that forks out and plugs into each sound engine is kind of thin. It seems shielded enough but only time will tell if it will hold up to extended use. However, all parts are interchangeable, which means if anything breaks you can purchase it for much cheaper than buying a whole new headset. It also comes with a soft padded carrying case (made out of neoprene for those who are familiar with the material) which will help against scratches, light drops, and being jostled around in a backpack. Just don't go chucking it out a window or off a building and you should be okay. The carrying case can be a bit finicky since it's soft and flops around when you try to put the headphones in, but it works like a charm.

So overall, for the price, I would give this a 5 star rating. All the characteristics that matter to me, (comfort, sound, aesthetics, and build) these Tracks are at the top (especially since you can get them for under $100 here on Amazon).

To wrap up:

PROS:
Great sound for the price range (I JUST CHECKED THEY ARE ON SALE FOR 87.95 WHAT ARE YOU WAITING FOR)
Comfortable even for those with large heads
Easily outclasses supposedly similarly ranked "Beats Solo HD"
Eye-catching looks
Sturdy build with interchangeable parts
Carrying case is nicely padded and included with the Tracks HD level

CONS:
Not the best noise isolation
Build of headphones feels really solid, cord, however, is questionable (time will tell)
Comfort is subjective, probably more on head shape and ear shape than actual size

title: Strong and works great, but you may have to add your own padding.
text:
I would have voted a 5 stars if the rubber pad had the right thickness, but they do not. You will have to create and your own pad to correct the problem. The slot at the bottom of the metal hub needs to aligned parallel to the camera in order to make the locking mechanism to work on the Movo MB1000 vest. For my Canon 5D mark ii and 1Dx, they were both in wrong position (one is 90 the other is 45 degree off the mark) when it is tighten. I cut a piece of thin and flat (1/2-1/4 of thickness of credit card) plastic from some package material, punched a small hole, put it next to the metal hub, cut the plastic into circular shape with the same size of the hub, and put on the rubber pad. I had to experiment with plastic of different thickness to get the hubs into the right position on camera. I would suggest that the manufacturer should supply a few extra rubber or plastic pad with thickness range from maybe 0.2-1.0mm, so user can choose one of them to align the hub to the correct position when mounted on the specific camera.

So if you are willing to do some pad making job yourself like I did, these hubs may work for you.perfectly. Otherwise wait for MOVO to resolve this problem before you purchase. You would NOT want to risk your expensive camera flying off the vest because it was NOT able to be locked into correct position :(unless you could sue MOVO for the damage resulted from the failed device).

title: Surprisingly fast for a budget-priced class-10 card [Update: Card died within 18 months]
text:
I purchased this product ([[ASIN:B004QU5GJU Wintec 3FMUSD32GBC10-R Filemate 32 GB Mobile Professional Class 10 Micro SD HC Card]]) mainly because it was one of the lowest-priced class-10 card available. Previously I have tested the full-side version ([[ASIN:B0046TJAJ8 Wintec Filemate 32 GB Professional Class 10 Secure Digital SDHC Card]]) and was less than impressed. This microSDHC card, however, exceeded my expectation.

I benchmarked the Wintec card upon its arrival, using the CrystalDiskMark program (v3.01 x64). My card reader used was the [[ASIN:B009D79VH4 Transcend Information USB 3.0 Card Reader (TS-RDF5K)]]. Here is the outcome:
- Its Sequential Write speed is 13.7MB/s, which means it exceeded the requirement of a class-10 card (10MB/s)
- Its Sequential Read speed is 34.8MB/s. Note that the Read speed is actually limited by the USB 2.0 port of my computer.

For comparison, the [[ASIN:B007XZM6VG SanDisk Ultra 32 GB microSDHC Class 10 UHS-1 Memory Card SDSDQUA-032G-U46A]] delivered slightly slower Write speed of 12.6MB/s, and identical Read speed of 34.8MB/s. On the other hand, the Sandisk did much better in terms of Random Write speed, scoring nearly twice as fast as the Wintec card in writing tiny files. See my benchmark results uploaded to 'Customer Images' section for details.

As of this writing, the Wintec microSDHC card is priced about 25% less than the Sandisk UHS-1 micro card, so I consider it s good deal.

Other points of interest:
- The Wintec card I received is made in Korea, while the Sandisk card is made in China
- The capacity of this Wintec card, as reported by my computer, is only 29.3GB. This is a bit less than the 29.6GB reported for the Sandisk card.
- The fastest microSDHC card I have tested is the [[ASIN:B00A4A1TYM Lexar microSDHC 300x 32GB UHS-I Flash Memory Card LSDMI32GBBNL300R]]. It achieved 25.6MB/s in Write and 35.0MB/s in Read.

[Update on Oct 20, 2014]
I have this Wintec card in my [[ASIN:B00AGAYQEU Noble NOOK HD+ Tablet]] for the past year. Just recently I noticed that the card is no longer recognized by the tablet. I removed the card and tested it on two different computers and card readers, but the card is completely dead. Downgraded the product rating for its poor reliability.

title: Composite enclosure, ready for finished spaces.
text:
This structured media wiring enclosure is made of a composite instead of the more traditional metal cases from leviton or other manufacturers on the market. The goal of this construction is to enable the homeowner to keep your main home gateway router and wireless access point inside the enclosure without having signals impacted by the enclosure material. And it works as advertised.

The enclosure is 35"x20"x5" with stud 'wings for easy mounting. The depth of the unit is designed for a traditional 2x4 wall construction with finished drywall, sitting proud with the door and flange covering the rough opening in the drywall. While this is best situated for installation before your drywall is in, its theoretically possible to do a retrofit install, providing your electrical and low voltage wiring is roughed in and you've allowed for the 20" width.

As expected it works with the Leviton media panel modules for low voltage terminations and the surge suppressor punch outs for single and multiple outlets for running switches or other devices in the enclosure. While the design of this enclosure is meant for running a router/AP inside with flow through venting in the door, you may want to make sure your devices are not running hot. The natural flow of heat out at the top should pull in cool air in the bottom vents with convection, you may wish to plan for a intake fan. YMMV. I've just used mine for wire termination and management.

Solid product line, fit for use, and removes the "ugly" when in a finished space.

title: good sensitivity bad software support for tweaking
text:
This mouse isn't bad but if you buy premium mice. If not you are going to notice a lot of features that A) one really doesn't need and B) its VERY sensitive and there aren't enough software features to tweak to keep its sensitivity from tripping you up.

I'm a CAD artist as well as an avid internet lurker so I depend on the wheel button to do a lot of tasks in my daily routine; from opening new tabs to navigating in 3D space and both of those things I find frustratingly difficult with this mouse until I learned the trick to it.

Like I said in the opening statement, unless you are used to using a mouse with a lot of sensitivity to it then you are probably going to have problems adjusting to this mouse, particularly the scroll wheel. Unlike older mice this one has no resistance to the scroll wheel and those users who have developed gross reflexes to click the mouse wheel will be surprised by the behavior of a failed click.

I knew the mouse wasn't bad when I got it but it took me about a week to realize I lacked a certain finesse for this mouse. Since there is no play in the default (w/ or w/o drivers) scroll function even the slightest turn of the wheel while pressing the button will cause the action you achieve to be a page scroll. This also applies to tilting the wheel. These problems come down to basically relearning how to middle click with this mouse without deviating your finger.

Furthermore the software, while useful, is not very responsive. While the mouse without driver software works perfectly fine (with the additional two buttons acting as "forward/back" browser buttons that you can't change or disable threw default mouse options) with the software installed every click you do is piped threw the software service adding a tiny delay to certain actions that don't conform to the default behaviors of the buttons.

For instance "Middle-Click" has a default behavior of "Flip" in the software which explodes the screen into window tiles you can chose from similar to Alt-tab on Linux or Mac. Useful? Yes, but not the behavior I expected. In browsing you might not noticed the delay in the mouse and chalk it up to page lag but in CAD the delay becomes more pronounced when trying to pan a camera and being forced to acknowledge the problems two fold, first the practiced click to activate panning then the lag that delays you by milliseconds which quickly add up to frustration.

For artists who depend on the middle click function of their mouse I would not recommend this mouse unless you are willing to relearn how to use it for the sake of precision. You can get a lot of precision out of this mouse with some very simple software however you have a lot of sensitivity that you can't do much about unless you can program and your willing to eat more delay in the mouse during your work flow.

Common application usage for gaming and web browsing of this mouse is fine if you can acknowledge the problem with the hardware and wait for the drivers to come out that solve the issue. Its very comfortable and useable on a wide variety of surfaces. Most red laser mice don't work well on my desk without a piece of felt glued to the surface but this one works on bear plastic/wood (textured) with a bit of gloss to it. For basic usage you get used to the sensitivity of the rest of the functions and they can easily be tweaked for your needs threw the mouse properties in the control panel.

I would recommend everyone getting this mouse go to microsoft.com and download the Intelepoint software for this device so that it works properly with all the programmable button features even if it costs you a little lag in your work flow. For a cheap mouse it offers a lot of good features even if its lacking a bit of control, the trade off isn't so much bad hardware for your money but functionality threw software that becomes the issue. I'll keep using this mouse at least up until the return period from the retailer I bought it from however individually I recommend you all heed this as a "buyer beware" that it might not work as you expect it to and consider it carefully before buying it and footing a return postage bill to send it back.

title: CLICK7 a nice DVD system with a a very nice mounting system
text:
I bought a new car but didn't want to pay the exorbitant rates dealers charge for their factory installed DVD systems. I also wanted a system that was easy to mount and looked professionally installed. The CLICK7 fulfilled that requirement.

The value pack gives you 2 DVD players, 2 wireless headphones, and 2 stanchion mounts. After you attach the stanchion mounts to your headrest, which takes no more than 5 minutes, you plug the mounts in and slide the dvd players on to the mounts.

The players and mounts attach very solidly so you don't have to worry about them jostling lose. I have noticed no skipping on playback and the wireless headphones supply very good sound, but the internal speakers are pretty quiet to the point you can't really hear them, so you really do need the wireless headphones.

I wanted to mount each DVD player in 2 different cars. They only supply one DC input cable with 2 outputs and they use a proprietary connector into the DVD players, both of which I found disappointing. For me, I used the DC input cable in one car and the AC adapter (supplied) in the other car where I was lucky enough to have an ac output socket installed, so I worked around the issue. It would have been nice if they had supplied 2 DC input cables for this purpose.

Another disappointment is that the DVD players are not Blu-Ray players. Not a show-stopper, but I have been buying mostly Blu-Ray movies lately, so it would have been nice if the players were updated for Blu-Ray.

In summary, these are good, but relatively pricey, DVD players with an excellent mounting system for those that want a system to entertain the backseat passengers which looks professionally installed.

title: Sounds Great, Not as bad as some make it seem
text:
For starters, I read a majority of these bad reviews, though still decided to risk it and purchase these. Just to get any expectations out of the way, here's what these ARE NOT:

-Sennheiser or anything comparable
-For someone looking for the best headphones money can buy
-Equipped with Dolby, DTS, SRS or anything of the like

This headset is great for the money, and while a tad uncomfy after a lengthy period of time, they'll become accustomed to your head shape. I have a large head, based on my hat size, and I wore these for 3 straight hours before they even started becoming uncomfortable. For those saying that Motorola shows the wrong way to wear them, you are wrong. They are designed to go over the ear, not under, and to further cement that fact, there's a rubber coated area where they rest on your neck, when worn properly. If you flip them, then the shiny plastic side rests on your neck, which negates the point of the more comfy rubber coating.

As far as sound goes, to me these sound great. I appreciate great sounding speakers and headphones, and while these aren't the best you can buy, they sound excellent for what they are. Part of the problem I think some are having is that these don't go in your ear like an earphone, but more rest just outside your ear canal, as they're too thick to be pushed into your ear, so the sound isn't as bass-y as an earphone would offer. These offer more of a surround type sound, though to me the bass was sufficient. You can download an equalizer for Android phones to further improve loudness and such, as some say they're too quiet. For me on my HTC Thunderbolt, I have the sound 3/4 turned up on the phone, and maybe halfway on the headset and it sounds plenty loud for me, with room to spare.

I work in service at a Dodge dealership, so there are plenty of loud noises from air tools and such to fight with for sound, and I still managed to hear my music fine. It's cold, so I'm not really sweating much at work, and I've had no shorting out of the controls as some say, and that's with minimal amounts of sweat.

17.3" 1920x1080 @ 60Hz

Now for my impressions:

Overall, I'm happy with the computer. The screen is beautiful. The trackpad works well. I've been able to run Minecraft at max settings with 60+fps, & Mechwarrior Online at max settings around 25-30fps. The fans are quiet & effective. The case seems well built, & a large panel on the bottom provides easy access to the hard drive bays, 2 open RAM slots, & one of the fans. The other fan is accessible from a separate panel.

The computer does have some minor issues, but nothing I can't deal with. They keyboard is mediocre. Not bad to type on, but not as good as the Vaio laptop I've used. Locating volume controls on fn+f10 through fn+f12 was a poor design choice. I would rather see them on fn+f2 through fn+f4, swapping places with keyboard brightness settings & the wireless switch. They're my most used fn command, & yet the hardest to reach. The home/pgup/pgdn/end layout is also a bit unintuitive to me. The one upside is a bump on the w key to help find wasd when gaming. The speakers are decent, but not great. The subwoofer receives a full range signal, & with the factory drivers may play even with headphones plugged in. Updated drivers will fix the headphones issue. Check the ROG forums for a link.

In summary:

Pros:
- Good performance for price
- Great screen
- Stays cool & quiet
- Seems well built
- Easily accessible/upgradable RAM slots (2 of 4) & HDD bays
- Raised bump on w key for wasd when gaming.
- Decent trackpad

Cons:
- Mediocre keyboard, not the greatest layout.
- Mediocre speakers, must update drivers to work properly with headphones

I would buy this laptop again.

title: A GoPro Accessory Best Buy!
text:
For eight bucks this suction cup mount can't be beat! I have this one and GoPro's (for which I paid a hefty $40). I haven't used GoPro's since this one arrived. Why? First, this one is smaller, a cup diameter of only 2-1/2" vs. GoPro's 3-3/8", and thus it's easier to store in my Pelican case and easier to work with in tight quarters. Second, and I REALLY like this, it has a ball mount that allows for almost limitless adjustment with the twist of a knob! The world is not linear, so with most camera mounts we have to go through all kinds of gymnastics to get the camera lined up right. With this mount -- problem solved!

If I'm ever invited to test drive an Indy or Formula One car I'll probably use my GoPro suction mount. Why take chances, right? But so far I haven't found anything that that one will adhere to that this one won't. I even stuck this on my freezer door and hung a 5 lb. Olympic barbell weight from it to see what would happen. Five hours later it was still there and I figured I'd seen enough.

I have not experienced any of the ball-mount stability problems other reviewers mention. I agree the thumbscrew feels like it's lighter weight than it should be. I keep waiting for it to snap as I over-torque it. But appearances apparently are deceiving because it continues to take my abuse. Besides, if it breaks I'll just buy a new one. I can get 3,4, or even 5 for the price of GoPro's.

title: Case Logic has created an unbeatable value for pro DSLR users in need of a holster.
text:
As a pro photographer, one thing that becomes clear very quickly is that costs can add up quickly. Accessories such as camera bags, flashes, light modifiers, memory cars, batteries, ND filters and CPL filters can all be quite expensive!

When I first handled the Case Logic DSH-103 Luminosity Large Pro DSLR Holster, the first thing I thought of was one of my go-to camera bags - the Think Tank Digital Holster 40 V2.0 - and that is a good thing, as the Think Tank is a high quality bag which is a similar style of holster carrying case. The holster-type designs are compact and make more sense for daily use than carrying around one of the larger "gadget bags" or camera backpacks. Like the specific Think Tank case mentioned, with the bottom fully expanded the Case Logic DSH-103 can hold a "pro" DSLR (i.e. full frame DSLR with integrated or user-attached battery grip) along with up to a 24-70mm f/2.8 lens with hood in shooting position or a 70-200mm f/2.8 lens with hood in reversed position. A thicker lens like the Canon 70-300mm f/4-5.6L should also fit fine in this bag.

Case logic takes a similar overall approach with a top handle and shoulder strap. There are several outer compartments - front, side and rear - giving this case more storage space than the Think Tank Digital Holster 40. The Case Logic DSH-103 also includes a rain cover like the Think Tank case, and inner compartments to hold smaller items such as batteries and memory cards. In addition, a velcro divider is included in case you want to use a smaller lens than the ones mentioned or to simply reduce movement in the bag. When held, the Case Logic case also feels a bit better balanced than the Think Tank case.

One large difference between the Think Tank Digital Holster 40 v2.0 and the Case-Logic DSH-103 is price; at the time of this review, the Think Tank product is $25 more expensive! The extra cost does seem to prove worthy in some areas; the Think Tank product has smoother zippers and the case feels more rigid & sturdy, and the think tank product also can attach to Think Tank's belt systems in addition to being a standalone product.

It is clear Case Logic has a winning product here. They have created an experience that is very similar to one that costs much more money. Now, while Think Tank does offer some quality improvements for that extra money, one must ask themselves if it is worth $25 for smoother zippers and more sturdy build. In some cases it definitely might be, but if you are not a fulltime professional shooter I believe the Case Logic DSH-103 will do the job just fine for a lot less money. After all, all those costly accessory prices add up to the cost you could be spending on a new lens! Highly recommended for photographers looking for a great design without breaking the bank.

title: These ear pads are very comfortable, and work extremely well with the QC15 headset
text:
This review is for both the Bose QC15 headset and the replacement ear pads, as used in combination. For starters, I've been a Bose fan since 2003 when I bought my first noise canceling headset. My current headset had started to fall apart after about 3 years of use. I've worn multiple brands of aviation grade headsets, and used several brands of earbuds. These ear pads are very comfortable, and work extremely well with the QC15 headset. As a note on installation, there are small tabs on the QC15 rim that you have to 'snap' the ear pads past in order to secure a solid fit. Due to the size of the headset, these ear pads are not a direct fit around your ears by just plopping them into place. They cup your ear, and snug up around your ear to more effectively block external sound. This simply means that you have to move them around a little bit to get a comfortable fit, and an effective sound barrier. I've worn these at 'moderate' temperatures, and they proved comfortable over a moderate work shift (3 hours or so between breaks, max). I have not tried them at high temps or for extended periods of unbroken use. From my use of aviation headsets, I'd expect these to remain comfortable for any reasonable duration of wear. The sound damping effect of these ear pads was at least as good, or better, than the original equipment produced by the manufacturer (Bose), in my personal opinion. I tested these in an open bay operations center with dozens of phones, work stations, and mission areas, all with rather intense levels of activity. When I put these on and activated the noise canceling electronics, the noise diminished. When I added some music, the chaos and distraction virtually disappeared.

Of note, the replacement mesh ear cup liners are an improvement over the manufacturer's version. They seemed (to me) stiffer than the original version, but that may be due to age on the part of my previous version. Overall, they felt slightly heavier than the original version. I also liked the + - ) smiley face on them. (the + and - are at a 90 degree turn relative to the 'smile', but I'm limited to what the keyboard can present). The adhesive strips were more precisely placed than the originals, the material seemed to be of bette quality, and they had a techy smile on them. i'd almost buy these for that upgrade alone.

Overall, the sound damping and comfort of these ear pads is at least as good as the original equipment. They bought me several hours of solace in an otherwise chaotic work environment, which I would consider cheap at twice the price. I would recommend these to anyone looking to replace their ear pads. I had previously bought a lower priced set, and they were 'worth what I paid', which is to say, NOT comparable to these ear pads. In this case, you get what you pay for, and these were well worth the money.

title: Battery pack poorly thought out
text:
The basic light itself is well made, very bright, and nicely variable. Also has a nice carrying case to protect it in transit. However, it has a very short battery life, making it difficult to use on longer shoots.

Enter the extra battery pack! Yeah!

Unfortunately the external battery pack is VERY poorly thought out. It screws into the handle end mount. Not a bad idea, except that the hole is not deep enough to allow it to screw tightly. Thus, it hangs and wobbles, and doesn't feel secure.

Then there is the fact you have to attach the battery power via a small external, loose cable that will almost certainly be lost. Custom cable, short length, not attached anywhere. Guess how long that will last?

Also, it is not possible to charge both the internal and external battery together. You must charge one, then move the charger to the other to charge it. Would have been trivial to allow a connection that charged both together, but apparently they just didn't think of it...

Lastly, the carrying case for the iceLight has no provision for carrying the external battery pack. I would have thought there would a longer version, or perhaps a flap to allow the battery to remain connected, but nope. The battery is yours to store elsewhere, meaning you have to disconnect-travel-reconnect (and the connection knob is hard to turn too...).

All in all, the battery is the weak link here. If you can get by with the standard light internal battery time, then this is a 5-star product. I wouldn't give the battery itself more than 2-stars though. Since this review slot is mostly for the light, I gave it the benefit and made the final a 4-star review.

title: If you're having problems connecting to the device, their support is terrible, they finger-point.
text:
This is a well-made piece of electronics which does exactly what it is supposed to do. Actiontec has done a good job making this little box. When everything is working as expected, it displays a decent (if slightly lossy-compressed) picture. I found it quite serviceable for playing simple PC games and viewing web pages, projected on my big screen TV. I was able to change the resolution of the screen and it worked as expected, and it did all of the necessary handshaking on the HDMI connection to make the TV set display a proper picture. I could do a multi-monitor configuration with an extended desktop, and it worked just like I'd docked it to a wired monitor. It all looked good for what I needed it to do. Also, two members of my household with newer Android phones were able to connect to it and display their phone screens on the TV, including screen rotation. Worked great, and this thing is really inexpensive to boot. I remember when WiDi first came out, the adapters were in the hundreds, which kept me from buying one. Now that this thing is out, it's cheap enough to have been a no-brainer.

(Note: I haven't tried playing movies on it, because I have other ways of displaying movies on the TV set. I don't know whether the lossy data compression would make movies look bad or not. I know it looked OK for showing my computer desktop and simple games which didn't require a lot of full-screen updates that would stress the lossy data compression.)

So if it works so great, then why the two-star review?

The problem is, this little box relies upon software that Actiontec didn't write. Your computer needs to be able to connect to the thing, and that requires driver software and connection utility software (in this case written by Intel), and that's where I ran into trouble. When I first got the Actiontec, and my laptop couldn't connect to it, I contacted, in order:

- Actiontek support (phone, India).
- Actiontek advanced support (phone, USA).
- Intel support (phone).
- Computer manufacturer support (Sony, online).

Each one, in turn, was unable to solve my problem and pointed the support finger at the next company in the chain. Each support person was not knowledgeable about the problem at all, even when, in one case, I was escalated to advanced support after being online with the first-level support for over an hour. Each support tech just parroted all of the things in the online user guides and troubleshooting guides, stuff I had already tried. Things like re-installing display drivers and network drivers which I had already updated to the latest versions.

One particularly maddening moment was when the Actiontec advanced support tech tried to tell me that my brand-new Core i7 1.8ghz laptop did not have a fast enough CPU for WiDi, and was therefore not supported. Despite the fact that the laptop manufacturer advertises this particular model as being WiDi-ready, the product specs for the Actiontec do not list any CPU limitations at all, and that the Intel WiDi web site specifically lists my Core i7 processor as being supported for WiDi. I was really upset that the tech tried to blow me off with that BS line.

So the moral of the story is, when you buy a device which requires someone else's software to work, expect to get the finger pointing circle. Nothing has changed, that's always been the case in the computer industry. With this particular device, the software problems were particularly maddening. I was eventually able to get it to work, but it took days of research and experimentation, and the support calls were no help at all.

I was eventually able to get it working. In hopes that this will help someone else, here was my problem:

The instructions for the thing say, "In Windows 8.1, open the Charms Bar, press Display, press Project, then select "Connect to a wireless projector". The problem is that I never got that option. Windows kept showing me a different list of options in the charms bar. The screen it showed me was the screen that lets me choose between the different ways to project to an already-connected projector (Local display only, extend, duplicate, external display only). I never got the option to connect to the thing in the first place.

I could go into Devices And Printers, and tell it to Add Device, and it would search for and successfully find the Actiontek device on the wireless network, and the Actiontek would prompt me with a PIN number for connecting, and I would enter that PIN into the computer, and then it would start the connection handshaking process and.... fail with an error message. Every time.

Since I was getting a screen that made it look like I was already connected to an external display, then I thought maybe it was because I currently had drivers on the laptop installed for a USB3 docking station with external monitors. So I uninstalled that docking station software. No change. Still the same problems.

I ran the Intel WiDi update utility which makes sure the computer has all the correct drivers. It always says "No updates needed, your computer is ready for WiDi. Open the charms bar and select Display, Project,..." ARGH.

I tried installing the Intel connection utility for WiDi, and it actually refused to install it, saying that the computer didn't support the utility. Though I triple checked all the system requirements and my computer met every one of them. And of course Intel's own WiDi update utility had already said I should be good to go. That same intel connection utility installed fine on a second PC from a different manufacturer, also running Windows 8.1. I was able to connect to the Actiontec device with that other computer, using that Intel connection utility. So I knew the Actiontec worked correctly and it was just the bad Intel software on my main PC that was sending me in circles.

I googled online, and after a lot of digging, found one set of forum posts that looked promising. People were suggesting that WiDi needed the Microsoft Virtual Miniport driver, which wasn't there on my system. To get it to appear, other forum searches said that I needed to reinstall the Microsoft Hosted Network feature, using commands such as "netsh wlan set hostednetwork mode=allow", and "netsh wlan start hosted network". Those commands also did not fix the problem, did not make the Virtual Miniport driver appear, and in the process managed to set up my laptop to be sharing its internet connection via WiFi, something I didn't want it to be doing in the first place. So no luck there.

I tried a whole bunch of other things, so many things I don't remember them all now. Anything I could think of that might affect the display driver or the network driver, including full uninstalls and re-installs of the display driver and network drivers. Nothing worked.

At the very end, in desperation, I tried uninstalling VMWare Workstation and Oracle VirtualBox. These were two virtualization systems which allowed me to run an older Windows instance on the computer. I had been experimenting with them because certain older pieces of software won't run on my Windows 8.1 computer, and virtualization systems are one way to work around that problem. I knew that these VM systems installed special network drivers and display drivers which allowed them to piggyback onto your existing system's hardware. I thought perhaps they might have been interfering.

It worked after that. I can now connect to the Actiontec and use it as intended. The Charms Bar looks correct now, shows me the expected options. I'm not certain that the VMWare/Virtualbox thing was the real reason or not, since I had been trying so many other different things at the same time. But if you're in the same boat and happen to have either of those VM programs installed, that's something worth trying. I didn't see anywhere else online which suggested this as an option. And of course, it was not suggested to me by any of the tech support people that I contacted. If I can get a hold of Actiontek advanced support again, I'll let them know about it.

*UPDATE*: I ended up reformatting my PC from scratch recently, and sure enough, the WiDi stopped working when I installed Oracle VirtualBox, and it started working again when I uninstalled VirtualBox. Again, Actiontek and Intel had no clue about this.

title: Definitely a good laptop replacement
text:
When I bought this I wanted a tablet with a keyboard attachment that had one of the faster processors available as well as a good screen resolution, as well as a smaller tablet 7-8 inches because I do a some reading with the tablet I currently own. So I was sort of stuck between this and the Nexus 7_2 as well as the 7-8" Acer with Windows. The atom processors for Windows tablets seem like they run sort of sluggish, and the Nexus didn't have the processor speed, expandable storage, and HDMI output so I decided on this one. I would recommend when buying a tablet to buy one that has been on the market less than 6 months because there is a large difference in performance and what you are paying for the tablet.

For the tablet itself, it has great sound compared to other tablets I have seen and it does have two speaker ports on the bottom. The screen looks beautiful, and even with a ton of fingerprints you don't notice the fingerprints on the screen. I'm not sure how they did it but definitely a good feature. The screen is very bright and I usually have it set for a lower setting, so the screen can be readable even on a bright day. The keyboard attachment has worked flawlessly so far and the extra battery life that comes with it is a nice feature. I also like how HP set up the keyboard to have the home button where a typical Windows button would be. The back button where the escape key would typically go as well as several other nice keyboard shortcuts that really make it seem like the keyboard was definitely made for Android and not just a generic bluetooth keyboard.

I do have a couple of complaints but they are very minor. I wish the bezel around the screen was a little smaller. I think it would be a little easier to handle otherwise. Still I don't have any problems holding it but makes holding with one hand a little troublesome when reading in bed. Also when using Android, some websites will automatically have you go to their mobile sites, which can be a pain. I wish their was a setting to have all websites default to desktop versions. This happens with all Android tablets so you can't really expect HP to fix an Android issue. Overall I feel this is a quality product and I am very happy with my purchase.

title: Unreliable; silent data corruption; effective warranty below 1y.
text:
For quite a long time I've been WD fan. I put WD drives in any computer I put my hands on. I've sinned, but I know better now...

5 months ago I've bought 8 of those drives to exchange 7 1TB drives in my Linux server. The 1TB drives were (and are - I use them still) OK, I just run out of space. Since then I did not have a single week without some kind of failure. 3 drives are failing mechanically (almost 40% failure rate!), I have random intermittent read errors. I rolled up my sleeves and run some tests; this is what I've found:
The read errors coincide with only ONE relevant (Power On Hours is not relevant, for example) changing SMART attribute - Multi-Zone Error Rate. The description of it is a bit misleading and nobody really seems to know, what it is; here: [...] it says something about writing errors, but the writes to the disk were always OK - after a retry or retries the correct data was read. The problems appeared only while reading. And only when this parameter was changing (i.e. - growing).

The real big, bad issue is that the drive does not inform me about problems it had reading data! So far it looks like when the disk hits a problematic sector (so the MZER grows), instead of reporting that, it returns some arbitrary data and pretends everything is rosy - no read error, nothing - just corrupted data! So you might copy a file and find it later corrupted. Or your system will miraculously crash.

I would suggest returning this drive on the very first sight of MZER>0; even better - just avoid it altogether.

As a result, yet another disk has been RMAd to WD; hopefully they will accept it under warranty, as they did before; I really wouldn't like to give them only one star...

Yet they managed. If the drive is RMAed, the replacement has a warranty of... ~100 days. If the original, 3y-warranty drive breaks in first 6 months, the effective warranty will be shorter than 1 year! Oh, well, that's easy, sell crap with '3y warranty', when it breaks, shorten it to 10 months. Well done, WD.

Update 2013-05-11: Yet another drive had is MZER gone up, checksums found another file damaged. I think by now all of my 8 drives have been replaced, and the ONLY improvement is- the error happens less frequently. But when it happens, the result is as devastating as ever. If you value your data - DO NOT BUY.

Update 2013-10-17:
I'm looking for the replacement for my 8 3TB disks. Got to the reviews of Seagate 4TB NAS drives, and was astonished they actually react to the buyers' complaints! Nice! The WD apparently does not believe in reaching out to their customers, it's you who should call them; I did so a week ago. I asked them to buy the drives off me - 2 more drives failed in a week and I have enough. They were surprised I do not want this walking disaster of theirs for a drive any more. All they did since then is to create a support case, that stays on their website, abandoned. Very nice gesture, indeed, even if utterly useless. It seems not only the QA does not work there, PR is also a bit of a problem.
I think I will surprise them once more and share my WD adventures with C't. They might be interested in how good WD customer support and product quality are, even if WD is not.

Update 2013-11-08:
Well, 4 disks failed on me in the last month - two of them had <200 power-on hours (i.e. they were replacements for previously broken drives). Come on, all you brave testers with 3TB of discardable data, unlimited tinker time and money to waste - buy these.

Update 2014-04-04:
The latest development with these drives happened last year; I've been slightly slow on reporting ;). After some fight WD agreed to buy all the 8 drives off of me for 75% purchase price. I coughed-up a few EUR for a 4TB NAS drives of another manufacturer, and returned the Greens. Since then I forgot I have drives. I do not have to check their well-being constantly. I could delete all the recovery data. What a bliss...

title: One Problem No Solution as of yet
text:
OK so first let me tell you my set up. MAC 10,1 (late 2009) in one room, Mini Display port to HDMI Moshi Adaptar to bluerigger hdmi cable 25ft to 32" 720p LCD DYNAX tv in the same room. working flawlessly as a dual monitor. NOW i also have a third monitor attatched to my mac via "Cable Matters Premium USB 2.0 to HDMI Audio Video 1080P Adapter for Windows and Macbook" to bluerigger HDMI Cable 50ft to "Tripp Lite B122-000 HDMI Signal Booster Extender Repeater, 24Hz, HDMI F F" to bluerigger 3ft hdmi cable to 26" 1080p LED VIZIO tv in the next room. So that is my set-up.

Here is my review. As a third monitor it works fine with a slight delay. The reason for this set-up is i got rid of my cable television and boosted my internet speed and now watch all tv from the MAC onto either tv or the comp or all three at once if it suits us. If you want to know more about triple monitor set-up via mac contact me this review wont be on that as much. When i first set this up there was no HDMI SIGNAL BOOSTER i put a BLU-RAY movie (KUNG FU PANDA) and played it on the third monitor in the kids play room and there was a massive delay in the frames. The skipping of frames was unbearable for me to watch (the kids didnt seem to care) when i put in a DVD (CARS 2) the delay was reduced quite a bit but still existed. In trouble shooting trying to find out where the weak link was, I switched the two displays. I put the USB to HDMI to 25ft Cable To Dynax 32" 720p tv and the Mini Display To Moshi Adapter To Bluerigger 50ft to 26" LED Vizio. RESULTS: The Mini Display Port to 50ft cable to Vizio in the other room worked completely flawless. The USB to HDMI to 32" Dynax was 100 times better but still not perfect. The frame skipping was still present but at much smaller intervals and really only during high action scenes. So my conclusion was the USB to HDMI was sending a much weaker signal down the wire and therefore over 50ft it was way worse than at 25ft. I thought if i got the HDMI signal booster that might help with the problem and make the kids room third monitor a bit easier to watch. So i ordered one with a three foot HDMI cable to complete the connection. When it came in i was excited to try it out in hopes everything would work better. The results werent much better this time around. I was greatly disappointed.

Conclusion: I believe the bluerigger 3ft, 25ft, and 50ft HDMI cables work just fine. The Moshi Adaptar minidisplay port to HDMI works perfectly. My heartburn comes with the USB to HDMI adaptar and the HDMI signal booster. I know for a fact that the USB to HDMI just doesnt have enough power output to create a perfectly clear signal but knowing the 25ft cable works WAY better the signal booster should have helped duplicate that but it just didnt. So unfortunately my disappointment has yet to be resolved. (before anyone asks the Booster was in fact facing the right direction or you wouldnt get any signal at all and i did try the booster on both ends first the tv end then the computer end... no difference)
