title: Not what I thought it would be
text:
I bought a Nikon Coolpix L120 camera, and while waiting to get it, looked for batteries and a charger for it. This charger states it's FOR the Nikon Coolpix L120, so came up in search. The Nikon chargers and batteries only come with 4 batteries and are much more expensive.
I saw that the extra 4 batteries with this were lower power (2900) but assumed they would also work, since it's FOR THE NIKON COOLPIX L120!
I got the camera and charger/batteries (from different places) The camera works with non rechargeable batteries but hardly works with the rechargeables. And I set the camera to "rechargeable". The 3100 batteries work for awhile, but the 2900 (even though I charged them till the red lights went out and left them an hour after to be sure) will turn the camera on, take 2 or 3 pictures than die and camera says "battery exhausted".
The camera manual tells the kind of batteries it uses, and for rechargeable says "4 EN MH2 rechargeable NI-MH batters..." and "EN-MH1 can't be used"
Are the ones that come with this charger maybe MH1? Who knows, where does it say?
And it says on the listing (for sale) they are for the Nikon Coolpix L120 camera.
I don't know what to do now, can I now buy more powerful batteries, maybe the ones made by Nikon and will they charge in this charger? Can I charge bigger, more powerful batteries in this? Do I now have to buy more batteries and another charger?
I was wary about buying a Nikon because it takes AA batteries, my Canon Rebel (I love but wanted more zoom and video) uses a square battery that comes with a charger (not AA, etc) The battery needs charging about once a week. I have had cameras that take regular batteries before and even with a charger it's a hassle.
I just thought batteries and a charger that says it's FOR the camera I bought would work.
I looked over many reviews, at least for cameras before I decided on the one I got (I am on limited income, too) but apparently didn't see reviews for this battery charger and batteries, beforehand.
It might be useful, charging batteries for my remote and other things I have that take batteries, but I'm going to have to buy something else for the Nikon Coolpix L120...
I know, I could probably return it, but that's a hassle, too and the bigger size batteries (if I keep them charged) seem to work for awhile.
LATER... I found the batteries work better when charged for a longer time. I now leave them plugged in overnight or all day. Even after the charged light goes off. The directions say to leave them plugged in for 30 mins after the light says they are charged, but I am leaving them longer. There are 2 sets of batteries so I eave one set in overnight and then the other all day. next time I buy a camera I will get one with a rechargable battery to use with it and not "sepeaate" AA, etc. ones. (which isn't the fault of the charger)

title: "Last year's" phone? Who cares? Expectations exceeded!
text:
I was reluctant to venture into the "phablet" market. I had a nearly 5" smartphone and a 7.7" tablet so I wasn't looking to obtain an unwieldy hybrid.
But my previous phone (Stratosphere II) was nearly out of usable memory (suffering from the infamous SD app lock out).

I'm also not someone who "needs" to have the brandest new, most super spiffy device so I wasn't looking to drop $200+ on a discounted phone/contract renewal.

Last year's Galaxy s4 - at $0.01 price! - has exceeded expectations.
First, at 5.38", the screen is noticeably bigger but not excessively or uncomfortably so. I do have big hands which might be a factor, but this is about as big I would go.
Having doubled the internal memory and restored the full read/write capability of the SD (though not sure if this will survive the pending KitKat 4.4.4 update), all previous apps are running much smoother and have been able to add a few that had to be removed to free up memory on my old phone.

Haven't found anything to dislike yet.

UPDATE 09/30/14 - Still love the phone, but a troubling incident. I went to register the phone with Samssung and was told the IMEI number is invalid. Spent quite some time in a chat with Samsung and a call with Amazon - no resolution. The phone is working fine - though it has the 4.4.2 KitKat upgrade apparently before it was released. No one can explain how/why the IMEI is coming up as invalid. Theoretically, Verizon should not have activated the phone if that were true. The Samsung rep relayed that they do not support Amazon purchases as AMZ often sells non-US devices to the US market.

title: Decent point and shoot
text:
I lost the charger for my little w560 and after looking around a bit I was surprised to find out that Sony makes point and shoots with CMOS sensors for around 150 bucks. That intrigued me and even though my trusty w560 is still in perfect working order besides for the charger, I decided to upgrade. What I have discovered is that I need a point and shoot with the low light capabilities of this camera.

It's really amazing to be able to take decent pics indoors without the windows open or using the flash. This camera can do it. This camera also has a host of neat little shooting modes and color options as well as being capable of HD video with stereo sound. I have played with this camera for a week now and I'm still discovering new things buried in the menus. I'm very happy with my 150 dollar purchase and it's worth every penny.

Now for the cons. The build of this camera is smaller than my w560 and feels more flimsy. The smallness isn't a problem but coupled with the plastic feel it's a little bothersome as far as worrying about damaging the camera. The shutter button is also another issue, at least on my camera. The zoom function is tied into the shutter button and it will actually rattle if I shake the camera gently. I thought I had broken my camera when I used the zoom function the first time, it moves around and isn't seated firmly at all. It doesn't seem very stout and able to put up with much use. The screen is smaller than I imagined which is just a nit-pick.

The anti-shake technology also isn't everything the company preaches it is. In low light it does much better than a normal camera however hand shake is an issue. I mean if you can hold as still as is humanly possible you can get some great shots but if your subject is moving or you are moving for any reason, the image isn't usable which I expected. Even my Sony CMOS DSLR has issues with low light without using flash but the company shouldn't use the anti-shake in low light as a selling point making people believe something that isn't even possible with more professional products from this brand.

Having said all that, this camera is still deserving of 4 stars. Only the build and the bit of flamboyant marketing is questionable about this camera. I am a firm believer in Sony as being more bang for the buck and this camera is not an exception.

title: Universal Router extender - however it won't help in a motel/hotel
text:
My first question was "What is 802.11ac?" - In December 2011 "802.11ac" was the next evolution of WiFi & enabled wireless speeds over a gigabit per second.

"b" was the first there was (802.11b) which provided up to 11 mbps data rates per radio in the 2.4 GHz spectrum.
"a" was the next evolution (802.11a) which provided up to 54 mbps data rates per radio in the 5 GHz spectrum.
"g"came out shortly after enabling 54 mbps per radio in the 2.4 GHz spectrum.
"n" was ratified in 2009 (802.11n) allows for data rates up to 600 mbps per radio.
"ac" builds on 802.11n.

setup took 2 minutes; I plugged the TP Extender into a wall plug outside the room the router was in. Wait until the `power' and `wi-fi' LEDs light up; then press the WPS button on the router (this is the reason it isn't going to work at a motel/hotel). Then I pressed the Range Extender button on the TP Extender the lowest on the front of the device (must do it within 2 minutes). The LED on the TP Extender should go from flashing to solid, showing that WPS connection has succeeded. Done.

tips:

there are 6 lights on the TP Extender the top two should be green, if they are RED your extender is too far from the router. If it is no color it means you need to reconnect the router and the extender by repeating the steps above.

> to minimize wireless interference keep the Range Extender away from cordless phones, Bluetooth devices and Microwave Ovens.

> If possible place the TP Extender in open corridors or spacious locations rather than a crowded room.

Frankly I have not noticed any difference in our wi-fi but we have a smaller home (1700 sq feet) the router we have is 2 years old and is in one room in the house while I use my 3 year old laptop (Sony Viao series E) in the livingroom 2 rooms away and 2 walls away. I do plan on bringing it with us on vacation where I am hoping that where we do get poor reception (where we have access to a router), we will get a noticeable improvement.

The device has a reset option (if the TP Extender doesn't seem to be working): While the Range Extender is plugged into a power outlet, press the RESET button (located next to the ethernet port underneath the TP Extender) with a pen for 1 second. Wait 2 seconds until all the LEDs flash once.

*Bonus - The Range Extender's ETHERNET port allows it to function as a wireless adapter for a wired devices (Blu-ray players, game consoles, DVRs and smart TVs) allowing the device to share the wireless network.

title: Awesome but not without it's flaws
text:
I've had my fitbit for a few weeks now and I do like it quite a bit. I was going to buy the flex, but it was on back order and I couldn't wait to get started counting steps so I ordered the one. One feature that I have enjoyed quite a bit is the floor (elevation) counter. I'm currently living in the Pacific North West and as such I got at least one strenuous hike every weekend including some that have a very impressive amount of vertical gain. I really wish they had not removed this feature on the Flex...oh well. I love being able to compete with my friends, it's a great way to stay in great shape. I think it interesting to log food occasionally too, but sometimes unrealistic since you don't always know how much of what you are eating.

Like I said in the title there are various problems I do have with the device. It is far from perfect. I've been using the sleep tracking feature of the fitbit and yet it still seems to count steps while I am a sleep. I'm assuming this is caused by me tossing and turning in my sleep. It would make sense to me that these should not be counted as steps.
Also, I'm not positive exactly how the elevation measuring feature works, but I've noticed that I will get floors climbed over a drive where my elevation changes. This is another instance where to me it would make sense for the device to only count elevation gained while steps are also being counted. My last complaint is that the distance traveled does not seem to be very accurate when I am running. I use a gps tracker & conjunction with my fitbit and the fitbit usually 1-2 miles short of what the gps tracker tells me. I've heard that measuring stride length and updating it in the settings can help this, so I am going to try it out.

title: stops working when you upgrade
text:
My love for Sonos just went down the toilet. They did an "upgrade" on the 19th that crashed our Sonos access and Sonos decided to stop supporting certain operating platforms without giving the users any notice that if your Sonos is set to auto upgrade (which it does by default settings) it is no longer useable without upgrading all the computers you use as controllers.

The Sonos controllers are very expensive (actually almost as much as the system!) but one of the reasons we bought two Sonos systems 3 weeks ago was because we could use the three different PC's we already have as controllers for the various rooms in the house. We have a five year old MacBook with 10.4.11, a new Kindle Fire and a one year old Samsung Galaxy. That way we could control each system without running around the house trying to find which room the controller was in.

I finally got my Kindle to work after the "upgrade" yesterday but after calling the help desk about the MacBook and Galaxy, the response was, "We are tracking a known problem with the Android controller app and I can have the Tier 2 folks call you and try and work with you on it."

The company decided to no longer support Mac's older than version 10.6 and did an auto upgrade without any notice to users that by upgrading you can no longer use the equipment without upgrading your operating system -- and oh, by the way, they don't offer a way to downgrade your system so that it will work like it did yesterday morning!

So I have to say it works well as long as you are willing to add the cost of buying the controllers for each room or by upgrading all your PC's everytime Sonos decides to do an upgrade. For me, the cost of having to buy new computers constantly is unreasonable when all I really use it for is to surf the web and email and by the time I add the cost of the Sonos controllers, the quality of the sound does not make the Sonos worth the cost.

title: Finally someone gets it right (mostly)
text:
I've been wanting something like this for a long time. GoGoGate, finally gets it right (mostly).

Installation may or may not be easy depending on your skill level as well as unique conditions of your garage. The instructions include a YouTube video that's really easy to follow and for most situations everything will be fine. However, as you're reading the instructions or watching the video, pay attention to what they are doing and why. It's understandable that they can't give instructions for every unique situation, so understand what they are demonstrating and use common sense to apply it to your own garage.

My (3 car door) garage has the wall buttons nowhere near a power outlet. My wife wouldn't appreciate the controller and the wires being placed near the buttons anyway. So for me the easy solution was to mount the GoGoGate on the ceiling next to one of the opener motors. That allowed me to run wires to each of the 3 motors going through the ceiling and into the attic. Other than the GoGoGate device being visible behind one of the motors, the entire system is hidden.

My motor had 4 wires going to it, not 2 (one red one white) like in the instructions. No problem, the GoGoGate is just a switch it completes or breaks a circuit. All I had to do was find which of the two wire connections when connected would open the door (the other two were for the lights).

The other issue I had was in placing the 3 sensors. That was hard in my case because there was a metal rail between the doors and the wall. This meant putting the sensor on the very top of the garage door and doing the opposite of what they suggest, that is the big piece needs to go on the door, and the smaller piece on the wall. It took some playing around, but it was really easy to figure this out.

The double-sided tape to secure the sensors works well if you make sure to clean the surfaces, and don't touch them (oil from your fingers will be a problem). Then when securing, hold the sensors down firmly for 30 seconds (no wiggling). Before doing this, tape your sensors in place to make sure they're going to work where you're placing them (with painter's masking tape). You can't re-use the double sided tape.

Make sure to remove the protective film over the phone light sensor before doing the set up. Otherwise it won't work. That film should have a notice on it, and I think that's causing a lot of problems. On the other hand, you don't need to use the phone light sensor. Follow the instructions and just go to "Find GoGoGate". The first time you do this, you need to create an open wifi network with your router, but once you've set up GoGoGate to recognize your SSID and password, you're good to go. Subsequent configurations and changes will work work without having to open your wifi. For me this is easier than doing the phone light sensor syncing because I need to move a car and get a ladder to get to where I mounted the device.

If your SSID has special characters it won't work with the GoGoGate, but that's exactly why your SSID shouldn't have special characters. Do yourself a favor and don't use special characters in an SSID, you'll appreciate this later when setting up the Internet of everything.

Room for improvements:

1) Both pieces of the sensor should have holes for securing it with screws. Currently only the small piece has these holes.

2) The "Warranty Void if Removed" sticker is placed in such a way that it broke (95%) on mine simply during shipping and handling.

3) The app has a funky web browser inside of the app. This is better than sending you to Mobile Safari, but it clearly not the same user experience as the native app section. I'd like to see this better integrated. One major improvement would be to remove the pop-up that asks you to open the web page. Instead, just open the web page. Put the website address in the Settings part of the app.

4) Alerts: It's great being able to get an alert. My wife used to forget to close the garage door sometimes. This lets me know this is happening. I'd like to be able to configure it so that alerts keep coming unless turned off by the app itself.

title: Sturdy Mount, Lots of Potential, Poor Quality Control
text:
I've owned this mount for about a month and was originally impressed with its weight and ability to hold my 55" LED-LCD with ease. However, a couple of issues make me hesitant to recommend it to someone else. The first problem is with the way the arms secure to the mount. After attaching the arms to the TV, the arms then "hang" on the mounting plate, and then a screw on the bottom of each arm is supposed to tighten upward onto the bottom of the mounting plate. My problem is that these screws are ever-so-slightly crooked and get caught on the edge of the mounting plate instead of tightening up to where they are supposed to. I called customer service and they quickly acknowledged the problem (after sending them a photo) and sent me a new set of arms. The problem: these arms were about twice the size of the originals and would not work with my existing mounting plate. I called them back and they apologized and promised to send another set of arms. They even allowed me to e-mail them a photo of the arms I needed and the incorrect ones that they sent. Two days later I got the new arms and they were a THIRD different style (also not compatible with my mounting plate). I will be calling them again shortly. I've lost any faith that they have any ability to send me the arms I need, so I'm hoping that they can send me a combo of the arms and matching mounting plate that will be compatible with the rest of my mount. I haven't read about anybody else having this problem, so I think I got a bad set of arms. This problem therefore probably isn't worth worrying about if you're considering this mount.

Second problem (which I haven't even addressed with them) is that the mount will not stay level when extended out from the wall. I have it leveled in its fully collapsed position, but if I pull the TV out more than a few inches, it twists noticeably (right side of TV will be at least an inch lower than the left side). I've read that others have had this problem as well. I'd be interested to know if anybody DOESN'T have this problem. In other words, is it apparent that another aspect of my mount is faulty, and should I therefore request a replacement of the whole thing, or is this mount just not capable of holding a 55" TV square when extended away from the wall?

As others have mentioned, the articulating arms are EXTREMELY stiff at first. But they DO loosen up nicely by spraying some white lithium grease on all of the joints. Spray it, work them in all directions, and let it sit overnight before mounting the TV. I even sprayed them again the next day right before mounting the TV. It's quite easy to maneuver now.

title: Two major flaws right out of the box!

I went to the BIOS to find "Battery Calibration", guess what, I couldn't not find any way to calibrate the battery. Asus, please don't rush with your product launch, do some testing and quality control. title: A different Point of View
text: I recently purchased the Bose Wave SoundTouch System directly from Bose. The only thing that I agree with the previous posters is the price. This my second Bose product and purchase after my experience with a Bose SoundTouch 20. Both products were purchased as replacements to my two 10 year old  Roku M1000 Internet Radios which both died almost simultaneously. The Roku was a clock radio equivalent to the Bose Radio SoundTouch without the CD player. In its day equally expensive. In 2005 about $250.00.i had one in my kitchen which I replaced with the  Bose SoundTouch 20. I was very impressed with the unit and its capabilities and the ease of setup. No problems with connecting to my wireless network. At the time I was unaware of the Wave radio version. In huge fan of internet radio as well as FM. The Roku filled that function very well as an FM receiver, internet and clock radio. So when I stumbled upon the Wave SoundTouch, I knew that I had found a replacement and I have not been disappointed. Now for some of the issues I have read in the previous reviews. I did use a laptop to install both units. You only have install the software once, you just add other units. They both sync with each other in using iTunes or Windows Media player through the app. I use my iPad or Android phone to control both devices. For Airplay I use my iPad. If you have  a Sirius/XM account you can download the Sirius/XM app to your iPad or iPad and use Airplay to stream to either device. You cannot use Airplay simultaneously play to both device which is a drawback. I use the power cord FM antenna for the radio and it works great for stations that I listen too and much better than the Roku which had a separate antenna. The current units have two alarms which you have a choice of sources to choose from to wake up to. The remote is diminutive, but functional and in my opinion not too small. The sound is far superior to the Roku pumping out much bass than is expected from such a small enclosure. Aside from the price which we can all agree is expensive. If you want more than a clock radio then the Wave SoundTouch would be an excellent choice. I think the unit is worth every dollar.

title: Simple to use - but not as accurate as older watch
text:
Pros:
1 - This is a simple watch to use if you don't need the full details that some of the other watches offer. Personally it does what I need - displays average pace since previous "lap," total time, and total distance - as well as heart rate.
2 - It syncs up to a satellite signal in reasonable time - faster than my wife's older Garmin 305.

Cons:
1 - My biggest complaint with this watch is the inaccurate distance measurements. My wife and I did a 5K, and it recorded my first mile 18 seconds faster than my wife's 305 - and we were running together. In the end, it reported a distance of 3.23 miles instead of 3.1. When you are keeping close track of your pace and distance, this is frustrating. It always records longer distances than the 305 - but not my a specific amount... it varies.
2 - Battery life. This watch seems to lose a great deal of battery after only a week of non-use while in regular "clock" mode with the GPS off. I have to remember to charge it very frequently, where the old 305 totally powers off and will hold a charge for weeks.

If I would have known what I know now, I would have saved some money and bought the older 305 rather than going for the newer, sleeker 110.

title: Never, Ever, Going To Buy Another WD Hard Drive
text:
This is what I get for buying a drive and not setting it up right away. But - hard drive warranties are useless, anyway. No one wants to return a failed drive to get a refurbished drive - i.e. one that already failed - yes, supposedly *fixed*. But, who would trust important information to a drive that failed once: a fool. Who would trust important information to a WD drive: Another fool.

The worst part about this is it seems this drive wasn't even new. The computer tried to boot from this drive because I was not paying attention - meaning I let it boot from a drive I thought was bare - and, surprise, I got a note on my screen that said the grub file could not be found or grub rescue. This is the message typically received when someone has used a drive as a dual-boot - Windows and Linux, typically - and then removed the Linux install without resetting the Windows boot - MBR, etc.

So, yeah, I was shocked. Although, should I be? It seems businesses think they can get away with anything these days. And, sadly, most do.

I will not waste money to return this drive. But, from curiosity, I ran a disk check on the drive. Failed x 10. Could not even make it through the disk drive check - and I tried a few (including dban, etc.). The drive froze. Every time. On different computers. This is a real pile.

Nice going, WD. You just lost my business. Forever.

title: In my opinion a great design all around
text:
I purchased this case right after the release of the B+ Pi, so there were few options to choose from. I was glad this was one of them. I would choose this enclosure over the many existing B case designs. It does not compromise on form or function.

Function: The Micro SD card is fully accessible. All ports are easily accessible. There is plenty of room around the Micro-USB power port for different size cable plug heads. There is a cutout for the GPIO header so you can add or remove the cable without taking the case apart. There are slots cut into the top for the camera and display cable.

Form: There is a vertical piece of acrylic that surrounds the HDMI, A/V, and power ports giving tight tolerances around the ports. It comes with metal nuts and bolts instead of nylon. It is low profile without exposing too much. The evenly stacked layer design looks awesome.

In my opinion a great case.

title: Poor product, even worse service
text:
The product and service I received have been so bad I feel I must write a review.

Ordered the M5A88-M board at the beginning of August along with an AMD FX-8120 as part of a new build. Assembled it and it wouldn't POST, nothing reaching the monitor. I went through all the diagnostic steps on the Asus website, tried other monitor, and verified other components worked. Contacted Asus service and they told me it had an out-of-date BIOS ver 0402. Why would a board that's been on the market so long be shipping with such an outdated BIOS?

I don't have any spare AM3 cpu's sitting around so they had me send it in for RMA. Three weeks later I received it back with no notes or comments and no apparent change to the board as it still had the BIOS ver 0402 sticker on it. Built up the computer again, and as I feared it didn't POST, just as before.

Finally got through again to Asus service and they said they would cross-ship me a new board. But now they're saying a replacement isn't available so they've offered me another RMA, which means I'll have to pay AGAIN to have it shipped just to get the same incompetent service!

Along with returning an unrepaired RMA, Asus has ignored some of my service request emails, responded to one email with an unclear message filled with misspellings, "accidentally" hung up on me during a service call, had unqualified reps doing service calls (one person put me on hold after every question because he said he had to ask another person since he normally did wireless service), and left me without an official product serial number since they didn't return the box which was the only thing that had a serial number on it (I had no choice since they wouldn't accept the RMA w/o the serial number sticker, so it looks like they've possibly screwed me out of a future RMA).

Not to mention 2 months of lost time, work, and money dealing with something that was advertised to work with my components!

title: Best TV for 2D image quality and fast action.
text:
What a great way to go out. Well by now most people know Panasonic is leaving the plasma business. I suspect they are unable to scale the process to 4K. I really wants in the market for a TV as I had an older Panasonic plasma. But I cannot stand the uneven back light bleed in most LCDs, but the thing that really gets me is the blur. Everything just looks like a mess on an LCD when motion gets moving. I checked out a number of 4K LCDs before pulling the trigger to see if they were all they were cracked up to be. Yes the 4K TVs look pretty good on a still image but in other areas they still fell short. Not knowing how long we may need to wait for OLED to mature I decided to pull the trigger.

In the end I am very pleased. Now I am no idiot who buys a plasma and then goes and screws it up, you need to know not to leave one image on and it helps to understand the tech you are working with. That said now days its so hard to burn them in for those that do it, it is usually no worse than the back light bleed on a LCD. So I operated my 5 year old Panasonic for all that time and had zero burn in or uneven ware. But right away I could tell the temporary image retention on the VT60 was better along with the other subtle image issues that plasmas have. Everything was just a strait up a big improvement.

There are a TON of features on this TV. Unfortunately we don't use any of them because we hook a PC up to the TV so all the smart apps and so on done better on a PC. And of course the sound is the same, don't buy a TV this beautiful and ruin the experience with any built in speakers. I never even tried them.

We wall mounted ours and it looks great, although it was more difficult to wall mount since it was so thin. None the less it went on to the same wall mount our last 54 inch was on without a problem.

Now to nit pick on a couple details.

I wish Panasonic had made the silver bezel liner removable. It does not fit with my décor I would have rather had all black.
I also wish Panasonic would have allowed us to use USB to hook up the built in web cam to our PC, this way we could Skype on the PC without needing to get our own camera.
In addition and this is more of a general TV complaint I wish that they would make the API to control the TV more open so that you could get other apps to control the TV. They have their own android app which is nice but everyone is sick of switching apps for every device. You need 1 app for your TV, 1 for your PC, 1 for you receiver, and in my case you need a Logitech app to control a couple items. I would prefer if they had a API that great apps like unified remote could tap into. Also their is a couple fans on the back and if things are quiet you can hear them if close. A TV this nice is going to be bought by audiophiles and should never risk upsetting them with any noise.

title: fits, but doesn't work for intended purpose
text:
What were they thinking to sell this product? The lens mount fits my Canon EOS camera just fine. The "C" mount lens screws on as it should. Everything seems honkey-dory ... except that it won't focus. What Fotodiox neglects to inform us (and I didn't bother to check beforehand) is that the "C" mount specification is:

Flange focal distance (C-Mount Face to Image) = 17.52mm, or approximately 2/3 inch.
Unfortunately, the Canon EOS needs a flange focal distance of 42.0 mm, almost 2".

There's no way a standard C mount lens can focus on a DSLR such as this without some sort of intermediate lens (that would interfere with the mirror function).

Thanks for selling a useless product.

title: Solid machine for working professional
text:
I am a full time consultant and spent a lot of time in Dec 2010 looking for a laptop that would mostly be a desktop replacement, but that I would also travel with to client sites. I have had this machine for over 20 months and it has done a great job. I don't do a lot of heavy computing, but when I do, the core i5 is surprisingly adequate. I don't do heavy graphics, but it is supposed to be adequate for moderate gaming. I bought this over the more expensive bamboo model because the latter did not upgrade to 8G ram, and the lights indicating things like whether you are plugged in, wireless is running etc were hidden from view. A small thing, but super annoying to have to lift up the computer to see these lights.

Pros:
1. amazing value for money
2. very capable for working IT consultant not doing super heavy computing
3. upgradeable to 8G ram
4. Small enough to use on a plane in economy seating
5. can do moderate gaming
6. backed by Asus 2 year guarantee and I can have it serviced at my local shop where I bought it - an Asus qualified shop.
7. The mouse gestures are really handy, especially for scrolling
8. Very reliable, have not had any problems to speak of
9. Windows 7 and DisplayLink make it very easy to have multiple monitors. I currently use 4, including the laptop screen.

Caveats:
1. not very light, if you want to travel a lot
2. battery life very poor; I get by with an extra battery, but even that only just lasts 4-6 hrs.
3. mouse pad not super smooth or responsive
4. no backlit keyboard

I can probably use this machine for another year or two if need be, but I am shopping around a bit, hoping that Asus will come out with a comparable model with the Ivy Bridge Core i7 chip with flash drive to make things more snappy. Some Ultrabooks have come out recently in this category, but I don't need to pay the premium for super small and light.

This would be a great machine to pick up used, if you can live with the caveats and want Win 7 rather than Win 8. I might be selling mine before too long ;-)

title: I'm in Love.
text:
Update September 9, 2012

Information regarding Iphones/Ipod:

Update August 7, 2012
Sorry I haven't posted a video. Several people have beaten me to the punch via youtube. Pretty nice videos too!

______________________

May9, 2012

Radio Installation: (skip to next paragraph for feature reviews)

First of all- I love youtube. I watched a video at least 15 times to see how to install a radio (Because it was my very first time installing it myself). I asked myself. "Why are they charging so much and it only takes them less than an hour to install? It must be a simple process. I'm the kind of guy who likes to make sure "things are done right." It took me about an hour to install it- but well worth the money I saved. Bestbuy was planning to charge me $100 for the receiver installation and wiring harnesses ($60 for the receiver + $20 for wiring harness+ $20 for DIN casing). I did the whole thing for about $20 (wiring harness + DIN case).

Feature Reviews:
My Car: 2002 4 dr Honda Accord SE

What I love
-Bluetooth
The sound on is great (stock speakers). It's not to loud. I placed the mic in the middle and hid the wires. I called my dad and he said I sounded clear. (Don't worry. I'll post an actual video demonstration really soon)
It also loaded my contacts! It was so easy picking up and hanging up a phone call. You can look up contacts on this this. The moment you disconnect your bluetooth, I don't think it saves your phonebook. It will only show if your phone is connected.

Pairing the phone and the receiver was easy. I made the pin on the receiver simple. I used the phone to find the receiver and paired it up. All done!

-HD Radio
WOW! Going from stock radio to HD radio is FANTASTIC! HD is FREE. This thing turns AM to FM radio quality, FM to CD quality, and HD channels to...well, HD. There is definitely a noticeable difference in sound quality. Bear in mind, I'm sticking only to my stock speakers (pioneer brand! so happy)
-Pandora, Slacker Radio, Amazon MP3
They all run awesome with bluetooth connection on my Droid 3 phone! At first it was buggy, but they just updated software for the droid 3 (May 8, 2012)...runs very nicely. You can also use an AUX in for direct connection. It won't read the song titles unfortunately. If you have an Iphone, the manual said it should read it. Sorry...can't give you the the review about the Iphone.
You can change songs with the radio. No need to mess with your phone while driving!
-Dual USB ports
AWESOME! I plugged my ipod in. It read the songs, sound is superb...and it charges the ipod! I did mistakenly buy two usb extensions because amazon recommended buying two of them with this purchase. It turns out the receiver already comes with one already. So just BUY ONE. Runs awesome though!
You can use the other usb for a flash drive to play more music.
-Color Customization
FUN! Sooo many colors to choose from! There's a "scan" option which constantly changes colors....I find it extremely distracting, but it's there for you. It's quite bright, but I don't think it's blindingly bright (depends on the color I suppose). You can definitely see it during the day or at night. You can mess with the contrast level in the options menu
-SAT Ready
This is just to notify you that it is READY, NOT BUILT IN.

Overall Receiver Operation
I think it's quite simple, yet great! I pretty much messed with this for about an hour to get comfortable with using it. Very easy!

LCD screen. Like others said, the clock is small in the bottom right- but you can fix that by making the time and date the Background. It looks nice! Big and definitely readable, haha.

Remote Control Works well. Buttons are easy to figure out too.

Sounds Options:
Bass Boost, High Pass Filter, 5 preset band equalizer, 2 custom equalizers (for your preferences), Low Mid High Loudness feature

I've only turned up the volume to 15 with Powerful Preset Equalizer, Mid Loudness, No bass boost. Sound is awesome!

The nob is pretty nice...easy to navigate with it. Setting up the tuner for my favorite radio stations was a breeze.

Detachable faceplate. Awesome for security purposes.

Conclusion
This looks sexy and sleek with a black and silver look. The color customization makes you admire it even more.
Sound is far more superb compared to stock radio.

Sorry for the long review. I just wanted to cover as much as I can just to give you an idea of how much I love the receiver and its features.

I'll post a video eventually so you can see it for yourself. Thanks for reading this review and good luck in finding one the fits your needs!

title: The LIFT30X is perfect for my needs, but required custom work on the studs to have the TV in the center of the wall.
text:
I needed a mount that could slide up and down (for perfect comfort when sitting down or lying down on the couch), it swivels left and right to accommodate all viewing positions in my living room and dining room, and one with a thin enough profile so that the TV doesn't protrude too much into the living space.

The LIFT30X was perfect for that. The "30" is for the maximum weight that this mount is rated for, and luckily my Samsung 46" weighs 27 lbs. (I added to that the small weight of the Kinect sensor but I was still under 30). The specs of the mount talk about TV sizes, but what really matters is the weight of the TV.

Two downsides:
1- The LIFT30X has an extendable arm, so if you want the TV to be dead center when it's parked flat against the wall, you have to mount the mount 17 cm (6 11/16") to the right or left of that center position. You'd better have a stud in that location, or you'd have to add a plate that spans the distance between two studs, and install the mount on that plate. It wasn't an issue for me because I was remodeling my living room, so I simply added a stud in the wall 17cm off center. (I had to measure that after I received the unit, it is not listed in the specs of the mount)

2- When you swivel or slide the TV vertically on the mount, he TV invariably rotates slightly clockwise or counterclockwise and if you're really picky you'd need to leave a bubble level within reach to readjust the rotation of the TV and make it level again. (the stone wall behind my TV has horizontal patterns that I use to eyeball the proper orientation)

NOTE: This review is for the __LIFT30X__, not other Omnimount mounts. For some reason Amazon is merging the reviews of similar products from the same company, I find it confusing.

title: Finally... the Ability to Stream Good Movies!
text:
I recently decided to drop the basic cable service I've had for years, so I was looking for a way to still get some additional channels beyond the regular over-the-air channels without spending a lot of money. For $50, trying the Roku seemed like a worthy experiment.

Setup was easy, and lucky for me, my TV has a powered USB port so I didn't need to plug the Roku into a power outlet in the wall. I was able to find a Roku remote control application for my Windows Phone that works great and provides a keyboard so searches are much easier to type in.

For most browsing, the device seems fast enough. The start screen loads pretty slowly, showing "ROKU" for what seems like well over a minute. Some channels, like YouTube, also load rather slowly but are relatively fast after the initial load. If speed is an issue for you, perhaps the Roku 3 would be better for you.

One feature I like about the Roku is that I can finally rent ($) and stream good, current movies instead of just the old, B-rated junk movies that Netflix and Amazon allow you to stream w/o Roku. It would be nice if I didn't need to create an account for every place that rents movies, especially since Roku already has my PayPal info... I'd prefer if they dealt with who gets paid for the movie rental payments.

As for free content, well, that's where I'm a bit disappointed and dropped the rating to 4 stars. There is plenty of free content, but I found very little free content that I actually want to watch. That's not Roku's fault, but part of the reason I bought the device.

title: Good sound world's worst software. Buy customized iPod instead.
text:
The audio quality of the A&K120 is fine. But, and this is a huge issue, if you currently use an iPod do not under any circumstances switch to the A&K unless you are prepared to spend 3-5 months completely re-indexing and re-tagging your entire music library. The professional reviewers of Astell&Kern transfer 8-20 files onto the device and then review it entirely for audio quality. Audio quality is high. But they make no practical tests of actually trying to use the device. Know the following:

1. It only works with their own dedicated iRiver music software.
2. The iRiver music software is possibly the worst software in the market today for managing your music library.

The iRiver software does not sort by Album, it will not sort by Artists, it will not sort by Genre. It goes without saying that none of the iTunes meta-tagging can be used, so you have to dig into Windows file codes to re-tag all your song files. If you have previously done this in iTunes know that your images are now entirely separated from your song files so you will have to find them and re-apply them one by one. Transferring files is a manual process, a nightmare, and has to be done every time you open the software. The meta-tagging in windows file code may or may not apply. If you re-tag using the iRiver software know this:

1. They do NOT store any library information. I spent a week importing files and editing those files to the library I wanted. The very next time I opened iRiver there was NO library file - I had to re-import all the files and none of the editing had been preserved. Completely useless. [Addition: I keep FLAC and AAC/MP3 versions of the music files - the iRiver just lists them all no matter how many times I edit the list.)

2. If you need to re-tag one file in an album, or create virtual albums, you must do so file by file by file file. If you select an entire album and want to change the genre, iRiver will change the names of every song file to the first entry on the list - so now my Billy Joel Album has every track permanently labelled Angry Young Man. [Be super careful]

3. There is no way to correct or undo anything that iRiver does - the changes are permanent and non-retrievable.

4. There is absolutely no customer support or any effort to even pretend there is customer support. The software is written in Korean so you cannot fix it under any circumstances. They expect you to do everything with playlists - if, like me, you have 100's of thousands of files, this will take five or six months. By default their expectation is you want to listen to music in random order so they have optimized the device for random listening.

5. If you search the device by genre you must then listen to the tracks in alphabetical order, if you sort by artist, then same applies. You cannot for example, sort by "Classical" and then play Beethoven's Fifth Symphony - you have to search 150,000 tracks one by one to find the first movement. [Listening to La Boheme in alphabetical order was surreal.]

6. If you have more than a few albums on the device it can take up to five minutes to boot up. EVERY TIME YOU USE IT.

Everything above can be done easily in iTunes. Do not switch from an iPod., If you want to spend this kind of money, go to a specialty site and buy a modified iPod with the Wolfson DAC chip and play it through a headphone amplifier. It will be cheaper and 1000% more functional. Or get an older iPod, which already has the Wolfson DAC and have the memory upgraded to 240Gb. Use good headphones and there is no difference from the A&K and it will cost 1/3.

The sound is fantastic, but this is the world's best sounding, most expensive paperweight.

FURTHER NOTES: I have now been using the A&K120 for six weeks with little satisfaction. When you transfer music to the device it does NOT tell you when it is out of memory. The software DOES NOT roll over automatically from the internal memory to the external Mini SD cards. You need to specify which card you are transferring music to. This is done presumably so you can swap cards in and out. What it does in fact is cause countless file transfer errors. You need to check the remaining capacity on each memory card constantly and decide with high precision what you are transferring to which card.

The bigger issue, and this is basically a deal killer, is that the software on the device DOES NOT index any of the files on the memory cards. As you search through the tree (Artist, Genre etc.) the files on the Mini SD cards DO NOT APPEAR. They are there - you can find them if you go to the "Files" display. The "Files" display will list each file folder you have transferred card by card, but the software on the device is of no use in searching for anything on the SD cards.

Effectively this means the capacity IS NOT 192GB, instead the usable capacity is only the internal memory which is 64GB.

The US staff has no role in the software and can only listen to your questions. The Korean staff does not speak English and has responded to every complaint (so far) by telling me to just "Create Playlists".

A FURTHER NOTE: I have been trying to listen to the music by using the "File Folders" option and have discovered a major software flaw. When you transfer the music to the A&K using the iRiver Plus4 software, it reverse all of your file folder conventions and creates new ones. So if you create a file folder labelled "Les Miserables," iRiver will instead create a folder for every actor in the cast, under which will be a sub-folder labelled "Les Miserables" containing only the songs sung by that actor. So the "File Folder" option is completely useless as a way to listen to an album. The designers of this device are of the firm belief that everyone wants to listen to music in random order. Forget about trying to listen to a complete symphony - you have to listen to every movement labelled "Allegro" instead. Once again, when I called to ask if this would be corrected, I was told that it was simple, I should just a create a playlist for every symphony I want to listen to.....useless, completely useless.

As I understand it, they have no intention of fixing any of these problems. Avoid this device - do not buy one. I would give it back if they would refund my money but they will not. I would give anything to talk to an engineer who knows the system and can speak English. I expect this company will be out of business shortly so buyer beware.

title: Asus Support is the Worst EVER!!
text:
This motherboard is a great compromise from the extreme high end gaming board (maximus extreme) and the non-gaming boards. I did upgrade to the latest recently but have yet to try overclocking again (running a 4770k with the board). When not overclocking, the board is perfectly stable for me. Highly recommended.

8/28/2013 Edit
Something happened to me that's never happened before. My motherboard has died. I was dusting it out with canned air like I've done in the past 15-20 years I've been using PC's. When I put the cases side panel back on and tried to power it up, nothing happened, nothing at all (never seen that either). Did all the troubleshooting techniques and could never get anything to happen while the power supply was connected to the motherboard. I have a power supply jump start connector I use to leak test water cooling setups so I connected that to the power supply to see if that was the culprit. The power supply was fine so it has to be the connection to the motherboard that is the issue. I received an RMA from asus and have shipped it back for repair. I'll post a follow-up to this once I hear back.

9/7/2013 Edit
I'm changing my review. I can't be certain if it was me or a defective motherboard but what I did I've done in the past numerous times and never had an issue (dusting out the case with canned air while the PC is powered off and unplugged). Now dealing with Asus support has been even more mind-numbing. Numerous chats with support while trying to get an update to my RMA yielded nothing but "it takes time to get your RMA in our system". Finally on Friday, September 6, with me telling them it was delivered to them and telling them the name of the person who signed for it, they finally acknowledge they never received the RMA. Now they're telling me that shipping and receiving will have to contact me (who knows when) to get me a replacement. I then talked to another support tech the next day who said it was in the receiving area waiting to be scanned into their system. He said the process usually takes 10 business days.

I've bought Asus parts for 15-20 years now. Never had any issues with them whatsoever. I can now say that dealing with support will have me thinking twice when I'm shopping for parts for my next build.

9/16/2013 Edit
It seems my motherboard never made it to the Asus RMA facility. After telling them through their support MULTIPLE times that I show it was delivered on August 28 and asking why there was never an update and having them telling me "if the tracking number says it was delivered, we have it here and are just waiting to input it in our system" I decided to contact FedEx and ask them to trace the package. Come to find out it was delivered to the wrong address. I'm now in the process of getting FedEx to find it and deliver it to the correct address. I can't fault Asus for the delivery but I can fault them for telling me they have it when they never received it. The tracking number even shows who signed for the package. Had one support guy on Friday (September 13) who actually works in the hardware area say he never heard of the person who signed for it while another who works the phones and internet chat support say he was new (inconsistencies abound). As of now, this will be the last item I buy from Asus. Their support is atrocious. Quite unfortunate as I really like their products but if you can't support your products you don't deserve my business.

10/11/2013 Edit
Unbelievable. Asus wasn't able to find a maximus hero so they sent me a gene vi even though I told them I would rather wait for the hero. They even sent me an e-mail saying I had 48 hours to respond or they would send me the gene vi. I sent them a response within an hour of receiving the e-mail telling them I would rather wait for a hero. They responded a couple of days later saying "Thank you for responding to our offer. We will go ahead and have the MAXIMUS VI GENE processed and shipped to you, since we do not have any estimated time when we will get the Maximus VI Hero. That is why we offered model change.". Seriously, what the heck? I told them I didn't want the gene vi, I would rather wait for the hero vi but they basically told me "no man, you really don't want that hero, you want this gene instead". Last time I EVER buy an Asus product, EVER!

title: Do NOT buy this mouse, the entire product line is FAULTY!
text:
Truly, I cannot believe that Logitech are still selling this mouse. Like thousands of others have reported, there is a CATASTROPHIC FAILURE in the design which means that after a while they start developing phantom double clicks. Which means that when you click the button, it generates two clicks instead of one. This is a HORRIBLE fault and makes the mouse completely unusable after a short period of time. You may try and ignore it, but believe me it is SO frustrating to use software with a mouse that generates phantom clicks. You will be tearing your hair out in no time.

I bought this mouse a couple of years ago and it developed the problem after 6 months. Since I couldn't find the receipt and just put it down to bad luck, I bought another one. It too developed the problem, this time after 4 months. So after researching the problem (and finding out that everyone else had the same problem), I discovered a statement from Logitech which gave steps to "fix" the problem (involving taking the batteries out and holding down the buttons for a minute). However, this is only a temporary fix and the problem soon comes back. After a while, the temporary fix stopped working. So this time I took advantage of my warranty and demanded a replacement. I thought that since Logitech were aware of the problem, they would have solved it in their newest production run.

Well, what happened was that due to a customer service error on their part, they ended up sending me TWO brand new MX Anywhere mice. Great! Or not so great...after 6 months, the first one developed the same problem. And now another 6 months later, the SECOND one has developed the same problem as well. So this totals FOUR Logitech Anywhere MX mice in my possession which have developed the phantom click problem. THE ENTIRE PRODUCT LINE IS AT FAULT AND LOGITECH ARE DOING NOTHING TO FIX IT. They figure they'll just keep taking everyone's money and selling a mouse that they KNOW is guaranteed to fail after a short amount of time. The vast majority of people won't even bother using their warranty (or will have lost their receipt), so Logitech aren't worried about having to replace a few.

If you are thinking about buying this mouse, PLEASE take heed of my review and RUN A MILE! Buy ANY mouse except a Logitech one. They used to be a top notch company manufacturing quality computer accessories. However that was many years ago. These days, their products are junk (and they know it!).

title: First purchase of a tablet
text:
I decided to get a tablet so that I could keep up with my email on the road. The decision was difficult because I have never tried this type of thing and trying it out in the stores proved to be impossible. So I conferred with a family member who had experience with both the ipad and the android tablets. He suggested that since I am not an Apple user, that I would like the Android better. We agreed that a 16 GB tab would be enough for me. I also did not want to pay a monthly access fee so I decided on the WiFi version.

I was surprised to learn that a WiFi tablet cannot become a 3G or 4G tablet by purchasing a montly plan.

At this point I've had quite a learning curve and probably can't do this review justice. The user manual is online and the tiny booklet that was included didn't mention it. This booklet was hardly enough to get me started.

I surfed the forums where I learned about the manual and relied on questions to family. Being a Windows user, I was not into the ap scene. Once I realized anything I wanted to do required an ap to work right, things got better.

One very easy part was the WiFi connection to my home network. The system searched for and easily connected to my network.

There are many features I have not yet tried.

I use the Yahoo mail, Gmail, and Facebook aps. I can use the web browser that is included.

The virtual keyboard takes some getting used to. If I have a lot to say I don't attempt to use the tablet. But is it great just for keeping up with email.

I have not tried the camera but it doesn't seem hard to use.

The display is fine for me.

It does take a long time - a few hours - to charge the battery once it's run down.

I like the tablet and probably will find more uses for it once I get into it. For now it's meeting my needs.

text:

I have been SO thrilled and happy with my decision! This camera is awesome. Right when I took it out of the box, I was so happy with the weight of the camera (doesn't seem as bulky as you would expect a dSLR to be).

It takes beautifully crisp and clear pictures even if you are just using it on Auto mode. No matter the lighting, the pictures always come out great for me. Anyone with young kids knows this is a MUST because sometimes you can't manipulate lighting, etc. when you need a spur of the moment shot of a big first or something cute they are doing. One night I took a picture of my baby on Auto in a completely dark room, and it came out very clear and clean looking.

I have been learning how to use the camera in manual mode, and am getting BEAUTIFUL shots. It has been pretty easy to learn how to use this camera. I am not trying to be a professional, but I feel as though I am able to get semi-professional looking shots of my kids with this camera.

title: Excellent little device
text:
I have had a 2nd generation Kindle for a long time, and my daughter has a 3rd generation Kindle. My wife owns an iPad2. And, I have an Android Bionic smartphone. So, we have a broad spectrum of related devices in the house on which I can make a good comparison. How does the Fire stack up? Pretty darn good, in my opinion.

Just like marriage, the Kindle Fire is all about expectations. For $199, I love it. It has performed as advertised. I was afraid I would miss the e-ink of my previous Kindle (and in fact, had often used this as a reason why the iPad was an inferior tablet for reading). But, I have to admit, while reading on a backlit display is not as sharp as e-ink, it is much better than I expected. I am able to read without any eye exhaustion, or anything like that. It is nice to read in bed, or in the living room with the lights down when the kids are watching TV. Of course, it's a pain in the sunlight, but not much you can do about that.

My wife's iPad2 is nice, but it leaves me feeling "meh". Every time I use one I keep thinking, "Sure, it's nice, but for $500? Really?" I don't have any such feelings when using my Fire. It works great, I haven't had any problems with it, and I enjoy the experience significantly.

One thing to note, is that I have found it very similar to using my Android smart phone. In other words, I was going on a trip recently, and I didn't want to take anything on the plane. I considered taking the Fire for reading, but realized there was nothing the Fire provided that I couldn't get on my smart phone, at least for the extent of a plane ride. I could read, listen to music, play some games, etc. *But*, when I am at home, or lounging around, I will use the Fire every time, simply because of the size and crispness of the display.

Finally, I haven't had any problems with the silk browser like some others have. I would strongly recommend visiting this link and change a few default settings. This sped up my browsing considerably:

[...]

I only ever give 5 stars for products that are practically perfect. I give the Kindle 4 stars because of Amazon's exclusion of some apps from its app store. I really wish I could get Google apps and Gmail (though the Kindle mail app is sufficient). I feel like I am missing out on a few choices that I would like to have. Other than that, I have been extremely pleased. I think you will be too.

title: It's a must-have...with conditions
text:
Took this on a two week hiking trip to patagonia. Everyone else had their SLR's in their bags and took time to get them out. You know the hassle if you photograph while hiking - either drop the bag completely to pull it out of the main compartment or slide around the sling. Thing of the past - I have a full DSLR and was shooting with a nikkor 18-300 - pretty heavy combination and the weight was handled easily.

Couple notes:
- The review about the camera falling out - I have no idea how that happened - you control the angle at which the camera has to be turned to remove it. The kit comes with a high-quality metal piece that screws into the tripod hole. There is one angle the camera comes out - you can make it 90 degrees, 20 degrees - believe me you'll understand if you get it.

- The piece they give you (to screw into the tripod hole) has a hole for the tripod - it's not ideal but it works fine.

- The safety strap is garbage - toss it first thing. You'll want to keep the neck strap and just loop it over your head like usual. The difference is there is no tension. If you need to take off your pack, however, you just let it hang like you always have done. Easy.

- The hand strap is garbage - toss it alongside the safety strap. It's set up for some kind of alien hand ergonomics. But it's free with the strapshot so whatever - if you like it. Don't buy it separately.

- Make sure your bag has a d-ring on the shoulder strap - you strap off of it and I wouldn't carry my camera without that security, even if you can rig it somehow without it.

- The instructions suck - there are none. They give you pictures and you figure it out.

- The chest strap is key for support and stability - without it, your camera will roll around on your chest.

But once it's up and running you'll be the envy of the hike - I'm telling you. If you're used to stopping the entire group hike or taking five minutes to unpack, shoot and repack, get ready for some true ease of use. I won't go on a photo hike without it again.

title: Great Basic DVD/VCR Combo
text:
I've been giving this unit a shakedown before I wrote this review. My 5 stars are for what this unit is capable of, what it is not as advertised, and the cost.

Toshiba is one of very few manufactures out there still making DVD/VCR Combo's and I'm glad for this. The manufacture date on the back of my unit was August 2012 so it was assembled quite recently as I write this. I have a large number of VHS titles that were never released on DVD or Blu-Ray so this type of product is still important to me.

Hook-up is very straight forward. I'm not sure how typical my hook up scenerio is compared to others, but I had this unit hooked up to a quality 7.1 Home Theatre System that includes one powerhouse Pioneer Elite AV Receiver. I connected the three component Video out cables directly to my HDTV (for DVD), the Digital Audio Coaxial cable connected to my AV Receiver (for DVD), composite RCA cables audio/video out to my AV Receiver (for VHS), and connnected my COX cable box to the audio and video composite in jacks on the back of this unit for VHS recording.

DVD video quality is excellent with 480p progressive scan. This unit is capable for bitstreaming both Dolby Digital 5.1 and DTS 5.1, another reason I give high marks. I watched an Enya music video compilation DVD with DTS and it was absolutely stunning, both video and the DTS 5.1 surround sound.

As for VHS, the picture quality is certainly not going to be DVD quality but is watchable. For those who have an AV Receiver capable of Video analog upscaling, the improvement works. VHS HI FI audio is an almost forgotten technology in this digital age but the quality is still outstanding with analog Dolby Pro Logic II surround sound. I'll sometimes swear it sounds better than it's Dolby Digital counterpart from some video sources.

Recording to VHS tape is something I didn't intend to use this unit for, but the quality is about as can be expected. Since I've gotten used to watching true HD blu ray and SD DVD, VHS viewing is not half bad as long as the recording speed is kept to SP mode and not the slow EP. VHS playback simply will not look as good on an HDTV as it does on a analog TV. If you have the equipment for video processing (upscale to 720P, etc) that really improves the picture. Any recording in the EP mode will look like crap on any HD set.

Negatives, I would say the remote could be layed out a little better but is still very functional. The VCR while playing tapes does have an audible noise up close, but if this unit is in a cabinet or reasonably far away I don't think it would be that noticable.

I haven't experienced any breakdowns like other reviewers have reported on. As such, for what Toshiba offers with this product and the low price point to own, this unit is worth 5 stars to me. Others have dinged this machine for their own missunderstanding of what this unit will or will not do, like "no tuner" or ignorance of hookups (the manual is very clear about cable hook up "how to"). These are unfair.

title: Upscale alarm clock
text: The Sony Dash is a nifty product designed for geeky nerds like me. Think of this is as an upscale alarm clock that receives push data depending on what apps are selected by the user. You can add more stuff to it depending on your configuration. It can stream Netflix and Pandora as well. By no means is this a perfect device. Don't expect Ipad like functionality. It's an upscale alarm clock. If you expect more, then you will be disappointed. If you are realistic with your expectation, then this Sony Dash will make you a happy camper. Unfortunately, Sony has decided to discontinue this product line. It will still support its legacy apps; don't know for how long though. It's sad this nifty gadget didn't get its dues. Yes it has some flaws and shortcomings, but I rather enjoy this product. I'm contemplating buying another and saving it in case my current Sony Dash dies and I need a replacement. I also owned the Insigina Infocast, too bad that died after 18 month of use. The Sony Dash is more elegantly designed than the Insigina. It is more refined aesthetically, however, the GUI interface is more intuitive on the Insignia. Unfortunately, the Sony Dash doesn't have a SD slot like the Insignia, which is a bummer. I can only load photos on a USB drive on the Sony Dash. Overall, this is a good product that wasn't properly marketed by Sony.

title: Easy set up, good price, needs more robust remote
text:
I purchased this last week. I was impressed with the price considering the features, specifically the built-in apps and wireless connectivity. Set up was a breeze. I had it up and running within 30 minutes. Fantastic picture, good sound, a big step up from my 5 year old Sony Bravia. It's close to my router, so I wired it in and am not using the wireless, so I can't comment on that. There's only two downsides, and these are minor. One is the remote. A qwerty keyboard would have been nice, but as it it you need to navigate through an onscreen keyboard with directional keys. This is big issue during setup...getting in passwords for Netflix, etc...but I don't imagine it will be a big deal for everyday use. Another is that the out-of-the-box built-in apps don't include Pandora. To get it, I had to sign up for a Yahoo account (yeah, I'm probably one of the last people in the world without a Yahoo account), then sign up for their app library, and download the app to the TV from there. Again, kind of a pain and not particularly intuitive, but once set up is done, it's no longer an issue. So thanks, Vizio for a great product, but give us a more robust remote and include Pandora in the built-in apps and you'll get 5 stars.

Added three weeks later: OK, now I've lived with this TV for a while. I've also learned two reasons why Vizio was able to reach such a low price point with it: 1) the backlight is fluorescent (CCFL) rather than LED, 2) the limited feature remote. I learned this after visiting Costco and seeing another Vizio model (M470SL) that at first glance looks identical to this product but is priced $120 higher. They were side-by-side, and try as I might I could see no difference in picture quality...both were excellent to my eye. Upon closer inspection, I found the only differences to be the backlight (LED rather than CCFL) and a full-featured remote (I couldn't get the remote out of the box, but it appears to have a qwerty keyboard, which would be great for someone who uses the TV to access internet apps like Facebook, etc). The LED model is thinner and probably more modern-looking to some. If you're really interested, google "ccfl vs led tv" and learn how much of this is marketing hype and how much makes a meaningful difference to the end user (that would be you).

I also noted that the reviewers at CNET complained that this model (E472VLE) does not render blacks very well, and rated it low for picture quality. I don't know what they were looking at, but the picture looks great to me. Comparing side-by-side in the store with more expensive models from other manufacturers, I could see no appreciable difference. And as noted above, it appears identical to the Vizio M470SL (to my eyes), that CNET seems to like better. The specs actually show a brighter picture (measured in nits, whatever they are) for the CCFL model.

I don't use the TV for internet work...I use my computer for that...so I'm fine with a less robust remote. The only time it bothered me was during setup when I had to enter a bunch of passwords. Fluorescent backlight means it will use a few bucks more worth of electricity per year (at my utility's rates it's about $6 per year), but picture quality (to me) is indistinguishable from the more expensive LED backlight. I've also read some other reviews where customers have complained that the LED backlight failed after a few months. So for me, I'm sticking with the model I have.

title: boomy bass, no mids, sharp treble
text:
my title says it all: the new UE boombox has plenty of sound, in contrast to the previous logitech boombox it doesn't reduce sound regardless if played from mains or from battery.

the bass is quite boomy, but at the same time has no power at all. even the much smaller bose soundlink produces a depper and more powerful bass with an overall more coherent sound. the mids are quite subdued on the UE boombox, vocals sound thin, while treble is really harsh and fizzy. overall the sound makes a rather "cheap" impression and seems to be tuned as if someone without any clue had tried to adjust the EQ for the worse.

although the ue boombox can play quite a bit louder than the soundlink, it already distorts near maximum volume. when both speakers are played outside at their maximum setting, the bose soundlink despite having a lower maximum volume sounds much cleaner and surprisingly more powerful.

i was really surprised that the UE boombox was not capable of a more powerful sound despite being more than twice as big as the soundlink.
but the weakest point is the internal battery. it is very small, about the size of an AA-cell with 3,7V and 2150mAh. logitech claims it to play for 6 hours, but during my tests the volume was already reduced after 1 hour, and after 2 hours the soundlink's maximum volume was higher than that of the UE boombox.

i like the design and also the fact that the UE boombox can stay connected to 3 bluetooth devices simultanously so that you can directly switch from one player to the other without the need of additional pairing. but the sound didn't convince me at all. the UE boombox is already too large to be called "portable", even the soundlink can be sometimes awkward to be taken along, but compared to the UE boombox the soundlink is really petite. i would have bit the bullet, but any other "boombox" (beats portable, altec lansing mix, etc) puts the UE boombox to shame soundwise.

title: A big leap for me, amazing performance!
text:
I have been shooting photographs since the 1970's. An avid fan of digital since it's inception I had moved up from basic cameras to a nice entry level Nikon DSLR in 2011. Feeling I needed something a little more serious I began researching the 'prosumer' class cameras including top end APS-C camers from several quality manufacturers. A little reluctant to move from Nikon I warily looked at specs of other higher APS-C sensor cameras. Not feeling I could justify the cost of a full frame DSLR but wanting a higher level of preformance I found the specs of this camera to be as appealing as it's price point, Went ahead and ordered the two lens kit with the 55-300mm lens and am totally satisfied!

The camera has a really nice feel to it. I don't have huge hands but average, and it feels really good and secure in one hand. The weight is good, a nice solid feel and well balanced even with the 55-300mm lens attached. I was pleased to see that with the 18-55 lens, though somewhat heavier than my Nikon D3100, this camera is more compact (shorter) since the VR is built into the camera and not the lens, allowing a more compact lens.

title: (Tries to) operate over congested 2.4GHz WiFi .
text:
Read Reviews before you buy!

Awesome sound, horrible implimentation.
When it works, it sounds great. Unfortunately, there are some un-recoverable flaws:

1- BIGGEST flaw - the wireless connection runs on 2.4GHz wi-Fi and requires a lot of bandwidth in spectrum that is all but used up in urban environments. Disclosure: I am a professional RF Engineering Tech so have training and access to spectrum analyzers and extensive spectrum surveys to verify that this is the cause of Harman Kardon's recurring issues. If your room is sufficiently RF isolated, and you are lucky you may find a location for your Bass unity that reliably connects (for now), but odds are that it will pop, crackle and click as it cuts in and out. HK did NOT put in wired jacks to connect the device when the wireless is un-workable.

2- No remote. Within constraints, you can program it to respond to other remotes. Depending on your remote, this may not work. The work-around is to procure a 3rd party remote.

3- We know that it is not a Surround Sound device, but it ALSO fails to flatten non-PCM signal standards. So if your source device is outputting surround sound only, this sound bar is useless to you. It can ONLY play analog signals.

Really, the only unresolvable issue is the wireless fail. ONLY buy this device if you've done a spectrum survey on the room it is going in and found it well sheilded. If you can't do a spectrum survey, my advice is don't even consider this device if the room it goes in has a window; probably not even if you live in a densely populated area. Don't forget RF environments change over time; just because the device works when you get it, does not mean that it will work in the same spot next month.

For me; this purchase was a horrible idea.

title: DLNA is useless!
text:
This device does not have a usable DLNA server. It's there, but the way it's designed, it's completely useless.

I should make note of a couple of things before I explain the problem. First, even though it is true that the DLink site indicates that the DLNA feature is coming on a future firmware upgrade, other users/reviewers had noted that it was already on the device, though I'm sure none tried to use it. So, I called DLink prior to purchasing the device and got confirmation that the DLNA server feature was in fact active. Well, it's not, at least in any usable way.

I was very excited a few weeks ago after purchasing this device on Amazon. I set it up and connected a flash drive with a sampling of audio and video media. I was able to play my FLAC files in the car, and my kids were able to stream movies, all via the 510L'S DLNA server.

I was about to leave a stellar review here, when I went back to the device and realized that each time you either remove and reconnect the media or turn the device off and back on, it removes the index it had previously built, and begins indexing the media from scratch. Now, this wouldn't be a problem if it took a couple of minutes to do so, but I tried putting just half of my music library and a handful of video files on a flash drive. An hour and a half later it was still building the index.

The only control over the DLNA server provided in the admin interface is to name it and turn it on and off. I installed the recent firmware release hoping to see some added control over the indexing, but nothing.

This makes the DLNA server useless for a mobile device. Think about it, if the power goes out in my house in the middle of the night or while I'm at work, and my home router has to reboot, and re-index, then more than likely by the time I wake up or get home, the re-indexing will have taken place and I'm good to go. Generally, no problem.

But if I turn the device on when I start my car, and want to listen to music on the way to work, how am I going to be able to do that if the existing index is tossed out, and it begins from scratch re-indexing. Right now it's indexing pretty slowing, but no matter how fast they get the indexing to work, it's not going to get through my entire collection in a few minutes. As it is currently indexing, it might take, let's say, 3 hours. But even if they reduce it to 30 minutes, I'm still at work before all of my content is available to me.

It's a mobile device, but the feature requires that it be left on at all times in order to be usable.

It's not as if it would require any serious logic to provide some re-indexing control in the interface. The index is written to the media, not built in memory, so it's still there when the device is turned back on, and it's there when the media is plugged back in.

DLink just took this off of some other device and put no thought into it. I put up a note on the forum, but it appears that DLink tech staff do not participate in that venue. I called tech support, got to a 2nd level, and was told they were sorry and would put a feedback suggestion.

I'm really disappointed in this company. They put out a product with a feature without putting any thought at all into it. It's a shame, really, because I really like this device. It does most things well. The interface is functional and relatively well designed. But this DLNA limitation brings it from a 5 to a 1 for me.

Just gotta find the box to send it back.
