title: Misleading description, but generally a good product
text:
The owner's manual doesn't say so, but the microphone input was evidently designed for a cheap crystal microphone, not a good-quality dynamic microphone. Crystal microphones generally have poorer sound quality, but a much higher output voltage. With the MAG-MDVD500 volume control turned up to maximum in DVD mode, if one YELLS into a dynamic microphone one can hear one's voice coming from the speakers faintly. I fault the distributor for not describing the microphone requirements at all in the manual and I fault Amazon.com for suggesting a variety of dynamic microphones to viewers of the MAG-MDVD500 page.

Although the unit can be partly controlled via the buttons on the case, to access all of its functions, particularly when playing MP3 music files from a CD, USB thumb drive or SD card, one MUST have the handheld infrared remote control. If the remote control breaks or if you lose it, you're out of luck, as getting a replacement remote control from the vendor isn't possible, as far as I can determine. The remote control is a bit larger than a credit card, about 1/4 inch thick, with a membrane keypad on one side.

The manual doesn't describe what kind of battery the remote control uses. IF you can get the battery compartment open, you'll discover a CR2025 lithium coin cell in there. These are common enough and the cell will probably last as long as you care to keep the boombox. The battery compartment in the remote control is poorly designed. The only way I was able to open it was to put it face down on the edge of a table, work the notch on the battery holder with the fingernail of one hand, the little latch to the left of it with the fingernail of my other hand and wiggle it vigorously until it finally popped open.

The power amplifier is a bit weak. Turning the volume control past about the 70% level usually results in annoying audible distortion while playing properly normalized recorded material. However, if the manual volume control is kept below distortion levels, the volume is more than adequate to fill the room with sound. A bass-boost button is available, but ordinary speech generally sounds better with bass-boost turned off.

When a disc, USB stick or SD card with MP3 music files is inserted, the unit automatically scans the storage medium and discovers all the MP3 files in the various folders. It doesn't understand Winamp playlists (.m3u files), and there's no apparent way of programming play order, but it does have a repeat mode that is accessible from the remote control. Also, a MODE button on the case allows one to select the disc, USB port or SD port for playback.

The TV-out connectors support composite video (yellow RCA jack) and stereo audio (red and white RCA jacks); a video patch cord is included. Using the remote control, one can select 4:3 or 16:9 aspect ratio and NTSC or PAL video output format.

title: Bought based upon reviews here, and I'm happy I did.
text:
I wonder how Kingston feels about all the reviews for this particular SODIMM being based, not upon the "laptop memory" role this is intended to fulfill, but rather the Synology NAS application so many of us seem to be using it for?

I recently purchased and installed a Synology 1512+ NAS ("network attached storage") system. This system comes with two RAM slots, the first (on the CPU side) already populated with a 1GB stick, but the other (on the opposite, and accessible, side) unpopulated. The system is set up to permit as much as 3GB of memory, and as is typically the case, adding more is sufficient to confuse the system and cause you problems (and potentially even data loss?)

Synology sells their own 2GB "add on stick" which I'm sure is ideally set up for this device, but which is inappropriately expensive based upon current RAM pricing, so I thought I'd look for alternatives. And here on Amazon, I found a TON of references to this particular stick as being "just as good, and a lot cheaper" than the Synology-provided RAM stick. So, I went ahead and picked it up.

It does seem to be 100% compatible, as the various other reviews state. I can't say for certain that it's better than any other 2GB stick with the same specification might be, but I can say that it's perfectly suited for this application and is a fraction of the Synology-provided part's price.

I've seen no change in the "normal" performance of my NAS after adding this, but large file transfers (such as backing up larger directories - like my entire "downloaded software archive" - to an attached USB3.0 disk which I'll keep stored in a safe place for security purposes) have speeded up noticably, so it's proven to be a worthwhile addition to my NAS.

And this is why I come to Amazon... the customer reviews (positive and negative, "real" or "fake" in some cases, all tell me SOMETHING about the product!). I'd probably just have purchased the Synology stick, and paid sixty dollars or so more, if it weren't for the reviews posted here. Thanks, guys!

text:

I am one of those Amazon shoppers that reads reviews like a crazy person before making the plunge on most things, but especially electronics. The idea of having a single CAT 5e cable to extend an HDMI signal to my second tv sounded great, especially for the price!! I had some reservations, thanks to the honest reviews by other customers. To put it simply, I should have listened to them. This product is not worth the risk! You might get lucky and have it work for you for quite some time, or at least enough time to justify the cheap price. However, there is a good chance that you will get a defective one or pair. This is where the big problems start.

Upon receiving the pair of HDMI extenders, everything seemed really nice. Good looking product, with an above average packaging. I took care to follow the very well laid out instructions from other users here on Amazon in regards to installation, buying the better CAT 6 cable, and being careful of power fluctuations/flickers, etc.. It wouldn't work with the 100' CAT 6 cable that I purchased new from Amazon at the same time I purchased these adapters. I tried it with an old, cheaper 50' CAT 5e cable I had lying around, and it halfway worked. Halfway being, no audio (regardless of source), video only at 720p, and green artifacting moving all over roughly 20% of the screen at a time. I emailed Elemenos customer service through Amazon, and the first reply came after 3 days of waiting. 3 days!! There is NO OTHER form of customer contact for Elemenos, short of Twitter. It took a few emails just to get to the exchange process, with each reply coming no sooner than 20 hours, and as much as 45 hours later. Now a week into owning a defective product, I have to ship out my defective devices, they have to be received, and then they will ship out a replacement. Maybe I'm just spoiled by Amazon, but this is a ridiculous policy! They ship out the replacements and I get them within 3 days. Good! ...not so much. They only sent me the receiver, and not the sender. They work as a pair, and I had sent back both, as per their instructions. Again I am stuck with a product I can't use, and going through the patience testing email hell once again. After 3-4 days of email dispute, they finally discovered that their receiving department mixed up my return with someone else's, and shipped out the sending unit to me. Another 3 days later, and I am finally able to try and do this all over again! Plug everything in with the 100' CAT 6 cable, no picture unless I bring it down to 720p, and still no audio. Try the 50' CAT 5e cable again, and everything is working!! Working at 1080p even! Wow this is freaking cool! Test it with my Xbox 360, Dish DVR, and Boxee Box. Everything is working at max resolution, and audio comes through great. Very cool product! (there are tons of options available, and I would not recommend this Elemenos option)

Fast forward 27 days, and it suddenly stops working. I ran over to check how hot it was, as some other reviewers have mentioned it running hot. The sending and receiving units both were not even warm to the touch. Both ends were power protected and conditioned, to make sure I didn't break them, due to the seemingly fragile nature of the units according to reviewers. Both devices still had their led power lights on. My sources were still outputting correctly when taking the extender out of the equation. (Moving a DVR just to test this is a pain in the a$$ by the way)

I am now out of my return period to return through Amazon, regardless of the fact that I had to do an exchange that took forever. I emailed Elemenos again last week to see if I could get some help, or maybe another replacement, or maybe even just some troubleshooting tips I hadn't already thought of. Still no reply. A whole week and no reply. This is pathetic.

Final Verdict:
Do not waste your money, do not buy. You have a better chance of winning the lottery than you do of getting a non-defective unit(s). Even if you do get a good pair of units, many other reviewers have mentioned them dying out after only a couple of months. Save your money, buy a higher quality HDMI extender, and from a better company.

text:
I BOUGHT THIS MYSELF. F (for Forget) those "they gave me 10 free samples in exchange for a positive review" reviews.

This is my second iSimple interface device and I'm impressed again. My [[ASIN:B001TH8O7E previous one]] had a permanently attached 30 pin input. It held up well over three years of daily use. I chose this over [[ASIN:B00GP3PB4G the one with the permanently attached lightning cable]] because although my 30 pin input worked until I swapped it out, it didn't have many months left. With this, you can just replace a cheap cable if the business end wears out or gets damaged somehow and you can use any type or color cable you prefer. Plus, this model is cheaper!

A word of warning; it doesn't come exactly as shown. The image here shows a USB receptacle just a few inches from the device along with a separate extension cable that terminates with a dash mountable USB port. It does not come with this dash mount extension cable. Instead, the female USB port is on a cable about six or 7 feet long, no separate extension. It terminates in a plain female port, no circular dash mount thing.

I ran the cable with the USB receptacle behind the dash then down into the glove compartment. From there I have a 3' USB to lightning cable which goes into [[ASIN:B00I9R8CF6 a dock]] for my 6.

I tested the interface to work with my iPhone 6, iPhone 4, iPod Touch (2nd gen!), and an Android "Droid Razr MAXX HD". The droid pops up a message saying that no installed apps will work with the accessory but Spotify played through my car speakers with no complaint.

Ultra simple install if you're comfortable working inside the dash. Red cable attached to +12 volt accessory power, black wire grounded to the frame, RCA cables into head units auxiliary input, and Bob's your uncle.

Just make sure your head unit actually has RCA inputs before you order (don't post a bad review because you don't know what you're getting into).

Buy it.

title: Impressive, but not really usable
text:
This was a fun toy to try out, but I ended up returning it. To test it, I:
-Watched How to Train Your Dragon in 3D
-Played Crysis 2 in 3D
-Did some work in Excel
-Did some web browsing

Background. I make my living working on computers and associated technology. I normally use a 3 screen setup: 1 16:9 23" screen and 2 16:10 22" screens. I'm used to watching TV on a 37" 1080p screen. And I have a very bad astigmatism.

The image quality of this visor is very high. Yes, if you really want to look for them, you can see the pixels but I really didn't notice them no matter what I was doing. Colors are very vibrant.

The 3D, when watching Train a Dragon, was amazing - very impressive, very cool. Surprisingly, it was much less impressive in Crysis 2. At first I wasn't even sure it was active but after a bit I was able to at least notice that it was 3D. I'm sure that's a Crysis 2 issue, though, not the visor.

It's effectively unusable for work - for me anyway. Others noted the blurring at the edges. Maybe it's worse for me because of my astigmatism, but it's so bad that I can't read my taskbar nor the location bar in my web browser. I'm effectively unable to read anything if it's not right in the center of the screen - unless I adjust it, in which case I can read the edges but the center is now blurry. Flunk for office productivity.

Web browsing was mixed. As I said, I was unable to read or even really see the top, bottom, or sides - making it difficult to see what page I was on, or to click a new tab. On the other hand, images were impressive. Yes, guys, those kinds of images too.

Comfort. In a word, not. Actually, the pressure on the forehead, while not comfortable, wasn't as bad as I feared. The eyestrain, however, was horrible - and not just in 3D. If anything, I had the easiest time when watching the movie. But, again, this could be a result of my poor eyesight. If yours is better, you might not have the eyestrain.

Ease of use. Not as bad as I feared. It did take me several minutes to figure out how to adjust everything just right for me. But, once I learned all the tricks, I could put it on and have it right in 10 seconds or less.

Stars. Definitely not a 5-star product. I debated between 3 or 4 stars but, because of the high price and its total uselessness as even a short-term work tool, I settled on 3.

Summary. Do not buy if you have a bad astigmatism. If you're looking for something to watch 3D movies or play 3D games, and you don't mind some forehead discomfort, this might be the toy for you. Personally, until Google Glass comes out, I'd rather have a couple of high-res 27" monitors. And I just might pay less than $800 for the two.

But it was fun to try.

title: Great all-around camera
text:
This is one of my favorite compact cameras – and I have several. It’s slim and understated and has an excellent 18.3mm f/2.8 lens – one of it’s main selling points.

This camera has a full complement of manual and automatic exposure modes..

The main feature of the Ricoh GR is its 16.2-million-pixel, APS-C-sized CMOS sensor. As has been the trend among many other recent cameras, the GR's sensor does not have an anti-aliasing filter, which means the camera should produce slightly sharper images than if such a filter was present. Excellent at capturing detail such as a field of flowers.

The sensor is paired with an 18.3mm f/2.8 lens, offering the equivalent focal length of a 28mm lens on a full-frame camera – or 35mm film camera if you’re old enough to remember those.
If you find that the 28mm focal length is too wide for portraits, street photography and many landscape images you can use the built-in crop mode that uses only a portion of the overall image to produce the same field of view as a 35mm lens on a full-frame camera. Due to the 35mm mode effectively cropping the full-resolution images from the camera, any shots captured in this mode are at a reduced resolution of 10 million pixels.

The GR has a huge range of options within the menu system. As well as the 35mm crop mode and native 3:2 aspect ratio, there is also the option to use either a 4:3 or 1:1 aspect ratio. Of course, each of these modes will again reduce the resolution of the images.

Raw shooting is possible, and these images can be captured simultaneously with JPEGs. That the Ricoh GR saves its raw images as DNG files should prove a huge benefit to many photographers. This means that the raw files can be opened in virtually any raw-conversion software, and it should ensure both forward and backwards compatibility with any future software.
I highly recommend this camera for the more advanced snap-shooter / photographer.

This is my backup Canon camera. I also have a 6D and a T4i; both made by Canon. I'm a Canon fan and I admit it.

I do not shoot professional photography but I do travel the world for a career and I take my cameras with me all of the time. That means a great amount of what I shoot is outdoor but when I do shoot inside I just can't stand a slow camera with shutter lag/delay.

I had Canon's wonderful S95 (this model previously) and later I purchased Canon's dismal S100. The S100 was a mistake in so many ways and I won't detail that here but the Canon S110 is now under my direction and I so love it!

My needs come down to my travels and I don't like handing over my SLR's to strangers or to people that might drop it if I am asking for shots of myself/wife to be taken by another. There are also certain times I just don't want to bring the SUV of cameras along for a day where it is essential for quality photography.

Canon's S110 shoots near SLR like quality that is so good that I can pick out the individual blades of grass in a outdoor shot. Or the stunning blue skies so detailed that the camera image is even better looking than that of the actual sky itself.

It's fast. Even inside. I can get 100 shots out of it in just minutes. It races to process the prior shot and stands ready for the next shot.

This is a POINT & SHOOT camera so you do have limits. Yes, there are tons of potential settings but for a Point & Shoot; leaving in the AUTO mode isn't a bad thing.

Is it perfect? NO WAY.

Canon fails on battery life with the S110. Yet in fairness, most have asked for a small pocket camera that can mirror-image SLR quality. Plus, at just $325 in price. So you'll need an extra battery at all times. Add to that the very slow recharge time it takes to recharge your Canon wafer-thin battery.

Now let's go to Canon's infamous POP-UP FLASH. It will push your thumb away from the body as it pops up so NEVER hold the camera without the strap to secure it. This POP-UP flash has been complained about for years but Canon hasn't changed it and they must have their reasons why. There's also no rubber grip on the cameras body front so again, have that strap always in use and around your hand so that you don't drop this camera.

If you want detailed SPECS here, I'm not going to list them as you can see them online at so many places including AMAZON.COM. My review here is SIMPLE. It's about image quality, camera response and speed and the pro's and con's.

This is a great (GREAT) camera for the money and it comes from the top name in digital photography.

Worth every dollar.

title: Vaio Pro vs Aspire S7 a comparative review.
text:
Comparative review: Haswell Acer Aspire S7, vs. Sony Vaio Pro 13
Tech specs:
Aspire S7: Core i7, 256gb solid state, 8gb ram, purchased clean (no bloatware) from Microsoft store for 1200 all in.
Vaio Pro 13: Core i7, 128gb solid state, 8gb ram, received fee from Amazon vine (1500 on Amazon)

I had the S7 for 30 days, I kept the Vaio because free was a better price.

I have split this review based on various features so that you can directly compare, I will have some additional info at the end to wrap up.

Design: In my opinion the S7 is the clear winner here
The S7 (4/5)

Pros:
1) Round edges make it comfortable to put on your lap
2) Cover tilts all the way back so that you can show it to somebody across from you, or more importantly adjust it to any viewing angle (and it also means you can hold it open for presentations.
3) Not a lot of body flex which means you can click on the trackpad regardless of the surface you are using.
4) Just looks nice.
5) Stiff hinge allows you to open it one handed and holds it in place really well (less typing shake)

Cons:
1) SD cards stick out of the slot a fair amount so you can't just leave them in there indefinitely. (mitigated by the larger HD space)

Vaio (2/5)

Pros:
1) SD card fully inserts so it can be used as permanent file storage for music etc.
2) Sturdy: I dropped it (not on purpose) and all it did was dent the corner slightly.
3) USB charger on the power cord is a nice touch.
4) Looks decent

Cons:
1) Sharp edges dig into your lap (really hurt)
2) Cover has limited movement, in fact I couldn't tilt it back far enough to type on my lap with an ideal viewing angle.
3) Slight tilt to the screen and keyboard mean that there is a gap when you close it.
4) Carbon fiber flexes a lot so sometimes you cannot use the mousepad because the keyboard has flexed.
5) Cannot be opened one handed.

Keyboard:

S7 (1/5):
Pros:
1) Sufficient key travel (unlike on the earlier S7)

Cons:
1) Keyboard has some weird organization choices, like no Function keys, not sure why
2) My spacebar only registered in the middle or left side, it missed most hits from the right side, this was a big problem. While this does not appear to be an endemic problem it is also not isolated. Had I planned on keeping the computer I would have had them fix it.
3) Backlight made it difficult to see the keys when the lights were on.
4) No dedicated media controls
5) One of the keys, either enter or shift was not full sized I cannot remember which.

Vaio (3/5):

Pros:
1) Decent backlight
2) Decent typing feel, full size keys.

Cons:
1) While decent to type on, it isn't a Lenovo quality keyboard... I wish it was.
2) No dedicated PgUP, PgDn, home, end buttons.
3) No media controls

General use and other features:

S7: (4/5)

Vaio: (3/5)

text:

title: A four star computer with a one star screen and two star trackpad
text:
I really wanted to like this machine.

But the screen was a dealbreaker for me. I had read that the screen was mediocre, and figured that that was fine with me -- a high end screen wasn't that important to me. But "mediocre" doesn't really begin to describe the problem with the screen. It's washed out to the point of distraction and eye strain. Colors look odd, blacks aren't black, and whites are covered in a bluish haze. I tried color calibration and even a combination of settings found in these comments -- but they don't really solve the problem. This is, as some reviewers point out, a viewing angle problem; the screen rises to the level of mediocre -- barely passable -- when you look at it from just the right, very narrow angle. But that angle is so narrow that it's impossible to maintain, because the slightest movement will put you out of it. So again, while I wouldn't put a high end screen high up on my list of priorities, this screen I find to be so bad that I can't ignore it.

Then there's the trackpad. It's not very responsive. Scrolling is terrible. This is something you can might learn to tolerate. If it weren't for the screen, I'd probably have thought seriously about just living with it.

Because otherwise, it's a very fast and very nice looking computer. It's a little heavy, but that's a worthwhile trade off for the price (you can find these refurbished with 6gb of ram for $599). But before you buy one, I recommend walking into a computer store and testing one and thinking long and hard about whether you can live with the display and trackpad. These are items that the average reviews make sound like minor irritations and drawbacks. And that may be true for some. But for many others, they'll make the machine unusable.

title: I'm not sure why one would buy this.
text:
I am not sure why one would buy the MED500X for $239, when you can buy the MED1000X3D for the same price. I'm not really sure why I purchased that either. The thing you should be aware about the Mede8er is the have a reputation for excellent quality play back. No stuttering. Unlike many players, even if you have network errors or a very slow connection it doesn't tend to crash the player, just make it just freezes the video and keeps playing the audio until it has enough video data to start rendering again. In the end it is a much more pleasant experience than say watching something on satellite TV on a cloudy day.

Now the bad. The navigation on the Mede8er is very poor. If say you connect to an 3TB internet share with movies and posters you have scanned, ripped, or downloaded, it is very likely your Mede8er will crash. You see it will do things like start converting all those posters in the background to thumbnail images, and that may consume too much resources to even update the screen for hours. There are a number of tools for the mede8er that help. There is TVRename, you can use for TV Series. There is Y2M for movies. There is really no tool that works for say "Movies with bonus features". Or say your folder of home videos... Both these re-arranging all your movies and tv series, removing the excessive image files, etc. With the Mede8er MED500X this is going to be even more complicated, because the jukebox only supports a maximum of 2000 movies, and you cannot nest folders more than three levels deep. So you naming needs to look something like "Z:\Comedy\500 Days of Summer\500 Days of Summer (2007).mkv". With the firmware updates for the MED1000X3D they have loosened this a bit. There is no fixed limit on the folder depths. Jukeboxes are still limited to 4000 movies, but you can make multiple jukeboxes act like one.

Still if you have an existing collection of media, you will easily spend months reorganizing your collection to work with this device.

To make matters worse, Mede8er reserves the right to change the codec support with every firmware release. Most companies automatically update to the latest firmware before shipping. So you have no way of knowing what codecs your Mede8er will play. For me the big gotcha is the Mede8er advertises Divx codec support. Most players now days do not, and I have 70% of my media collection in a Divx format. That made the Mede8er seem like an obvious choice. To make a long story short, Mede8er silently dropped divx support because apparently they never bothered to pay for a patent license for the device. So far I spent 2 weeks converting my tv series from divx to xvid. I can expect it to take another 2 weeks to convert all of my movie collection. In Mede8er's favour, they did provide link for a tool that can update fast in bulk. (Of course all the tool does is change the tagging of the video, so they are still violating the Divx patents by playing the video.) All the tool documentation and such is in German. The one part I could understand is where they told me to back-up my media first. A full backup takes about 1 month to complete, so I really would not save any time.

title: After all the negative reviews, I thought there was hope.

After a hard fought battle to find something that was decent as a note taking device, I settled on the Lenovo ThinkPad Tablet. I had high expectations of this machine as something professionals would use...boy was I wrong.

I today's world it's hard to find someone who isn't walking around with some sort of smart device. But when you look at it from my perspective, I'm looking for something that's really going to help me out, not something that is a glorified entertainment center. When I saw this tablet I thought for sure this was the one made for the working person.

I've had the tablet for 4 days now and here's what I've found I like and hate about this machine.

Likes:
-Very sturdy. Many people have complained about this tablet being too thick or too heavy but the way I see it, the tablet fits nicely in the hands and has ports (USB, sd card, sim slot) that others do not. And as a professional using this thing, these were items I needed so the added thickness didn't bother me.
-It comes with some nice apps pre-loaded but again, for a business tablet, there's a lot of stuff that shouldn't be loaded on there from the get go.

Dislikes:
Where do I start...
-Major issue, the tablet comes with a micro USB charging cord that takes about 8 hours to charge. If you want to pop for the optional docking station it charges in about 2-3. I ordered one to see if it worked better but...
-The micro USB port broke internally after plugging it in for the 3rd time. I wondered why it wasn't taking a charge. After an inspection of the micro USB internal pin connections, I could see it was broken and pushed into the tablet case.
-Average battery life is nowhere near the 8 hours claimed. Maybe you would get that if everything was turned off (wifi, bluetooth, screen brightness) but I was seeing 3-4 hours the two times I got it to charge.
-The Google Android market account sign up screen was always running in the background. I really don't care if this was an app that I could have opened but it was almost like it was a requirement to sign up for another e-mail account through Google. Hey Google, I already have other e-mail accounts, let me use those to sign up for the Android market.
-The default Google web browser would freeze up on most web pages. I tried getting on PBS Kids for my son to play some games and I had to reboot the tablet in order for the page to load. I tried downloading other web browsers but some didn't support flash and others were difficult to use. If I can't utilize the full potential of this thing, why did I spend $500 on it? I can get a laptop for a lot cheaper.
-The e-mail account app would regularly not load or would have discrepancies for my Yahoo and work e-mail accounts. If I had 100 messages in my actual Yahoo inbox, this thing wouldn't see all 100 messages. More along the lines of 80 or so. Where did the others go? Apparently lost in Google land.
-Transferring and saving files to SD card is a nightmare. Part of this problem may come from my works security settings but when I would download a file to the tablet from one of my e-mail accounts, if it could download the file, the file names would change. So although I had the files downloaded, I couldn't recognize what they were. In order to make them recognizable again, I had to download a file management app to go in and change the file names back...manually. I think I got about 20 files in before the cussing started. In other words, apparently tablets are made for people that have spare time on their hands. From my point of view, if this thing is really supposed to be a professional's tool, make it professional.

So now, I'm about to put the return label on the tablet to send back for another since I have no way of charging it at this point and I wonder if it would just be a better idea to buy $500 worth of legal pads to take notes on. At least then I'll be able to use them to the fullest potential. Right now all I've got is an expensive paper weight.

Getting a little off track, those being my first Android item, I'm finding that quality control is losing its meaning. Apparently it's all about the first to get something to market, not the better product on the market. I teach in the manufacturing industry and this this is a big letdown. I'm going to stick it out to see if the upgrade to Android 4.0 brings any positive to this situation but from reading the new features I'm likely to see, I'll be able to unlock this thing with facial recognition but I still won't be able to do much of anything productive with it.

Thanks for reading my rambling. I hope you seriously weigh your options before going with this one.

title: a good compromise for a pol
text: Polarizing microscopes (indispensable to examine rock thin sections) are very expensive products (usually $3,000 and up). Amscope offers this one at less than $300. Of course, at this price, it's not a true polarizing microscope, only a brightfield microscope with a polarizing kit, i.e. a supplemental round stage with a polarizing lens that is set on the original stage and a removable analyzing lens which adapts on the top of the binocular. In a true "pol", the polarizer is under the stage and the analyzer inside the head. The biggest drawback of the polarizing kit is the impossibility to adapt a camera over the analyzer. Another drawback comes from the reduced space between the extra stage and the nosepiece. And, of course there's no Bertrand lens, Koehler illumination etc that characterize full-features pols. But other sellers of brightfields with polarizing kits ask for $700 or more, so Amscope's product is really cheap. Its quality isn't cheap: sturdy construction, good optics (up to x1000 with oil, but x400 is enough for rock thin sections). The documentation is scarce, written in bad English. The packaging is very good and everything arrived in perfect condition. Because of its limitations, this product would deserve only 2 or 3 stars. But there's no free lunch, and for somebody with a limited budget, it offers an excellent way to look at thin sections, hence the 4 stars I give it.

title: The almost perfect Windows 8.1 8 inch Tablet
text:
The almost perfect 8 inch Windows 8.1 experience. I want to first say that I absolutely love this tablet. The screen is 1200 x 800 but for an 8 inch tablet this is not an issue. The tablet had the auto-brightness feature turned on by default which made the screen look a bit dim. This can be turned off and then you can adjust the screen brightness to suit your preference. Since the display is an IPS display the colors are vibrant. Watching a Netflix program on the tablet looks great.

The first thing you will want to do with the tablet is download the newest BIOS and Firmware from Dell. Dell makes this simple by using the installed DELL app. Also I was pleasantly surprised to discover that once I registered the tablet my Warranty is good until June of 2015. I was only expecting a year warranty.

Instead of giving a run down of the system specs and benchmark results I will list why I decided on this tablet. The need for a full Windows 8.1 tablet experience was what I desired. Working as an IT System Administrator I wanted a tablet that would run all of my Windows Applications. Windows 8.1 RT was not an option. By being a full Windows 8.1 experience I can run all of my Desktop apps on this device. With the inclusion of Office 2013 Home and Student all I need to do is install Outlook 2013 and connect it to my corporate network to enjoy a full featured Microsoft Exchange experience. I do wish Outlook 2013 had been included with this out of the box but I can understand why it was not. With the 64GB version I have more than enough storage. Then adding an additional 64GB micro-SD card along with a network drive I do not see myself running out of storage. By being a full Windows 8.1 experience you are not limited by what is available in the Microsoft App Store. As I said earlier, if you are running a program on your desktop computer than you can run it on this tablet.

There are things to consider before buying. The screen is small and if you have issues with seeing small fonts on your display then this will be an issue. You will need a Blue Tooth Keyboard and Mouse to be able to use this in a productivity environment. I have not purchased a stylus yet for it but I could see where that would help when running Desktop Applications. Since the tablet does not have a kickstand a third party case with a kickstand is a necessity.

Everyone who I have shown the tablet to have been impressed. When I tell them the price which was $329 they become more interested since many of them have been looking at the IPADs and Android solutions which are available this season.

I wish the tablet had stereo speakers instead of just having one speaker. I wish it had a full sized USB port instead of the micro USB. I wish it had a mini HDMI display port. I wish it had a user friendly replaceable battery. If those items had been included then I would have rated it five stars.

title: It saved a DVD with 500 images on it!
text:
The Aleratec 240131 is a CD/DVD cleaning and repair system that works well. I've saved several DVDs by using the repair function of the Aleratec, and several other DVDs just needed cleaning to get them to work.

There are three levels of maintenance. The first one is Disc Cleaning. The Aleratec comes with cleaning fluid and two cleaning heads. The second level is Disc Repair. Likewise, it comes with repair protective solution and two repair heads. The third level, and most drastic, is Disc Buffing. It comes with two buffing units.

(A head is a cylindrical device about 1 ¾" in diameter and about ¾" tall with a cloth-type material ring on top of it. The material varies with each type of head. A buffing unit is the top half of a head.)

From the User Guide:
"It is generally recommended to begin with the Disc Cleaning procedure first,
and if necessary move to the more intensive procedures."

To operate the Aleratec, first decide how damaged the disc in question is. If it has sustained minor damage, then just a Disc Cleaning may be in order. If after cleaning the disc it is not sufficiently restored, then try the Disc Repair Procedure.

If the disc sustained major damage, the User Guide says to first clean the disc, then use the Disc Buffing Procedure, followed by the Disc Repair Procedure.

After deciding which procedure to use, select the two correct heads, open the Aleratec (it opens like a clam shell), insert the two heads into it, (in the case of repair, dribble three drops of repair protective solution on the right repair head) insert the disc to be repaired on top of the heads with the spindle in the Aleratec protruding through the hole in the disc, close the top, and push either the clean button or the repair button.

If the disc is being cleaned, it will spin around for about 20 seconds. If it is being repaired, it will spin for about two minutes.

Then if all goes well, the disc should now work. Like I have said, I have saved several DVDs, but there have been a few I wasn't able to save. It did, however, rescue a DVD that I thought was trash that had over 500 images (photos) on it.

One of my DVDs, which I actually retrieved from the waste basket, I had to use the Disc Buffing Procedure on. After that, it worked! But the Disc Buffing Procedure is the last resort because it "removes a small amount of plastic from the disc, allow(ing) deeper levels of damage to be repaired."

The heads don't last forever. The cleaning heads last for 220 uses. The repair heads last for 20-25 uses. And the buffing heads last for 10-20 uses. (These figures are from the User Guide.) Also, the Aleratec comes with a 10 ml. tube of repair solution and a 30 ml. bottle of cleaning solution. There is a refill pack available for the Aleratec that costs $22.91 at Amazon (240138). There are also available separate cleaning refills ($7.99), repair refills ($8.99), and buffing refills ($8.99).

I'm very happy with the Aleratec 240131 CD/DVD cleaning and repair system and would recommend it to anybody who has some discs that don't play well or don't play at all.

title: Look Out OPPO You Have Tough Competition
text:
I have used this unit enough to know that it is well built, fast loading and the picture quality is absolutely amazing, but a little overdone. I recently bought a Pioneer Elite BDP-62FD to use as an everyday player, and I am going to go back to my review and lower the score. Well that was a mistake, but it took me beyond the Best Buy return time to realize the Pioneer was overrated and really a piece of junk for the price. (For Example: The Pioneer has trouble loading many blu-ray discs, the remote only works in a limited range and no WiFi adapter for its overly high price.) I decided to Try the Panny, and OMG am I impressed. Why this unit is not sold in stores behooves me. The unit is really good looking, and does the one thing most player makers have totally forgotten about. WILL IT PLAY BLU-RAY Discs? This one does, and the picture quality and the 7.1 surround are absolutely amazing. Setup was easy, but the touch screen remote takes some time to get used to, and I recommend that you read the book about the remote, because once you figure it out it, is actually pretty neat. It was a customer from Amazon that commented on this machine that convinced me to buy it, and he was right. I won't compare it to Pioneer, but I will compare it to my OPPO BD-93 by scores of 1 to 5, 5 being the best.

Ease of use OPPO 5 Panny 5
Remote Control OPPO 5 Panny 4.6
Picture Quality OPPO 5 Panny 5
Pro Look OPPO 4.8 Panny 5
Sound OPPO 4.8 Panny 5
Hard to Load Discs OPPO 5 Panny 4.5
Speed OPPO 5 Panny 4.9
Streaming OPPO 5 Panny 4.
TOTAL 4.95 4.75

As you can see, these two units are almost equal. The reviews are correct, the Panny does not stream as well as the OPPO, or for that fact the LG and Pioneer. Since all units stream, I had to rate it, and this Panny unit does not stream as well as their cheaper models. Of course, the OPPO is the industry studio standard, and if you want a well rounded everyday Blu-Ray Player, this unit is right their with the OPPO. I do not understand what is wrong with the industry. They call these machines Blu-Ray players, but the OPPO, Panny, high end LG and Sony in this order are the only machines that actually play discs without a problem. I have also learned, if your machine, no matter what brand loads and plays discs when you get it, and you are not into streaming, DO NOT upgrade the firmware until you have a problem loading discs. For example, my Pioneer was great until I upgraded the firmware, the the load problems started. I have also found out from Pioneer and LG, that most firmware upgrades are for streaming, and have nothing to do with the unit's ability to play blu-rays, so on Monday, I am going to call Pioneer, and ask them to send me a disc to back the firmware up.

In conclusion, the Panasonic is a fine unit, and its quality if right up there with the OPPO, except for one thing. How long will it last? The OPPO weighs over 11 pounds due to its heave duty motor and quality of build. The Panasonic weighs about 4 pounds, and this makes me wonder about the longevity under heavy duty everyday use. I will update as time goes on. However, if you want a high quality player, that plays discs well, looks professional, just plain works great, and cannot afford the OPPO BDP-103, this is an almost equal unit. Plus, if you do not stream, you will love this unit. I am giving this unit 5 stars, because I could care less if the unit streams. It was made to play blu-ray discs, and this one really does.

title: Love this reader, but the white cap is loose, get the BLACK one instead
text:
I really love the Elago readers, but the cap on this white one is loose (as other reviewers have already noted). The cap stays on normally... but if it is loosened just a little, it will fall right off. Creative use of paper, superglue, rubber, and other such materials can fix the problem, but unless you are dead set on the white, I would recommend getting the black one instead, it's cap stays on very well.

[[ASIN:B002HGFKR8 elago Mobile Nano II USB 2.0 microSDHC Flash Memory Card Reader (Black)]]

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The following is a copy of my review of the black one. Except for the cap, all else is the same between the two units:

This has become my keychain flash drive of choice. As others have mentioned, it cuts your chance of losing data in 1/2 due to a failed memory controller. I Used the modification shown in one of the customer images to drill a small hole in the cap. PERFECT. You can also heat up a needle/safety pin with a torch and melt a small hole if you don't have the right drill bit handy. Example image here:
http://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-media/permalink/moKMX1IOND1HUR/B002HGFKR8/ref=cm_ciu_images_pl_link

Really I could sing the praises of this thing forever, I REALLY like them. BUT there are a couple catches which people should know about:

1) COMPATIBILITY: Driver support and compatibility on older computers can be SKETCHY. Of the roughly 30 older model (windows XP era) computers I've tried it on, approx 1/4 of them would not read the card. Popped in a different flash drive I had laying around, worked just fine. Ive never had trouble with it in a newer computer.

2) SPEED: This reader is about 20% slower than top end SD readers. I informally tested the transfer speeds of a class 6 microSDHC card in both the elago reader and in a Sandisk MicroMate SD reader using a SD adapter and found the Sandisk reader to be about 20% faster. Your results may very of course...

All in all, it's a fantastic reader which i think everyone should have in your arsenal. It would get 5 stars if not for the compatibility problems with some older computers. If you use you're SD card to carry important tools and documents which you NEED to be able to read on ANY computer you encounter, then this guy may not be for you. But due to it's size and extreme utility, I'm willing to forgive that and I use it every day. Two thumbs up for a great product.

~~UPDATE~~
I got about 9 months of heavy keychain wear out of it before it died on me. I replaced it with a couple more and am now up to 3 of them on my keychain, no further problems. I LOVE THIS DRIVE. I also keep a tiny [[ASIN:B005FYNSUA SanDisk Cruzer Fit Flash Drive]] for any compatibility issues I might encounter with certain computers. The sandisk writes VERY slow however, I prefer the elago readers.

text:

Very minimalist, tight design, but maybe too much so. The button interface...AUGH!! Just ... no. Too dang complicated. Hold buttons to do this, push two buttons together, etc. Come on! No need for all that! Just add a couple of more buttons and don't make me remember secret combos like I was playing Street Fighter!

Also, the sound is very much "just OK", and certainly nothing exceptional about it, especially again compared with other units in this range and size.

I do love the design of the box itself...the grill with the red is very cool, but too bad the buttons are so frustrating, and that the speaker itself doesn't seem to separate itself from the 2,765 other BT speakers out there.

Just OK, I would seek out others in this range before plunking down for this model.

[[ASIN:B007P4YAPK ASUS Transformer TF300 T-B1-BL 10.1-Inch 32 GB Tablet (Blue)]]

3rd UPDATE NOV 15 (system keeps rebooting)
-------------
After the 2nd time at the service center, the touch screen was replaced. When we received the tablet back the touch screen worked perfectly. HOWEVER, the tablet now continuously reboots itself. We can't even go 5 minutes without it rebooting. Even when we're not touching or using the tablet I noticed it just reboots itself. After 3+ of purchasing this tablet we still have not been able to use it and I'm assuming customer support will tell me to send the tablet back to the service center for a 3rd time. Don't they test their products before selling them to the public. Any confidence in Asus products has gone out the window and I would never purchase anything of there's in the future and i would recommend for anyone to stay away!

2nd UPDATE OCT 25 (touch screen still does not work after being serviced)
-------------
After contacting support, I was told to create an RMA and ship the tablet to one of the service centers. After a couple of week I received the tablet back, when I turned on the tablet the initial screen worked and and i set it down. When I came back and had to swipe the lock, ONCE AGAIN THERE WAS NO RESPONSE FROM THE TOUCH SCREEN and I CANNOT DO ANYTHING WITH THE TABLET.

What was the use of spending my money to ship the tablet to the service center and they can't even fix the issue! Once again I'd recommend NOT purchasing this product, even when you ship it back to get repaired they send it back with the same issues.

------------------------------
FIRST COMMENT (touch screen does not work)
Bought this tablet a month and a half ago. Without even installing any apps the system started constantly freezing. Its completely useless when everytime I try to browse or open gmail the system freezes. Rebooting and cold rebooting doesn't help.

Then 2 weeks after amazons 30 day return policy, the touch screen completely stopped working.
I tried to reboot, cold reboot, wipe data and now all i get is the startup screen when you boot up the tablet for the very first time and because the touch screen does not work I can't get past the initial page.

When the tablet is working, it's great!! But needless to say as much as I do not want apple products, maybe I should have gone with an ipad. As much as Asus is still probably trying to work things out with their technology, my suggestion to you is to stay away from Asus tablets. More of a waste of time trying to get repaired and probably a complete waste of $300.

title: Great Concept But Slightly Bulky and Unreliable Dock Connectivity
text:
Update - 4/16/14: Star rating unchanged.
I was experiencing erratic usage times as the "Sleep" mode was consuming more battery than it should. It was almost the same as the leaving it on - it would run down in a few hours. I tried to use the "Hibernate" mode, but no option was available in the power options nor was I able to enable it using Microsoft's instructions. I decided to create a shortcut and have been using it to sustain my battery life. The "Hibernate" start-up times are very similar to "Sleep" mode and battery life is the same as where I left it when hibernating.

Right click on a blank area on the desktop, Select 'New -> Shortcut', type 'shutdown.exe /h' in the 'Type the location of the item:' text-box. Click 'Next', Type a name for the shortcut and click 'Finish'. Find the shortcut on the desktop and click 'Properties' to set a 'Shortcut key' or to 'Change Icon' There are great icons available for free on the web to fit in with the WIN 8 schemes. You can add the shortcut to your Metro interface for a one-touch Hibernate!

*~*~*~*

The T100 is a great little Windows 8 transformer laptop/tablet with a few flaws. It fills in the void for those who need a reliable keyboard laptop but yearn for a tablet.

The T100 is equipped with a new generation Intel Atom Quad Core Processor with 2 GB of DDR3 RAM and a 64GB SSD. The sum of this configuration greatly aids the T100 to deal effectively and efficiently with Windows 8 and its intensive graphic and touch features. My T100 operates just as well on Win8 as my Retina iPad does on iOS7!

The T100 has a bright, clear 10.1" 1366 x 768 HD IPS multi-touch display. The touch function coupled with the snappy hardware delivers. There is barely any lag.

The tablet docks into the keyboard which houses a full size USB 3.0 port. The tablet has a micro-USB port which is the charging port but can also be used as a regular micro-USB port. It is also equipped with a micro-HDMI port, a micro-SD card slot and a 3.5mm headphone jack.

The T100 is primarily constructed of plastic composite and glass. It weighs 2.46 lbs - 1.26 lbs for the tablet and 1.2 lbs for the keyboard. The keyboard does seem a little heavier than it should be, especially since it does not house any batteries. The top of the keyboard including the wrist-rest and touch-pad areas could be aluminium and might explain the weight. The back of the tablet is smooth plastic while the back of the keyboard is rubberized.

The keyboard is smaller and in proportion to the size of the laptop. The keys are a little smaller but just as functional as any regular laptop. The keys do not feel like an add-on peripheral, they feel more like a built-in laptop keyboard.

The primary issues I have had with the laptop:
1. The laptop is charged through the micro-USB port. This would not have necessarily been an issue but for the fact that, unlike conventional laptops, the T100 needs to acquire some (~10%) charge before it starts and is usable.
2. The battery has been of a little concern. Starting with a 100% charge, the behavior has been inconsistent. At times, it will hold its charge in standby for 4-5 days with very little decay. Other days, it will be discharge in standby mode within a day. I have been playing around with settings in Win8 as it seems that the batteries have the potential to hold a charge for a long duration.
3. The dock connection is a little flimsy. Even after the tablet has clicked into place, closing it over the keyboard seems to press against the dock release button and causes it to slip out of the dock. 9 out of 10 times I will pull it out of my case and the tablet would have partially slipped out of the dock.
4. Though this might be more an Win8 issue, the touchpad seems to, at times, have a mind of its own.

Bonus Features:
1. Microsoft Office 2013 Home/Student included - this is a very valued bonus.
2. Unlimited ASUS cloud storage for 1 year.

A definite Recommend.

Pros:
* Good convertible laptop/tablet
* Bright, clear 10.1" 1366 x 768 HD IPS multi-touch display
* Great hardware: New generation Intel Atom Quad Core Processor with 2 GB of DDR3 RAM and a 64GB SSD
* Valuable ports: MicroSD, Micro HDMI & Micro USB
* Well built keyboard
* USB 3.0 port on keyboard
* Up to 11 hrs battery life
* Microsoft Office 2013 Home/Student included

Cons:
* Unlike conventional laptops, the T100 needs to acquire some (~10%) charge before it starts and is usable
* Keyboard is not backlit
* Dock is a little flimsy, the dock release button seems to get activated when the tablet is closed over the keyboard
* The dock design adds bulk to the laptop and is un-elegant

title: Easy to install and works great!
text:
I have a '97 wrangler and like others before me, it's just hard to get a good ground plane with a 5/8 antenna. I tried mounting my 2m amateur radio antenna behind the spare tire with a mount and grounding strap but SWR was over 3, so obviously that wouldn't work. Tried other locations as well and couldn't get a good SWR reading. So I bought this as a last resort. Installation was a breeze and build quality is great. I wanted to try it out without installing a grounding strap to see where it stands. My SWR was better (just below 2.5) but still not where I would like it. Then I added a 1 inch thick grounding strap that ran under the rear window and bonded to the inside of the cab (sanded paint off first in the cab). After making the metal to metal connection and screwing the strap to the inside of the cab, my SWR was now 1.5:1.

This is an excellent mount and easy to install. I hear some people get a good SWR with no grounding strap needed, but I did need to run one and once I did, it worked great.

title: A nice improvement over the original CotourRoam
text: I had purchased the original ContourRoam camera about a week before they announced this one. Luckily I had saved my packaging so I returned it and bought the ContourRoam2. There are some small but very worthwhile changes to this camera that make it a better choice. First, of course, is the 60 fps video option. I haven't had a chance to test that yet but it's a nice addition and the main reason I went with the 2. Next, there is a locking button on the recording slider. This is useful to avoid either accidental starts or stops, as it locks in both positions. The printed numbers on the lens barrel are clearer, brighter, and far easier to see. The card formatting is now done by pushing and holding a small button. In the previous model you had to use the supplied tool or a paper clip and stick it into a hole to format the card. The new ContourRoam 2 also came with a nifty little cloth bag that has an attached lens cloth and a small pocket to hold the included memory micro SD card and micro SD to SD adapter. All-in-all a few small improvements that make a great little video camera even better!

title: This tiny remote works flawlessly
text:
I was searching for a wireless shutter release remote for my Nikon D7100 and I came across FotoTech FTML-L3 remote.
I was not sure if I wanted to but a wired remote or wireless remote but after going through several reviews, I realized what I needed. I generally go with OEM's for my purchases but with so many reviews and such low price, it was worth giving a try.

The remote was delivered within time and when I opened the package, I was surprised to see the size of the remote. It was really tiny and super light weight and convenient. The package did not arrived with instructions but honestly, you do not not need any instruction to operate this remote. I have read many people complaining about the remote not working but I think unless they got got a lemon, it is the camera setting.

After I turned on the setting on my camera, it worked flawlessly. I am happy with this purchase and I am hoping that the battery doesn't run out of juice soon. I haven't had chance to use it much but I am certain that I will it use it every time I mount my camera on the tripod.

Likes -

1. Tiny size and fits any pocket
2. Good response time
3. Good range
4. Good build quality

Dislikes -
1. A power sliding switch would have been a plus to protect battery
2. The cover that came with remote could have been of better quality
3. "For Nikon" font size could have been small. The current font size gives a cheap look

I would certainly recommend this over the OEM if you want to save some money (I haven't used the OEM, but I am sure that this will solve the purpose at half the price of OEM).

title: Can Find No Fault With This Backpack
text:
Though I am giving a review for this backpack, I can't come from the perspective of having used it for a while. I only received my Targus backpack yesterday, but from the looks of it I am pretty darn sure this backpack will last a long, long time. I've used MANY backpacks in the past carrying books, laptops and supplies during the time it took to earn two separate college degrees, and at my previous job of 17 years. I had to carry tools, manuals, laptops and assorted parts to calibrate monitoring equipment around my state. I was rough on the backpacks and some wore out.

I really wish I had had a backpack like this one. It's very well constructed out of strong materials, has a plethora of pockets and places to organize your stuff, and though I don't have a 17" notebook as of yet, it appears to be deep and wide and should easily fit one. There are even slots for file folders and inside zipper pouches. There are pockets on the inside and pockets on the outside. The bottom inside has a foam rubber "shock pad" that neatly folds down flat on the bottom of the backpack and is about 1/2" thick. Plus the bottom is covered in a waterproof rubbery material that should definitely help keep water from seeping up into the bag. That happened to me several times on my job with my other backpacks and it was really frustrating. It's very easy to set your backpack down on the ground not realizing the area is wet.

The shoulder straps are padded and adjustable, and it has a waist strap for extra stability. Even if you didn't use this backpack to tote your 17" marvel of technology around, it would serve well as a camper/hiker backpack. I can't wait to start using it. If something should go wrong or tear up, I will most definitely update this review telling about it, but for now I can find no fault whatsoever with it.

title: Could have been really good .. Except for defects / problems!
text: I thought for awhile that this was going to be a fine receiver. Then the volume control started shorting out to full volume at any position. It isn't just dirt or a bad solder joint. It is a very poorly designed volume control mechanism. I tried to set it at one volume and leave it, but sometimes I would be out of the room and it would come on full volume. I would have to go back and mess with the volume control again. I'm wondering if I got sold an older version of this receiver, because I thought most of the problems of past versions had be fixed / redesigned. I guess not! The attenuation doesn't work well and I'm pretty sure it's a common problem the circuit itself. I only had the thing about 5 months when the volume went bad. Eton needs to stand behind their products and fix this receiver. They know these problems exist. Edit: Update: December 2019 - The manufacturer / seller never once contacted me. Apparently they never had any desire to resolve the problem with my receiver.  I would stay far away from Eton products. Oh and I've been told that other receivers sold under different brands / names have the same volume control issues. Beware!

title: Four displays, no waiting!
text:
I purchased this card to replace a Radeon 6770 FLEX to drive four displays. The Radeon's DisplayPort connection always stopped working when the monitor attached was powered off.

The good news is that the DisplayPort connection powers back up on this card when the attached monitor is powered on. All four displays (DisplayPort, DVI-D, DVI-I, and HDMI) work simultaneously in Windows.

The bad news is that the POST screen (anything before the Starting Windows logo) only goes to the DVI-I port on boot. It's not a showstopper, but it is somewhat annoying. There's no indication that nVidia or eVGA plan to address this issue with a BIOS update.

title: Cure that "LED envy". Fix that dim picture!
text:
Appears to be genuine as claimed. Identical right down to the packaging when compared to the bulb I bought directly from Mitsubishi 4 years ago. (I kept the old housing and box.)
Wow! What a difference a new bulb makes.
For the last 6 months it seemed the picture was a little dimmer than normal. After seeing a friend's new 75" Samsung LED, I was quite envious of their bright, colorful picture. I guess I forgot what a nice picture looked like. I came home, and tried changing my energy setting to bright. Although that made an obvious improvement, it still was nowhere near the quality I was hoping for. I figured it was time for a new bulb. After replacing it, I once again am impressed with the picture on my "antiquated" DLP. Yeah, I guess it was a lot more than a little dim.
It has completely cured my "LED envy".
In hindsight, it seems sort of silly that given the investment I have in my home theater, I would struggle along watching such a dim, inferior picture that could have been fixed for a relatively small sum and a few minutes work.

title: Very low quality
text:
I decided to take a chance on this kit since reviews for other products from this manufacturer claimed the muslin backdrops were better than most in the price range, here are my findings...

1) Light bulbs: Provide a decent quality of light for the price but are somewhat lacking in power, you have to have the umbrella within a few inches of the subject to get enough light. They would make decent hair lights if used on boom stands to cut down shadows behind the subject but are not viable as primary lights.

2) Light fixtures: 99.8% plastic (part of the screw is metal... only part mind you), that said only time would tell if they hold up but this kit is going back but I would be willing to bet the tightening screws on this fixture would strip in short order anyway.

3) Umbrellas: Appear fair for the price out of the box, however I am a little concerned that the label tag stitched in and the manufacturer logo embossed on one section would cause shadows if used with a brighter bulb and the included bulb is too weak to penetrate the umbrella very well.

4) Light stands: These are the kits shining glory and the reason this kit is getting two stars and not just one; The light stands are sturdy and well built but still very light and easy to carry.

5) Back drop stand: Poor at best, very weak, top section of telescoping pole is about as thick as my thumb and bows toward the weight of the backdrop.

6) Muslin: The Green Screen muslin was so bad I did not even bother to open the white and black ones... The muslin alone is so thin I could see wall in relatively dark room through it and the wall was about 3 feet away; the included "protector" that is meant to also help reflect light back is a joke... If you ever bought a device with an LCD screen and said screen had a thin white cloth like protector on it that was somewhat akin to a piece of cheesecloth than you will know exactly what this alleged protector looks like excepting for the fact that it is green.

Final verdict: If it was under $50 I would keep this kit for a light weight emergency backdrop stand since it doesn't take up much space and the light stands are fairly good but the rest of the parts are junk and would only be a waste of space. All in all kit is going from unpacking to repacking for return in just 4 hours as it is far too low quality overall for the price.

title: This is NOT broadcast quality - not even close!
text: So my corporate masters decided to cheap out & make an edit bay out of an iMac. It's fast enough but there are no card slots. As a result we had to wait until there was a Thunderbold-connected breakout box. We have the Blackmagic one. I'm not reviewing that here. The monitor SUCKS. The blacks are completely blue. Skin tone is purple. There are zero controls on the monitor and the preferences control panel offers NOTHING to help warm the color up. The luminance is just barely acceptable. The blacks are crushed, which would be fine if this was a TV set. It isn't. When no signal goes through the monitor it's supposed to display black. There is a preposterous amount of light leak, from all four sides, so that you get a blue-grey cloud where you should see black. There's also a dead pixel smack-dab in the middle of the monitor. There's also a sync delay. This is not surprising, but you can't fix it, even though there is a control for it in the preferences. If you're trying to figure out what your project will look like on TV do yourself a favor: get a different monitor.

title: Additional Information
text:
I purchased four(4) of these Acer #VM4620G-Ui5333X PC's for my small business (my first Acer PC's). The Acer website had only basic information about this system. Here is some additional information which may be helpful to prospective buyers:

The I/O bar across the top of the chassis includes:
- 2x USB 2.0 ports
- microphone input
- headphone output

The back of the chassis includes the following connectors:
- PS/2 mouse (not used by included mouse)
- PS/2 keyboard (not used by included keyboard)
- DVI-I (analog and digital) (single link) for display
- 2x Display Port
- 2x USB 3.0
- 4x USB 2.0 (in addition to those on top of chassis)
- Ethernet
- RS-232 serial port (9D)
- microphone input
- 2x audio outputs (type unknown)
- optional knockout for 9D connector
- optional knockout for 25D connector

Expansion Slots are:
- 1x PCI
- 1x PCI Express x1
- 2x PCI Express x16 (one more than indicated on the website)

Miscellaneous items include:
- Power cord, USB mouse, USB keyboard.
- DVI to VGA adapter (a nice touch).

Not included:
- Any software DVD's or documentation.
- Any cables other than the power cord.

The system powers up directly to Windows 7 Professional. The startup wizard allows installation of a variety of software utilities, including "Windows XP Mode" (for compatibility with older programs) if desired. This PC is very quiet and well built. The chassis cover attachment system is the best I have ever seen. Has nice chassis intrusion detection capability. These PC's are a bit more expensive than lower end PC's, but the included 3 year warranty indicates to me that Acer has more confidence in the motherboard and power supply durability than for their 1 year warranty machines, which appeals to me greatly. All in all these machines appear to perform very well, are very quiet, have just about every I/O port you could want, come with a 3 year warranty, and are very reasonably priced.

title: Neat addition to any garmin GPS
text:
I got this along with my gpsmap 62sc, and I'll say it has made my hiking experience very interesting. Pairing it with the GPS unit is very easy... so easy that it's not even really documented in the manual. For the gpsmap 62sc, you go to the menu, then to ADT settings, and select "search" or "find" or something, then put the battery in the tempe. It's a little bit slow with the uptake sometimes, but I suppose that's to be expected. The range seems to be pretty decent, about 15ft line of sight. The clipping system is very secure, I don't worry at all about having it knocked off something.

My first inclination was to clip it to a belt loop, but I realized that between my body heat and my shirt covering it it would get a skewed reading. I now clip it to the back of my pack when I take my pack, and to my the crossing laces in the middle of my shoe when I don't have my pack. My pack is black, though, as is the tempe, so when I'm hiking in the sun, even if it's 30 degrees out, it would report as 50F or higher. Finding a place to put it that was both out of the sunlight and not right up against my body is something I have not yet been able to do.

title: Satisfaction Guaranteed.
text:
I didn't buy this card on Amazon, I bought it at a local computer store. I came from an AMD 7970. WOW what a difference. That card was horrible. I built a budget gaming PC last year and that card was $450 and I thought I was getting exactly what I needed...I was sooo wrong. AMD is notorious for bad drivers, micro stuttering, etc... I had all of these issues from the moment I took it out of the box. I finally decided to build a new PC this year with no budget and after many hours of careful review, I decided on the GTX780. I am SO happy with my choice. I have never had one issue with this card, EVER. It plays every game I own, (and I've got about 30 or 40 now) on the highest settings without a single stutter or glitch. I also got a Shield a few days later and laying in bed playing any PC game I want is freeking awesome. What IS really, really stupid though is I unwittingly bought this card 1.5 months before the $150 price drop...and you know what? I don't even care. I just got done walking around in Skyrim, and even though I've logged over 120+ hrs using the horrible AMD card, it all seems new to me. I swear it's like putting glasses on for the first time. Everything is crystal clear and buttery smooth @ 1080p, ultra settings. With the 7970, I had to launch Skyrim in windowed mode and then use a program called simple borderless window? along with SKSE just to make it where the whole game wouldn't have stutters in it! And I put up with stuff like that for over a year! I hate AMD now and I don't care if they come out with something that is 4x the Titan for $99...I will NEVER be tricked by AMD ever again. Nvidia is hands down the graphics card leader and I am so happy that I bought this little beast of a card...even if I took a $150 hit right on the nose. Bottom line...if you're here trying to decide whether to get this card or the new r9 blabbidy-blah mirage that AMD has come up with, get THIS and it will work flawlessly right out of the box.

PS, I took a look at some of the reviews for the new AMD card and guess what? Driver issues!!! Hahaha!

title: Onkyo TX-8050..."Check spk wire"...
text:
WARNING: This is NOT a positive review of the Onkyo TX-8050 - so if you do not care to learn from my experience..."be happy and move along..."

I pride myself in doing a lot of research when buying electronics (and many other things) - I do research for a living, I'm an analyst.

So - I saw the overwhelming number of positive reviews on this Onkyo TX-8050 here at Amazon - no reason not to believe my fellow reviewers, I'm absolutely sure that they are happy enjoying their units - I just want to talk about mine and what seems to be a common problem with these units. I did not only read the reviews in Amazon - I went further, deeper and read everything the Internet brought back to me via the search engines - everything seemed to indicate that this was an awesome unit - again, I'm pretty sure the ones that work are great - unfortunately, that is not my case, I probably did a few mistakes starting with buying a "used-very good" unit from the Amazon "warehouse deals" (which I bought from in the past with no problems) - is one of those things that nagged me at the back of my mind: "wow, this deal seems too good to be true!" - I should've pay attention.

I always wanted a receiver that could play Pandora and Internet radio stations - I had a work-around through my Airport Express set up that I had hooked up to my "mini" system (Pro-ject boxes), enjoying the sound through my Martin Logans "Purity" speakers (which by the way, are awesome!) - through my set-up I had to: have my Mac on, using the "Airfoil" program, and streaming it to my living-room so I could enjoy my music through my "big" speakers - the set-up worked great, but I had to have a few things on working at the same time and I decided to minimize the equation by getting a receiver like the Onkyo TX-8050 - just one piece of equipment, "talking" to my wi-fi (which is always, securely, on.)

Mind you - this was meant to be my Christmas present to myself! :-) I worked very hard all year long and I believed I deserved a little something! :-)

I was very excited, I even downloaded the user's manual before the unit got to my place - I read everything the night before, I felt like a little kid on Christmas day!

The unit arrived - I took time off work and rushed home to unpack and hook the unit to my set up - I un-hooked my Pro-ject boxes and gently set them aside (after many years of faithful service!) and I hooked everything up according to the instructions (followed to the "t") - everything looked awesome, everything was just right, then...I pressed the "on" button and then disaster struck...I heard a click and a brief message flashed on the display: "Check spk wire" I tried it again with the same results - I unhooked everything then referred to the manual, followed everything and all I was getting was the same "Check spk wire" flash-message and the unit would turn off automatically. I was "beyond believe" that my unit would not work - did I do anything wrong? I retraced everything, and no, I did not, I followed the instructions to the letter, yet the unit would not work. I called Onkyo's support line...I got an automatic reply telling me something along the lines of: "...we are experiencing a "high" call volume, your approximate wait time will be 21 minutes..." followed by some annoying "wait" music...so, I waited, and waited...28 and a half minutes later I get...guess what? voice mail!..."Please, leave your name and number and nature of you problem and someone will get back in touch with you...." talk about adding insult to injury here!!! Onkyo I hope you're reading this (but then again you don't care, which is obvious!) - you dropped the ball fathoms into the depths of incompetence!

So, what to do with this unit? I didn't give up - I still had hope...maybe there's a "reset" button and once I press it, everything will be all-right - nope, no reset button...maybe if I unplug it and wait an hour and plug it back in, it'll fire up and I'll be enjoying all my Pandora stations in no time! - nope - didn't happen, and it didn't happen after leaving it all night unplugged and plugging it back up first thing in the morning - this thing was absolutely and irrevocably Dead on Arrival (DOA!) While I was doing all this "waiting for a miracle" I continued to do my research... I went into a few search engines and wrote: "Onkyo TX-8050 Check spk wire" - lo and behold there was a lot of information available - many angry customers (understandably enough!) ...and get this, not only with the TX-8050 units but other Onkyo models too!...ay caramba!

It even gets worse...since Onkyo's telephone support was abysmal...I still held hope that some competent, caring technician would answer an email I sent them through their portal online, do you think it worked? I have contacted many "support" departments for a diverse number situations over the past 10-12 years - it's standard practice for any business that I dealt with (and currently dealing with) to get an "automated" response..."someone will be in touch with you within 24-48 hours" or at least a small acknowledgment (...yeah, we hear you...) didi I get that from Onkyo? if you guessed NO, you're right! It took them 3 days to get back to me - by which time I already had the unit packed and ready to be sent back to Amazon - their email?...."oh, yeah someone will get back in touch with you..." is this the best that Onkyo can do for customer service?

CONCLUSION:

1 - Amazon return procedures - I rate at a definite 5 stars - nice and easy and my refund is being processed - I'm happy about that! :-)
2 - Amazon "quality control" on used items - ZERO stars - shame on you for selling defective equipment!
3 - Onkyo (overall) - based on my experience - Negative -5 stars - your telephone wait time: RIDICULOUS! your email response: PATHETIC! Onkyo's "caring" of their customers: NON-EXISTING!
4 - Will I ever buy Onkyo again? NEVER!
5- Will I ever use Amazon "warehouse deals"? Maybe... for smaller things.
6 - What did I finally get? a Denon AVR-1613 - surprise...it worked straight out of the box - I highly recommend this unit! Their customer service? I called their 800 number and I actually talked to a human being in less than 5 minutes - go figure!

The Alan Parson's Project, Supertramp, ELO, The Eagles, Pink Floyd, Stevie Nicks, Blondie, Bon Jovie, Def Leppard, Scorpions, Joni Mitchell, Abba, Neil Young, Eric Clapton, 10000 Maniacs....... many more artists.
