title: The only affordable pci wireless AC adapter for desktops
text:
Update after owning this for a few years:

This thing is a pain:
* When I wake my computer from sleep, more often than not it comes up with no internet. After fussing with that for a year I finally found a fix.. but now it has the same problem when I wake using Wake on LAN. Forums are full of people with similar problems.
* The bluetooth stops working every few months with an error in the device manager. I can fix it if I unplug it, power things off, remove and reinstall drivers, etc. - royal pain.
=======================================
Original Review:
This is the first wireless AC card I've seen for desktops that isn't ~$100.

Works great! Antenna has a much higher gain than the one I was using (according to inSSIDer). The cable is only 4 feet long, but it gets it out from under my desk. Speedtest blows away my old N card.

Only issue I had was that the pin orientation on the bluetooth cable is labeled backwards. I flipped it over and bluetooth worked.

title: Awesome Product.  Honestly surprising you can get them at this price.
text:
First of all, I have never had any metal-case Netgear switches fail. Ever. I and my businesses have had probably 100 all together and they all either still work or worked when taken out of service. This is my first GS108T, however.

Excellent managed switch for the price. Does everything you'd expect (I just needed VLAN support) and, in my case, more. You can power the switch with PoE, which I think is probably implied or stated in the description but I did not see that.

I have had trouble using the power port for data, too, so I just don't. The problem is probably not the switche's fault, since I have a kind of BS PoE injector, rather than a real PoE switch. It is hooked up directly to the PoE injector already in the closet with no data line connected and that works fine. It's worth it to me to use it that way, though, as saving space on the adapter is worth sacrificing a port.

Note: It seems you cannot (or at least cannot easily) manage this switch via HTTPS.

title: REALLY GREAT DESKTOP!!
text:
There are many reviews from buyers who are only rating the operating system (Windows 8) and not the actual computer. For people who are looking for a review of the actual PC (not just the OS), you should be pleased to know that this computer is GREAT!

I originally purchased this computer on black friday for $379, and with all the features the computer comes with, especially the HDD and RAM space, it was a steal.

After many weeks of using this computer, I am more than pleased with its performance. I gave it 5 stars simply because this computer will not disappoint. Here are the aspects that I really like about this computer.

== PROS ==

(1) REALLY FAST START UP: After the first time turning it on, it quickly went through the start up process in which it booted windows and took my info. Very easy process. There are many unnecessary programs that come pre installed with any new PC, so after uninstalling all of the trial apps that came pre loaded with the unit, the computer literally starts up in seconds!

(2) ITS QUIET: You can barely hear the computer when its on, there is no noise from the fan that I can hear. You may even forget its on - thats how quiet it is. Its great if you need to turn on the computer without waking anyone.

(3) THE SPECS: Like I said before, for the price I paid for the unit ($379), 1 TB hard drive space plus 6GB of RAM is a steal. This unit also has WIFI, so I have it connected to all of my devices on our home network, it even connects to the printer wirelessly.

(4) FAST: Did I mention its fast? With all the RAM space, running apps to surfing the web to playing music and watching videos, everything is done with top notch speed.

(5) COMPATIBILITY: Almost every program that worked on previous versions of Windows should work like a charm on Windows 8

(6) MULTIPLE PORTS: There are multiple USB 2.0 ports in the front of the PC, and two USB 3.0 ports in the back of the unit. I also have the [[ASIN:B002HWRZ2K Logitech Z313 Speaker System]] attached to the audio port in the back which also works flawlessly

== CONS ==

There arent many faults about this computer! The only fault I saw is the removal of the "start button" in the Windows 8 operating system.

(1) NO "START" BUTTON: This is a setback i've seen in many reviews of Windows 8, but there is a solution to this "problem." If you dont like the new start menu in Windows 8, you can download a free app which restores the start button that we all know and love! I have been using it since purchasing this PC, and it works like a charm! The app is called "StartMenu8" (iobit[dot]com/iobitstartmenu8[dot]php) which is produced by a company called "IOBIT." This app is really useful to anyone who wants the functionality of the old Start Button in Windows, it really works! It essentially brings back the taskbar to the way it looks in Windows 7!

== REVIEW ==

I had to write a review for this PC because I saw too many were reviewing only one aspect of the unit (the operating system), but that doesnt do this computer any justice! I love this desktop and I hope you buy it too. I bought it when it had no reviews and I'm glad I did. The price for this unit has increased since the time that I purchased it, but for what its worth, its a great PC. If you do not like the way the new Windows 8 looks with the removal of the Start Button, there are alternatives to bringing it back, as mentioned in my review! So overall, this is a great PC, if you are on the edge in deciding, JUST BUY IT, you will not regret it!

title: I really wanted this Bluray player to work for me but ....
text:
Saw a boat-load of these on sale at Costco today and couldn't help myself. I bought it and as the headline says I thought this would be the most convenient disc/smart TV setup for our bedroom but alas it would not recognize my network automatically. It would see all my neighbor's wireless networks but it would not see mine. Ah, you say, but you can manually setup the network connection. Yup, I tried that too. I connected in an on-line chat with a Sony support center where I was put on to wireless connection support how-to pages that referred to instructions that were written for software versions previous to the software version loaded to the bluray player I had bought. Then it was on the phone with the support center by voice and their instructions sent me back through setup instructions I had already tried. Then they suggested I re-setup my network that supports Apple, Windows PC, and mobile devices alike to change it to accommodate the Sony Bluray player. At that point, I stated to the phone rep that I expected the Sony player to see and recognize my wireless network automatically like all the other wireless internet capable devices in my home. So, we parted ways and the Sony is going back to Costco tomorrow.

I'm not mad. I'm disappointed and sad. I wanted to play DVDs and Blurays. I wanted to stream content off the internet sites like Netflix and Hulu and also Amazon Prime among others just like my Roku XD. Having both abilities in the same appliance sounded like a sweet deal and from the reviews of similar Sony wireless capable Bluray players I thought it would be the best one for my needs. The ability of the Sony to access Amazon Prime was the clincher because so many of the other brands didn't have that ability. But...no.

title: Best router I have ever worked with
text:
I don't typically get excited about network hardware. Who does? As long as it doesn't drop connection and gives your reasonable sustained speed with no lag, life is good.

Then I saw this product. I have a Linksys E4200v1 that I purchased about a year ago back when it came out and everyone thought it was the end-all-be-all of routers, but this leaves that one (and, I'm going to assume, the E4200v2) in the dust!

Long story short, an associate of mine was paying for 3 separate internet lines for his home, rental home and their small business across the street. All are close, and so I began looking for network hardware that might reach all three reasonably and reliably. This router not only does the job, but does in remarkably well and very reliably!

Let's start with the unboxing:

While it is superficial, you will never have a more visually attractive router. It looks great and it is heaviest home router I've held! It has a great aluminum heat sink setup to keep it cool.

On the performance side, while I haven't tried to "benchmark" it at long range (the furthest computer is probably a linear 160 feet away with several walls in between), I can tell you that I get 2-3 bars of service with no disconnections at that distance. It is the least used computer of the bunch, if it needed to be closer it could certainly be moved, but it works where it is at. Every other computer in range (all running on the 2.4 GHz network) connect flawlessly, and there are 7 of them. The router setup is straightforward, as it auto detects your internet configuration and you are up and running in very little time. Network interface is very robust and overall I like it a lot. Best part: well placed, this has consolidated 3 bills into 1 and has provided centralized network storage and access for all involved. And, thanks to the integrated USB ports, network storage amounts to simply slapping a USB drive in to it, no NAS to deal with separately (unless you need terabyte-level storage).

It is a well made, with excellent reliability. You just can't find this kind of range with lag-free performance from any other product.

title: Gorgeous! But beware of glare and dark scenes!
text:
Full disclosure - I prefer Samsung products. All my previous LEDs and LCDs have been Samsung.

But I decided to pull the trigger on the beast for the price, 4 HDMI outputs, the reviews, and the 6 included glasses.

And now I'm a very happy customer.

Out of the box, it is easy to set up. Had the whole shindig up and running within 15 minutes.

An ethernet cable can be inserted (or wireless if you prefer) in the back - it runs well with the browser. However, perhaps it's due to the single core nature of the beast, but it occasionally lags when it goes to the menu options or through the internet. Perhaps the dual core model will beef it up. In any case, that's not why I bought the TV.

The 3D is simply amazing - while the 2D to 3D conversion isn't perfect - it gets the job done for the most part. Very cool feature. ESPN 3D here we come! Movies in 3D look great. However ...

It's time to end with the reason I could only give it 4 stars. You will definitely need to configure your settings to ensure a better picture. Due to the size and the screen, there is definitely some glare so beware - depending on the scene or the lighting in your room, you can see your reflection. Furthermore, with dark scenes, it is hard to resolve the images - so that can be annoying. So get ready to tamper with the settings depending on what you are watching.

All in all - I'm happy with the product and glad I pulled the trigger!

title: BEST SECURITY SYSTEM PERIOD!

title: Great Picture. Battery Pack. Portable.Tips n Tricks here.
text:
I just bought two of these Digital Prism ATSC-710 7" Portable Handheld LCD TV with Built in ATSC/NTSC Tuner (Black)
About ten days ago they were listed at $36.xx. With shipping they came to just under $50 each.
I have been looking for a smaller portable TV since my good old Casio handheld was relegated to paper weight status with the digital change over. I selected this brand for the price and the fact it has a rechargeble (on board) battery pack.
Cosmetically, this is a very nice looking unit.
The picture, when you can get a signal, is spectacular.
I had no illusions that reception with a small aerial is spotty at best. Movement of any kind is fatal to receiving the digital signals. Those that complain simply don't get it.
The main purpose I purchased these were for emergency/storm/power outage reasons. Here are a couple of work arounds to getting a good signal.
Using the supplied antennae or another larger antennae run the set up search for channels. Get the channels you desire locked into the data base. You may have to go outside. Now that the data base is set you can navigate to your preferred channel. Next time you may have to adjust the antennae or move the unit around, but if there is a signal your channel will play. I found decent reception even while in motion in a vehicle WHEN TRAVELING IN THE PROPER DIRECTION. Turn and you then have to realign the antennae. Just saying, no way around that.
Here is how I set up for at home use.
I have internet via a cable provider but a satellite for TV. I was told (?) that the cable company can only send a minimum signal. Therefore, I was receiving some of their basic cable package along with my internet signal.
Using a basic cable splitter I provided signal to both my modem and the tv. Modem still works fine and then I ran the set up on the tv. Net channels on the tv clocked in around 50. The main one's I was looking for are the locals for during storms when bad weather interferes with the satellite signal.
I went one step further. I have a small 700 watt inverter hooked to lawn tactor battery. When the power goes out, I unplug the power strip that powers the modem, tv, and wireless router and run them off the inverter.
Tv, internet during no power scenario. Overkill? Maybe. Living in north tornado alley of Iowa, (and in a mobile home to boot) I take it seriously.
I haven't tested the battery pack longevity, but the manual gives around two hours use.
As I said, the main reason I chose this unit was the price when I saw it because I wanted two. One for home and one for if I have to bug out. Btw, a vehicle power port cord is included.
Great little tv with a great picture if you have a good signal or are using cable/sat for your feed.

title: Large, great quality monitor
text: After about a month of using this monitor, I can say that this has been a great purchase.  I've been very pleased.  The 32" inch size is fantastic for my needs, which include digital photography, gaming, and general computer use.  Previously, I used a higher-end 24" monitor, and wanted a larger high quality monitor that could be calibrated for accurate color.  I had pretty much settled on one of the 30" IPS monitors...until this BenQ was recently released.  Overall, I'd say that the BenQ is a better monitor than the 30" alternatives that I've used.  The fact that it costs less is a nice bonus, as well as the 16:9 format for viewing movies (though I dislike any 16:9 for anything smaller than 27", due to being too short from top to bottom for many uses).  I'm definitely a fan of VA monitor's, preferring them over IPS.  I won't go into the technical aspects, since there are a few reviews out there that cover them.  The biggest negative I can mention is that the included cables are too short for some people at only 5' each, instead of a common 6' length.  On the other hand, BenQ decided to include cables for DisplayPort, HDMI, DVI, VGA, and audio...which is more than most manufacturers choose to do.  This monitor is also slower than those designed for high-speed gaming, but works fine for my needs and would probably be fine for most gamers who don't insist on a 144Hz low-latency monitor.  If you require accurate color, those fast monitors wouldn't be acceptable anyway.  One thing to consider is that the 2560x1440 resolution requires a more powerful graphics card compared to 1080p.  Overall, I'm very happy with this purchase.  It's a great monitor for the money, and would still be a good value at the MSRP, compared to the high-quality 27" and 30" monitors on the market.

title: Still looking for the perfect case - this is not it
text:
In my quest for the perfect case for my iPad Air, this one misses the mark. It's a mixed bag.

First I'll share what's good.

The keyboard is nice. Key size and placement are fine with an assortment of specialty keys that I don't really use. It comes with a USB charging cable. It arrived completely uncharged, which was a surprise. It fully charged in a few hours and the charge lasts for a long time. Bluetooth Sync was straightforward. Installing the iPad was easy and it seems to stay secure with just two bands (left and right in landscape mode).

The flip stand comes out of the back and stays tucked away when not in use with magnets. It provides good support for using the touch screen.

The surface feels "rubbery" but does seem to resist fingerprints.

Now the problems.

The right side attachment band covers part of the home button! Really. This makes it hard to use the home button on the iPad. There is a home button on the keyboard itself, but that's not how I'm used to doing things.

The power switch, volume buttons, and slider switch are also somewhat obstructed. Volume buttons are available on the keyboard.

The case is heavy. This is primarily due to the keyboard, which is not removable.

The case closure is via magnets that are not very strong and the case sometimes accidentally opens up.

It is not a "smart case." The iPad does not turn on and off when you open and close the case.

The sensors don't always stay lined up with the holes in the case.

Sometimes the case wakes the iPad by accident if a key is pressed while the case is closed.

My conclusion - ambivalent. I'm still looking for the perfect case

----

Update 12/20/13

I had to stop using it and I dropped the star rating from 3 to 2. I just can not stand this case any more. It is impossible to use with the keyboard folded back and the problems with button access just become too frustrating.

title: FAST FAST FAST
text:
Cox communication in San Diego (Encinitas).
Just switched to Ultimate service which promises 50Mbps.
I am now getting 56Mbps (7Mbps up) with my Moto 6120.
I had the service just below which promises 30Mbps (was getting solid 31-32MMbps).

Note that the folks at Cox seemed confused.
They insisted that I needed a technician to come on premise and install or configure
my modem (which I already owned and was already working on the Cox network).

So the tech came, did not have to do anything and the speed was the very same as before...
After over an hour of poking around and measuring all the signals, swapping my modem for their
preferred Cisco Docsis 3 modem and even replacing the inside wiring, nothing had changed (still 30Mbps).

Finally the tech left and said Cox would call back and follow up.
5Min after he's gone, my line goes dead. I reboot my modem and router (for the nth time)
and this time the service comes back at 56Mbps.....

Looks like the folks at the central may have forgotten to enable my new bandwidth or something.
Never underestimate a large organization's ability to screw things up.

Anyway, it's now blazingly fast and the modem seems solid as ever.
Note that if I were to purchase a new one today, I might consider the newer SB6021 if the price
is comparable.

title: Great Camera; Poor Customer Service
text:
I'll start out by saying that I've had this camera for almost a year now, and I love it.
I was a novice photographer and I've learned so much by using the PEN's accessible yet advanced system and have collected an amazing gallery of pro-looking photos. I have a several different lenses which have all been fantastic, and many people have commented on the quality of my photos.
That being said, I really wish that Olympus was more customer-oriented. I was given this camera by my husband as a gift and he was so proud that he spent weeks and weeks researching which of the interchangeable lens cameras was the best. It was really one of the most expensive and thoughtful gifts I have ever received. Unfortunately, about five days after using the PEN, the mode dial just popped right off! For having paid $900 for this camera, it felt like a slap in the face to my husband who had been so proud of his "quality" decision. It also felt like such an expensive machine should not have such a flimsy construction for a pretty important part.
I contacted Olympus shortly after and explained that I was disappointed in what had happened and asked them what they could do. I received a very dismissive email back from them implying that I should just deal with it as they can't control the quality of each machine and the tone was basically "s*** happens." They also said that if I wanted to send the camera in to get fixed, it would take three weeks plus shipping time for them to get it back to me. When I called I was told that no, I could not just glue the dial on myself because it would void the warranty. So my options were to part with my camera for a month to get a piece glued back on, or fix it myself and void the warranty. Wow. I was a little disappointed that they did not try to something more for us, like at least give us a discount on accessories or something - really, a little bit of compensation goes a long way.
All this being said, I do love the camera but I really feel Olympus should do a better job keeping their clients happy and loyal because with all the competition, a pretty good product can only go so far, and you only realize how important it can be when something goes wrong.
So keep this in mind when deciding to drop a large sum of money on an Olympus.

title: Very pleased with this printer
text:
This printer isn't state of the art, but it seems to compare very well with the older, more expensive Canon photo printer it replaced. When printing photos, I can't really tell the difference between the two printers, even though my older printer used more colors. Text looks pretty decent too. It's not speedy, but it's not super slow either. Perfect for the occasional home printing of just about anything. It's cheap and it's performance level seems no worse than some of the better printers from a few years ago.

I did have an issue with 4" X 6" photos having lightish backgrounds coming out with a light streak towards the right side of the photos when I first started testing the printer. The printer pauses for a second when it gets towards the end of a print and it seemed to make the first line of print a little lighter when it started back up. Setting the printer properties to spool the whole job before printing 99% solved the issue. Then, I uninstalled the software from the included disc and installed the latest drivers and the latest version of "Easy-Photo Print" from the Canon web site. The issue was 100% solved after that, with no visible streak at all. Strangely enough, the printer still pauses for a split-second towards the end of printing a photo, but it no longer effects the print quality.

I've been using the Canon printers and software for years. Here are a few helpful hints for decent photo output...

1. Try printing without manually aligning the print heads. It seems if I manually align the print heads for plain paper, photos on thicker photo paper look grainier than if I just leave the alignment at default.

2. Turn off "enable auto photo fix" in the "Easy-Photo Print" preferences. Your camera already adjusts the photo to look as good as it's going to get. More unnecessary processing is only going to make a photo look worse. Also select "quality priority" and "print with the best quality when selecting quality priority".

3. Activating "photo noise reduction, normal" seems to make photos look smoother without any negative artifacts.

4. If you select "auto on" and how much time you want the printer to wait before shutting off in the printer maintenance menu, you'll never have to worry about turning the printer on or off.

title: A new portable closed headphone enters the market!
text:
Pros: Environmentally conscious, wood housings, great isolation, removable cable, lightweight, clean sound, good instrument separation, good level of detail.
Cons: Soundstage can seem congested at times, can come off sibilant with Magni, mid-bass can come off as pushy.
Style: Full-sized, supra-aural.
Tonal Balance: Neutral with a slight warmth
Preferred Genres: Progressive rock, jazz, synth pop
Stand-Out Tracks: The Mars Volta - Cicatriz ESP, Wes Montgomery - California Dreaming, Passion Pit - Carried Away
Preferred Amp: Asgard 2
Listening Set-Up: Musicbee -> Schiit Modi -> Schiit Magni/Asgard 2

Design and Build Quality

Aesthetics
I've had a few people over my house recently where they've seen my wall of headphones and one thing that has been remarked is that the thinksound On1 look very nice. This praise has been without any attention given to the headphones on my part, these stand out on their own. I find that the On1 are eye catching headphones as well, after all there aren't many wooden portable headphones! The uniqueness of the wood will certainly draw up conversation.

Build Quality
When I first looked at the On1 I doubted their build quality, notably in the headband region. The headband is thin and looks rather cheap and fragile. I then gave a look at the documents provided to me and found a letter with some pictures. The letter seemed to indicate that they are aware that the On1 look fragile, but included were pictures of the On1 with the headband contorted in a few stressful positions with no harm done. I gave this a try and sure enough the top of the headband can take some twisting with no harm. The sides of the headbands are still made of plastic though, with metal hidden beneath that the headphone slides up and down to adjust. Adjusting the size of the headband feels sturdy, there's minor resistance so they will stay in place.

The cups are held to the headband by rigid plastic that looks very susceptible to breakage. They connect into the wooden cups which appear to be made from locally sourced lumber rather than the exotic woods that you'd find on the LCD2, for instance. The cups are finished nicely though with a chestnut stain and a minor gloss. The cups look nice, but they feel well made as well. There are no rough edges to be seen or any imperfections. The cable is removable and enters on a single side as a 3.5mm cable. The port is very slightly recessed into the cup, but looks secure.

Looking at the whole picture my only concern about the durability is the plastic that holds the cups together. One wrong foot placement and they will likely snap. Everything else is solid.

Wearing the On1
The first thing I want to note is that the On1 feel counterintuitive to me when handled. I am used to single ended cables being on the left side, rather than the right, and I am used to the headphones swivelling flatly going forward rather than backwards. The headphones come with an in-line cable though, which makes a lot of sense for the cable to be on the right since most people are right handed.

Aside from that, the On1 are actually pretty darn comfortable for supra-aural headphones. The pads are plush and rather soft with a firm clamp. I find it very easy to get a good seal with the On1, which in turn provides excellent isolation that is on par with any IEM. Leaking is kept to a very bare minimum as well, though I wouldn't use these in a public library at loud volumes. While the pads are soft, the headband unfortunately isn't. There is mild padding and the headphones are lightweight, but I feel pressure on top of my head after an hour or so. It's not painful, but certainly a reminder that I'm wearing headphones.

Sound Quality

Amping and Burn-In
I used the On1 with my Schiit Magni and Asgard 2 to compare them back and forth. Overall I feel that they can get by without an amp, but I preferred them most from my desktop set-up. I experienced no burn-in during my time with these.

Bass
On the whole I consider the On1's bass to be a bit north of neutral with good control, texture and extension. When listening to extremely bass heavy songs such as Jay-Z's Holy Grail or James Blake's Limit to Your Love I find that the sub-bass is quick, tight and add no distortion. I also find that the quantity of the sub-bass is more than acceptable to those of us who are not bassheads.. While I find the sub-bass to be quality, I find that I'm not fully satisfied when listening to bass heavy songs. I feel that the sub-bass comes off a bit thin, lacking the full weight that bass heavy songs demand. The sub-bass comes so close to having the big bass necessary to fully carry the energy of these songs that it feels a bit of a tease when all is said and done.

As for the mid-bass, I feel that it is slightly warmer than neutral with a muddiness that I find when listening to the On1 through my Asgard 2. The muddiness isn't consistent, but I find that in many less than stellar mastered albums that the mid-bass can seem congested, pushy, and muddy. The Magni seems to provide more punch and cleanness in this regard, in most cases. I feel that the On1 really shows it's capabilities when listening to classics like Pink Floyd's Money though and other classic albums with exquisite mastering and recording techniques. When listening to these recordings I feel the On1 provides a slightly warm mid-bass experience that near faithfully reproduces these frequencies. I find a slight artificial tone to these, but none more than I've heard in any other closed headphone.

TL:DR: The sub-bass extends nicely, but lacks the weight to really bring out the energy of bass heavy songs while the mid-bass can come off congested and muddy at times. The mid-bass is very dependant on the quality of the recording.

Mids/Highs
On the whole I found that the mids can come off mildly recessed depending on the source and recording, it's a fine line. I feel that the mid-bass has a tendency to fight for the spotlight with the vocals in many instances. I find that this is amplified when listening to the slightly warm Asgard 2 and that I, generally, prefer the Magni when listening to vocal recordings due to the brighter mids and highs. That isn't to say that the mids are bad though, I find that vocals are intimate with a natural tone to them while guitars are detailed and synths feel weighty. For instance, the guitars in David Bowie's Moonage Daydream roar from the intro with control and a near goosebump giving energy, while the synths of Crystal Castle's Untrust Us are appropriately thick and fill out the sound for the vocals to settle into.

The highs are well extended, but even with the Magni I find that they lack the sparkle that I love so much in headphones like the Grado SR80i or the Audio Technica Ad900. I tend to like my headphones a bit on the bright side though, and I feel that the highs are, overall, well represented. Horns and wailing guitars both sound very clean even when at their highest pitches even with the volume louder than normal. I do not find that the On1 increases any discernible sibilance or distortion throughout these frequencies, but I do find that the On1 isn't shy about showing off flaws in recordings. I don't find these to be the most detailed headphone, but they do show off a recordings imperfections in upper region distortion or sibilance throughout the mids or highs. This is heightened when listening through the Magni and kept at minimal when listening through the Asgard 2.

TL:DR: The On1 offers clean and intimate mids with clean treble extension that lacks the sparkle and energy of brighter headphones.

Presentation
I find that the soundstage, separation and imaging qualities of the On1 are slightly better than other closed headphones that I've experienced, especially when considering headphones that isolate as well as these. The On1 suffers from what most supra-aural closed headphones do, a slightly narrow soundstage. This is offset by the quality imaging from left to right, imaging depth, and instrument separation. The On1 feels layered, with room to breath, rather than wide, cozy would be a good word. I feel that the sound is front focused though, never fully enveloping me in the sound.

TL:DR: Narrow soundstage that is offset by quality imaging and instrument separation.

Conclusion

Thinksound has made somewhat of a name for itself over the past few years for being environmentally conscious as well as creating a quality product. I first fell in love with their ms-01, once calling them my favorite ~$100 IEM and now I've become a fan of their On1. The On1 are a headphone I can really put my support into not only for thinksound's excellent customer service and ideals, but because they are a beautiful headphone that not only sounds great, but will draw a lot of attention as you attempt to drown the world out.

title: Just barely fits my gaming laptop - MSI GT70 20C-065US (16.85"x11.34"x2.17")
text:
I bought this laptop because the successor (RBP-217) is a ridiculous $90 on Amazon and more elsewhere. I'm not sure if they changed anything aside from removing the flaps on the new model but if that's all they did and they're going to charge $30 more to use less material and re-label it as a new model, that's crazy.

Possible con:

It has the capability of holding many things if you're using a smallish 17.3" laptop. If you're using a gaming laptop, it does take up a little more space. With my laptop, I also carry a 1400 page (2") physics book and a 450 page (1") linear algebra book along with its 1/2" thick solutions manual and a 2" binder with 200 pieces of notebook paper. It's pretty much tapped out at this point. Since the laptop and my physics book weigh about the same, I'll sometimes opt to carry the book instead of walking around campus with 30lbs strapped to my back.

Pros:

1) Fits my MSI GT70 20C-065US (16.85"x11.34"x2.17") gaming laptop but just barely! It won't zip right up but you won't have to struggle to zip it up either. It's a slightly snug fit in there.

2) Bunches of compartments! Two tablet compartments (very front and another in the same compartment the laptop is in) that look to be able to fit ~10.1" tablets since both front and rear tablet pockets are 9" wide, a main compartment for books, binders and whatnot, two mesh pockets in the very front and main compartments, the very top compartment I use to keep my Altoids in, two side pockets I've found no use for yet and one pocket on the lumbar support is where I put tissues (because you never know when you may need them).

3) Shoulder straps are nice, thick, durable and padded well. My old one was going on two years with no noticeable wear before being stolen and I would expect the same from this one.

4) I see no use for the compression straps but I'll probably end up using it one day.

5) The whole area the laptop is housed in is padded (front, rear, bottom and even around the edges). I don't believe laptop backpacks need all too much padding. Just be gentle when you're setting it down.

All in all, it's a great backpack and seems to be rather well thought out.

title: Clearly a budget mount
text:
I ordered this mount for my 55" 75lb Bravia LCD. Had a Sanus tilting mount in my last house, for about 2x the cost. After reading all the positive reviews I thought I would try this one.

The Sanus is heavier gauge steel for the wall mount and hangars, and the hangars have crossbar reinforcements; this mount does not. I would not call this mount 100% flimsy, but is is much weaker than the Sanus. Regardless, it came with a good complement of hardware and decent simple instructions. I used the included 2" lag bolts and they worked fine. I used my own level, the built-in one matched it. If you're going to simply mount and hang, it works fine. Would not go much more weight than my 75lbs.

One precaution: The stops on each end of the wall mount don't seem effective enough to keep the hangar arms from sliding off . Plan on hanging your TV centered and don't slide to the ends without diligence. The tilt is not so smooth, but if you are going to hang and lock in place it's fine.

Finally, you'll probably use an electronic stud finder for locate your studs. But also go to Ace Hardware and get a $3.00 block magnet that you can sweep the wall with; it will pick up the drywall nail or screw and show you exactly where the center of the stud is. I was mounting on an exterior wall so the electronic finder was not precise. My magnet worked like magic.

title: Spend the extra $30 for this one
text:
The quick review:
Functions great, the multi RAID support is perfect, transfer speeds are stable, noise is very minimal, overall excellent choice for large, external storage.

Quarks: To facilitate file transfers between the Vantec external enclosure and a NAS or Windows/Mac the OS settings need to have "USB selective suspend settings" disabled otherwise programs that automate file transfers (aka, backup programs) will fail halfway through the backup job. Once that problem was remedied the external enclosure was very stable.

Some things to consider before buying: Definitely spend the extra $30+ to purchase the HX4R (NST-640S3R-BK) and not the HX4 (NST-640SU3-BK). The HX4 does not support RAID; which in my opinion is absolutely pointless to have on a 4-bay external enclosure. Without RAID support you cannot do redundancy between the drives and you cannot stripe the hard drives....it's basically just a collection of separate drives. If you're connecting this to a NAS there is a possibility that the NAS won't maintain a constant connection to the external enclosure which could cause some issues with backup jobs. From everything I've tested/seen, it's mostly in the Vantec suspending/sleeping the hard drives after a period of time. However, connected directly to Windows/Mac and with active suspend disabled, the drive functions perfectly!

Overall excellent choice for large external storage!

title: Pretty decent - could be better
text:
For starters, I do love the size and weight of this tripod. Build quality all round feels good; however a couple minor design changes could make this a much better tripod.

- Different style of quick release on the shoe. Everything is knobs on the tripod head, and this includes the part that fastens the camera to the tripod. In the dark, fumbling around with these knobs, it is easy to mistake one for another and accidentally loosen the camera, at least until you get the hang of the tripod. Seems to me a simple lever system would be just as effective at keeping it in place, and yet provide a clear distinction between all the other adjustments.

- Allan key required on the shoe. I've got another, much cheaper tripod that has a great little system where a metal bit flops down from under the shoe allowing you to easily tighten it. This particular tripod requires you to use a separate tool, which means you have to keep that in your pocket (or somewhere!). It's not that hard to build in a system that allows a good finger tight solution.

- There is a bubble level, but it is on the top most part of the head, not on the lower part. So, you've no guarantee that your tripod itself is level, but only that the camera on top is - at that particular adjustment. This does you no good if you were hoping to setup a shot where you'd pan across a valley for instance. Having a second level in the lower position would be nice.

The legs are fairly strong, though not exactly rock solid. I guess that is to be expected on a tripod of this weight. That said, on a series of long exposure night shots I noticed a huge difference when I hung a log off the bottom of the tripod using the handy built in hook for that purpose.

Watch out for sand in the leg adjusters - you can clean it out, but it is a royal pain to loosen them all off and clean them.

Overall, for the price, size and weight of this tripod I am quite happy with it. A little more thought on the design end of things and I would have given it 5 stars for sure.

title: Light Bucket 'o Fun
text:
I debated for nearly a year between getting the XT10 or the Apertura 12, honestly in the end, the site selling the Apertura 12 ended up being backordered for a few months, so the XT10 won by default. That being said, I cannot say I have been disappointed by the performance of this 10-inch mini-beast.

Being a mechanical engineer by day, and (extremely) amateur astronomer by night, I read a lot of reviews before buying this scope. First, it is big - wife-annoyingly big, unless you have direct and flat access to the outdoors, you are going to want to think about where this is going to live. If you have to haul it in and out by hand, you are not likely to use it often. The Orion XT8 and down are "man-portable", but this one has to be disassembled to move around. I got around this issue by assembling a little heavy-treaded garden wagon with a wooden deck and three holes for the turntable's feet. This gives me a very portable platform that I can store in the garage.

Second, it is a Dobsonian, which means that there is no equatorial mount to use with any of the great J2000.0 star catalogs. However, with a laptop and the software that Orion ships with the telescope, and a cheap inclinometer (which you can get from Amazon for $20) it is not excessively difficult to devise a pretty good altitude-azimuth system with this telescope.

For looking at deep-sky objects with 20mm++ lenses or <10mm lenses for objects in the solar system, this is a great telescope. It just drinks in the light. But, for finer, high magnification objects, the Dobsonian mount precludes any but the most cursory glances. Though 300x is possible (and on the moon looks pretty good) objects on the celestial sphere are really moving. The friction bearings on both axes allow the observer to use comparable force in both directions, but without a great deal of accuracy. While it can be easy to find an object in a wide field, it is tough to track in the narrow field. I will admit I tend to use this in concert with my cheaper, but easier to adjust Orion 130ST.

All-in-all, I love this telescope. Mounted on a garden wagon I can drag it out of the garage whenever the sky is clear and have an enjoyable couple of hours observing without a massive amount of setup and teardown. Even in the moderately light-polluted environment I live in, I have no difficulty finding the Messier objects. Downside - unless you have somewhere easy to store this thing, it will likely serve as an excellent dust-collector in a corner somewhere.

title: Great bookbag, big main compartment, lots of pockets
text:
I bought the larger, 17" version. The dimensions I saw when I bought it weren't right. The dimension that goes away from the back is not smaller than the stated 16" version, not that I wanted/want it to be. It's like they picked a different way of measuring it, or something.

The side compartments could be bigger, like 2" taller/up the back dimension, and 2" more outward in the across the back dimension. The mesh gets a little worn out easily. These side pockets has material on the bottom inside that help prevent items from falling out, if you forget to zip it up.

(this is ordered top to bottom, and going around outside vertically, then in)

The pocket at the very top is really nice/usable, although with a 2cm to 1in longer zipper, so that it could fit my organizer in there perfectly(it fits, just doesn't go in there easily). I can use this pocket to put in my computer mouse, etc... It's really nice, but I'm not so sure on how good this pocket would be with the smaller version of this book bag, books in the main compartment might hit it.

The main compartment is really big. It fits all my books, notebooks, binders, gym clothes, etc... Even when I feel like taking a lot of stuff with me, it'll still fit it all. It also has a mesh pocket on the other side that's away from the wearer's back. The big main pocket is the main reason I picked this book bag.

The handle looks really strong, feels better if you keep a loose grip on it rather than a tight grip. If there nothing in the book bag, it can flop down at times, getting in the way of the main zipper.

The picture looks like the top pocket is a single handle zipper, but it's really a two handle zipper, like I think it should be (<-not sure on the words to use for this, two handle, double handle, two way, etc...?), and this pocket goes all the way to the bottom. (just not the zipper part)

The pocket on the bottom front is padded on the outside and has smaller pockets inside, etc...

There's a mini pocket on the front of that pocket that's big enough to easily fit a 3"*5" note card pack, and some mechanical pencils/pens. (didn't try a non-mechanical unsharpened pencil)

The bottom is padded.

The back has a padded pocket on the bottom, good for holding snail mail letters to mail.

The middle of the back is quite a bit looser than the rest of the back and doesn't have nearly as much padding, When I'm not wearing the book bag, and go over this area with my hand an fill what fills like wrinkles in that section. The outer cushions are fairly big, and I've only felt the wrinkles in the middle area maybe one time while wearing the book bag.(could have just been my shirt?) The top back and bottom cushion are kinda fraying a little.

After using the book bag for a while, the shoulder straps, like most book bags, feels like it could need more cushioning. However, it does have this neat elasticy thing at the top that makes it feel better to catch a full book bag when taking it off, etc... The straps might be too long for a short, skinny person during the summer, and there isn't a waist, or a chest strap.

The laptop pocket has an inner pocket for smaller computers, like my 15.4" laptop. There's a Velcro strap that I'm guessing is supposed to help if the book bag ever gets flipped upside down, however the ends of the velcro don't really meet that well with my size laptop, or smaller. They could just simply make the non-strap side longer, for it to work. There's an inner pocket at the top of the laptop area, I haven't figured out any good use for it. Don't want my laptop directly hitting anything hard.

I've been in the rain with this book bag a few short times, and nothing gotten wet inside.

Overall main pros:

big main compartment
top pocket/others
looks nice, "stylish"
elasticy part on shoulder straps

Overall main cons:

back feels kind of weird?
no belt, or chest straps
might be too big for a person who's small, and/or doesn't carry much
side pockets could be bigger

Update:
The bookbag gets old like a normal bookbag:
The cover of the handle at the top cracked at it's outer edges, you can feel it when you pick up/put down the bookbag using this handle; might be more comfortable without this cover. (but I'd have to rip open the cover(which make the cover completely useless) to take it off to test)
The shoulder strap padding became ineffective, as the fabric has tears there, and the padding has stuck out instead of cushioning.
The side pockets have tears that allow items to go between the main compartment and the side compartments.
The bottom edges are cracking.

title: Only small antenna I found that receives ALL TV frequencies
text:
This antenna is small enough to be installed unobtrusively and strong enough to receive all TV stations. For me it's pulling in eveything in the Cleveland, OH area. I'm in an eastern suburb, about 25 miles from most towers. No other small antenna I tried could receive all of the hi-VHF in the area. The ANT751R pulls in all the CBS (WOIO 19) and FOX (WJW 8) channels - which everyone complains about.

This antenna really should be installed outdoors on a rooftop. However, before going to that trouble I decided to test it first by just using a couple of coat hangers to hang it in my BASEMENT and point it out a window. I connected the antenna to my old cable/antenna signal amplifier which then splits the signal to all of the RF cable outlets in my house.

To my surprise, after adjusting the direction it was pointing a few times (to fine tune it), every station in the area came in perfectly. I'm not even going to bother mounting the antenna outdoors (or in the attic, as many people do) unless reception changes once the trees are in full blossom this spring.

When setting up a TV antenna to receive the new digital broadcasts, be sure to rescan the channels on each TV after you adjust the position and direction of the antenna - and give the TV time to 'learn' the new signal. Digital signals and receivers do not work the same as the old analog equpiment - it can take a few minutes for the signal processors in the TV receiver to adjust and settle. This is important... many people return perfectly good antennas thinking they don't work because they haven't taken the time to adjust, re-scan and wait a bit. Have patience and persistence - it's worth it.

The ANT751R comes fully assembled and the elements simply unfold and lock in place. It also comes with all mounting hardware and a very nice mounting pole set-up. All you have to provide are screws to mount the base to your roof/wall/deck, etc., and the RF cable to connect it to your TV (or distribution block).

I wish I'd known 4 years ago that I could receive all of the local broadcast stations (nad sub-channels) in such high quality (HD) - for free. By bye cable... hello online streaming and FREE BROADCAST TV.

A note about TV antennas:
They are NOT all created equal. Many are designed to be effective only on UHF frequencies even though they claim to receive both VHF and UHF. That may not be a problem for most major markets since nearly all of the stations now broadcast in the UHF frequencies. Cleveland, Ohio is one of the exceptions - the CBS affiliate made a bad decision in 2009 and chose to broadcast in the hi-VHF range... which means you must have an antenna specifically capable of receiving hi-VHF frequencies. When buying an antenna, make sure you can return it if it doesn't work for you. If you're splitting the signal to more than 2 TVs - or running your cable more than 100' - you may need either an antenna pre-amp (I didn't need one) or a signal amplifier/multi-media drop amplifier (or both).

title: Original, not a clone
text:
I ordered the Openbox S10 from Amazon and the supplier was L33T Group, Inc. I think experiences may differ based on who supplies it. I've been using this receiver about a month now.

Some people are selling fake clones of this receiver so I did check it based on information on a forum. The Openbox I received is an original and not a clone. The problem with clones is that if you update the firmware or change the OS, it will brick after 10 on and off cycles (forums did have work arounds for clones though).

I am using this strictly for FTA on Hispasat 30W. I don't use any cams or cards so can't tell you anything about compatibility with them. I use a fixed offset dish so I can't comment on motor controls but the menu has everything to use a motor. The receiver did not come with Hispasat freqs preloaded. I did a blind scan and it found every free to air tv and radio channel listed on LyngSat. I was not able to get EPG (electronic program guide) to work though. I think that HispaSat may not have an EPG for the U.S. beam though.

I connected a 16 Gb USB stick and use the PVR function. It works very well. I have it setup to auto-record whatever channel I am watching so I can pause or rewind live shows and it starts recording immediately after changing channels (1 to 2 seconds).

I noticed that audio/video sync was off on most channels by about 3 seconds and was quite annoying. I updated to the latest firmware and it fixed the problem. I think there are multiple ways to upgrade but the method I used required me to download it to the USB stick. You insert the USB stick into the Openbox and go to "Upgrade by USB" in the menu. It loses all settings after upgrading but HispaSat was in the new firmware. I had to set my LNB type and scan for all the channels again. Definitely worth it though for the synchronization.

The receiver has an excellent picture. It changes channels quickly. The remote worked well for the 2 days I used it before setting up my Harmony universal remote. I have never had the Openbox lock up or reboot on me. The box is small and light. It gets pretty warm but not too excessive. My entertainment system is in a sealed closet and it hasn't overheated even with the stereo heating the closet up pretty good.

I have one issue that seems to be a compatibility issue with another device. I use a RE BL IR repeater/ IR to blue-tooth PS3 controller. If you are one of the rare people who uses one of these, you might want to know about this otherwise disregard. At a distance of over 11 ft using the RE BL and the wired emitter, the channel up and down function often outputs a number rather than channel up or down. Instead of being able to scroll through the channels you will keep ending up at the channel number that the RE BL relays to the Openbox. I have definitely confirmed the problem to be with the RE BL and not the Openbox.

Update 12/26/2015: I just wanted to mention we are still using two of these OpenBox S10s. One of them will freeze...well let me be more specific. There is a specific channel that if it is left on that channel for several hours, the box stops accepting inputs. The screen does not freeze. I still have sound and picture. It just doesn't do anything when pressing buttons on the remote or face. I have to turn it off with the switch on the back of the unit. Otherwise, that is the only problem since installing these. Definitely still satisfied and the next box that does what this box does is still double what I paid then.

title: MIXED REVIEW WITH POSITIVES & NEGATIVES
text:
PROS:

*Streaming media content is excellent. Nearly as good as a Roku. It's best feature.
*Remote is excellent, well-laid out and easy to navigate.
*Very easy to set-up/follow the well laid out prompts.
*Built-in Wi-Fi is excellent/strong signal/glitch-free streaming.
*USB ports will take on photos and 1080p AVCHD files with ease. Second best feature!

CONS:

*For $250.00, it is cheaply built.
*Design is very poor in functionality.
*Must use a remote for EVERYTHING. Everything, every function.
*Front display requires superior vision and close-up viewing only.
*Loading time is still slow despite the claims not to be.
*No on-screen initial start-up information when inserting a disc.

So I am impressed but I also dislike so much about Sony's 2012 BDPS790 Blu-Ray player. I'd still suggest against it as a purchase unless you were looking to spend $100 on a Media Streaming Device but instead wanted to add a DVD player.

I also have a 2012 Denon 1611UD Blu-Ray player deck which runs circles around the Sony. Yes, in fairness, it's $400 vs. $250 but the quality is extreme and the claims about Denon picture quality are 100% accurate. Plus it loads at least 2-3 times faster than the Sony.

As said, what makes the Sony still attractive is the fantastic Wi-Fi signal strength, the wonderful and ample streaming selections (includes Amazon PRIME and Amazon Instant) and the front and rear ports for USB that can take on just about anything you toss at it. Even those massive 1080P AVCHD files play with ease using a portable hard drive or USB stick instead of a DVD.

I need a second pair of reading glasses to read the front panel of the deck and how about a ON/OFF button, Play button, etc, etc? What Sony has provided are UNMARKED (they are only unmarked when the power is off) braile-like places on the top of the deck that you can 'FEEL' for to power up/down the unit. But you have to actually feel for it and then wait for your finger to touch the correct area. Remotes do get misplaced Sony.

So, Sony did a great job at releasing a high-end player and placing the contents/parts of that deck into the plastic case they'd use on their entry level player. There's nothing professional about this professional player.

Take a look at other decks as well before you decide/purchase the Sony (such as Panasonic or Denon instead).

I'm very picky about quality, especially for things like this and I'm very happy.

title: Solid Processor, Modest jump from Gen 3, Not for overclocking
text:
This is Intel's 4th Generation i7, the 4770 is a direct replacement of the 3770. This CPU is not meant for overclocking (does not have an unlocked multiplier), you want the [[ASIN:B00CO8TBQ0 Intel Core i7-4770K Quad-Core Desktop Processor BX80646I74770K]] for that.

That said you will need a new motherboard to upgrade from any of the earlier generation CPUs as this generation uses the 1150 socket while the other 3 used different ones. One nice thing here is aftermarket CPU coolers that fit 1155/1156 sockets will work on this CPU.

This CPU is a Quad Core, 8 thread running at 3.4GHz with boost to 3.9GHz as needed.
It is an 84 Watt CPU. The only currently available faster Intel 4th Gen CPU is the 4770K running at 3.5Ghz (and able to be overclocked thanks to the unlocked multiplier).

It comes with HD 4600 integrated graphics which is an upgrade over the HD 4000 in the 3rd Generation 3770.

Depending on what site you read for technical reviews this processor will give an improvement of 1%-20% over a 3rd generation CPU. Personally it seems about a 5%-10% increase in performance in most bench tests I have seen...

When looking at this consider some of the following things:
1) This will require a new motherboard ($100+)so budget that in
2) This does not have an unlocked multiplier, so overclocking is out.
3) With a $300+ price tag and a minimum $100 for a motherboard you will be spending at least $400+ to upgrade so even assuming the best performance increase that's $20 per % of increased performance.

If the price fits what you are looking for and you have no desire to overclock then this might be a solid choice of CPU...

I personally decided on the i7-4770K because if I ever choose to I can overclock it. I upgraded from a 3770K (not overclocked) and didn't really see any real world performance increase (Not overclocked).

I am using it in my media center PC which serves 6-8 TVs, streams music and maintains my media collection. so I am not pushing it with extreme gaming, but I do have it running without a hitch while streaming 1080p 3D movies to 6 TVs at the same time...

If you absolutely must have a 4th Gen i7 Processor and price is a major concern then this might be a good fit, but if top performance is more what you're looking for go with the 4770K... The performance bump over the 1st/2nd gen CPUs does seem worth the price.

If you are happy with your 3rd Gen i7 I would skip the upgrade since it's not that large of a performance boost overall...

title: Was: Best helmet camera  for off-road enduro motorcycles Now: Buy the TCL SVC200 instead.
text:
Previously, I wrote the below review. A lot of it was based on my first version on the camera which was a TCL SV200 bought at the end of 2012. TCL is a Chinese maker that Coleman obtained the exclusive rights to sell in the USA during 2013 2014. I lost my TCL and bought another Coleman. Unfortunately, the latest Coleman does NOT come with all the mounts that the TCL did. Particularly, it is missing the windshield suction cup mounts for running in dash cam mode.

In recording videos with my Coleman's on dirtbike rides I noticed I was running out of battery power after just an hour, where with the TCL I was getting two hours. I thought it was bad batteries, so bought a half dozen Nokia BL-5C's. Further tests show that the battery is only recording reliably for 1hr15min. I believe this is because the Coleman does not blank out the LCD screen after the video recording starts, which I think the TCL did. The other difference is that the Coelmen had different firmware. The best resolution is HD1080p60fps (I uses 1080p30fps). The TCL's best is 1080p30fps. That could affect battery life as well. For uploading to youtube, you do not need the Colemans better resolution. I now have to stop every hour and change batteries. BOTTOM LINE, Buy the TCL SVC200 as it is a better value, at least for what I do.
http://www.amazon.com/SVC200-Waterproof-Surveillance-FHD1920X1080-Accessories/dp/B00BTWAO0O/ref=cm_cr_pr_pb_t

Previous review...
I own three of these, 2 of which is costs as much as one Gopro with all the attachments . The battery lasts almost exactly 2 hours and takes 2-1/2 hours to charge. A 32GB class 10 MicroSD card will hold about 8 hours of video at 1080p 30fps or 60fps. A good card is critical to keep from getting dropouts while recording. It will also do 720p 60fps. It can take a 64GB MicroSD. Sandisk brand is recommended. I use these on my motorcycle to record our off-road trail rides. The kit comes with several mount configurations.

Even in its waterproof container, you can talk while riding and it will have very good audio. I think you would have too much wind noise if you do not use the housing, but you can mount it that way, if you wish. Some folks have heard a high pitch whine on some of the videos, but my older ears cannot hear it. The nice thing about these, is that when you are ready to ride, it will start recording, when in its waterproof case, by just sliding the yellow bar forward until it clicks. To stop recording, slide it backwards. There is a magnetic inside the slide that starts it. The LED on top will flash red when recording a video. Outside of the case, you have to first turn it on then slide the yellow slide switch forward. It takes really good snapshots outside the case. If you go to one of my youtube videos on my Channel: tele rover down at Ouray, Colorado, you'll see us look at each other as we switch the cameras on and off to save the batteries and to get a different point of view.

The view screen (not available as a standard item on GoPros) helps in orienting the camera to the horizon. Keep it in the waterproof case, as I have dropped one of these on concrete and chipped the lens. I could not find any contact to get it repaired. It was still usable (you'll see a couple of blurry spots on the lower right corner of some clips), but since I lost it on my last ride, I get to get a new one again. :o) My riding friends have all bought these now as well. It is more streamlined than a Gopro, and can be mounted on the side or top of your helmet.

I got my first one at the beginning of 2014 and recorded a 7-1/2 hour ride around Moab's White Rim Trail, of which 2 hours are on youtube. This is the same camera that was sold in the UK as a TCL SVC200, but rebranded in the USA by Coleman as a CX7WP.
It comes with a charger cables (a USB) and another USB cable for downloading.

It needs spare batteries for most of my rides, if I want to show the whole adventure. The battery that comes with it is a BL-5C 3.7V 1050ma 3.885Wh made in China. I tried buying a supposedly higher capacity battery directly from China a BL-5C 3.7V 2450mAh, but I have not seen it last any longer than the one that comes with the camera. BTW these are phone batteries for 36501100. I'll keep trying. Maybe the charger that comes with the camera does not like these other batteries. Oh, yeah. You can only charge the battery when it is in the camera using a wall adaptor. You cannot charge it using the USB port on your computer like other cameras. I find it quicker to remove the MicroSD card and put it directly in the computer USB port with adaptor to download the videos. While I am doing that I charge the battery in the camera. When I do multiple days of riding, I have to download files and recharge the batteries at the motel in the evening for the next day, so many things are going on. The LED will be red while charging and turn green when fully charged. When the battery is about to die, while recording, it makes chimes, but I never hear it with my helmet on and when its in the waterproof case. You'll hear it though when you go to edit the video.

I use sport mode where it creates individual files until the card is full, but if you set it up for auto (car) mode, in case of accidents, it will take continuous recordings and overwrite the files. In the event something happens that you need or want to save, just turn it off sometime after.

I have not immersed it in water yet (its been in rain), but that will happen soon as we do some river crossings where I'll place it in the stream to take vids of our wheels going by. I'll use a little tripod on the screw mounts.

I think you'll like it for the price. Again, check my youtube channel: Tele Rover, to see if you like the output.

title: Awesome Bluetooth speaker with many other cool features
text:
[[VIDEOID:2cd5b6f93db1af0f31fae98991f6bdf9]] The CoolStream Portable Bluetooth Speaker is great to have if you are a music lover like me.
What is in the box:
-CoolStream Portable Bluetooth Speaker
-Aux cable
-USB charging cable (round plug)
-Instruction manual
How to setup using Bluetooth (Bluetooth 2.1 + EDR):
1) Hold power button for 3 seconds to turn the speaker on
2) Press the "M" button to change the mode to Bluetooth mode
3) Find the "CoolStream BTS201"on your Bluetooth enabled device
4) Tap on it and connect to it
5) Choose a song and play it
- You can control the volume by using your device and the speakers volume control buttons
- You can pause, play and skip songs using the speakers controls
This speaker also features an aux input so you can play any device that has a headphone jack on it that is 3.5mm. It also features a USB port for playing music off a flash drive, an SD card slot for playing music off of, a microphone for taking a phone call and a built in non-removable battery that lasts up to 3-5 hours depending on how you use it. The speaker is made of plastic with metal screens covering and protecting the speakers in the front.
This speaker sounds great. It can get really loud but keep the sound quality great the same time. I do not notice any distortion when playing music over Bluetooth or aux. The sound quality is also great and clear when using it to talk on the phone.
I can use this speaker while camping out in the woods and when I am home out on the deck relaxing. This speaker is really portable.
Overall this Bluetooth speaker is outstanding in terms of sound quality, loudness and portability.

Watch my video review.

I was supplied a sample for test and evaluation, and I promised that my review is fair and honest.

I purchased this to replace my old XP laptop, primarily because XP will lose all support shortly. I chose it because of excellent expert reviews for this computer found on the Web. My remarks here are limited by my lack of personal knowledge of competing Windows 7 laptops and newer laptops in general. I was disappointed by the changed aspect ratio (greater screen width compared to the height) but I suspect that's standard in newer computers.

Since my purchase was of a used computer I was not surprised that the battery was apparently not operative. I say "apparently" as I have no interest in running the computer on battery (I use the machine as a desktop). However, the bright battery charging light was constantly flashing, and this was exceedingly annoying. I *was* surprised--unpleasantly so--to find that the battery is built into the computer. That is, removing the battery leaves a hole on the back of the computer for which no cover is available. (One must either replace the battery or leave the hole.) This affects the machine's balance and stability on the desk or table.

On the plus side, Dell offers 24/7 phone support even though I bought the computer used.

UPDATE. The good folks at Tampa-Laptops (the Amazon merchant from which I bought this product) offered to send me a replacement battery free--until they realized it was beyond the 30-day warranty period. They've persuaded me nevertheless to purchase a battery, not only for my reasons stated above but because that would stand me in good stead in a power outage. I can get it at Amazon for about $14 (with free shipping for a $35 purchase). Tampa-Laptops provides helpful technical support, but to get it you might have to bypass the phone extension for technical support and instead connect to customer service.

title: Value buy, not great quality
text:
I have been soldering up my guitar effect pedal circuit boards using a PanaVise knock-off from Harbor Freight. I wanted something to hold the pcb closer to desk height afterwards while I tinkered with off-board components. This was the cheapest option. It is definitely lacking in quality craftsmanship. Also, my pcb boards (1.6-1.7 mm thick) wouldn't fit in the slot at first.

I took 10 minutes to make some fixes, and now it's just what I needed. First off, the slots are made up of 3 metal strips layered on top of each other, with the middle layer inset a little to allow the circuit board to sit in there. I took off the top layer (by removing 2 screws), and put a small washer just underneath that layer. This created the depth I needed to fit the board in the slot. Also, don't expect this to hold any tools other than smaller screwdrivers at first. But there is a big cavity (if you take the thing apart you can see it), so drilling a few extra holes will allow you to put your common tools within arm's reach, as the picture shows.

I normally wouldn't deal with making fixes to an item I just took out of the box. But I knew this price couldn't be beat, so it was definitely worth it for me...thus all 5 stars.

title: Superb service (UPDATED)
text:
UPDATED 07/26/2013:

My original rating was 5 stars because of the superb warranty service I received from Logitech. I thought I got a bad mouse which they promptly replaced, no questions asked. However, the replacement mouse developed the exact same problem as the original one (see below) in exactly three months after being replaced. This mouse is absolute trash. If you cannot click or drag as you normally would, what good is its ability to track on any surface? STAY AWAY.

Original review:

My exact version of this mouse is not listed at Amazon, so I cannot review it per se. My Logitech Anywhere Mouse MX TM is P/N (810-002902). The mouse was perfect until it began double-clicking where you wanted to single-click or drag-n-drop, which was for less than three months. Googled the issue. Turns out the issue is common and there is even a YouTube video where a guy shows how take the mouse apart and glue on some plastic pieces to the worn out button pieces. In other words, the mouse itself is garbage as it does not last.

HOWEVER, I give the mouse 5 stars because of Logitech support. In the last year I had to deal with them twice: The first time when my 3-year old G-5 mouse broke (after nearly 3 years of very heavy gaming use). But the G-5 was still under warranty and they replaced it quickly and without any headaches or runarounds following some basic over-the-phone troubleshooting. They did not even ask me to send my broken mouse back to them.

I received the same annoyance-free service when this Anywhere MX TM broke. They answered the phone quickly, walked me through some (previously unknown to me) troubleshooting steps and then sent me a brand-new Anywhere MX mouse of another version. Again, they did not ask me to mail the broken one back to them.

In short, you are safe buying Logitech products (and this mouse in particular) as should anything go wrong you can count on being taken care of by Logitech support.

title: With a little effort, works perfectly on Mac OSX Mountain Lion
text:
After reading the reviews, I figured that I would try my hand at getting this card working. It is a bargain price, and would be a welcome upgrade. I received the card and tried the drivers first. Both the Oyen and LaCie drivers didn't work. I then tried running Multibeast and restarting with the card in the slot. It showed up in System Information and worked with several usb devices I tried. Great!
Now the big test: I tried turning off the power to the card via the menubar and removing the card. Other reviewers could not get the card to work again without a reboot. I inserted the card again and it still worked perfectly. I also tried shutting down, and rebooting without the card inserted, and then inserting it after logging in. Still absolutely no problems. This card works like a charm.

My only kick against it is that it does seem to use extra power, running down my battery quicker than normal, but this is to be expected for a powered card. Also, without careful handling, removing usb devices may pull the card out as well.

Overall a fantastic card well worth the money. System Information registers 2.5 GT/s (Giga Transfers per second), though I'm not sure it that is combined for both ports or 2.5GT/s for each. Either way, 2.5GT/s of input and output means 5GT/s bidirectional, as advertised.

title: Seem to hold power about the same as original - but die after about a year of use
text:
UPDATE:
After about a year of use all of batteries I bought became bulged which made them impossible to fit into the camera. This has also happened to Wasabi Power batteries which probably means they're the same just differently labeled. If it were possible to give zero stars I'd still give 1-star because they've worked and held power about the same as original battery for about a year, but I was hoping they would last at least couple of years! The charger still works, and deserves 5-stars as it's better than Fujifilm's original. But I can't split this into two sets of stars, and averaging is not useful for other buyers I think. If these batteries are designed to work for a year, it should be labeled so, and reflected in the price.

Comparing to the original battery the cost is still considerably lower. I need at least 5 batteries when traveling because these cameras go through them pretty quick especially if some days you don't get a chance to charge them. If you only need 1 more battery, maybe buying original for $50 is not so bad. But for me it's $50 x 5, so I'll still go with 3rd party ones to replace this junk.

It's worth buying 3rd party batteries instead of original ones, even if you replace them every year. Because even original battery has a lifespan and will degrade overtime. Although it's been 2+ years and as of now original still performs adequately.

There seem to be couple of other brands now, will try to buy different kinds again, not to put all eggs in one basket (even if they're the eggs are all from the same chicken just branded differently)

=== my original review ===
I see there aren't a lot of reviews on these so I'll add my not very technical review here. I give these 5 stars because I can't really feel the difference between these and original battery that came with my Fujifilm X-E1.

I also bought 3 Wasabi batteries, so had 6 batteries in total. I got used to using the original battery you kind of get the feel for how long it lasts. For example when I had my Canon 5D/II, I bought 2 other generic batteries, and I could tell they lasted at least 1/3rd less if not even 1/2 (then they died after about a year). Well I had these ones and Wasabi for couple of months now, and they're working fine about the same as original and I can't tell the difference between any of these. So if there is a difference it's not really significant.
