title: Amazing hot iron!
text:
I bought this hot iron from my hair stylist, she highly recommended it because I have wavy, frizzy, thick hair and I constantly hot iron and chemically straighten and relax my hair. At first I was skeptical, because I already had a pretty decent ceramic hot iron that cost me less than $50. However, I had gone through about three $20 hot irons and my $50 was on its way out- so I figured I would give this pricey one a shot and I am so glad I did! I have had the same one about 3 years and I absolutely love it. The first time I used it, I could instantly tell why it was worth the extra money.

The main thing that sets this hot iron aside from the rest is the fact that it uses Vapor Fuel. I has a little compartment that you fill with Vapor Fuel with that is loaded with great stuff: Their patented "Quadramine Complex" that is supposed to reconstruct and protect your hair; antioxidants that also protect hair- particularly against damaging free radicals in the environment; essential fatty acids which are always great for shine, flexibility and manageability and softness; botanical moisturizers also for moisture and softness; and "featherweight silicones," which are the key to frizz elimination. From the very first time I used this hot iron, to today 3 years later I still see incredible sheen, and feel amazing softness of my hair.

One thing to mention is that quite a bit of steam is emitted from this device. Sometimes when people see me using it, they think I am burning my hair! I just have t reassure them, and myself, that it is just the goodness of the Reconstrx Vapor. Another thing to mention is that, for me anyways, by the time I am done straightening all of my hair, all of liquid had run out. I do have rather long hair, below my shoulders, but not quite below the bra strap. Just know you will be refilling the reservoir quite often. One other factor that isn't ideal, it the "burnt" smell. I'm pretty sure EVERY hot iron comes with that smell, but this one is more unique. I believe anyway that the smell is coming from the burning vapor and not the burning hair as would metal irons. There is also an annoying film left from the vapor on the hot plates, it easily cleans and doesn't effect the function of the device.

The actual hardware of the flat iron seems to be pretty good- however, it took me forever to figure out how to "lock" and "unlock" it. It's really not that difficult, just not typical. At the very bottom, where the 2 sides meet, there is like a series of grooves, and to lock and unlock the device, you must sort of put your finger inside a groove and push it outward. The actual clear section where the vapor has to go, must be removed in order to refill. I feel this is a poor design, but again its not difficult to remove it, just not typical and sort of annoying. To remove it and place it back in, you must hold a "button" down and wriggle the section out in a very particular way. The same goes for putting it back in. Also, to actually refill it- you have to life a small flexible stopper and insert the nozzle of the bottle and squeeze. My issue with this is that it tends to overfill quickly and spill a bit. Its kind of fun to squeeze it in though, and watch it fill up. There is a tiny piece of plastic that broke inside of my reservoir and is just floating in the liquid. No clue how it broke off, and the whole device seems to still function well , but I felt it was worth mentioning.

Overall, my hair is silky, shiny, smooth and strong and I think it has a lot to do with this iron. I do use lots of other products that benefit to good hair, but I believe metal irons destroy your hair, and this one actually aids in repairing it! I highly recommend this product =)

title: Fantastic!  Better range and throughput than Asus RT-N12 (DD-WRT)
text:
~~EDIT~~ - 2 MONTHS LATER: I started getting oddities after a month of use where my throughput would drop to 0.5Mb/s (I usually receive 24Mb/s). I lived with it for a couple of days, thinking it was a fluke, but it worried me enough to go and search for an answer on Cisco's website. Thank goodness - it was just a software setting. By default, the router has the Quality of Service (QoS) and WMM turned on. If you have any always-on VoIP devices (like an Ooma), the router eventually starts handing over ALL of its bandwidth to the always-on device. You can tweak it, or turn it off. I just turned off QoS. This instantly solved my problem and I haven't had a recurrence of this issue over the past month.

NOTE: I have only owned this router for a day, so I will edit this review if anything changes.

I am truly impressed by this bottom-of-the-line router from Linksys. This is the new line/family of routers introduced for 2012, and runs about $60 at Staples or Office Depot (but it's about $40 on Amazon or WalMart). The router is very understated; it's matte-black which keeps fingerprints from appearing, and it only has port lights on the back of the device (which you can turn off if you don't want any lighting). The device is VERY light; it feels as though it's just a piece of hollow plastic. There's plenty of ventilation since the entire underside and sides of the device are porous. The router took about 2 minutes to set up, 3 minutes to update to the latest firmware, and if you use the included CD, it'll automatically create wireless connections on your Windows computer. After a day of heavy use, the device runs much cooler than my Netgear 54G router or my Asus RT-N12 router. The range is fantastic as well. At 3 feet away, I have a ping of 26ms, download of 29Mb/s and an upload of 1Mb/s. At 40 feet away, through three walls, a microwave, a TV, and with 15 other neighbors' wireless routers interfering, I still have a ping of 26ms, download of 15Mb/s and upload of 1Mb/s. Compared to my optimized Asus RT-N12 router running a custom firmware of DD-WRT, this is MUCH improved. The Asus has two external antennas with a 2Dbi gain, but at 40 feet away in the same location, I was getting a ping of 160ms, download of 5Mb/s and an upload of 0.5Mb/s. This router, even with its stock setting, is truly impressive. Some reviewers are getting limited download speeds, but Cisco's website has a guide to fix the advanced settings to make the router settings compatible with their specific mdoems.

Also, the router does come with advanced options such as QoS, Port Forwarding, UPnP, MTU, etc. The only feature it's missing is the ability to go from a mixed wireless 802.11 B/G/N to a pure G or N network; it is fixed to a mixed mode broadcast. However, you can access the settings wirelessly by going to the 192.168.1.1 address in a browser, and it takes about 1/2 a second to switch between settings and a couple seconds to commit the changes to memory. Also, the router can auto-update its firmware without needing you to hard-wire your computer into it; it has enough memory to auto-download firmware updates and update itself.

If you want to eliminate mixed mode broadcast, are looking for dual-band 2.4Ghs/5Ghz output, or looking for gigabit connections, then look elsewhere, as this router does not provide those functions. However, with the ease of use, the cost of $40, its understated looks, and the range/throughput, this is easily a recommended purchase.

I ran a Black Magic speed test with both the USB 2 and eSATA connection using the Vantec NexStar eSATA adapter with a Seagate Drive.

Black Magic speed test reported write speed of 37.9 MB/s and read speed of 38.3 MB/s on USB 2 (without this adapter).

With the Vantec eSATA to USB 3 adapter, Black Magic reported write speed of 155.2 MB/s and read speed of 166.7 MB/s.

I knocked one star off because the cable has to be connected in a specific order or it will not work. I initially connected the cable end to end (Drive to adapter to computer), then powered up the drive and it didn't work. After checking the directions, it said to connect the drive to the cable and adapter, power up the drive and then plug the USB 3 into the computer. Drive mounted almost instantly.

title: Where have you been all my life...
text:
well, maybe just the past 5 years.

I bought the D700 the first week it came out from this very website. It has served me incredibly well over these years but I have always wanted a small hand held to carry around to make life a little easier. I've tried the fuji, the 4/3rds the nikon's and all have just been so far from my expectations of image quality that I have sent them all back. This camera will not be going back. The IQ is as good (if not better) than my D700 with my Nikkor VRII 70-200 or 28-70 on it (the sharpest zooms on the market in my opinion). The sharpness is amazing and I get wonderful pictures up to and including ISO 6400 (I don't like going past 3200 on my D700).

A lot of people complain about the auto focus, but honestly I have not had a problem with it at all (even in low light indoor shooting). Tack sharp autofocus on all of my ISO 6400 shots. Sure it's much slower than the D700, but that's really an apples to oranges comparison. Some people complain about having a 35mm focal length. This is not your mom's point and shoot, so if you are not comfortable with using the lens properly and framing your shots efficiently, then this is not the camera for you. I love the creativity it brings out. It's a totally different experience than the DSLR with zooms.

If you have the means and want to make an investment in a camera that simply has NO issues in image and is simply a joy to shoot, then go for it. Once you get over the buyers remorse (lasted about 30 shots for me) than you will be as happy as can be. For me the search is finally over!!!

title: Fantastic device after some initial pain.
text:
I must admit, I was very, very close to returning the T100 as a defective item, thinking it was the worst computer I had ever purchased. I had the same issues as everyone else who found this device problematic. After going through the setup process, setting up office, and installing other software applications, the T100 became very unstable. It went into the restart, repair loop and crashed several times. I was at my wit's end before I read a couple of the reviews that provided a solution to my problems.

NOW IT'S MY FAVORITE DEVICE. Here's how I made it work.

After nearly giving up on this device, I read a review that suggested a factory reset would solve all my problems. I figured, why not. If that didn't work then I could always return the item. After I reset the T100, it's become a fantastic device. Here's how I solved my problems:

1. Go through the set up process.
2. Instead of continuing to load everything else, go to step 3.
3. Go to the charm menu in the Metro Interface
4. Select Change PC Settings (bottom right)
5. Select Update and Recovery
6. Select Recovery
7. Select Remove Everything and Reinstall Windows
8. Make sure you install all the important Windows updates

The reinstall will seem very slow at first but will speed up afterwards (maybe after 10 - 20 minutes). After the re-installation process has been completed, you can proceed to continue the set-up process as normal. You will find that the T100 is now a lot more stable, the touchpad a lot more responsive, and the system seems faster.

I don't know this for sure, but I believe the 3rd party anti-virus software will cause some conflicts with the system, so I opted to stick with Windows Defender. Also, I uninstalled some of the Asus software (reading mode & cloud storage). I don't know if they caused any of the conflicts, but I did not need them so I thought there was no harm in it.

Now, I love this little machine.

Pros
- Ability to run full Windows 8.1
- Decent display
- Responsive Keyboard
- Very responsive interface
- Quick and nimble operating system
- Full Version of Microsoft Office
- Built-in full USB 3.0 port, HDMI, mini-usb, bluetooth

Cons
- Initial problems setting up the device
- Problems installing MS Office ( if you run into problems where it's stuck trying to finalize the installation of Office, Google stopping print spooling. You'll have to restart print spooling after installation is completed)
- touch pad is sometimes responsive, sometimes not

I hope this review helps others who have problems with this great little device.

title: An average router for the price but Buffalo Tech Support is horrible
text:
Well, to be honest this is a very good piece of hardware based on the price. It has a modern dual-core ARM processor, 128MB Flash memory and 512MB RAM which matches with many high-end routers that would cost you twice the money. However; without a quality of software the hardware becomes mostly useless. This is where Buffalo lacks substantially. And don't get fool with open-source firmware options such as DD-WRT. Even though Buffalo is well known with their support to DD-WRT as well as many of their stock firmwares are based on DD-WRT this particular one doesn't compatible with DD-WRT. You can install but you would loose some functionality as well as there is no way for going back to stock firmware. So the enticing technical specs wouldn't gain you any flexibility unless you wouldn't want to split your hair to figure out how you could make it work with an open-source firmware.

Since most of the users wouldn't want to deal with the mods, I would say the stiock firmware is adequate for an average user with basic networking requirements. If you need NAT Loopback, mounting an USB drive with NTFS or EXS format, good wifi range and routing performance just move on to your next router option. The radio and WAN/LAN routing performance of this box is also very disappointing. If you want to put many wireless users, transferring large files over wifi or streaming multiple HD video streams over wifi and such heavy use; this box would not satisfy your needs. The range is not good and when you going further away from the router wifi bandwidth drops substantially.

There is another very important feature of Buffalo products that come with 3 years of warranty which is a substantial differentiator. Again don't fool with the marketing terms. The support is not exist so that it wouldn't make any sense even if it comes with 10 years of warranty. I had to return this router not to any of the cons I have mentioned above but due to lack of support. The USB port of my unit wouldn't spin up my external drive. I have created a support ticket and waited for a few days with no response. Then created another ticket just to remind them the problem I had been suffering from. The response was they couldn't have found my first ticket so that they haven't known the problem. I was asked to re-create the ticket which I did but still no response. However; I have received a customer survey from Buffalo about the technical support I had received. It was ironic but I filled out the survey and let them know my frustration. Usually you would expect them to take your problem more seriously, wouldn't you? No, they wouldn't. I have kept waiting 4 more days to hear back either from tech support or from customer service. So I have nothing but to return the product back. Long story short the 3 years warranty is just a marketing gimmick based on my experience.

And my final word is if you want to have same technical specs, better routing and wifi performance as well as experiencing opensource firmware options like DD-WRT, Tomato, Merlin ASUS-WRT etc, I would suggest ASUS RT-AC56U. It may cost you $20 more but it worth it

title: A little known GEM for the price!
text:
Let me preface by saying that I am a very happy owner of the Dr. Dre Beats Studio's. However, sometimes I would like to listen to music around the house without having to use battery power, being extra delicate with the product, or without being dead to the world (aka my roommates trying to get my attention or my phone ringing). Thus the V-Moda's are perfect. I don't believe in "burn-in" but when these first arrived they sounded VERY muddy. So I turned my ipod on and let these run for about 7hrs straight, initially (30hrs total). I noticed an IMMENSE difference in sound quality (the mids were MUCH more clear). Also, they hurt my head to wear for more than 10min but I checked the website which suggest you bend the headband out multiple times to loosen up. These things are DURABLE so bend the headband flat a couple times, if you have to, and comfort will be a guarantee.

FOR THE PRICE you can't really find a better-looking/sounding pair of headphones if you like bass (I do). Also, they say noise "isolating" but please note that this only "isolates" not "cancels" and it's mostly when actively playing music. Thus in example, if I am playing the music at a decent level, I can't "hear" what my roommate is saying if he speaks to me but I can hear enough outside noise to know that SOMEONE is speaking to me.

Comfort - A
Sound - Solid B (if you like mids) to B+ (if you like bass)
Design - A
Build Quality - A+++

title: Well suited for DD-WRT
text:
Operation of unit was as expected. Quality packaging, except that the box was cardboard instead of the "glossy" original, packaging was as good (probably better) as the original. Everything that came with the original included (disk, power supply, short Ethernet cable).

I have a number of WRT54G units I program with DD-WRT and use as access points. I have been buying WRT54G's because they are cheep and when loaded with the DD-WRT "micro" version code they work fine as access points. But recently I tried programming one to run as a router with some the the additional features enabled, like DNSMasq, and it would run out of memory and the WEB interface would lock up. The GL has twice the memory as the G and can be programmed with the standard code instead of the micro, which has a number of additional features. Have DNSMasq enabled for both DHCP and DNS and it is working great as a primary router. I now have many devices on the network identifiable by URL rather than IP address.

I believe this to be a very reasonable price for a WRT54xx with the 4/16 MB memory configuration. You can find the WRT54G's (2/8 MB memory configuration) much cheaper, but you are limited to using just the DD-WRT microcode. So obviously the larger are both more desirable and more rare. And fetch a significantly higher price.

title: Pretty Dang Good at Controlling Reflections!
text:
Bought this about 2 1/2 weeks ago when the prices began to drop (Samsung is discontinuing Plasmas like everyone else). My main concern was the glossy screen and reflections. Our current TV was a 42" 720P Panasonic Plasma with a semi-matte screen (from 2007/2008). At that time, we picked it over LCD as we liked the better blacks and motion handling with plasma AND the matte screen addressed any reflections issue.
Flash forward to 2014 and there are no more matte screen TVs - every TV has a glossy screen. Some have a "filter" and others use a coating or (worse) film, but none are true matte or even semi-matte. Over the Summer we picked up Samsung's F5300 plasma, but got it home and immediately realized both the reflections and even basic shine/glare were going to be an issue for us. I'm not talking just lamps or windows either. Staring at our white walls, pillows on the couch, heck, even US sitting on the couch was immensely distracting. A week later, we returned it. We CONSIDERED the F8500 series with its AR filter but just could not bring ourselves to ttake another chance, especially given the 3X price delta.
Flash forward again to November. The price has plummeted and I decide to go for it.
The verdict: it's a keeper! All of the "normal" reflections like the walls, sofa, us on the sofa, etc. are all a NON-ISSUE. The filter mutes all reflections and I even find myself wondering "how are they doling this). It even works when the TV is off 0 everything is muted. Think of it as a partial black hole where light doesn't escape and full brightness. Now, I DID angle the TV slightly to avoid direct reflections from our patio doors during the daytime and we have no lamps directly across from the TV. If you have the latter (a lamp) you might still be OK, but the former could still be an issue.

Overall, very satisfied at this price point until a better technology like moth eye comes along.

title: Great Features For The Money !!!!!
text:
First of all, I reviewed quite a few similar products before making the final decision.

PROS: Seems to be well made, but probably not for rugged use. Some degree of care is required.

Station reception is very good, but I do live in the suburbs of a major U.S. city. Harmonic AM hum can be eliminated by tilting out the solar panel part way as a stand, and lying horizontal. FM very clear. SW is adequate, better with a clip on Sangean antenna (ANT 60). I did not expect the capability of my Sangean ATA 818.

Multiple power options. Crank works well, not flimsy. Solar charge will power radio by maintaining an existing charge level. Optional AC adapter charges unit fairly quickly. AC adapter can overcharge if left connected for long periods of time, and can shorten battery life. Since I am an electronics geek, at some time I will swap out the 600 Mah internal battery for a larger capacity. An AC charge of 4-5 hours is adequate.

My intent was for a lightweight jobsite radio that doesn't chew up batteries, and also will serve for emergency use in off grid situations.
I have been using as such for about 10 days, without any hiccups. It runs for about 7 - 8 hours a day. I loaded it with 3 Sanyo Eneloops, which I have hardly used, and are the backup power.

The flashlight & "reading lamp" are bonuses in my view, but you never know when they may come in handy.

Backlight display is very good.

Digital tuner is superior to analog any day. Scan function is a big plus, especially on SW

I receive 5 out of the 7 NOAA weather stations in my area, all crystal clear. I have not had the need to use the auto warn feature as of yet.

VOLUME is more than adequate.

CONS:

Tuner knob is very sensitive. The overall compact design puts my big hands in contact with some of the knobs & buttons inadvertently, causing changes. I'm still getting used to using the lockout button AFTER setting to a station.

WISH LIST:

Add a crossover circuit to charge the 3 main batteries as well (AC & solar only)

Add S.A.M.E. capability for weather and other emergency alerts

Use a larger capacity rechargeable battery on solar / crank / AC circuit. A 1200 Mah would run this sucker for about 10 - 12 hours, but would require more or extended re-charge. ( A lot more cranking )

BOTTOM LINE:

I WAS NOT DISAPPOINTED IN THE LEAST, and will purchase a few more as gifts for family.

title: Ignore the Bay Cover (Unless You Actually Own a T60); Buy This for the Caddy, Rails, and Mounting Screws.
text:
It fits perfectly, but I'm not using it in a T60. I purchased this for and installed it in a T420. Read on, and I'll explain.

I'm glad that I saw the image for this product and followed up to read the product description, because the product title doesn't do it justice.

The descriptions lists a bay cover, a drive caddy, mounting rails, and mounting screws.

The title describes only the cover, which I didn't need. I was more interested in the caddy (the primary picture Amazon uses for this item), rails and screws.

Lenovo's ThinkPad T series uses standardized parts whenever possible; using the same exact parts in many subsequent models helps keep costs down. The caddy, rails, and screws in this kit represent an equivalent to Lenovo's part number 41V9756, mounting hardware for a 9 mm Hard Disk Drive (HDD) or Solid State Drive (SSD) in the internal drive bay.

As in the product title, this mounting hardware was used in the ThinkPad T60 (a seven (7) year old system that was first demoed just before CES 2006), but this exact same hardware is still used today to mount 9mm drives in the internal bays of the T410 and T420 ThinkPads (two and one generations older than current, respectively, as of the time of this writing). I confirmed compatibility via part numbers in publicly available Hardware Maintenance Manuals, and based on parts detail photos on Lenovo's website, I suspect this hardware is also compatible with the current generation T430.

Getting back to the bay cover, this part is what appears to actually drive the price of this and similar parts kits. Identical drive mounting hardware, packaged with bay covers for newer ThinkPads, currently sells on Amazon for as much as 60% more (including per-item shipping costs) as what I paid for this kit. Other websites charge as much as 500% (NOT including shipping) of what I paid for this kit on Amazon to get a kit with the bay cover for the T420. The ONLY difference in these kits is the bay cover, so as long as you still have the bay cover that came installed on your system, all that really matters is the mounting hardware.

What follows is somewhat extraneous but possibly useful information and a TL/DR summary.

Why did I need the mounting hardware?

My T420 came with a 7mm SSD in the internal bay, and I had a 9 mm HDD on hand from an older notebook that I wanted to add to the system. The mounting rails for 7 mm drives won't fit 9 mm drives.

I could have put the HDD in an optical bay drive caddy such as [[ASIN:B00A2AWBKU 2nd HDD or SSD Caddy Lenovo ThinkPad T420,T430,T510,T520,T530, W510, W520, W530]], but ThinkPads have a wonderful 'Active Protection System'. This system will, if it detects rapid motion such as falling/being dropped, attempt to park the read/write heads of an HDD to prevent or reduce damage from the inevitable head crash upon impact. However, according to the documentation, this system only works if the HDD is in the internal drive bay.

Both the internal drive bay and the Serial Ultrabay Enhanced (optical bay) are SATA III/6 Gbps ports, so by putting the 7 mm SSD in the optical bay drive caddy and the HDD in the internal bay, I retain the full speed of the SSD for booting and application launch, while having better protection for the HDD which will be used for large media files.

TL/DR: Mounting hardware works in many models newer than the T60. I used it successfully in a T420. The bay cover is irrelevant.

title: Great computer
text:
Kind of a long review sorry...

The Acer Chromebook is a great computer for someone looking for a computer to do internet browsing, light gaming, and light productivity. You can not download any programs to it, but there are a ton of apps available to fit almost every need (word processing, spreadsheets, photo editing, games,etc.. check google chrome store to see what's available if you have any questions). Think of it like a tablet with an app store in that regard.

Way too many bad reviews on Chromebooks from people who do not understand what they are buying and don't understand why windows programs won't work on it. A lot of bad reviews are from people who have never even tried one. Unless you are a hardcore MS office user, or serious gamer who needs a lot of computing power this computer can do almost everything you need.

At first I wasn't sure if this would work for me, because it looked like a low end limited use netbook. But it kept getting great reviews and for $200 something bucks, and the option to return it if I didn't like it, I'd give it a shot. There are tons of reviews from people who have moved away from using their much more expensive computers because the Chromebook is just a better online experience for most of their needs. I now know why.

Honestly if I need something, I know my Chromebook can be up and have me searching Google quickly in seconds. Long before my other computers can get to my homepage (even from standby). I also know all my plug-ins are always up to date and ready to go. Why even turn the other ones on unless I absolutely have too then? Having to sit through windows load/resume screens gets old really quick once you realize you don't have to. Chromebook quickly became my go to computer for anything online.

Due to the fact it doesn't run a bulky OS like windows, it doesn't need that much processor power to breeze through websites very quickly. You would be amazed how fast this little Celeron chip (its actually a stripped down dual core i3 sandy-bridge processor) runs when its not having to support a lot of OS background processes. It is just as fast browsing online as my much more expensive i5 computers.

Power off to my internet homepage is under 10 seconds, standby to my homepage is 1 second or less, and total shutdown is under 5 seconds.

However I tried it out at best buy (they have it for $199), and due to the fact they have so many machines running on the WiFi at the same time it seemed slow in the store. Trust me it is very fast on a good WiFi. Remember it is cloud based, so it is only as fast as your Wifi is. If you are using a slow connection your whole computer will seem slow. Faster the connection, faster the computer will be.

It is cloud based, everything is saved, auto updated and configured on the cloud. Since nothing is saved locally on the computer (unless you want it to be) your files (pics music documents movies etc) are available on any computer with an internet connection if you are away from your Chromebook. If you have to replace or upgrade your Chromebook simply log in and everything is instantly restored from the cloud, including every setting, preference, app, and all your saved data and files. Plus since nothing is actually on the Chromebook, no one can steal any info or files from it. Try that with a windows machine. No reason to ever do any maintenance on anything ever. No worry about viruses/malware because there is no real operating system to infect, no old files to clean out, no registry to maintain, no updates to manually install, no defrag, no virus scans, no maintenance at all since nothing is actually stored on your computer (except the OS and offline apps).

Also, since it is cloud based, no matter how much you download or use it, it does not affect the computers speed. Nothing is stored on the computer to bog it down. It actually just keeps getting faster with every auto update. It is the only computer I have ever used that gets faster as you use it.

HD 1080p video streams smooth with no frame rate issues, even in full screen. Aquarium WebGL renders 40 fps on a high setting with 500 objects on screen, and 35 fps with 1,000. The HD webcam is great, and video chat works with no issues. The speakers are a little quiet for my taste, but you can hear everything just fine, just don't expect it to fill a noisy room with sound. HDMI out works perfect with my HDTV.

You can download music, pics, files, pretty much anything, you just can not run any exe. files if you download them. The Chromebook only runs internet based apps, and apps from the chrome store. The chrome store has a great selection of apps to meet almost every need and is growing quickly.

While it only has a 16gb SSD hard drive, you pretty much only need it to temporarily hold files while you transfer them to the cloud, that is where all your data is stored. The 320GB hard drive is larger but much slower. I opted for the smaller faster 16gb SSD one as I store everything online and it allows the machine to run much faster.

Only downsides are

1. You can't pin favorite websites to the desktop, you have to start the browser then pull them off favorites. I'm sure that will be addressed soon as it seems to be a common complaint.

2. Also you need to have a wireless cloud based printer to print directly from chrome book. Otherwise you need to access your cloud files from a different PC to print. While it has USB ports, it has limited plug and play, they won't work with printers...yet. USB mice, cameras, cell phones, hard drives all seem to work fine though.

3. It is limited with Java plugins but then again not much is in Java anymore so it probably doesn't matter.

4. Volume a little low for my taste, but still very audible.

5. Not the best looking construction, but it is durable.

6. Trackpad might take a little getting used to if you're used to separate left and right mouse buttons, but works great once you get it down (Alt key plus left click, or 2 finger click both work for right click).

The biggest question is why buy this over a similar priced windows laptop that can do everything?

One answer... speed. While a cheap windows unit can do more overall...there is no comparison between this and a cheap laptop. Side by side, its much quicker, smoother, and is just overall more convenient to use. Think of windows like a pickup tuck, and Chromebook like a sports car. You can do more with a pickup, but it's not as fast or fun as a sports car. That combined with the super quick boot up times, zero maintenance, and cloud computing, makes it so quick and easy, that I actually don't use my more expensive computers unless I have too.

Acer vs Samsung Chromebook... Acer is somewhat faster and smoother, and is upgradable. While Acer says 4GB ram max...the chrome OS will actually accept and use any amount of RAM you jam into the 2 slots with a few easy tweaks (I've seen these with up to 32GB of ram running). You can also swap out the SSD and battery for better ones if you want. It has a delete key and caps lock key (the Samsung doesn't for some reason). Battery life on Acer isn't great though. The Samsung has much better battery life, looks a little nicer, and has a nicer feeling keyboard and track pad but is not upgradable. It is sealed shut and everything is soldered in. Pick what features are more important to you. There are some other minor details but those are the biggest.

While it is not for everyone, if you're looking for a computer to just browse the internet, watch videos, app and internet based gaming, do word and spreadsheets, photo editing, video chat, etc... basically what 90% of people do with a computer anyway...this is the one to get. If you want to play games that you need to install to the hard drive, run a serious business, or have a slow or spotty internet connection this is not the one to get.

title: EVGA Cashing in on their good name.
text:
I ordered my card directly from their site on launch night, and eagerly awaited my package. When it arrived it looked perfectly normal, nothing seemed off or damaged. When I unpackaged the card itself, the cooler felt flimsy, and made slight creaking noises that thin plastic makes when shifting. Again, nothing seemed broken or improperly installed form the factory. I carefully replaced my older EVGA 670 FTW Edition that had faithfully served me for the past 2-ish years and inserted the new 970. After getting everything plugged back in I was incredibly excited to try out my new card on various benchmarking programs and high resource games.

It was upon boot that my face dropped as the sound of a shrill coil whine filled my room. Louder than my fans on both my case and my old card had ever put out. When sitting on the desktop it gve a lower pitched whine which would increase in frequency when I started a game. Even on low resource games like Dota 2 and CS:GO, the whine would fluctuate with the frames in an almost comical singing. It was noted that ridiculously high frame counts could also cause that problem on any card, and that limiting with v sync would stop the problem. Well I made sure that the frames never went past 144, as I have a 144Hz monitor that I expected this card to handle with no problem. I decided to ask EVGA what could have gone wrong. They suggested that there was insufficient power coming from my PSU. After diagnosing that that was not the case as per the EVGA reps suggestions, I had full authorization to return the card. (I could have gotten a replacement, but I'll explain why I didn't in a bit.)

The problem was I had to pay for shipping back to the factory which cost me a whole 14$

Let that sink in for a second. Their policy for returns is that you must foot the bill for sending back a defective product that they tried to sell you. So why not just get a replacement at no cost to myself? Well, after doing some research while waiting for EVGA to respond to my query, I stumbled upon some very disheartening information. As it turns out EVGA has decided to try and cut costs by any means with this new generation of cards, and not only that but these practices affect every variation of the 970 in one way or another. Here is a link (...) that explains that not only has EVGA tried to re use a cooler design for a different chip, but that this cooler in and of itself is of poor design and quality. Not only that, but they have allegedly used subpar quality components on the PCB itself which results in that coil whine.

Overall, EVGA is by far the worst manufacturer to go with on this generation of cards. Their build quality has dropped significantly from past generations, and with other options like the MSI and ASUS versions offering vastly better coolers and quality assurance it becomes obvious that there is little reason to go with EVGA now. To top it all off, I am now short 14$ for a bad product.

title: Many pre-built computers have a lot of unnecessary bloatware installed on them in order to try and ...
text:
It is generally hard to review a computer because a computer buying decision is generally made by the specs on the computer. As such, I will try and use this review to provide information that is generally not available from just looking at the specs on this machine.

Power Supply: One of the responses to the question above about the power supply on this computer said that it had a 300 watt supply. I opened the case on the computer and it said that it has 460 watts max. As I was able to install a Radeon 6850 video card without upgrading the power supply, I do not see how there could be a 300 watt power supply on this thing.

Bloatware: Many pre-built computers have a lot of unnecessary bloatware installed on them in order to try and have you purchase additional software. Generally this bloatware can significantly reduce the speed at which the computer operates. I have even purchased a computer that had the hard drive partitioned with software on the partition that the company wanted you to buy. That is not the case with this computer. There is very little additional software installed on the computer that would not have otherwise come with windows 8.1. There is an icon to install Microsoft Office icon (You have to pay for it if you want to install it). In addition, Cyberlink media suite essentials is installed. You have the option to use the basic version of it, or to upgrade it to the Pro version. Cyberlink can be useful for watching DVDs on your computer. It is a decent program to have.

Video Card:The computer is installed with a NVIDIA GeForce GTX 745 4GB DDR3. Apparently this card is a "high efficiency" card that is only used in pre-built systems. Will it play games? Yes, it is a pretty decent card. I swapped the card out for my prior Radeon 6850, which was a $150 card about 2-3 years ago. The 6850 outperforms the video card that the Dell comes with.

Gaming: Prior to changing the video card, I played a few games on it. Guild Wars 2 was handled fairly well. With the game set on the highest setting I was getting about 20fps, which is a little low. (This was bumped up to about 40fps with the new video card.) Set on medium the game played very smoothly. I was also able to play Skyrim on nearly maxed out settings. Please note, it is my understanding that both of these games rely heavily on the CPU as opposed to some other games which rely more heavily on the Graphics Card and this computer has an amazing CPU.

Setup: Setup was very quick and easy to do, I think most people should be able to handle the setup of this computer, even if you are not very computer literate. I had intended to describe the setup process, but honestly, it was so quick and easy, that I cannot even remember what I had to do.

Small quirk: There is a little, but powerful orange LED inside the computer that stays on all the time that the computer is plugged in. It will even stay on for about a minute after the computer is unplugged. As I have the computer in my bedroom it is fairly noticeable at night time.

Overall, if you are looking for a higher powered pre-built system, I would highly recommend this computer, it will handle pretty much everything you can throw at it (with the exception of some high end games, set to the highest settings, with multiple monitors).

title: Excellent projector, with some pros and cons
text:
Pros:
1. The image quality is excellent! Small text can be read easily.
2. Color contrast. Compared to my laptop screen, this projector has MUCH brighter colors and more contrast.
3. Brightness. All I have to do is close the blinds and turn off the lights and I can watch movies during the day.
4. Sound level. This projector is very quiet, even on high altitude mode, which turns the fan speed up.
5. The image can be shot from the floor or the ceiling. I keep the projector under a couch so it can't be seen.
Cons:
1. The zoom is very small, so the projector will have to be placed at a specific distance from the screen for the picture to be the right size. The zoom really doesn't do anything.
2. No horizontal keystone correction. This means that the projector will have to be placed in the center of the room.
3. Doesn't come with a lens cover to protect the glass. I just made one myself out of cardboard and tape.
4. Doesn't come with a case. But if you're just keeping it in one place, that shouldn't matter.
Overall:

title: Works Flawlessly!
text:
Set up was easy to do. I had my iPhone, my computers (both desktop and laptop) and tablet up and running in no time. Just plug the Adapter into your Wave II or III system (note: read the instructions carefully that comes with the unit, the Wave II and III systems set up slightly differently). The Adapter doesn't have a power chord, it gets its power from the unit. That in itself is great and no need for yet another device plugged into your outlets!

For those who are new to bluetooth as I was, the devices have to be "discoverable", so follow your device's bluetooth setup instructions carefully. All of my bluetooth enabled devices discovered the Bose Adapter easily. The Adapter memorizes 6 device settings...more than enough for what I needed. My laptop and desktop were not bluetooth enabled so I purchased the Medialink USB Bluetooth Adapter - Version 4.0 (Newest Bluetooth Version Available) Class 2 Smart Ready Adapter w/ Low Energy Technology - Windows 7 32/64 Compatible from Amazon and installed it on both computers. Both computers are Win 7 and I had no problem installing and getting it to work on either one of my HP computers (note:I did go the Medialink website and installed the updated Windows 7/vista drivers just in case. I probably didn't have to, but a few folks who purchased the bluetooth adapter mentioned that they had a few problems with installation on their computers with Win 7 on their reviews). As far as my tablet, my Toshiba Thrive recognized it immediately and had that operating in less than a minute.

I have the Bose Wave III system. When I heard Pandora,Spotify and other music sites from my computers and my iTunes from my iPhone over the those Bose speakers, I was blown away! The sound is as incredible as the CD's that I play on the Wave III system itself. You too, will enjoy the great Bose sound you get from your devices compared to the inferior speaker systems on your devices!

Finally, one more tip for the non-techie people like myself: If playing music through your computer, you will need to change a couple of settings on the computer itself. First, make sure that the computer setting is set for bluetooth (go to control panel,systems and security,then change to allow bluetooth devices). The other is make the Bose sysem as your main speaker output for your computer. To do that, go to control panel, then devices and printers, then change the speaker setting on your computer to the Bose system instead of the speaker default. If you don't change that setting, it won't play on your Bose. To do that in Windows 7, simply go to your control panel, click hardware and sound, then manage audio devices. You can change your playback device to the Bose system there.

If you love your Bose system as much as I do, why just hear your CDs and the radio on them when you can use the Adapter to connect up to 6 of your audio bluetooth devices to it and enjoy that great Bose sound on all of them!

title: Great player with the best sound vs cost variable that I have heard, but has some quality control issues worth knowing about....
text:
This Onkyo CD player was my very first Onkyo product and I could not be more happy with it's build quality or it's performance.
Priced at $180 it's by far the best cost Vs. performance deals that you will ever come across.
This player can handle ( . Flac files -Wav files-MP3 files- and regular CDs ) It's a newer design than the Yamaha S-300 and yet cost $120 less. With a 11.7 LB weight it's built really well. It's center mounted transport is well above average for such a low cost player.
Has a nice aluminum front panel with a ergonomic button layout that's easy to get used to and a nice brushed aluminum remote control.

With the Wolfson DAC this Onkyo player has the same DAC as many of the $500 and up players being sold. It's power transformer is
huge and adds to the weight and sound playback of this excellent sounding player.

Sure there are better CD players on the market but at the $180 price point this sells at it's worth a listen as it compares with the other Wolfson DAC players like the Cambridge Audio 640c V2 that retails for about $600.

Notes:
I had a issue with quality control as I received several defective players in a row that needed to be sent back to Amazon but the returns cost me nothing and I finally got a working player. From what I could tell A****** received some bad units mixed within a few pallets, which was not A***** fault.

I also had a laser failure after 3 years of using this player almost everyday. So I spent $60 to buy a entirely new transport that included a new laser and the player now works like new again. Probably not on Onkyo as lasers usually last over 20 years.

As far as I'm concerned your better of buying a player like this brand new than a used NAD or Cambridge Audio player from 2000 or 2005

Technology has been improving and since CD players are based on good modern electronics buying a new one is always in your best interest.

Added Note:
I recently had my Onkyo C-7030 converted into a CD player with a twin tube buffer with a X10-D Music Fidelity clone for $170.

It has the buffer added into the main enclosure that's nice and roomy for the extra board and transformer. See Photo's

Absolutely incredible sound from this low cost CD player!

So now my Onkyo C-7030 is a C-7030 T and wow what a difference in it's sound output!
So for those looking for a expensive tube buffered Cd player this one can easily be modified by someone that really knows his electronics.

At this players current price point of $180 the up-grade for most people would cost about $300. So for under $500 you can own a Tube Buffer Cd player which is a great price

Just go on Ebay and look up Tube Buffer Cd players and you will see how expensive they all are. Even the Carver Tube Buffer player from 1990 still sells for $750 or more.

Great sounding player that's built like a tank and has plenty of internal room for the tube buffer up-grade.
Woflson DAC- .flac file capable, .wav file capable and MP3 capable with any CD-R media that's burnt to properly.

I used Winamp's freeware to take downloaded .flac and reconvert them to new .flac or .wav in the 16 bit 44.1k Redbook standard and they worked perfectly

This Onkyo is a very good CD only player that can handle every type of music file you can ask minus SA-CDs. So for $200 or less it's the best CD player I have heard and it has the specs to back that up.

Specs are not super important but the basic specs should all be nearly the same with CD players below the $500 barrier.

This players specs:

S.T.N.R. at 106 DB, D.R. 100 DB, T.H.D. .0028% overall frequency response of + or - .25 DB 20 to 20.

To use as comparison: The 2 Teac players sold below the price of the Onkyo both have the same specs:

S.T.N.R. at 100 DB, D.R. 96 DB, T.H.D. .003%, and most importantly + or - (2 DB), Yes a full 2 DB from 20/20. This huge amount of play across the audible frequency range is more what you would expect from a good pair of speakers, and not from a source input CD player.

I'm not a Teac hater, but there 2 cheapest players sold here have this horrible range during playback that cam actually be heard!

title: So Far I love it.
text:
So far I love this system. I have a nearly 17 year old severly disabled child and this monitoring system came just in the nick of time, as he was very sick again last night. I was able to easily monitor when he was gagging and needed suctioning, when he was uncomfortable and needed repositioning and so forth. It kept me from hearing his radio and only hearing him, which is exactly what I needed. (The fact that it monitors his room's temp is awesome too!)

I actually bought a second camera to go with this, so I could monitor both sides of his bed for when he's turned on his side. The anxiety I usually feel when I'm not in the room with him has been relieved. I also don't seem to have the lack of sound issue that people seem to complain about. True, I don't hear his breathing when it's normal but every other sound is very clear, even across the room I'm in at the time. Honestly, if I had to listen to all of the little sounds it would annoy me, so I'm more than happy not to hear them. The picture both when there is light and complete darkness is crystal clear - I was actually surprised at the quality of the night vision that it offers.

Anyhow, seeing as how we've only had this one night, I will update my review should things change. However, despite my not normally leaving feedback so soon, I was so excited by what this system is already doing for us, I just had to leave a review now. I plan to upgrade if all things go well - like rechargable batteries for the cameras and two more cameras for outdoor security.

title: Impressive! SLIM! 3D, 240hz, 1080p, cloud based apps in a lightweight, energy efficient package!
text:
Wow! I am simply blown away with this Super Slim, HIGH EFFICIENCY LED-LCD 3D HDTV. It has 240hz 24p for very smooth play of rapid sports action. The video quality is absolutely remarkable.

Cloud apps came pre-installed and ready for use:
Amazon Video on Demand (and PRIME!), Netflix, Hulu+, Youtube, etc all came pre-installed on the HDTV. Additional apps , both free and paid, are available with activation of a (free) cloud storage account. This makes the number of apps allowed limitless! We have watched videos on all the apps listed above, very smooth! No hiccups, no streaming issues, no waiting for videos to load, no issues. I activated our wifi on the slower 802.11g channel to test the tv's handling of a slower wifi signal. We also experienced flawless operation on our 2.4 ghz 802.11n wifi connection. Our ISP/home network is a rock steady 30 mbps connection with multiple wireless video streaming devices - again no issues with bandwidth or video loading with this combination.

High Efficiency: the energy label indicates $15 / year cost to operate; well beyond the lowest end of the scale. Ladies, if you are planning a tv for the bedroom and are concerned with hot flashes, this is your tv! We have left ours running a full 24 hours for days on end (the Roku box allows the HDTV to be used as a very large digital photo frame, yet we still cannot feel any extra heat anywhere around this model.

Package included the expected:
* 47" 3D HDTV - superslim and lightweight!
* Power cord, base stand (star trek style...), owners manual
* 2 remotes w/ 2 AA batteries for each - the "extra" remote is a remote touchpad allowing easy web navigation. It appears a blue tooth keyboard will connect as well!! :-)

Package did NOT include:
3D glasses - to my husband's dismay! He wants it all included!

Impressive # of Ports:
Inputs: 4 HDMI*, 1 PC, THREE USB, 1 SD Card, 1 cable/antenna, AND 1 Composite (via included adapter... it's small enough I have left it attached so I won't have to hunt for it later when needed..)

NOTE: the HDMI ports on this model are NOT powered ie will NOT operate new devices such as the soon to be released Roku Stick. Quite honestly, with the cloud based apps we are already considering the retirement of our brand new Roku 2 anyway.

Output: 1 digital audio out

All in all I would give this 3D HDTV 10 stars. It is simply an amazing cutting edge HDTV ahead of it's time. We own two of the high tech, wifi, internet apps [[ASIN:B003ICXCZM Philips 46PFL5705D/F7 46-Inch 1080p 240 Hz LCD HDTV with NetTV, Black]] which are only 15 months old... even without the 3D aspect considered, the video technology upgrade of this Panasonic over even the newer HDTVs is absolutely remarkable.

title: Beautiful lens with disappointing autofocus
text:
I was weary to buy this lens due to many review of the autofocusing not behaving. I bought 2 copies to hope that one would work with my camera. I noticed within the two copies that one was softer than the other. The autofocus is also not super at low light situations.

My previous Canon 50mm f/1.8 II had better autofocusing than this Sigma. This Sigma compared to my Canon that the focal length is slightly wider and it allows much more light, even at the same apertures.

That said, when it is focused, it is extremely creamy background and wonderful contrast. There is a light color fringe but not noticeable and easy to adjust. Personally I find its best widest aperture to be around f/2-f/2.8. I find the lens is extremely soft even in the center of the frame on apertures f/1.4 to f/1.8.

The other concern is that it is fairly heavy. It can be hard to carry the camera and lens all day with no camera strap. This lens is significant to most small primes.

I believe this lens is the best of price and quality. It has better optics than than Canon f/1.4 and f/1.8, on par to the L f/1.2, but at a third of the price.

If you are concerned about the autofocusing, I would either buy multiple copies from a retailer that allows easy return shipping or mail it to Sigma for calibration. They do this for free within the warranty, which is a nice customer support.
Report this review

On a final note, I have had this lens now for a few years, and notice that over time it needs to be calibrated again. It's main issue is it has trouble focusing on distance a few feet versus the 3 feet to infinity. If you are choosing this lens, and will be relying on autofocusing, you will need a camera that can micro-focus adjust or send in to Sigma for calibration every year or so.

This is my go to lens for wedding or portrait on my 7D, and get lost of complements of the creaminess and color this lens provides.

---
Using the Sigma 50mm on a Full Frame Canon 6D
---

I wanted to write an update using this Sigma 50mm lens on a full frame camera with the Canon 6D. This lens is still just as amazing with its color and sharpness along the edges of the full frame sensor. Using it as a true 50mm field of view of 46º has a different perspective than a short telephoto for portrait. The corners are softer than on an APS-C and this slightly causes pause when having subject matter in the edges. Stopped down to f/5.6 makes the sharpness even out, which is this lenses sharpest aperture

Coming from an APS-C I feel the 50mm look is slightly wide angle for landscape views. I will admit that now seeing the extreme corners of this lens, it does have a slight barrel distortion at the far extreme ends. title: Poor Quality with Samsung
text: I purchased this TV in November 2010.  In October 2011 the TV was unable to read the signals from the HDMI ports.  I have an Xbox360, Samsung Blue-Ray player, and Direct TV DVR attached via HDMI.  If one stopped reading I think is it likely a cable, but all three must be a component on the TV which went bad. I contacted Samsung CS and it was recommended that I unplug the TV and plug it back in.  No change, the problem didn't go away.  They scheduled a service tech to come to the house a few day later and during the waiting period I decided to leave the TV unplugged. When he arrive he plugged the TV in and it worked!  Wow what is going on here.  The tech suggested if the TV exhibits the same behavior to leave it unplugged for several minutes.  Between the October incident and mid January 2011 the HDMI ports stopped reading one time and I needed to wait about 60 minutes before the TV would read the HDMI ports.  At this point I'm thinking what kind of BS is this?  I never had to do this with the RCA!  And how long do I have to limp along with this crippled TV.  Since I had not registered the TV when I purchased it the CS offered to extend my warranty for 90 days if I would register it online.  I did and Samsung honored the extended time on the warranty. Thank you Samsung, because in mid January the TV would not turn on.  It would just display the red light on the front panel and click every second or second and a half.  Another call to Samsung CS to arrange for repair and another visit with the same tech.  This time a board needed to be replaced and the tech had it with him.  I thought everything was going to go well after this repair.  You know things break and Samsung honored and even extended the warranty.  No problem.  At the beginning of February 2011 I was sent an offer to purchase an extended warranty.  I decided to go for the 2 year warranty and I am glad I did, because today the clicking behavior has returned to the TV.  Strange as it may seem I also received a class action settlement letter from Samsung today related to the clicking behavior.  Unfortunately this model is not included in the settlement. I hope going forward over the next couple of years Samsung is able to figure out what has gone wrong with this TV, because I don't want to keep taking time off to wait for the repair guy.  The TV this model replaced was 17 years old and never needed a repair.  Going forward Samsung has joined the ranks of Sony and AT&T and what that means is I will not knowingly purchase any products manufactured or sold by these companies.  They have grown so large they no longer concern themselves with individual customers or quality products.  Based on a couple of searches around the internet my experience is not unique.  Please reconsider purchasing this TV and use my experience as a guide.  I do not recommend this TV.

title: Great All-Around Windows Laptop
text:
I'm very happy with this machine. Fast, light, solid build, good-looking, great screen, comfortable back-lit keyboard. About identical in size and weight to a 13-inch Macbook, but with a 14" screen. Screen resolution is 1600 x 900, equivalent to Macbook and a step up from the 1366 x 768 standard on a lot of Windows laptops. (Sony touts its "full HD" 1920 x 1080 displays, but I found it made screen objects just too small. This is a happy medium.) It's quiet: the fan hardly ever comes on, and when it does it's not too loud. Good battery life: 5 to 6 hours easily without even going to the "max" power-saving scheme.

I have no real complaints, only a couple of wishes. More USB ports -- it has one 2.0 and one 3.0 (although personally I've never needed more); a Blu-ray drive; a Core i7 option.

I bought this after returning a 15.5" Sony Vaio S-series, which had a flimsy, wobbly screen with the aforementioned "Full HD", an annoying off-center touchpad, and a form factor that was just too big and wide. I'm much happier with the Samsung.

One recommendation: whichever power-management scheme you use, edit it so that the wireless card is set to "Maximum Performance" when unplugged -- the default slows wireless to a crawl in order to save a little juice. (If you see Samsung dinged on forums for slow wireless, that's why, and it's an easy adjustment that completely resolves the issue.)

Update 7/9/12: I'm still very happy with it. No changes to my earlier comments. Some people complain about the touchpad, it is very sensitive by default, but I lowered the sensitivity using the control panel and now it rarely misinterprets random thumb or palm touches as taps.

title: Great receiver for the price except for rca output delay.
text:
First off, i'm highly experienced at audio receivers, owning 7 myself currently, and 20 in my life, I've got allot of experience with them. This particular one replaced a Panasonic i had in the living room on 3.1 system. The Panasonic had the unfortunate problem of cutting in and out on certain sources, questionable a copyright verification error, but i digress.

Lets get the easy stuff out of the way:
Quality:
Every receiver today is pretty much going to accurately reproduce what you put into it
Form Factor:
Pretty standard layout, on the face, remote is a bit confusing where the numbered buttons on the top pick your source, but fine once you figure that out.
Volume:
Pretty darn loud. if you got much louder, id question why you didn't buy a professional amp.

Now onto the unique stuff:
This receiver will pass through video when you turn it off. super awesome for saving the nice speakers for movies without extra complicated wiring. this allows one wire to the TV even if you want the receiver off.

Simple menu doesn't block the screen or cut off the video feed altogether when you pull it up, a annoyance of my last one.

Cons:
It will not pass through from the hdmi to the audio output, nor the USB connection. but i haven't heard of any that specifically do this.

it adds a small delay to the audio output, as i have this wired to a whole house amp would like to play them congruently occasionally, this makes this particular setup impossible. (my easy fix will be to purchase a splitter and split the signal of my analog source before it gets to the other amp.) this was not an issue with my last setup.

This is most everything i could ask for in a standalone receiver and then some. I only deducted one star because of the delay.

title: Sounds great, great battery, were a bit heavy on my ears
text:
I researched bluetooth headphones with some sort of moisture/water/sweat protection after my LG Tone (no protection against moisture), which I liked very much died. I ended up purchasing the Sony MDR-AS700BTL and the Plantronics Backbeat Go 2 with charge case to compare. The headphones are priced about the same and are both "sweat proof" which I don't take to be water proof, but at least resistant. I wish the LG Tone was "Sweat Proof" since I prefer those over either of these pair, but both of these are good too.

It was a difficult choice, both are good headphones but neither is perfect, I went back and forth at first thinking I'd keep the Sony but ended up keeping the Plantronics Backbeat Go 2 because over long listening periods the Sony was heavy on my ears.

Sony Pros:

* Solid build
* USB door seems better for keeping out moisture
* Very good sound quality, better than Backbeat Go 2 or LG Tone
* May be better for workout due to noise in Plantronics on motion although
* Better bass response
* Great battery life (so does the LG Tone)

Sony Cons:

* Bluetooth range on this set was not good, any obstruction breaks it. I sent them in for repair for this, don't know the outcome yet but I assume it was defective
* A bit heavy on ears and can become uncomfortable on ears, this was ultimately why I chose the Backbeat Go 2
* Bulky and looks large
* Sound output seams to have good volume initially (louder than the Backbeat Go 2) but with background noise it can be hard to hear music since these are on ear and not in or over ear
* Limited feedback on battery level etc when you turn it on (it does not give any information about connection or battery, I assume you can check the battery level but with such simple controls who wants to learn something that isn't obvious)

Plantronics Pros:

* Small and decently attractive
* Pretty good sound and detail, I preferred the Sony but I prefer on/over ear in general
* Good Bluetooth range
* Great feedback on power/connection/battery
* Good connection management/control (plays active audio app when connected)
* Sound output is more consistent than Sony due to being in ear (they seemed lower at first but once you have background noise these keep up better)

Plantronics Cons:

* Short battery life - I have the charge case which is nice but the battery life is really too short
* Noise when I move my head around and cord rubs on clothes
* In ear - it's a preference thing, I prefer on/over
* Have to adjust in ear now and then, cord gets tugged by clothes etc which as noted creates noise, but also moves ear buds
* Controls are hard to feel out even with the lumpy buttons, have to make sure I've felt all three before I press one

LG Tone: I also had the LG Tone before, after several times being submerged in H2O, the finally died. If these were water resistant I'd buy them again in a minute, I prefer these overall over the Plantronics or Sony headphones but really wanted something with some level of water/moisture resistance.

* Battery life is great
* Fit and comfort is better than either of the others above
* These can also sit on your neck with one ear bud in, which neither the Sony or Plantronics do well
* Sound quality is good, comparable to the Plantronics from memory, although I did not have them at the same time to compare side by side. No noise issues like the Plantronics moving around or touching the cords, also being in ear they block outside noise well and were plenty loud.
* Controls are easier to use than the others and more advanced
* Poor feedback on battery, they beep every minute or so for a long time when the battery is low, I hated that, also no information when you turn them on about battery life, have to do some button combo or long press to get battery info

title: Excellent Phones Comparison Review.
text:
After reading a lot of reviews I decided to go with these headphones.

A little about myself. I am not an audiophile. I like to sit down at my desk downstairs with my parents. When I want to work or whatever I want to do, I like to isolate my self with some music. I really dislike hearing noise when I want to do something on the computer or anything with concentration. With that in mind I first purchased a set of Bose qc15's. Previous headphones before that were some skull candy headphones which I thought were cool but made my ears hurt after extended use because the music scratched my inner ear when the music was medium volume.

I want to do a comparison between these and the Bose because I am pretty sure I am not the only one that was caught in this situation. I had the Bose qc15 for about 2 days and then I returned them to best buy. I didn't return them because I disliked them. In fact I thought they were pretty good. The thing that bugged me the most was I really felt I didn't get my money's worth with 300 dollars. At best buy it was actually 370 total with warranty. A warranty is a must for an expensive pair of headphones, plus I've read Bose charges you extra for broken phones. Anyway back to the point, The Bose was really soft and comfortable, I was really impressed with the noise cancellation until. Then I thought about it, it really isn't that impressive for what your paying for at all. It goes like this, Someone is talking and you hear them well, you put the Bose headphones on they sound a little less then before, then you turn noise cancellation on and then they sound more less and distant but you could hear them clearly. When you turn on music half way they are totally gone. The sound quality was okay, it started sounding more crispier after the 1st day of use but nothing crazy. Now some people ask well if price wasn't an issue with the Bose would you get them vs the ath-m50? I would say id go with the ath-m50. The sound is much better. I will explain the quality as best as I can later. When money becomes the issue and for most of us is the deciding factor on which phones will give you the best bang for your buck. The ath-m50 definitely gives you the value for your money.

Now to the Audio Technica ath-m50. I love the fact you can get headphones that are great for this price range. Some reviews complain about comfort, I really can't say that they are uncomfortable. I find these headphones to be really comfortable. The Bose would be like a 10 and these would be like an 8.5. The ear pads are not very soft but are soft on your ears that make it comfortable. I don't have that clamping problem, overall they fit very well on my head. I don't have a head shaped like a bball, it's pretty avg. As far as the sound goes, I only burned these in about 5 hours but the music isn't powerful. I didn't expect them to be punching your ears in. The bass is really good(I have an amp fiio e6). The sounds are clear and crisp. The Bose seemed to have to much bass and uncontrolled compared to these. The music flows very nicely and doesn't cause fatigue. I think I can have these on for a while without it bothering me to. I mean for the bose at best buy with warranty your paying 370. With these and an amp i paid 196 now if i had a budget of 370 again, i could also add in some sick in ear headphones or maybe the seinheisser hd-25 II(200$). These Headphones are not for portability, and I honestly don't care i do most of my listening at home, but down the road I will invest in some other portable headphones.

In conclusion if you want a good pair of headphones for home use that will block out noise just as good as the Bose qc15 when the music is on, get these. The sound quality is really good, and for the price, you can't beat it.

title: Caution:  severe display scratching problem with the Charge.
text:
I purchased, and returned, this product. Because I like the software, which works on my Windows Phone, I wanted this device to be my ultimate solution. That didn't happen.

First, the product advertises automatic sleep detection. It simply doesn't work properly. Of 3 nights, the first it was OK, the second it cut off about 30% of the way into the night, and the third time it didn't even activate.

More importantly, the display scratches from contact with ANYTHING, including clothing, sheets, very soft materials, even armrests on the furniture. I have a lot of display device, and none of them, except the Charge, ever scratched. In 3 days, this one was covered with deep scratches and the roughest material it encountered was a very soft sweater sleeve.

I am not the only one with the problem. It is well documented on the Fitbit Forum, and people who call customer service are being told "we are not addressing that issue."

In an age of really solid display materials, there is simply no excuse for this occurring. It is not a problem on other devices, and even a Fitbit One worn under a belt, or riding inside a jeans pocket, does not scratch.

title: Would be 5 stars if not so pricey
text:
I waited a couple years to buy this expecting someone (Sony, Apple, whoever) to build something like this a little more reasonably priced. My kids' iPods are on par with the cost of this thing and do 10 times more things. If iPods had an AM tuner I'm sure there would be an app that would render the Witness+ obsolete. Sorry, had to get that little whine off my chest...

I've had this a couple days now so here are my first impressions. The Witness+ is smaller than I thought, about the size of a deck of cards. The user interface is well thought out, it was very easy to program stations into memory and schedule recordings. I have no problems pulling in every station I listen to in my location (about 25 miles from downtown Detroit) on this radio's tuner. It even pulls in smaller stations I didn't know existed. The instructions are very well written. Recording quality is variable, easily changed, and at higher quality levels sounds exactly like live radio.

Hooking the Witness+ up to my computer went without incident, Windows XP recognized the unit immediately. When I first charged the unit and turned it on, I did notice that the AM radio tuner was not working right off the bat, just got screeching noises. I powered it down, flipped it to FM and back to AM and it cleared up after that (not sure the exact steps I took but it works fine now).

I'll update this review if I have anything significant to add or change, but as of now I'm pleased with the quality of the Witness+.

title: Does exactly what it says it will do but kinda ugly. + 3D insights
text:
This little guy is awesome. Yes, it looks cheap but I'm telling you you'll forget all about that when you see the effects. The only way I can describe what it does is that it clears up your image, washing away a blurriness on your screen that you never even knew was there. You need to find the sweet spot depending on what you are viewing, 45-55 on 'HD' mode seems to be the best to 'set and forget' but depending on the quality of the media you are viewing, you could easily go higher and see benefits.

One of the neatest parts of the Darbee is that you can switch it on and off on the fly, so you're not wondering how much of a change it is making to your media, you can see it clear as day by the push of a button.

I read somewhere that the Darbee may have issues with short hdmi cables, so I ordered two 10 ft cables, one for the input and one for the output, no problems to report here.

The way mine is set up is between my TV (Panasonic ST50) and my Yamaha 5.1 receiver, again no issues.

One feature I really liked was that you can go into the menu and turn off the L.E.D.'s on the darbee so it makes no extra light, good for when watching movies at night.

I am honestly shocked at just how great this product is, it does exactly what it claims to do, which is simply make your image sharper, clearer, and with greater depth. I can't wait to try this out in 3D.

Edit: tried this with my 3D TV and the effects are even more pronounced ! It's simply amazing. A MUST have for us who enjoy good 3D content.

title: Changed from a 5 star to a 2 star. FOR 37" & 47" ONLY
text:
Read the bottom for the final update that changed the review from 5 stars to 2.

So let me first start off by saying this. Never, never buy a flat screen tv online. They usually do not have the same warranties that in stores do. I usually always buy off Amazon and other online avenues, but I know tv's like these can bite the dust at anytime. I bought mine at Costco because this tv comes with a 2 year warranty and with a 3 year additional warranty for just $30. So I ended up buying this tv for less and have a 5 year warranty. These warranties usually apply at most warehouse and department stores.

Now, on to the actual tv review. I've had this tv for a couple weeks and I have been very pleased. The Neflix app is amazing and comes in HD (1080) (which I note because if you are currently using your Playstation (720) or Wii (480) this does not appear in HD). The menus and functionality are awesome too. Oh, and the sound is great too. The sound really packs a punch for such a razor thin tv. Paired with the the HD package I have with my cable company this is just pure heaven while watching tv. I'm giving this a very fair 5 out of 5 because it deserves it.

Again, I do recommend this TV whole heartedly, but please be smart and buy any TV at a reputable vendor that offers a really good warranty. These newer TV's are great but they are notorious for biting the dust. Amazon may be the cheapest but their warranties don't go far. Save yourself the heartbreak later and buy the warranty, and make sure the warranty is backed by a good retailer.

Warranty + This particular TV = Awesome Sauce

*******UPDATE*******

So I actually was so impressed with my 370sl (37") model that I actually talked my wife into letting me buy the 470sl model (47"). Both models are superb. The picture is amazing and the apps are awesome. Plus both these models are very affordable (I bought both at Costco due to their awesome warranties and return policies) I fully recommend both these models. Oh and by the way, no I am not a fake review by some ad agency. I too hate it when bogus reviews falsely praise crappy products, but you can rest assured that these two tvs (370sl and 470sl) completely are legit. Just in case though, always check reviewers by their past reviews. Hope this helps anyone. Cheers!

******FINAL Update****
Sadly after buying both the 370sl and 470sl models both had a flaw that made me cringe. Both the models volume controls crap the bed. I loved both these tv's because they had the very best picture available in my opinion. My 37" volume started going up and down during programs, mainly during apps like Netflix. Then it started happening to the other one. Then it started happening while watching cable. I did some research and found out that it is kind of common with these models. I'm really bummed because I thought these tv's were amazing. After working with Vizio on the phone with a firmware update they said they could send someone out. I declined due to the fact that I had already read 3 reviews where this had been a problem and even the techs were unable to fix it. I decided that maybe these were a bad omen of things to come. I returned both tv's and bought a higher priced Samsung. After making the switch I now know why Samsung has a higher price tag. Samsung far surpasses Vizio in every way, except apps. The apps on Vizio can't be beat. Vizio's interface is ultra fast processing apps. I'd say the apps are Vizio's best selling point. I don't want to get into comparisons between Samsung and Vizio, because I don't feel people read these reviews to hear about other products. Also, I think Vizio is a great company and I don't want to bash on them. Sometimes these things happen. In my case it happened twice.

In conclusion, I would do some research on these models. I found that this specific model has had the same problems with fluctuating volumes. The rep at Costco also said that I was not the first person to return these model tv's with the same problem. I hope anyone that buys this has better luck than I did. I love Vizio. I have owned 4, not including these and been extremely happy. Anyways, hope you can see how things started great with these tv's but soon went down hill. Oh well, I'm happy with my Samsung.......for now. I'm giving this tv 2 stars and not one because it is unfortunate that such a great tv, with great apps and picture quality, had to have such a flaw. Anyone else run into this?
