title: Excellent value and the Passive 3D is really amazing
text:
I just upgraded from a 50" Samsung Plasma. I miss my plasma and it is my preferred choice, but I have a little one now and the idea of a 100lb TV with a glass front crashing down on her made the switch a necessity. I will say however, that the M Series made the switch a lot easier ;-)

The Physical TV:

I went with the 55 inch from Best Buy that was on sale for the same here. Amazon said 3-5 weeks on ship time and I would have had to take time off work to be home when it arrived. I did have to pay the sales tax though, but it worked out just fine for my situation. First, it fit in the exact same space as my 50" Plasma because of the razor edge design, so that was a nice bonus. Second, it really is easy on the eyes and very, very thin. I'm not the biggest fan of the silver, as all my devices are all black, but a week later and I don't even notice it and its black around the front edge, so it really isn't a big deal. The screen gloss is not as bad as my plasma, but perhaps more than what most LCD TV viewers are used to seeing. I guess the reason for this type of screen has to do with the Passive 3D, but I don't find it problematic. Again, I'm used to full glass with plasma and I only get a lot of sun in that part of the house early in the morning. So far, even with the sun coming in, it hasn't been an issue, although the cartoons my daughter watches in the morning are the very bright, newer looking shows like Littlest Pet Shop. Wow, I just mentioned Littlest Pet Shop in an electronics review. Its possible having a child has, in fact, destroyed my ability to relate to adults ;-)

Picture Quality:

The picture quality is amazing, and that is saying a lot coming from plasma. I'm still playing with a lot of the settings and fine tuning the colors, but so far I prefer the Calibrated settings with some tweaks. I don't like the soap opera effect, so during normal TV viewing, I turn the smooth motion off. However, I watch a lot of Cardinals baseball games and it looks great turned to high. I also prefer it with 3D as it eliminates a lot of cross talk and makes the image look more like a full 1080p image. More on 3D below. Update: I am no longer experimenting with smart dimming. Its an unusable setting IMHO. It creates too much blooming and flashlighting in the corners. I some may not notice it, but its way too noticible to me to be used. You can still get an outstanding picture with the feature off, so there is no reason to lower my 5 star score. Also, you might like it, so the take away is that you have a lot of options to adjust the Picture Quality just as you see fit. I will say, however, that I am not experiencing the screen bleeding at the edges that a lot of others are mentioning. This is an edge lit display, so some should be expected as it's a drawback common with the technology, but for me, it isn't an issue and certainly not a distraction of any kind. However, about a 1/4 in around the edge by the bezel, the pixels are slightly darker. Its not always noticeable and its likely a result of the 3D coating on the screen. All and all, the black levels are very impressive for a non-plasma tv, regardless of your settings. I promise you won't be disappointed in the picture quality, regardless of you personal tastes.

3D:

I have to say that I'm a true fan of passive 3D and this TV's 3D capabilities are a reason to own this set (so I'm hoping 3D doesn't fizzle out and die - thanks ESPN 3D). I have viewed content in the form of Blu-ray, side-by-side/top-bottom on demand from cable and gaming with the PS3. I have not yet tried the Sensio 3D but I imagine it's very good if their claims of maintaining higher resolution quality are true. I will likely download the 3DGO app and try it at some point. So to address a few common concerns, my TV arrived with firmware version 1.02 and I needed to upgrade to 1.04 before I could manually tell the TV to switch my Uverse signal to 3D. I followed the instructions for a service call addressed in another review and then waited. One person said you had to register your TV for the update, but for me, I just had to be patient. I am connected wirelessly and after about 3-4 days, it was updated. I didn't have to even tell it to install, I just went into my system settings to get my serial number so I could register the set, and it was displaying 1.04 firmware. I immediately tested it with an On Demand preview and it worked perfectly. I was able to select 3D and then the type (top/bottom, side by side, Sensio). As far as the Smooth Motion, I actually like it in the 3D mode. With Jurassic Park, there are definitely some jerky moments unlike the other Blu-rays that we watched (The Hobbit and Avatar), but I still preferred that to the lower definition you get without it. I would just say play around with it to see if you like it. There are two ways to turn off the Smooth Motion in 3D. Either turn it off before you enter into 3D mode, or select the computer setting and it will turn off. If it's off and you enter the menu and cycle through other picture setting, it will come on and you can't get it off, so that's when the computer setting is useful. I have only played one game, Crisis 2, in 3D, but I didn't experience any lag issues. I am curious to see how third person games will look. Unfortunately, I just traded in Assassin's Creed 3, which is 3D, so I don't yet have a game to test it.

Other:

The remote really is as bad as people say. You need a clean line of sight and you need to point it toward the bottom left. Then you just need to be patient. I'm glad an update is coming to switch it to wi-fi, but I have a harmony remote, so it's not too bad. I still have some issues, so it's likely the TV's IR that is bad more so than the remote, but who knows. I have looked at a few apps but I haven't given them much time. They seemed a little slow to me, but it's my first go with a Smart TV, so maybe they are par for the course.

Overall, I will say that I'm very impressed with the TV and it's an acceptable substitute for plasma given my situation. The price point and passive 3D are what really sold me. I have always been a Samsung TV owner, but I'm glad I made the switch. Vizio is proving that you can still get an impressive TV with the features you want at an affordable price. I would definitely recommend this TV.

Update: The firmware update changed some of the 3D menu flexibility. Looks like game mode is the only way to remove the smooth motion, however, in 3D, I really like the smooth motion, so its not a big deal to me. Also, once you launch 3D, it automatically switches to Vivid Mode, so you will have to change off if you want one of your preferred settings.

UPDATE: My settings

I am running the image through a Yamaha receiver, so it's possible the image is slightly different if a source is direct to the TV - perhaps not as its just passing through, but others have said the Yamaha improved color and PQ, so I thought I would mention it. Also, I have switched to Cnet's calibration settings that they did when they reviewed the tv. However, I have come to dislike the Smart Dimming feature so I have tweeked them to not use SD, which was a feature used in Cnet's calibrations.

Settings: Calibrated
Backlight:62
Brightness:45
Contrast:90
Color:49
Tint:0
Sharpness:0
Color Temp: Normal
R/G:489
G/G:462
B/G:381
R/Off:517
G/Off:510
B/Off:515
Adv.Setting:
Auto brightness: Off
Black detail: Off
Smooth Motion: On with most 3D and sports, Off with normal tv and movies
Smart Dimming: Off - Its very aggressive and when you go from a light scene to a dark one, the four courners take a few seconds to light up and its very distracting (flashlighting?) Also, when in letterbox, the four corners are rounded and its highly distracting. Because of this, I just cant use SD.
Reduced Noise: Off
Reduce Block: Off
Film Mode: Auto

I have found these settings to be the best balance between a super dialed in picture with amazing color and acceptable black levels. Using smart dimming does make the black levels better, but there are too may problems with it as of this update. Should firmware updates fix the flashlighting and uniformity issues, I might very well go back to using it. If you like SD or dont notice its problems, then look up the Cnet settings and enjoy the outstanding PQ :-)

title: BlueRigger HDMI Nightmare

I contacted the company via email to explain the issue and the steps I had used to confirm the faulty cables. Driver support for it is non-existent, and spent way too many hours trying to get it to work, which I eventually did. Then the POST screen for the card just became too much to bear; it literally takes 2 minutes to get past.

Finally decided to just yank it, and replaced it with the StarTech PEXESAT32, which works right out of the box, and POST screen lasts about 3 seconds.

Also, the fan has a blue LED light, which is incredibly annoying, especially if you're using it for a media server in a dark room or placed in the bedroom. However, this is easily replaced by removing a few screws and an additional 10 bucks.

title: Mostly Marketing Lies
text:
The Samsung40EH5300 bears no resemblance to the pretty marketing claims made by the company.

It took me a week to get it working reasonably well and then another month (about 20-25 hours) to get most of the settings right, although I still have to fiddle with them.

The Samsung40EH5300 is advertized as a 120hz type of TV, but the function provided is much, much worse than the 60hz setting. This is a 60hz TV and NOT 120hz.

Changing from one cable channel to the next takes 2 - 5 seconds (skipping ahead 15-20 channels takes about 90 seconds - This definately kills channel surfing unless you have 60 minutes to cycle through your channels)depending on the picture resolution of the next channel.

Advertized prominately is connecting a hard drive to the TV to show your family photos. This is so excruciatinly slow as to be worthless. There is no index of any kind and you can not skip to the "Z" titles without going through each of the 1000 pictures before "Z". Maybe you are supposed to view your photos only during a 12 hour Sunday afternoon - not mentioned in the Marketing HYPE.

The CPU in this TV is a real joke. For what I paid for this Samsung40EH5300, I could have purchased a real computer with a crisp monitor. The picture crispness is no where near what I was led to believe by the company marketing HYPE. I tried to return the Samsung 40EH53300 to Amazon, but I was told that since it was not technically broken (only lies in the marketing literature) I would have to pay an extra $90 for shipping to purchase a TV that worked, which I can't afford.

One last thing. The TV comes with a "remote controller or wand". In order to use this device, you must point it within about 25 or 30 degrees of the right, lower corner of the TV. Thats about 6 or 9 inches in width. If you click while pointing a foot away or (GASP) at the screen, you can click all day and nothing will happen. My Cable box also has such a remote. I can point it 180 degrees from the box, the signal bounces around the room, and the channel is changed in half a second. The technology exists, SAMSUNG just won't let you have it.

title: Don't own one yet, reading these reviews to decide
text:
First of all, I gave this product a 3 star rating because I don't actually own one yet, but wanted to give my thoughts about it, and you can't post a review without giving the product a rating...

At the end of this August, I ordered one of the latest Standard Kindles, with the e-ink, physical buttons, and no advertising. Needless to say, I was extremely irritated when I received an email from Amazon about the new Kindle family just a day or two before my order was scheduled to arrive! Looking at the products in the email, and seeing the Paperwhite, I got very angry that they would even sell me the older Kindle without warning me that a new version was to arrive for sale at about the same time that I would be receiving my order! I have been watching the reviews for the Paperwhite to see what people thought of it, because I have been pretty satisfied with the Kindle I did receive... I have been considering buying the Paperwhite, and using it along with my standard Kindle(or giving it to a family member, or selling it to someone). I'm still somewhat undecided, because, as I said, I'm pretty happy with the Kindle that I did wind up getting... I don't read in bed much... when I go to bed, it's to go to sleep. But if I DO decide I want to read for awhile while laying in bed, guess what? I have the Kindle reading app on my smartphone... backlit, yes, but I don't seem to get the eye fatigue from it that some people seem to, and I don't read in bed long enough for it to bother me, if it ever would. So, while improved resolution and contrast is tempting, I've decided that I will wait to upgrade until the bottom LED shadowing (read some of the reviews on this, if you don't know what I'm talking about) is resolved, but more importantly, I WOULD LIKE TO SEE A MICRO SD CARD SLOT! I'm one of those book hoarders that likes to have my entire library on my device, and while the availble 1.25 GB is a lot of space, can you imagine 16 or 32 GB? That would be awesome! I have a 32GB microSD card in my phone, where my Kindle content is saved to... will NEVER have to worry about storage space there... I also store music and videos there. KINDLE NEEDS A CARD SLOT! I've decided that when they include that, THAT'S when I'll upgrade, unless I see enough reviews compelling enough to make me upgrade sooner...

title: Excellent tablet for movies and reading books/magazines
text:
I bought my Kindle Fire HD 8.9 in Best Buy more than one month ago and I definitely like it very much. Using Amazon prime to shop and watch videos is totally a pleasant experience. Using the micro hdmi cable plugged in your TV is an amazing feature to watch videos. Performance is OK, not the fastest tablet but for reading a book, watch movies and shop Amazon goods you don't really need a huge power house, and it is not expensive compared to other tablets. It has a vivid screen with excellent resolution ideal for reading books and magazines and watch photos and movies in full HD. I like the speakers a lot, they aren't very loud but sound quality is way superior to other tablets I have. So far this device has become my primary tablet, I use it every day to read the news, emails, books and browse the web instead of using my smartphone.

The reason I'm giving 3 stars is because unfortunately the tablet is still plagued with bugs and crashes easily with the Silk browser. So far the bugs that I have caught are the following:

+ The Silk browser delivers a very bad user experience. It crashes very often even if you just leave the tablet idle while reading a webpage, you will be asked many times to reload your tabs. In some cases, the whole tablet is unresponsive while using Silk, and it reboots after 2 or 3 minutes of being frozen. If you try to open more than two websites with the tabs, Silk slows down significantly and begins to shutdown your previously opened webpages (when you return to them it reloads everything again so you lose track of what where you doing) this is really bad if i.e. you are filling a form or making a payment (you need to enter all the information again), I would expect this behavior to happen when you open around 5 or 6 websites to prevent running out of memory perhaps, but not 3 tabs. You can side load Dolphin browser to mitigate these issues, however there is no excuse of why Silk performs so poorly.

+ The keyboard input has a considerable lag, you can't write too fast since it will begin to miss key inputs, this forces you to write slowly (lag is less/more depending on the application you are using). Also something quite annoying I found is if I press the space key in the left/right edges while in landscape (just below, the 'x' and the 'b' keys respectively) it doesn't register any input even if you get the sound feedback you did press the key, to make it work you need to press around the center of the key.

+ If I transfer 1080p videos from my smartphone they don't play properly. However 720p videos work fine.

+ Sometimes the calendar app is shown as a gray empty rectangle in the carrousel instead of showing the correct date.

+ It happened to me that while using the Shop application and the Silk browser sometimes I see black rectangles randomly in the screen (seems like a rendering issue from the graphics processor), most of the time going to the homescreen and returning to the app fixes the issue. In the case of Silk, reloading the webpage makes the trick.

In summary, the tablet excels at watching movies, reading magazines, reading books, playing games and shopping amazon goods. Up to date it performs poorly as a web browser so if this is your priority task you may need to look for another tablet or wait until this is fixed by Amazon (I would rate 5 stars if the previous bugs where not present).

Note: All the issues above have been reported already to Amazon, hopefully they create an update to fix them.

text: I bought this keyboard as a career investment. After 2 weeks of use, it fulfilled all my expectations. This equipment totally disregards flawed and unergonomic designs of traditional keyboards, surprisingly kept to this day since the 18th century type writer. The key wells, thumb clusters, split design and the smooth and tactile  mechanical key switches are what I love. They are extremely practical designs. After a few days of initial adjustment, I am at normal speed or even better. I am surprised that the pain, which I thought to be normal office syndrome, is totally gone. I could not place it on my office keyboard tray due to it's excessive thickness. I place it on the lap which I think is indeed a very relaxing position. The flimsy rubber function keys are the only let down both aesthetic and feel for a 200++ usd keyboard. Despite a very steep initial price, for lack of a cheaper option, it is worth it for long term health and comfort. I intend to use mine daily at work, at least for the next ten years or more.

title: A superior alternative to Motorola DOCSIS 3.0 modems
text:
Like many others, I became fed up with my service provider (Time Warner Cable) charging me a "rental" fee for my equipment. Given the unfortunate fact that I will likely remain a TWC customer for years to come, I decided I would take this opportunity to "upgrade" to a DOCSIS 3.0 modem. Even though I do not require DOCSIS 3.0 for my current level of service, it seemed like a good idea to be "future proof" in case I wanted to upgrade later.

My review of the Zoom 5341J by necessity begins with my experiences using a different modem: the [[ASIN:B004XC6GJ0 Motorola SB6121]]. After browsing its overwhelmingly positive reviews, I purchased that device on Amazon and had my provider activate it. Although the activation process went smoothly, and although initial speed tests were fine, it wasn't long before I noticed the device rebooting periodically.

See, although my signal levels were good enough for my old DOCSIS 2.0 modem to truck along just fine, and were *normally* good enough for the SB6121, every now and then things would get dicey. As the signal drifted out of spec even for a moment, the modem would simply give up and reboot, knocking me offline for a minute or two and logging a T4 timeout. This would happen multiple times a day, and it presents a very bad scenario for streaming video, gaming, VPN, telephony, etc.

If you've ever had the misfortune of dealing with TWC technical support, you know that as a rule they refuse to do anything useful in a situation like this. After fruitlessly pleading with them to fix their service for a couple of weeks (being greeted only by suggestions that I upgrade to SUPER MEGA ULTRA EXTREME TURBO service at twice the cost), I decided that my only hope was to return the SB6121 and to find a modem that would be more tolerant of the marginal service TWC was providing me.

The Zoom 5341J is exactly such a modem.

There's no higher praise I can give this device than to report the simple fact that it works where the other product failed. Yes, it would be great if we all lived in a world where the lines were good enough for the Motorola modems to function (and based on the SB6121's reviews, most people actually *do* seem to live in such worlds). But for those of us living on the edge - where service is good enough for our ISPs to blow us off without fixing anything, but maybe not good enough for a finicky device like the SB6121 to stay happy - the 5341J is our savior.

I'll close with some observed readings as reported by both of these modems, and let you be the judge. I reckon the 5341J isn't *much* better, but in my case it's *enough* better. From where I stand, even though the Motorola modems will work for most people, you might as well save your time and buy the 5341J rather than risk disaster with Motorola.

Typical readings on the SB6121 (when operating normally):

SNR: 36-37 dB (four channels bonded)
Downstream power level: 3-4 dBmV (four channels bonded)
Upstream power level: 46 dBmV (single channel)

(Note: these readings are all within spec. When the device reboots the SNR is substantially lower (it's difficult to get precise data since the device retains no long term signal strength data))

Typical readings for the 5341J:

SNR: 40-42 dB (four channels bonded)*
Downstream power level: 2-3 dBmV (four channels bonded)
Upstream power level: 46 dBmV (single channel)

All of these values are within spec, and you would see absolutely no difference in performance from the 5341J's slightly better readings. However, the fact that the 5341J fares better in normal operation implies to me that the device is of a superior design, and it may tolerate conditions the SB6121 will not.

*** UPDATE August 2013 ***

I'm happy to report that this modem continued to work flawlessly - until, that is, a power surge killed it dead. It's my own fault for not having it on a protected outlet, of course!

After that, my choice for a replacement was easy: I simply bought another one, which works just as well as the original. This time on a surge protector, though :)

title: Denon again!
text:
Since approximately 1 year ago I decided to start an expensive (but worthy in my mind) comparison of AV Receivers in my home. There is no other comparison giving better results: you must be in your home, same room, same speakers, same connected equipment.
I was coming from a Denon AVR-3312ci, very nice performer to tell the truth, and I just wanted to check if it was as good as I thought it was by comparing it to other non-Denon models.
I went first with an Onkyo 818: even nicer than the Denon 3312, which in fact I sold about a month after having tested the Onkyo side by side. Not sure if it is all in Audyssey XT32 as most audio-geeks would say on AVS Forum (I have my doubts: since when amplification does not count a dime???), but indeed the Onkyo performed better expecially with movies, with a much more intelligible dialogue, more impacting and also better distributed bass. Then guess what, the Onkyo died on me for the infamous HDMI board issue. Replaced by the manufacturer with an TX-NR828 (disappointing, definitely a downgrade from the 818) and later with a TX-NR929 (this excellent). While the 818 was on repair for 3 months I tried Pioneer (SC-1227K, same as SC-1222K in the US), Marantz 5008, Harman Kardon 2700 and 3700 and finally landed on this Denon x4000.
This Denon represents for me the middle ground between the Harman Kardon "warm" sound and the Pioneer "cold/clinical sound. The Marantz is somehow close but I can hear some more details in the highs with the Denon (note that the Marantz has a lower version of Audyssey, so not exactly a fair comparison between the 2), which is also evidently more powerful with a lot of reserve to drive my Energy RC-70/10 speaker set. The Onkyo 929 is a very worthy contender. Possibly a stronger performer on movies and with bass in general, but its sound appears to me quite a bit "drier", for lack of better terms (Neutral? Flat?) than the Denon. The Onkyo remains a better performer for action movies, I could tell that it is designed to be a very home-theater oriented receiver, while I believe Denon designers had the goal to deliver the best all-around receiver in the category.
With this Denon you cannot overlap tone control (independent Bass/treble tuning) when Audyssey is engaged, with the Onkyo you can and I think this is a worthy feature that I will miss.
What I love of the Denon is the ability to remember all the previous sound settings for each input, while with the Onkyo you have to re-set something (or nearly everything) everytime you switch. Both units have a great remote. I like better the GUI of the Denon and also its Android app vs. Onkyo's ones.
It also works very well with my Harmony Smart remote (most do but the Harman was a pain).
Overall I think that I have found "the one" in this model. It is indeed the best balance between music and movies performance, absolutely defects free (mine is even a refurbished unit), powerful enough and not clinical sounding like some receiver nowadays can be.
The Harman Kardon 2700/3700 are very worthy contenders for music listening, sounding IMHO closer to a vintage amplifier (more so than the Marantz) but not nearly as powerful as the Denon. The Onkyo 929 is the one to beat for movies (especially action movies) and also comes with Bluetooth and WiFi (I do not care for any of those, but you might), albeit without Airplay (I am an Android user, so I could not care less) and in particular with a more neutral/flat sound which can be perceived dry by some (like myself) or perhaps more appropriate by music purists/audiophiles (something certainly I am not). It is also more expensive than the Denon but you get also 2 more amplified channels being a 9.1 receiver.
I am not sure whether I'd have come to the same conclusions with another speakers set, so please take this review as just a personal experience. Also noteworthy, I tested them all with acoustic jazz, flamenco and some downtempo electronica CDs or FLAC files through a WD TV Live media streamer. If I were listening mostly rock or hip-hop perhaps I would have had another pick in this bunch.

UPDATE 22 JULY 3014
I have now owned this refurbished unit for one year now. I have experienced ZERO issues. I thought this was worth mentioning with an update of my original review since nowadays the foremost concern when buying electronics is reliability and durability. Denon has not disappointed me and this receiver rocks! I can only recommend it even more than before.

UPDATE JULY 2015:
My love affair with this unit continues even after having changed entirely my speakers setup: I now use it with an all KEF 4.1 setup, LS50 front, R100 surround, Kube 2 sub. As you might know the LS50 are deemed very hard speakers to drive, to the point that most people recommend to drive them with a dedicated, powerful stereo amplifier. Well, the Denon drives them admirably. Perhaps a 5000£ integrated amplifier might do even better, but I do not feel as I am missing something when listening in stereo mode through the x4000.
Additional element to add: I tried for 2 weeks a Marantz SR7009 and it went back. Quite surprisingly I have found the x4000 quite warmer sounding and better with bass. The Marantz sounded great too, possibly marginally better in Stereo mode, but I preferred the Denon. The Marantz has the newer version of Dolby Surround which in my personal experience is a step back vs PLIIx (the sound gravitates too much toward the front speakers) and it did not feel any more powerful.
Now more than ever I still cannot recommend more the Denon x4000.

Great video explaining the router on UTube if you want details. Search for "asus dual-band wireless ac 1750 gigabit" in UTube.

***UPDATE*** 3-months in

Changed my rating to 1 star.

Just starting to have problems with the router. Both wired and wireless devices connected are having access problems. If I directly connect to my cable modem with a PC access to the Internet is great so it is definitely an issue with the router. If I ping the router I see highly variable round trip times (1 to 50 ms) but with no packet loss - these should be quick (under 1ms) and consistent. I see these variable round trip times whether I connect wired or wirelessly or with different devices so I know it isn't a device or radio interference issue. Similar to so many of these home routers they get too hot and start to fail. For those that have many devices connected (24 in my house) with large amounts of traffic I have come to the conclusion that a home quality router isn't adequate. I've had similar issues with Netgear, Linksys, DLink and now ASUS. They all seem to work great for a period of months but then start failing. Very frustrating. I am going to buy an industrial style Cisco router.

***UPDATE*** Year later - Changed rating to 5 stars

I ended up trying a Linksys, returned that when it fried, and bought the ASUS again 2/13. It has been fantastic. They must have had hardware issues with earlier models. I get great speeds, great coverage and it has been very reliable. Tempted to buy a second one as a bridge. Looking at the AC68U but noticing some hardware issues for some purchasers. I am starting to wonder how reliable reviews are on Amazon. I wish I could filter based on the time span and number of reviews a reviewer has entered. There are alot of fake reviews particularly for hot products.

title: ... bought one of these computers at Staples - we loved it at first for its high capacity
text:
I also bought one of these computers at Staples - we loved it at first for its high capacity, sleek design, smooth keyboard action, and superior speaker sound quality. That was until we noticed one day that the plastic right side hinge had worked its way loose, making it difficult to open and close the lid, and worse, causing the screen to separate slightly from the lid cover. Repeated phone calls to Toshiba resulted in never-ending hold, good natured but profoundly unhelpful customer service representatives assuring me that I should not worry and that they would call me back in 24-48 hours (never happened, not once), and finally being told by a manager that the problem with the computer was "physical damage" that wasn't covered by the manufacturers warrantee, and not covered mechanical failure (which is exactly what the problem was). The best solution I was offered was to take the computer to a nearby service center and pay to have the computer repaired. I resented the insinuation that I had somehow damaged the computer and appalled by Toshiba's outright refusal to take responsibility for the failure of their product to withstand the normal wear and tear of everyday use when they know darned well that this is a common problem with their computers.

Some quick research on the internet reveals that this line of laptops has a track record of hinge failures just like the one that my computer sustained, and not one of the reports suggested that Toshiba happily or even willingly offered to stand by their product.

I have owned at least a dozen Toshiba products over the years, and some have lasted longer than others, but this is the first time any of them failed while it was for all intents and purposes still brand new. Do yourself a favor and do not buy this laptop or any other Toshiba that features these cheap plastic hinges. You may get it to operate nicely for a few weeks, a few months, even longer, but you will always have to wonder when one of the hinges may come loose on you, threatening to damage the screen and causing the lid to flop back and forth limply. And you can pretty much count on Toshiba giving you the run-around. And if you do buy it, don't say you weren't warned.

title: It's a great product for the price.
text:
First and foremost, remember that it's a $15 portable radio. It's not going to be spectacular the way the more expensive ones are. That being said, in my opinion it's more than adequate for just about any situation. Here are some of the potential issues and my personal experience:

1) It's very lightweight so if you want to go running with it you certainly can. I haven't had any issues with shock while walking or running etc. even though the walkman doesn't seem robust. I don't imagine you can drop it on the sidewalk a bunch of times and expect it to work but that's true of a lot of portable radios.

2) The reception is fine for me. I haven't had a problem with it. There's static sometimes but it's very little. I haven't had multiple radio stations coming in on the same frequency or had so much static that I couldn't hear the music or talk show. I know people have claimed to have problems with that but I haven't. Like I said above, if you have issues just remember that it's a very cheap walkman you're buying. It doesn't have the power that a clock radio or car stereo has because it's designed to be small. You have to sacrifice some capability in order to get the small size.

3) I've heard people saying they're not happy about having no way to go backward through the presets. You can only go from 1 up to 10. You can't go backwards. The small size makes it hard to put the extra button that would be required to have that option. It's possible and maybe they'll add it eventually but it's been very rare that I've found a portable radio that allows that anyway. The bigger units have that sometimes but not always even though there's room on those ones. My solution was to use all 10 presets for the handful of stations I listen to. For the 2 FM stations i listen to, I used all the odd numbered presets for one and all the even numbered presets for the other. You still have to click through the presets a little but it's far less than if you just set 2 or 3. It's a little more complicated but not grossly so. Setting the presets is really easy, especially if you're using one station for multiple presets, so you can set the whole thing up a minute or less.

4) Also, people have said that the batteries die really quickly. I haven't really had that problem. Ideally, you'd want to be able to use your walkman every day for several hours and still have the batteries last months. The problem again is the size of the unit. The reception is pretty good and that takes power to do with such a small unit. My batteries have lasted weeks already and the reception is still strong. It might just be the quality of the batteries themselves. I tend to not keep packages of batteries laying around my house for years on end so I bought a new pack. I also bought the new version of Duracells instead of getting the generic brands that're cheaper. That might not make a difference but maybe it does. When you're thinking about buying this radio, just keep in mind that you might burn through batteries relatively quickly. Rechargeable batteries might be a good idea so you don't have to throw away batteries constantly.

5) Lastly, people have complained about the headphones that come with the radio. Considering the least expensive headphones you can get tend to cost about the same as this entire radio, it's not really reasonable to expect awesome headphones. I used them and they worked just fine. They don't fit in my ears properly so I don't use them now but when I did I didn't have any issues. I pretty much only buy cheap headphones. I get a good long life out of the $10 ones I get all the time. If you want to use the headphones that come with the radio, you should be able to without issues. If you want higher quality headphones, you probably already have a pair so you can just throw away the cheap ones in the package.

If I think of anything else, I'll add to this later but for now I think that covers pretty much all the issues people have mentioned. title: Awesome style with awesome comfort

I want to point out that the keys are not in their exact traditional places. The top row is more spread out, as well as the bottom row, and also the Ctrl, WinKey, and Alt keys. This makes doing Ctrl+C, X, Z, etc shortcuts a bit difficult at first, but again, you quickly get used to it and seems to be more comfortable after some use.

If you're hesitant in learning to hold your hands a little differently, and having to change a bit how/where you hit the keys, then you may not want to invest in this keyboard. But in my opinion, it's worth the little bit of change.

The keyboard keys are pretty quiet, and soft and easy to press. They feel a little plastic-ey sometimes, but better than most keyboards I have tried.

I noticed for some reason at first days use on and off, the key input was sometimes delayed, like those old Macintosh computers from the 90s, but maybe it just had to sync or learn somehow, as I haven't seen it happen again since. Or maybe something interfering with the USB RF receiver?

All in all for the $60 msrp it is by far my new favorite keyboard. I just purcahsed another one for home use as well. Ford Cars Chevy Trucks, Microsoft Keyboards Logitech Mice (matter of opinion).

Notice how I didn't mention the extra backspace key? Because I think it's utterly useless. Learn how to type better vs. having an easier way to backspace even more conveniently. I don't and won't use it. Cool idea though Microsoft. Some people might enjoy it I guess.

title: Disappointed
text:
I wanted to like this tablet. I really did. In fact, I would have considered keeping it, but for that much money, I'd rather get something that I can really count on. First -- I didn't have the keyboard, so that's not an issue for me. I was very impressed with the build quality. It is extremely good. The screen is great, and although much larger than my ipad, I rather liked the size. It was not heavy. The battery life was very good (never timed it, but I'd guess it was more than 8 hours). Yes, it's plastic, but so what? It felt good in the hands and was sturdy (much more sturdy than the Acer Iconia w500 I returned.)

Here's the thing. For $650 -- as much as an expensive ipad which would work perfectly (I'm not an apple fanboy. I've always had windows, but I HAVE had an ipad, so I know), it just isn't there. The tablet would lock up at least 4 times A DAY -- requiring a hard reboot. Now, the reboot was really fast -- faster than an ipad. But my ipad only needed a hard reset maybe 4 times a month. In addition, the sound on the 500T (which was otherwise GREAT -- stereo and plenty loud) would randomly stop working, requiring a soft reboot -- maybe 4 times a day, again. Now, again the reboot was fast, but REALLY??? I've NEVER had to do that with my ipad -- or even my 5 year old WINDOWS desktop & laptop. Lame. Lastly, wifi connections were iffy. They seemed to drop randomly and for no reason. In addition, the tablet only picked up my 802.11n signal twice (not showing it at all on all other occasions.).

Now, being accustomed to random problems with windows, I'd have even put up with all this -- because, as I said, the reboots were FAST! BUT -- and I tried to get by this as hard as I could -- the apps just aren't there. Listen to what I'm saying. I LIKE WINDOWS 8. It's fast. It seems stable. I like the metro UI. But the Metro apps just aren't there yet. Yes, you can use the desktop because it is real Windows 8 (not RT), but that doesn't always work well without a keyboard. There are several bible apps that I've grown to depend upon (I'm a pastor), and although they have metro apps available -- most of the functions present on the ipad and on android are missing. And, as noted above, the desktop versions are not finger friendly. But whatever.

The problem is that this seems to be true generally for other apps as well. For example: Flixter doesn't let you find local (or any) showtimes. What's the point of that?? The "good" Google Maps app (which is not free) is pathetic (No real street view.) The ebay app doesn't let you "search item description." (??!!) The Kindle app takes up to one second **or longer** to turn ONE page in a book. The chrome METRO app doesn't let you pinch and zoom -- or manually zoom at all (outside of settings). (IE in metro is actually great.) The Amazon app was nothing more than a "window shopping" app. If you wanted to do anything serious -- like look at your account, it kicked you over to the web. Although the calendar app is OK, there are NO other options in the Windows store at all. These are just a few examples of the Metro app shortcomings. Other concerns are that the games my kids played on my ipad (almost all of them) are not available. I'd even have re-bought them, but you can't buy what doesn't exist.

So, despite my misgivings about iPad I'm disappointed to say that I'm going back there. At least the things I need and use ALL THE TIME actually do what they are supposed to do.

title: Product with potential marred by poor craftmanship
text:
I bought two of these from Recording Store to use them in my home hi-fi system. The product arrived in a timely manner and was well packaged. Installation was simple, but I noticed somethings immediately:

- The RCA jacks on the pack panel are undersized, resulting in loose connections unless the connectors on your cables are tighter-fitting than average
- The RCA jacks are semi-recessed, meaning most RCA cables could not fully engage the connectors
- The AC power adapter is of questionable quality and may be responsible for a slight background buzz/hum

Sonically, while not the most transparent, it works. I tried all the features and they seemed to work as advertised.

But here is the single reason why I ended up returning the product. The knobs are poorly aligned to the marking on the panel. And there was significant variability between the two units I got. This meant that when I set a particular knob to 3 o'clock position on both units, I was not guaranteed to get the same (or even close to same) effect. As a result, I could not achieve a properly balanced sound between the two channels.

I praise Rolls for making a useful product very affordable, but based on my experience, the result is not a good value overall.

title: Mediocre due to shortcomings
text:
Review of Vizio Sound Bar, Model SB4021E-A0

As stated by previous reviews, this Sound Bar will not make you forget your mid-priced Home Theater speakers or sub, but it is a small step up from some TV speakers. The Sub is on the weak side.

In spite of an appealing visual appearance, there are several major problems with this product. The input panel is designed (poorly) to require the use of 90 degree angle cables or adapters. This is the case if you want to hang this unit, or have it sit on the credenza in front of your TV. In fact, if you want to have the sound bar snuggle up adjacent to the front of your TV you will discover that there is no bottom clearance and your TV stand/bottom plate will interfere with placement. You will need to go out to your shop and get a few small 1 x 3 blocks to raise the sound bar to clear the TV stand. (Cables will also interfere here, too).

Even with right angle connectors or adapters, the Optical input is unusable unless you have an adapter and modify it as I described in a comment to a previous reviewer.

The Vizio remote is very weak and IR connection is haphazard even when used in close proximity, directly at the unit. The Harmony 300 remote does work very well. Other Universal Remotes that I have also work well, once you have the correct codes. Vizio Technical Support insists that this unit uses code 1517 and variants, but that is NOT correct (apparently, they do not have a universal remote to try out...?). If you need the correct EFC codes, you should check the RemoteCentral web site where you will find a discussion, some correct info and the codes to use in your remote.

At Amazon I purchased right angle connection adapters for the 3.5mm, the RCA and the Optical Inputs. All worked well, although the Optical adapter had to be modified, due to poor design by Vizio, not the maker of the adapter.

Summary: this is a nice looking unit, both the sound bar and the sub. It would be even nicer if `feet' were provided and blocks weren't needed. Other design features are ill conceived, and you might have to use workarounds to make everything work the way you want it -- which is really too bad.

title: Best bang for the buck
text: I purchased the Philips Fidelio after side-by-side comparison with the JBL Flip, Bose mini and several Sony and Soundfreaq models.  The Philips has a truer, cleaner sound (more "fidelity") than the other options I sampled, save for the Bose, but the Bose is much more expensive.  The Philips and the Bose are the only ones that faithfully render stringed instruments in classical, bluegrass or folk, as well as clean vocals in in opera or jazz.  So far, I have been impressed with the battery life.  I have used it about 2-3 hours total after a full charge and the battery indicator light is still showing 4 out of 4 bars (Side note: the battery light indicator is a cool feature.  The lights are off most of the time, except for when you first turn it on, but if you pass your hand over the indicator lights, they light up telling you how much batter is left.). Since I've gotten this, he has dropped it edgefirst and screen first in parking lots, and on both occasions, the Case made the iPad bounce just slightly and then it settled down. I picked it up, hoping for the best and expecting the worst, but it was absolutely fine. All I had to do was brush the dust off.

If there is any "con" to this, it's that there's no flip top cover, which usually have the benefit of turning the iPad's power off when closed. If you're frequently out and about, you may need to manage your power settings to ensure the device shuts off when not in active use.

Bottom Line? Replacing a screen costs $100 and up. This Case costs $30 plus shipping. If you have a small child this is a great investment. If you're clumsy (and I'm afraid my son takes after me there), it's also worth consideration.

title: Not perfect, but great for the price.
text:
I scrapped my first review, which was 100% enthusiastic. Now I have had some more experience with the set and am more aware of its flaws as well as its strong points.

First, the TV itself is beautiful. It is on par with the latest displays from other manufacturers with a thin frame and its depth is minimal, perfect for hanging on a wall. The picture quality playing HD movies through the HDMI inputs is superb. I tried playing basic cable through the antenna input and encountered the lip-sync issue others have mentioned, but HDMI movie playback audio is perfect. I have not observed ghosting at all with any input.

I am now using this unit as a computer monitor using a 1920 x 1080 input (DVI to VGA) and its display is much better than the 37" 1080p monitor it replaces. My PC graphics card is not capable of 4K output, so I have not tested that. It is interesting that the owner's manual does not show any input higher than 1920 x 1080 while the HDMI inputs themselves are marked "4K". There is definite evidence of upscaling which is not perfect and is most apparent with text. I don't know if a scaling algorithm exists that can effectively quadruple resolution without showing some evidence of that in the display. But at three feet viewing distance (which is very usable with a monitor this size) the effect is hardly noticeable.

Overall, I am very pleased with this unit and it is working out very well for my purposes. I am a little unhappy that shortly after I snapped up the Lightning Deal, Amazon dropped the price to the same level. Sorts of saps the joy out of the bargain.

title: READ THIS BEFORE BUYING!!
text:
No Firefox. No Google Chrome. No iTunes. No Torrentz. No Adobe Shockwave. No Adobe Flash. (Only Adobe Reader)
--I'm sure there's a lot more, but those are just the ones I tried.

Because this computer is preinstalled with Windows RT, the only apps available are the ones that come preinstalled, and only the ones you can download from the Windows Store (which isn't much besides the basic necessities). Well, you might say, "I don't need apps, I'll just download the program directly from the website." Wrong. This computer will not allow that either. I eventually decided just to buy the upgrade to Windows 8, but it wouldn't allow that either. So I called Microsoft and they said you cannot upgrade nor downgrade to another operating system like Windows 8 or Windows 7 because this is more of a "tablet" than a computer.

I like this computer, it's small, it's battery life is amazing, BUT...I don't need it for much. Just school, social networking, and music. So, if you're like me and only really need the internet, Microsoft office, and Pandora...then you will be fine. I like the folding aspect of it. I was concerned about the keyboard hitting stuff but I bought a keyboard cover and it works great. HOWEVER, I do not like Internet Explorer. It's too slow and outdated. But that is my only concern (given I'm not a major computer techie). I just try not to have many apps running at once when I use the internet. Seems to help a little.

(There's no disc drive either. Didn't realize that till I got it, but that's an easy fix if you just want to get an external drive that hooks up to USB.) My gf tried to hook hers up to our TV to watch some movies via an HDMI cable, but it said, "Screen Resolution is too low to play this file." We tried everything to fix that but nothing worked. We never had an issue like that on her old computer.

Hope this helped!
-Aliya

title: This lens for sports
text: I just finished taking about 350 photographs of my grandson's football game last night at our high school stadium.  The lights are OK, but not great.  The common wisdom is that you need a fast lens for such situations.  That is no longer the case if you have a camera that will take quality photos at 3200 or 6400 ISO.  My D800 does very well at 6400.  I was able to stop action at 320 of a second and get sharp shots at f 5.6.  In Aperture I increased the exposure about one stop in post although it wasn't absolutely necessary.  The pictures were very sharp and I am pleased with the results.  I bought this lens for bird, wildlife, and grandkid sports photography.  I couldn't be more pleased.  My wife has the older version of the 80-400 and while it is a good lens this one is much better.  The VR is very good.  Good digital cameras don't need an extra fast and heavy long lens.  With my D800 I can crop to get the equivalent of an 800 mm lens and still get quality enlargements.  I worked in a camera store in college in the 1960's and I'm amazed at how things have changed in the last five or six years.

title: You should buy this computer.
text:
THE GREAT
One word for this Chromebook: Value. No way you're going to find a better quality device at this price. The keyboard and trackpad are EXCELLENT. Miles better than any Windows PC under 1000 dollars or Chromebook I've ever used, with scrolling performance rivaling a Mac trackpad. The build quality is equally impressive. Pick this thing up and nothing bends, nothing creaks, nothing's loose. Because of the fanless design there are no ugly vents or openings, making it fairly attractive from any angle. It has the most solid construction of an all plastic laptop I've ever used. And, last but not least, BATTERY LIFE: absolutely ridiculous for a machine that's 250 bucks. 8+ hours with pretty heavy use, 10+ with average use. If you do have to charge, it charges quickly, and the power adapter is tiny and the plug clicks into the laptop nicely.

THE FINE
The screen is decent, not as bad as some reviews will make it out to be but totally usable. Internet connectivity is also generally good and quick with a variety of routers, but a little slow to connect when resuming from sleep. Also, the speakers do their job, and aren't fantastic but definitely on par with most laptops under 1000 bucks, let alone under 300. They make noise and don't sound awful.

THE MEH
Compared to my i7 desktop (also an ASUS), performance is slow, but that's the MLB vs Little League. Doing some Wordpress editing with facebook, twitter, gmail, and play music open works fine, but isn't super pleasant. This can't be your main computer for content creation, but it wasn't supposed to be. (again, it costs $229). Scrolling through the web and using Google hangouts is definitely a breeze though, and doesn't stutter unless you have 10+ tabs open. Performance is on par with a high end tablet or a windows PC under 500 bucks. Also, remember that Chrome OS will soon be getting a major overhaul, and will be able to send texts when connected to a phone and run a variety of Android apps, which will greatly increase its value as a communication device. Sacrificing a little performance to get great battery life is fine with me. If you were looking for better performance at the expense of battery life, build quality, and trackpad, then go for an Acer C720 w/ a Haswell chip.

THE BAD
Holy guacamole does the lid of this thing pick up fingerprints. Didn't remember rubbing my hands in piles of grease, but you'd think I do on a daily basis by the lid of this Chromebook.

BOTTOM LINE
Buy this, it's a high quality, portable way to browse the web all day on a single charge. It works, it's cheap, and it looks good.

title: Outstanding camera for stills but one glaring weakness for video
text:
I have owned this camera for over a month now for the purpose of having a good quality travel point-and-shoot that could rival the image quality of my old Canon G6 for still shots with a brighter lens and have a decent HD video camera that could rival my Sony DSC-HX9V with much better sound quality in a single package. Well, every objective except one that I had with this camera was met. The low light light performance and image quality on both settings were outstanding, as advertised. However, the one glaring weakness in the EX2F was where Sony had the clear advantage - image stabilization while recording video. Sony is still the undisputed king when it comes to this area. The easiest way to test this is by simply walking while shooting video. The Sony with its Active Image Stabilization on is so solid that the image looks like it glides as you move forward while the EX2F looks like it's on a very bumpy road making the video very difficult to watch. Yes, it may be possible to correct this via software later in post production, but this is an extra process that can take additional time and effort when it could be resolved by the camera's stabilizer in the first place. The sound quality blows the Sony out of the water (it can record good rich bass!) plus having an articulated OLED screen is also a plus when shooting video. I have contacted Samsung Technical Support if the "Dual Stabilization" mode was operable for video and the response that I received was not encouraging since it only works for still shooting. That's why I ended up using both cameras during my recent trip to Walt Disney World. Both cameras had their strengths and weaknesses, but the image stablilizer technology is what always keeps Sony in the game because no other manufacturer that I've seen so far (Canon, Casio, Nikon, Panasonic, Pentax, Olympus, and now Samsung) even comes close with the point-and-shoots (small and compact size is very important when I am always running around trying to keep up with my 2-yr old toddler). So for the EX2F, kudos for every other category except for an effective IS for video. Update (6/22/13) - This camera has become my go-to camera because of the superior audio when shooting video. I also own the Zoom Q3 HD and the Olympus LS-20M, and I could say without a doubt that the EX2F sounds better than either of the two. That is high praise when you consider that you get better HD video and audio in a single package. I have used this to record live bands and night clubs at high volumes and the recorded audio sounds rich in bass, full midrange, and crisp high's with very little distortion.

Update (6/25/13): Despite the issues with image stabilization for video, the EX2F has become my go-to camera because of the sound quality and flexible OLED screen that I often use at the end of a monopod. I cannot say enough good things about the audio because it really is that good. I am really glad that Samsung has placed emphasis on the product design because this is often an afterthought from other manufacturers figuring that most users will never know the difference playing on their portable devices and not high quality sound sytems like in a home theater.

Update (7/25/14): Over the past couple years, I finally realized how much of a sleeper this camera was to a point where I am raising it one star. Besides the high points of the EX2F that I mentioned above, this camera can even take up to (6) full resolution 16:9 still photos while simultaneously shooting video. Even the famed Sony RX100 series is not capable of this. Although the video quality itself cannot match the higher bit rate codecs of a few other competing current models (i.e. Sony RX100 III with the 50 mbps XAVC S mode), the other strengths make this camera a long-term keeper. For future interations of this model, I would hope that Samsung would address the following: 1. Improve the image stabilization for video 2. Have the option for a higher bit rate video codec 3. Add an external mic input. 4. Change nothing else. If these are addressed, they would have the perfect point-and-shoot camera for my use as an event camera person.

title: The Best 15.6" Ultrabook Touchscreen at its Pricepoint
text:
I own three of the latest tablets/laptops and this is by far the best of the bunch in terms of balancing power, weight, and usability. The other two laptops I own are a Microsoft Surface Pro (too dinky and unstable) and a core-i7 Dell w/ a maxed out graphics card (too big and heavy).

Before I begin the technical part of my review, let me say how I use my computers. As an information systems & digital media professor I use my computers for basic tasks like writing papers, lecturing, and presentations. With it's 15.6 inch touchscreen, it's perfect for those. However, as part of my research and teaching, I also use my computers for programming, 3D modeling, animation, visual effects, digital inking, and video production.

My computers need to be powerful enough to not only run Microsoft Office, but Adobe Photoshop, After Effects, and Premier, as well as Autodesk Maya, and the Visual Studio programming environment.

Rather than just list features I'll describe why I feel the ASUS is better than my other computers.

Why the Asus is better than my Surface Pro: Both the Surface Pro and the Asus S550CA have core-i5 processors running at the same speed. The Surface Pro has better screen resolution (1920x1080 vs 1366x768). HOWEVER, the Surface packs 1080p into an 11 inch screen, which is too small to use especially in desktop mode where it's hard to touch the tiny icons. I find the ASUS's 1366x768 *perfect* for selecting icons in desktop mode. Of course the Surface Pro is more portable, but you pay for that portability. It only has a single USB 2.0 port, whereas the ASUS has 2 USB 2.0 ports and a USB 3.0 port. The ASUS also has a VGA port, which is still the standard when you're hooking up to projectors. If you want to hook up to a VGA projector on the Surface, you need to buy a $40 adapter. So to summarize, the ASUS is just as powerful, easier to use in terms of the touchscreen, and has better connectivity.

Why the ASUS is better than my maxed out Dell: the Dell's too heavy and gets too hot. Yes, when I need speed for my apps and when I want to play games I use my Dell with it's quad-i7 and discrete graphics card. But the Asus is fast enough for all the applications I mentioned and I only notice the lack of power when I render videos & animations--not while I'm creating them.

Anyway, I don't want this review to get too long. I want to end by saying that I compared the features of my Asus to other ultrabooks at the same price point like the Acers, HPs, and Lenovos, and what I found, to my surprise, was that these other ultrabooks were missing the DVD writer and the VGA port that my Asus had. You may not need these features, but they're important for what I do.

Bottom line: Highly Recommended!

title: Perfect fit for Ipad charging brick and additionally fits all phone chargers.
text:
I bought this bag during a major re-organization phase of my carry on luggage. I have now moved into separate individual bags which house related items versus a couple of bigger bags loaded with all my cordage and chargers.
I carry two laptops (Macbook Pro 17" and Dell Precision) an Ipad and all the relevant cables and cords through airports on twice weekly basis and was tired of getting stopped at security so they could open up my "suspicious" cable bags and re-run them through the x-ray. This prompted me to change my system entirely, and I wound up purchasing this bag along with several of ThinkTank's other bags to separate and segregate each set of cords.
Now my check-in is a snap. All i do is unzip the partition of my Osprey Meridian bag which exposes all of the individual bags, (which have clear windows so you can see whats in them)take out each laptop and the Ipad and run through the line.

Now for some more on the bag:
1: There is a removable partition in the Powerhouse Tablet, which easily fits an Ipad charging brick and cell phone charger with Euro adapter and appropriate cables. It will also fit a rechargeable battery/additional phone battery perfectly
2: The material is robust enough that it has survived a vicious attack from our new Shepherd puppy. I caught him soon enough, but he was unable to inflict any injury, much to my surprise. (this happened on another Powerhouse bag, but the material is the same)
3: The front panel has a see-thru mesh viewing panel on each side of the partition. This is VERY handy for quick ID to make sure you're grabbing the right bag, or just to see if something is missing.
4: There is a business card panel on the rear which is handy for various reasons, but I actually put business cards in it.
5: The top zipper opens wide enough to fit anything through that will fit in the bag. In the past I was using a bag for this charger with an opening that was smaller than the actual bag, so this is a big deal for me. It also has 2 zippers which allows you to open the bag by pulling perpendicular to the zipper pattern. This is a very fast method to open the bag.
7: The bag will sit upright on its own. It is made from a robust material and is very well designed to stay upright while loading/unloading.

There are no CONS to report at this time. I have already been using it now for about two months and I am thoroughly satisfied with my purchase.

I've been a globe trotter for over ten years now and have been optimizing my system as I go along. To date, this is the very best setup I have ever had and my traveling efficiency has benefited greatly. A lot of time saved with these bags, not just at the airport, but while packing as well.

The price is steep for a bag, but I'd gladly pay it again.

Bottom line up front? Solid 5 Stars

title: Netgear AC1450 Review
text:
I purchased this Netgear AC1450 router from Costco, the reason I got this router because of its USB 3.0 port support; it is easy to setup and go online. Once I went the customized configuration, I was able to connect my drives (1 USB 2.0 and a new USB 3.0) drive to the router; there is a trick to connect the second drive, because Netgear by default created a share called USB_storage once plug in the USB port; the usbsequent drive is also called the same share name, so the 2nd drive was not recognized due to the name conflict, so I have to plug in the first drive and renamed the share to something else like USB_Storage1; then the second drive was recognized after I plug it in. Then I started to move my movies from the slow USB 2.0 to the USB 3.0 disk, 5 minutes into the copying process, all network is down: both the Wired and Wireless network; I then went through my configuration to make sure there is nothing wrong, I could not find any error, at the mean time I also have internet access w/o issue. I then restart my copying process after rebooting the router, samething happened again; I was able to duplicate the problem 2 more times; finally I concluded that the router is good by itself with internet access, but once both the USB ports are initiated simultaneously, it could cause a network service shutdown. I hope Netgear will take a look into this, it is a good router with smaller footprint than the AC1750.[[ASIN:B00DR7EG0I Netgear AC1450 Dual Band Gigabit Smart WiFi Router]]

Update 8/4/2013

I was surfing on the Netgear site yesterday and went to the firmware download section for the AC1450, I found there is a new update V1.0.0.14_1.0.6, it describes adding new feature for the AC network regarding AC Beamforming+; I went back to Costco and purchase the same router once more; I then reconfigured the router and went directly to the administration/Router update; the installed version on the box was V1.0.0.08.XXX, I running update check, it reported it is up to date, but I did the manual download earlier and the version is newer than the one in the router, so I performed a manual update and finished the configuration of the router; I repeated the same process earlier and this time everything was working flawlessly.

title: New persective on the world
text:
First of all, to the previous reviewer who called this a "rubbish lens," because it has "the most serious distortion I have ever come across,": did you really just pay hundreds of dollars for a fisheye lens without knowing what a fisheye lens is? Seriously? In case anyone else is confused, this lens is nothing like a normal lens. It provides a warped image which, when skillfully composed, can be quite unique and interesting (see the example images on the description page).

The Sigma 15mm Fisheye lens is well-made and provides sharp images. It has an aperture ring which locks in the f/22 position for use on modern cameras which set the aperture electronically. The lens cover is a sleeve which slides over the build-in lens hood. Oddly, there is a removable lens cap on the front of this piece. I don't know why you would ever remove the cap and leave the sleeve on, as this results in serious vignetting.

I enjoy this lens because of the new creative opportunities it provides. I love how you can get so much context around your subject, but beware, objects in the viewfinder are closer than they appear. It's easy for your pet or child to put his wet nose on your lens (which you can't protect with a filter). I recommend this lens for the photographer who has everything. You won't use it on every shot, but it offers a whole new perspective on the world.

title: A Video Review on the SMS 50 Cent Wired Headphones
text:
[[VIDEOID:ac6f5e792f26b46882d0293a3c03a791]] I have owned the SMS Sync by 50 for several months. While I was initially impressed with the overall performance I quickly realized that the (far cheaper) V-Moda P2's completely outperformed them. With that as my background I was skeptical when I received the SMS Audio 50 Cent Wired Headphones, since they are a much lower price point than the SMS Sync by 50. Oddly, this is a case where the cheaper headphones are far superior than the their more expensive brethren.

I am very impressed by the SMS Audio 50 Cent headphones have very good sound volume and performance. They have smooth performance although they are a little bass heavy.... at times they even sound a bit punchy. So while I wouldn't say that they have a *flat* performance they are smooth everywhere but the lower frequencies. In truth, many people will prefer this to the *flat* performance of a V-Moda LP2.

Notes-

- I did allow the headphones to break in for about 60hours. I did notice that a pick up in efficiency and sound performance between hour 0 and hour 60. Soooo.... I would recommend breaking them in for a few days before you pass judgement.

- Efficiency - they are very efficient.... to the point where using full volume on my iPad is too loud for comfort.

- Leakage - a bit surprisingly there seems to be very little sound leakage.

- Comfort - comfortable, but not exceptional .... no problems in wearing for several hours at a time.

- Noise isolation - Again... good but nothing exceptional

- The wire has a built in microphone and iPod contols

- Durability - they seem to be very well constructed

- Case - the headphones fold up and fit nicely into the case. The case is the smallest of the three that I have tried.... which to me is important since it means that takes up less space in my carry-on

Final Verdict - I really like these headphones - and while I still *slightly* prefer the V-Moda LP2's I would certainly recommend the SMS Audio 50 Cent Wired Headphones for anyone who is looking have solid performance and are a little heavier in the bass.

5 Stars

I told them that I could not be without a computer for so long and I suggested that they just send me a new one, since the one I had was brand new anyway. They refused. I then told them that I would just return it to Amazon and get a replacement, since their customer service is so good. Asus insisted that I not do this and that I send it to them for repair. On to the product.
The laptop works wonderfully! I use it for editing high def, high frame rate video and this thing along with my software renders video faster than any other computer I've seen. title: Easy to use, weatherproof and a whole lot more.
text:
Read the reviews left by others. They're very informative and will explain this camera better than I can. I was looking for a weatherproof bridge camera for a trip to Florida and the specs of the S1 fits the bill.

I'm far from a camera expert. So far I find this camera very easy to use and for my needs takes great pictures.

UPDATE 8-24:

I wanted this camera to take on a vacation with the family to Florida. It worked better than I had hoped. The weatherproofing handled an afternoon T-Storm, waterparks and direct hits from Shamu. I just wiped a few drops off the lens and continued to snap away. That evening I wiped down the entire camera because the whale pool is salt water.

I was also impressed with the picture quality. As I said before, I'm far from an expert. But this camera made it easy for me to get great shots. The camera focuses and shoots so fast it's hard to miss a shot. From butterflies to whales breaching the surface the shots came in clear and sharp. SR Auto easily handled most of the shots in the parks during bright, sunny days. Filters like partial coloring look incredible. I got a shot of my son walking through a forest using the green filter. The vegetation and forest canopy are green and vivid while my son and the path he walked on are B&W. Truly amazing. Low light and evening photos where good using the flash or HDR mode. Anti-Shake was rock steady while holding the camera with one hand and the rubberized grips handled wet or lotion greased fingers. The zoom speaks for itself.

I can't speak on the video because I didn't really use it. I had trouble with the zoom during video. I don't know if it's something with the camera or me. I'll need to read the manual

The only issue I had was fogging of the lens when leaving my 70 degree room in the morning and stepping outdoors where it was 85 before 9:00am. I'm also going to order a wider neck strap.

title: Many reviewers around the Internet have loved this machine and found this connection problem to be ...
text:
Other reviews have covered tech and specs, this review is how it feels to use this transformer in November of 2014. There has been, by history, a problem with how the tablet attaches to the keyboard. Many reviewers around the Internet have loved this machine and found this connection problem to be the most notable flaw. The machine I got was manufactured in March of 2014 and I am thinking they have done some correcting work on this problem or I just got lucky. The connection is acceptable. If you wiggle the keyboard section with the tablet attached the tablet will wiggle a little bit- but ti certainly isn't an issue and doesn't cause a problem.

I wanted a 10 inch screen because I wanted a smaller unit with me to take anywhere. The obvious issue with a ten inch screen is that some applications, like Facebook, will seem cramped on this smaller screen as compared to how they present on larger screens. And while you can run multiple applications at once you are not going to be doing any split screen work on this tablet.

The keyboard feels cheap next to the tablet, which is of high quality with great finishing. Let's go with cheap feeling but functional. The buffed metallic surface of the unit resists fingerprints. If you are like me, though, you are going to get fingerprints all over the touch screen. Best to pack a glass cleaning cloth with you.

The screen quality, as other reviewers have noted, it is just stunning. This machine came out in 2013 and it still has one of the best screens around. Who knows, ASUS may come out with a new model any day- and having gotten a bargain price with a Black Friday deal and having this lovely screen- I won't be bothered in the least if they do. Watching a movie on Netflix or catching something on Hulu really gives this very high quality screen a chance to shine and makes the viewing very enjoyable.

I don't know why they put a single speaker on the back of the unit just about where you put your hand to hold the unit. Better with earphones.

There is a camera, front and rear facing, with this model. I don't have any intention of taking photographs with a tablet. My only concern with the camera is that it functions adequately for Skype for those long distance family get togethers. The camera is adequate for that job.

There are a lot of apps and games to choose from. The one I find surprising that I like is the Google voice command widget. It is pretty good at understanding what I want for simple searches. I leave it on the desktop and just tell it where I want to go and I get there without having to type in search terms in Google.

The weight and thickness are not like some of the super thin models that have come out this year. At around two and a half pounds it is not going to weigh me down and is certainly lighter on the pocketbook than some of the recent slimmer models.

This transformer certainly has "fun factor" going. There are lots of things you can do with it and it is responsive and lively. Using it- it almost seems like the tablet itself is kind of like an eager puppy that wants to play. It is colorful and speedy and has lots of options to play Android games and play with software and widgets. I feel more happy and playful using it than I do with my more staid Macbook Pro.

I had read that ASUS tech support was pretty bad repeatedly. So when I had to cal them (because I was experiencing a problem that was my fault) I found the tech support guy I spoke with to be friendly and helpful. The first thing he said was- "This is such a great little machine that I am sure you are going to want to take with you everywhere- so let's get it going so you will be able to do that!" Wow. Enthusiastic about the tablet, his job, and helping me- and very knowledgeable and kind. What more can we ask for in tech support? (By the way the number for ASUS tech support in the USA, 24 hours a day is 1 888 678 3688 )

The last thing I will mention is that the documentation and manual that comes with this transformer is pitiful. If you are not used to doing searches to find the documentation you need and checking out YouTube videos about the machine and this is your first tablet- I hope you have a tech savvy friend who will help you find your way.

title: Great camera when it works
text:
I have been wanting to get a GoPRO ever since I started seeing the awesome action shots show up on the web. I finally decided to pull the trigger recently for an upcoming backpacking trip I had. I bought all the accessories I needed, an extra battery, a high speed micro SD card, and was ready to go.

While I was backpacking everything seemed to be working great. The remote and phone apps were both triggering records or pictures as expected, the battery lasted about as long as I would have hoped, and the accessories made this device truly awesome.

Things went downhill from there. When I got home to review the videos, I found that they have a feature that cuts videos up into sections. Which at first didn't seem like much of a problem. However what I found was that every second section of a video recording would not play. I would get a black screen with no audio. I searched the web up and down to figure out what was going on. Apparently this is a normal problem, usually due to cheaper/slower SD cards. However I checked and double checked to make sure the SD card I had was compatible and it was.

I eventually tried 3 different solutions on how to recover the video. From what people were saying online, the only thing that was missing was the file headers for the avi files it generates. The files were 2+ gigs each, so I know the video was there. I just had no way to view it.

After failing at every attempt to see the video I recorded, I gave up and returned the GoPro.

I may one day try this product again, but I am very very disappointing I lost all that video from my trip.

title: power problems?
text:

UPDATE 10/30: In the midst of my SuperStorm Sandy power outage, I had a brainstorm. I took apart the enclosure and disconnected the 3 wires (green, black, red) connecting the power button to the back board. Then, I inserted a simple jumper over the where the green and black wires should go and ... voila! ... the unit is now ALWAYS on ... even after a power outage!
